'''Herbert Anthony Stevens IV''' (born February 23, 1987),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://thugradio.net/absoul-main.html |title=Ab-Soul |publisher=Thugradio.net |access-date=March 29, 2012 |archive-date=March 29, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120329012330/http://thugradio.net/absoul-main.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> better known by his stage name '''Ab-Soul''', is an American rapper. Raised in [[Carson, California]], he signed with the indie record label [[Top Dawg Entertainment]] (TDE) in 2007, where he formed the [[West Coast hip-hop]] group [[Black Hippy]] alongside fellow California-based rappers [[Jay Rock]], [[Kendrick Lamar]] and [[Schoolboy Q]]. His third album, ''[[These Days... (Ab-Soul album)|These Days...]]'' (2014), peaked at number 11 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. He is Black Hippy's sole member to remain an [[independent music|independent]] artist.

==Early life==
Herbert Anthony Stevens IV was born on February 23, 1987, in Los Angeles. He spent the first four years of his life in Korea while his father was in the military, until his mother moved back to his grandmother's house in [[Carson, California|Carson]].<ref name="germany">{{cite web|url=http://www.csnowheaties.com/2012/07/24/the-source-presents-ab-soul-documentary/|title=The Source Presents: Ab-Soul Documentary (Video)|date=July 24, 2012|publisher=csnowheaties.com|access-date=September 19, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102192306/http://www.csnowheaties.com/2012/07/24/the-source-presents-ab-soul-documentary/|archive-date=January 2, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He once recalled being five years old: "I was serious into [[video games]] and basketball, at five. But video games for sure. Five... What was that, [[Nintendo]]? [[Sega]]. [[Sonic the Hedgehog (series)|Sonic the Hedgehog]]. [[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles]] on TV. But I know early on, I really, really liked [[Michael Jackson]], like we all did. Newborn babies loved Michael Jackson."<ref name="Billboard">{{cite magazine|author=Ramirez, Erika|title=Ab-Soul's Timeline: The Rapper's Life From 5 Years Old to Now|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/ab-souls-timeline-the-rappers-life-from-5-years-old-to-now-480657/|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=August 8, 2012|access-date=December 7, 2012|archive-date=January 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220120194700/https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/ab-souls-timeline-the-rappers-life-from-5-years-old-to-now-480657/|url-status=live}}</ref> At the age of 10, Stevens contracted [[Stevens–Johnson syndrome]], which caused him to be hospitalized and is the origin of his dark lips and [[Light sensitivity|light-sensitive]] eyes.<ref name="Billboard"/> In his adolescent years, Stevens was severely [[Teasing|teased]] about his condition.<ref name="complex4">{{cite web|author=Ahmed, Insanu|title=Who Is Ab-Soul? – His Nickname, Black Lipped Bastard|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/his-nickname-black-lipped-bastard|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|date=July 10, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012|archive-date=October 9, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121009071620/http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/his-nickname-black-lipped-bastard|url-status=live}}</ref>

Stevens encountered music at a very young age, due to his family owning a [[record store]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/videos/id.14056/title.ab-soul-grew-up-at-the-record-store-turning-points|title=Ab-Soul|author=HipHopDX|date=August 22, 2013|work=HipHopDX|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-date=February 12, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150212115241/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/videos/id.14056/title.ab-soul-grew-up-at-the-record-store-turning-points|url-status=live}}</ref> Stevens also began crafting his [[rapping]] skills at an early age: "I was on [[BlackPlanet]] [[Freestyle rap|freestyle]] [[Online chat|chat]], rapping my ass off. Text [[Battle rap|battle]]. It is a very interesting world. I think that it still exists online, where you [[Freestyle rap|freestyle]] but you type it. They call it keystyle. I think that is where I developed my rhyming skills. I had been rapping a little earlier, maybe around 12 [years old], but when I hopped online and into that culture, that textcee culture. It really got me going as far as being a rapper."<ref name="Billboard"/>

Stevens claims to have written his first [[Verse (popular music)|verse]] when he was 12 years old, to the [[hip hop production|beat]] of [[Twista]]'s "[[Emotions (Twista song)|Emotions]]".<ref name="complex2">{{cite web|author=Ahmed, Insanu|title=Who Is Ab-Soul? – Learning How To Rap|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/learning-to-rap|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|date=July 10, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012|archive-date=October 9, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121009072252/http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/learning-to-rap|url-status=live}}</ref> Rapping continued on as a [[hobby]] for Stevens, whose parents "saw a bright, college-type future" for him and enrolled him in advanced classes.<ref name="Billboard" /> It was not until Stevens graduated from high school that he began to take a career in music seriously.<ref name="complex2"/> Stevens is also associated with a clique of high school friends known as Top Notch, which he has described as his "first real clique" and commemorated with a hand tattoo.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VZD4ZEixv-s |title=Ab-Soul interview |website=YouTube |publisher=<!-- interviewer/channel name if available --> |date=2014 |access-date=January 8, 2026}}</ref>
== Musical career ==

=== 2002–2010: Career beginnings and signing to TDE ===
[[File:Ab-Soul.jpg|thumb|right|Ab-Soul in 2011.]]
In 2002, Stevens recorded his first song. In 2005, he signed a recording contract with StreetBeat Entertainment, but just a year later, in 2006, he met [[Punch (rapper)|Punch]], President and Chairman of Carson-based [[independent record label|indie record label]], [[Top Dawg Entertainment]] (TDE), who as Stevens says, "saw more in his music than [[metaphor]]s and [[Punch line|punchlines]]".<ref name="complex3">{{cite web|author=Ahmed, Insanu|title=Who Is Ab-Soul? – Joining TDE|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/joining-tde|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|date=July 10, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012|archive-date=October 6, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006141050/http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/joining-tde|url-status=live}}</ref> Before signing to TDE, Stevens was a part of a [[rap group]] called Area 51, alongside [[Brooklyn]]-native and fellow American rapper Snake Hollywood.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nahright.com/news/2013/09/13/snake-hollywood-ft-ab-soul-choke/|title=Snake Hollywood ft. Ab-Soul – Choke – Nah Right|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-date=April 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402182332/http://nahright.com/news/2013/09/13/snake-hollywood-ft-ab-soul-choke/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hiphopfeeling.com/2013/09/13/audio-snake-hollywood-ft-ab-soul-choke/|title=hiphopfeeling.com|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-date=January 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112134955/http://www.hiphopfeeling.com/2013/09/13/audio-snake-hollywood-ft-ab-soul-choke/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2007, Stevens officially became part of the TDE roster. In 2008, Stevens made a brief [[cameo appearance]] in the music video for his TDE-mate Jay Rock's commercial debut single, "[[All My Life (In the Ghetto)]]". Also in 2008, he began recording music for his debut [[mixtape]], at the TDE Recording Studio: House of Pain. In December 2008, Stevens released his first music video, for a song from the mixtape, titled "A Day in the Life", through YouTube.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SKcXPeijs8k|title=Ab Soul "Day In The LIfe"|date=December 4, 2008|work=YouTube|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-date=May 19, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140519054024/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SKcXPeijs8k|url-status=live}}</ref> The mixtape, entitled ''Longterm'', was released in January 2009. It was the first in a series, that Stevens claimed would have four installments: "When I did the first ''Longterm'' I knew that there would be four of them. When I did the first one. So there will be four of them: ''Longterm 1, 2, 3, and 4''. So right now we're at two. You'll have to wait for the next one. That's for the next Ab-Soul interview.".<ref name="complex5">{{cite web|author=Ahmed, Insanu|title=Who Is Ab-Soul? – The Themes of Vision and Light in His Music|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/the-themes-of-vision-and-light-in-his-music|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|date=July 10, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012|archive-date=October 9, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121009071625/http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/the-themes-of-vision-and-light-in-his-music|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2009, he formed supergroup [[Black Hippy]], with his frequent collaborators and TDE label-mates Schoolboy Q, Jay Rock and K-Dot. Stevens released his second mixtape, and the sequel to his first, on June 28, 2010. The tape, titled ''Longterm 2: Lifestyles of the Broke and Almost Famous'' was highly acclaimed and featured Stevens singing on several songs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.djbooth.net/index/mixtapes/entry/ab-soul-longterm-2/|title=Ab-Soul – Longterm 2: Lifestyles Of The Broke & Almost Famous|work=DJBooth.net|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-date=March 16, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150316134022/http://www.djbooth.net/index/mixtapes/entry/ab-soul-longterm-2|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2011–2012: ''Longterm Mentality'' and ''Control System'' ===
{{Main|Longterm Mentality|Control System}}
In February 2011, Ab-Soul revealed he was working on an album titled ''[[Longterm Mentality]]'', and subsequently released "Hell Yeah", a track featuring Schoolboy Q.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/02/10/ab-soul-hell-yeah-f-schoolboy-q/ |title=Ab-Soul – Hell Yeah f. Schoolboy Q |publisher=2DopeBoyz |date=February 10, 2011 |access-date=April 2, 2013 |archive-date=July 14, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714172953/http://2dopeboyz.com/2011/02/10/ab-soul-hell-yeah-f-schoolboy-q/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On February 22, 2011, Stevens released another promotional recording taken from the album, "Moscato", a collaboration with another fellow Black Hippy, Kendrick Lamar.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/02/22/ab-soul-%E2%80%93-moscato-f-kendrick-lamar/ |title=Ab-Soul – Moscato f. Kendrick Lamar |publisher=2DopeBoyz |date=February 22, 2011 |access-date=April 2, 2013 |archive-date=July 14, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714202343/http://2dopeboyz.com/2011/02/22/ab-soul-%e2%80%93-moscato-f-kendrick-lamar/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2011, Stevens also embarked on the "Road to [[Paid Dues]]" [[concert tour]], after being enlisted by fellow American rapper [[Murs (rapper)|Murs]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.13905/title.murs-launches-road-to-paid-dues-tour-with-tabi-bonney-ab-soul | title=Murs Launches Road To Paid Dues Tour With Tabi Bonney, AB-Soul | work=HipHopDX | publisher=Cheri Media Group | date=February 1, 2011 | access-date=April 2, 2011 | author=Paine, Jake | archive-date=February 12, 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110212155549/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.13905/title.murs-launches-road-to-paid-dues-tour-with-tabi-bonney-ab-soul/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 21, 2011, Stevens released the music video for a song titled "Nothin' New", in promotion for the album.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/03/21/ab-soul-nothin-video/ |title=Ab-Soul – Nothin' New (video) |publisher=2DopeBoyz |date=March 21, 2011 |access-date=April 2, 2013 |archive-date=March 24, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110324125213/http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/03/21/ab-soul-nothin-video/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On March 25, he released "Gone Insane", the fourth track liberated that was taken from the album.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/03/25/ab-soul-gone-insane/ |title=Ab-Soul – Gone Insane |publisher=2DopeBoyz |date=March 25, 2011 |access-date=April 2, 2013 |archive-date=June 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130615063144/http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/03/25/ab-soul-gone-insane/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On March 30, a [[trailer (promotion)|trailer]] for ''Longterm Mentality'', was released via Top Dawg Entertainment.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/03/30/ab-soul-longterm-mentality-trailer/ |title=Ab-Soul – LongTerm: Mentality (Trailer) |publisher=2DopeBoyz |date=March 30, 2011 |access-date=April 2, 2013 |archive-date=May 2, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502223918/http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/03/30/ab-soul-longterm-mentality-trailer/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On April 1, 2011, he released the music video for "Gone Insane", directed by Top Dawg in-house directors Fredo Tovar and Scott Fleishman.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2011/04/01/ab-soul-%E2%80%93-gone-insane-video/ |title=Ab-Soul – Gone Insane (video) |publisher=2DopeBoyz |date=April 1, 2011 |access-date=April 2, 2013 |archive-date=September 3, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903030613/http://2dopeboyz.com/2011/04/01/ab-soul-%e2%80%93-gone-insane-video/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Stevens has stated the respective [[independent album]]s of his label-mates partly inspired material on ''Longterm Mentality'': "I compare [the process behind] ''Longterm Mentality'' to the process with all of my joints. Kendrick's ''[[Overly Dedicated|OD]]'' had come out and Q's ''[[Setbacks (album)|Setbacks]]'' had come out. I had these bodies of work to go off of as references, as inspiration. I hear what Kendrick is talking about, I hear what Q is talking about, I heard what Jay Rock was talking about. So how am I going to piece this all together and add my own two cents, too? How do I continue the sound but have my individuality as an artist? It's the same challenge every single time."<ref name="complex6">{{cite web|author=Ahmed, Insanu|title=Who Is Ab-Soul? – His Longterm Mentality Series|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/his-long-term-mentality-series|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|date=July 10, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012|archive-date=October 9, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121009072247/http://www.complex.com/music/2012/07/who-is-ab-soul/his-long-term-mentality-series|url-status=live}}</ref> Stevens released his first [[independent album]], under Top Dawg Entertainment, exclusively through [[iTunes]] on April 5, 2011. The album subsequently peaked at No. 73 on the US [[Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/longterm-mentality-mw0002238997/awards | title=''Longterm Mentality'' – AB-Soul > Awards | publisher=[[Rovi Corporation]] | work=[[AllMusic]] | access-date=April 2, 2013 | archive-date=March 26, 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210326060347/https://www.allmusic.com/search/albums/longterm+mentality | url-status=live }}</ref> The album, although its title is ''Longterm Mentality'', is not the third part of his ''Longterm'' series.<ref name="complex5"/>

Soon after the release of Schoolboy Q's second independent album, ''[[Habits & Contradictions]]'' (2012), Stevens began promoting his second independent album, releasing a song titled "Black Lip Bastard", on January 17, 2012. The song was produced by TDE in-house producer [[Willie B (producer)|Willie B]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2012/01/17/ab-soul-black-lip-bastard-prod-willie-b-of-digi-phonics/ |title=Ab-Soul – Black Lip Bastard (prod. Smith]], that would have allowed the [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. government]] to control the Internet.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2012/04/24/ab-soul-sopa-f-schoolboy-q-prod-nez-rio/ |title=Ab-Soul – SOPA f. On May 1, 2012, Ab-Soul released another music video, for a new song titled "Empathy", the song features vocals from Stevens' late longtime [[girlfriend]] [[Alori Joh]] (December 16, 1986 – February 6, 2012), who had committed suicide earlier in February.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.beatsandrants.com/2012/05/new-video-ab-soul-empathy-featuring-alori-joh-and-javonte.html |title=New Video: Ab-Soul – "Empathy" (Featuring Alori Joh and jaVonté) |publisher=beatsandrants.com |date=May 1, 2012 |access-date=May 27, 2012 |archive-date=June 8, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120608103118/http://www.beatsandrants.com/2012/05/new-video-ab-soul-empathy-featuring-alori-joh-and-javonte.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Joh's death had a huge impact on Stevens and the recording process of ''Control System''.<ref name="alorijoh">{{cite web|author=Alexis, Nadeska|title=Ab-Soul Had To Address Alori Joh's Death On 'The Book Of Soul'|url=http://rapfix.mtv.com/2013/02/25/ab-soul-had-to-address-alori-johs-death-on-the-book-of-soul/|publisher=[[MTV]]|date=February 25, 2013|access-date=April 4, 2013|archive-date=June 18, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130618054952/http://rapfix.mtv.com/2013/02/25/ab-soul-had-to-address-alori-johs-death-on-the-book-of-soul|url-status=dead}}</ref> On May 4, 2012, it was revealed "Black Lip Bastard" was [[remix]]ed and would feature his Black Hippy cohorts, Rock, Lamar and Schoolboy Q.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2012/05/04/ab-soul-black-lip-bastard-black-hippy-remix-preview/ |title=Ab-Soul – Black Lip Bastard (Black Hippy Remix) (Preview) |publisher=2DopeBoyz |date=May 4, 2012 |access-date=May 27, 2012 |archive-date=May 10, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120510184402/http://www.2dopeboyz.com/2012/05/04/ab-soul-black-lip-bastard-black-hippy-remix-preview/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On May 8, 2012, his collaboration with Lamar, titled "ILLuminate", was released. ===2019–present: ''Herbert'' ===
{{main|Herbert (album)}}
On November 3, 2019, Stevens performed his set at the Day N Vegas music festival and revealed that he "been cookin' the bird up slow", referring to his album. He then ended his set by [[freestyle rap|freestyling]] and promising a new album in 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Williams |first1=Aaron |title=Ab-Soul Promises His New Album Is Coming In 2020 |url=https://uproxx.com/music/ab-soul-new-album-2020/ |website=Uproxx |date=November 6, 2019 |access-date=April 21, 2020 |archive-date=August 10, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200810161449/https://uproxx.com/music/ab-soul-new-album-2020/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On April 20, 2020, to celebrate [[Top Dawg Entertainment]] founder and CEO Anthony Tiffith's birthday, as well as start off TDE's Fan Appreciation Week, Stevens released the single "Dangerookipawaa Freestyle".<ref>{{cite web|last=Price|first=Joe|title=Ab-Soul Drops Song for TDE CEO's Birthday Featuring Mac Miller Tribute|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2020/04/ab-soul-dangerookipawaa-freestyle|work=[[Complex (magazine)|Complex]]|access-date=May 1, 2020|archive-date=April 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200430101516/https://www.complex.com/music/2020/04/ab-soul-dangerookipawaa-freestyle|url-status=live}}</ref>

On April 22, 2022, Stevens released the single "Hollandaise", which was produced by TDE in-house producer Kal Banx.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Navjosh |title=Ab-Soul Ends Hiatus with New Song 'Hollandaise': Listen |url=https://hiphop-n-more.com/2022/04/ab-soul-hollandaise-new-song/ |website=HipHop-N-More |date=April 21, 2022 |access-date=22 April 2022 |archive-date=April 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220421180821/https://hiphop-n-more.com/2022/04/ab-soul-hollandaise-new-song/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On November 18, 2022, alongside the release of the single "Gang'Nem", Stevens announced his fifth studio album ''Herbert'', would be released on December 16, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-18 |title=Ab-Soul Announces New Album 'Herbert,' Drops 'Gang'Nem' Video |url=https://hiphopdx.com/news/ab-soul-announces-new-album-herbert-drops-gangnem-video |access-date=2022-12-20 |website=HipHopDX |language=en |archive-date=December 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221220222901/https://hiphopdx.com/news/ab-soul-announces-new-album-herbert-drops-gangnem-video |url-status=live }}</ref>

''Herbert'' was released on December 16, 2022, featuring guest appearances from [[Joey Badass|Joey Bada$$]], [[Big Sean]], [[Jhené Aiko]], [[Russ (rapper)|Russ]], Fre$h, [[Ambré]], Alemeda, [[Sir (singer)|SiR]], [[Punch (rapper)|Punch]], [[Zacari]], and [[Lance Skiiiwalker]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ab-Soul Returns With New Album 'Herbert' f/ Big Sean, Joey Badass, SiR, and More |url=https://www.complex.com/music/ab-soul-herbert-stream |access-date=2022-12-20 |website=Complex |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2023, Stevens performed an [[List of Tiny Desk Concerts|NPR Tiny Desk Concert]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carter |first=Bobby |date=February 23, 2023 |title=Ab-Soul: Tiny Desk Concert |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/02/23/1151374272/ab-soul-tiny-desk-concert |website=[[NPR]] |access-date=March 2, 2023 |archive-date=August 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230811011959/https://www.npr.org/2023/02/23/1151374272/ab-soul-tiny-desk-concert |url-status=live }}</ref>

In June 2023, ''These Days'' was removed from [[Apple Music]] and [[Spotify]] in the United States for currently unknown reasons. However, the album returned to most streaming platforms in July 2023.

In November 2024, Stevens released his sixth studio album ''[[Soul Burger]]'', an album dedicated to Doe Burger, who died in 2021.

== Artistry ==

=== Influences ===
Ab-Soul cites fellow American rappers [[Twista]], [[Canibus]], [[Eminem]], [[Nas]] and [[Lupe Fiasco]] as major influences, with [[Jay-Z]] being his biggest influence.<ref name="influences">{{cite web | author=Baker, Soren | url=http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.24280/title.ab-soul-cites-jay-z-as-his-biggest-influence | title=Ab-Soul Cites Jay-Z As His Biggest Influence | publisher=Cheri Media Group | work=HipHopDX | date=June 11, 2013 | access-date=June 11, 2013 | archive-date=June 13, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130613044050/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.24280/title.ab-soul-cites-jay-z-as-his-biggest-influence | url-status=live }}</ref> He stated: "There are so many others, but those are the ones that came to my mind at this time. Those artists are basically the template to my format as an [[MC]]. They all capture me with their music, whether it be the vibe, delivery, [[Cadence (music)|cadence]], [[Storytelling|story]], or just the [[lyrics]] in general."<ref name="influences"/>

==Personal life==
Stevens has cited the book ''[[The Autobiography of Malcolm X]]'' (1964) as being highly influential to him.<ref>Afromighty (June 29, 2012).  [http://respect-mag.com/exclusive-interview-ab-soul-appointed-genius-of-tde-is-much-more-than-meets-the-third-eye "Ab-Soul, Appointed 'Genius' of TDE, Much More Than Meets the (Third) Eye"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120705040021/http://respect-mag.com/exclusive-interview-ab-soul-appointed-genius-of-tde-is-much-more-than-meets-the-third-eye/ |date=July 5, 2012 }}.  ''[[RESPECT. (magazine)|Respect.]]''  Retrieved December 31, 2012.</ref>

Stevens dated fellow label mate [[Alori Joh]] (born Loriana Johnson) from high school until her death in 2012. Joh died of suicide after jumping from a radio tower in Compton. Stevens references the relationship and loss on his song "The Book of Soul" from his 2012 album, ''[[Control System]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ab-Soul Had To Address Alori Joh's Death On 'The Book Of Soul' |url=https://www.mtv.com/news/9dtpcc/ab-soul-had-to-address-alori-johs-death-on-the-book-of-soul |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005075734/https://www.mtv.com/news/9dtpcc/ab-soul-had-to-address-alori-johs-death-on-the-book-of-soul |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 5, 2022 |access-date=2022-11-18 |website=MTV |language=en}}</ref> Since then, Stevens has reportedly dated model Yaris Sanchez.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kFn-zJDYk50 |title=Ab-Soul in love with Yaris Sanchez, living in the BX & loving HipHop w/ Ebro & Laura |date=2014-06-26 |last=HOT 97 |access-date=2026-07-29 |via=YouTube}}</ref> 

In 2022, he [[attempted suicide]] by jumping from a highway overpass, but survived when a car broke his fall. He revealed in an interview<ref>{{Cite web |last=Abraham |first=Mya |date=2022-12-16 |title=Ab-Soul Says Failed Suicide Attempt Strengthened Relationship With God |url=https://www.vibe.com/music/music-news/ab-soul-suicide-attempt-1234720000/ |access-date=2024-05-20 |website=VIBE.com |language=en-US}}</ref> with [[Charlamagne Tha God]] that his suicidal thoughts were drug-induced and that he would normally not have such feelings.<ref>{{Citation |title=Ab-Soul in love with Yaris Sanchez, living in the BX & loving HipHop w/ Ebro & Laura |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kFn-zJDYk50 |language=en |access-date=2022-11-18 |archive-date=November 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221118181018/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kFn-zJDYk50 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Ab-Soul.text:
Herbert Anthony Stevens IV (born February 23, 1987), better known by his stage name Ab-Soul, is an American rapper. Raised in Carson, California, he signed with the indie record label Top Dawg Entertainment (TDE) in 2007, where he formed the West Coast hip-hop group Black Hippy alongside fellow California-based rappers Jay Rock, Kendrick Lamar and Schoolboy Q. His third album, These Days... (2014), peaked at number 11 on the Billboard 200. He is Black Hippy's sole member to remain an independent artist.


== Early life ==
Herbert Anthony Stevens IV was born on February 23, 1987, in Los Angeles. He spent the first four years of his life in Korea while his father was in the military, until his mother moved back to his grandmother's house in Carson. He once recalled being five years old: "I was serious into video games and basketball, at five. But video games for sure. Five... What was that, Nintendo? Sega. Sonic the Hedgehog. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles on TV. But I know early on, I really, really liked Michael Jackson, like we all did. Newborn babies loved Michael Jackson." At the age of 10, Stevens contracted Stevens–Johnson syndrome, which caused him to be hospitalized and is the origin of his dark lips and light-sensitive eyes. In his adolescent years, Stevens was severely teased about his condition.
Stevens encountered music at a very young age, due to his family owning a record store. Stevens also began crafting his rapping skills at an early age: "I was on BlackPlanet freestyle chat, rapping my ass off. Text battle. It is a very interesting world. I think that it still exists online, where you freestyle but you type it. They call it keystyle. I think that is where I developed my rhyming skills. I had been rapping a little earlier, maybe around 12 [years old], but when I hopped online and into that culture, that textcee culture. It really got me going as far as being a rapper."
Stevens claims to have written his first verse when he was 12 years old, to the beat of Twista's "Emotions". Rapping continued on as a hobby for Stevens, whose parents "saw a bright, college-type future" for him and enrolled him in advanced classes. It was not until Stevens graduated from high school that he began to take a career in music seriously. Stevens is also associated with a clique of high school friends known as Top Notch, which he has described as his "first real clique" and commemorated with a hand tattoo.


== Musical career ==


=== 2002–2010: Career beginnings and signing to TDE ===

In 2002, Stevens recorded his first song. In 2005, he signed a recording contract with StreetBeat Entertainment, but just a year later, in 2006, he met Punch, President and Chairman of Carson-based indie record label, Top Dawg Entertainment (TDE), who as Stevens says, "saw more in his music than metaphors and punchlines". Before signing to TDE, Stevens was a part of a rap group called Area 51, alongside Brooklyn-native and fellow American rapper Snake Hollywood.
In 2007, Stevens officially became part of the TDE roster. In 2008, Stevens made a brief cameo appearance in the music video for his TDE-mate Jay Rock's commercial debut single, "All My Life (In the Ghetto)". Also in 2008, he began recording music for his debut mixtape, at the TDE Recording Studio: House of Pain. In December 2008, Stevens released his first music video, for a song from the mixtape, titled "A Day in the Life", through YouTube. The mixtape, entitled Longterm, was released in January 2009. It was the first in a series, that Stevens claimed would have four installments: "When I did the first Longterm I knew that there would be four of them. When I did the first one. So there will be four of them: Longterm 1, 2, 3, and 4. So right now we're at two. You'll have to wait for the next one. That's for the next Ab-Soul interview.".
In 2009, he formed supergroup Black Hippy, with his frequent collaborators and TDE label-mates Schoolboy Q, Jay Rock and K-Dot. Stevens released his second mixtape, and the sequel to his first, on June 28, 2010. The tape, titled Longterm 2: Lifestyles of the Broke and Almost Famous was highly acclaimed and featured Stevens singing on several songs.


=== 2011–2012: Longterm Mentality and Control System ===

In February 2011, Ab-Soul revealed he was working on an album titled Longterm Mentality, and subsequently released "Hell Yeah", a track featuring Schoolboy Q. On February 22, 2011, Stevens released another promotional recording taken from the album, "Moscato", a collaboration with another fellow Black Hippy, Kendrick Lamar. In February 2011, Stevens also embarked on the "Road to Paid Dues" concert tour, after being enlisted by fellow American rapper Murs.
On March 21, 2011, Stevens released the music video for a song titled "Nothin' New", in promotion for the album. On March 25, he released "Gone Insane", the fourth track liberated that was taken from the album. On March 30, a trailer for Longterm Mentality, was released via Top Dawg Entertainment. On April 1, 2011, he released the music video for "Gone Insane", directed by Top Dawg in-house directors Fredo Tovar and Scott Fleishman.
Stevens has stated the respective independent albums of his label-mates partly inspired material on Longterm Mentality: "I compare [the process behind] Longterm Mentality to the process with all of my joints. Kendrick's OD had come out and Q's Setbacks had come out. I had these bodies of work to go off of as references, as inspiration. I hear what Kendrick is talking about, I hear what Q is talking about, I heard what Jay Rock was talking about. So how am I going to piece this all together and add my own two cents, too? How do I continue the sound but have my individuality as an artist? It's the same challenge every single time." Stevens released his first independent album, under Top Dawg Entertainment, exclusively through iTunes on April 5, 2011. The album subsequently peaked at No. 73 on the US Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums. The album, although its title is Longterm Mentality, is not the third part of his Longterm series.

Soon after the release of Schoolboy Q's second independent album, Habits & Contradictions (2012), Stevens began promoting his second independent album, releasing a song titled "Black Lip Bastard", on January 17, 2012. The song was produced by TDE in-house producer Willie B. On February 28, 2012, Ab-Soul, alongside Schoolboy Q, appeared on Sway Calloway's #SwayInTheMorning radio show, where Ab-Soul called "Black Lip Bastard": "pretty much one of the title tracks", The first song that appears on the album, to be released was "Showin' Love", also produced by Willie B.
On March 24, Schoolboy Q announced #TheGroovyTour; a month-long tour with Ab-Soul accompanying him the entire way. The tour began on April 20, at the Bill Graham Civic Auditorium in San Francisco, California. On April 6, 2012, Ab-Soul liberated a song titled "Terrorist Threats". The song features frequent collaborator Jhené Aiko and fellow American rapper Danny Brown, who proclaimed on Twitter that "Black Hippy the new Beatles and I'm Harry Nilsson". On April 17, 2012, Ab-Soul revealed the album's title to be Control System and unveiled the release date to be May 11, 2012. That same day, he also released a music video for "Pineal Gland", a song inspired by the psychedelic drug DMT and of course the pineal gland, a small endocrine gland in the vertebrate brain. On April 24, 2012, Stevens released another song, "SOPA". The song, produced by Nez & Rio, references the Stop Online Piracy Act (SOPA), a United States bill introduced by U.S. Representative Lamar S. Smith, that would have allowed the U.S. government to control the Internet.
On May 1, 2012, Ab-Soul released another music video, for a new song titled "Empathy", the song features vocals from Stevens' late longtime girlfriend Alori Joh (December 16, 1986 – February 6, 2012), who had committed suicide earlier in February. Joh's death had a huge impact on Stevens and the recording process of Control System. On May 4, 2012, it was revealed "Black Lip Bastard" was remixed and would feature his Black Hippy cohorts, Rock, Lamar and Schoolboy Q. On May 8, 2012, his collaboration with Lamar, titled "ILLuminate", was released. The day before the album's release Ab-Soul revealed the track listing and released snippets from the album. The album, as written on the back cover, is "Dedicated to the beautiful soul of Loriana Angel Johnson aka Alori Joh".
Control System was released exclusively through iTunes on May 11, 2012, under Top Dawg Entertainment. The album sold approximately 5,300 units in an abbreviated week, debuting at number 83 on the Billboard 200 and appearing on several other Billboard charts as well. The album sold an estimated 3,700 the next week. During 2012, Stevens toured with the rest of Black Hippy and fellow American rapper Stalley, on BET's Music Matters Tour.
In late 2012, Stevens was featured on Joe Budden's mixtape A Loose Quarter on the track "Cut From a Different Cloth". The song received praise as one of the best songs on the project. Budden has since announced that he and Ab-Soul have recorded many songs together which will be seeing the light of day in the near future. Budden went on to praise Ab-Soul as "one of the best things going in hip hop right now".


=== 2012–2018: These Days... and Do What Thou Wilt. ===

In October 2012, American singer-songwriter and record producer JMSN, who previously produced "Nibiru" for Stevens earlier in August, for what his label called "TDE Fan Appreciation Week", announced he and Stevens would be releasing a collaborative project together. The lead single for their collaborative album, which was set to be titled Unit 6, was officially released via iTunes on January 22, 2013. The single, titled "You're Gone", features vocals from both artists, as well as production from JMSN. On March 26, 2013, it was announced that Ab-Soul would be featured on XXL's 2013 Freshman Class issue, alongside Schoolboy Q and other up-and-coming rappers.
On August 6, 2013, after a near four-month hiatus, Stevens released a new song produced by Willie B, titled "Christopher DRONEr", alluding to former LAPD police officer Christopher Dorner. Along with the song, he announced he was working on a new solo project. The following day he would speak to XXL and say that he and JMSN had finished the Unit 6 album, however their management could not "see eye to eye", so the project was ultimately shelved for a possible later release, with Stevens saying: "As of right now it's sounding like prequel to my album." He went on to confirm that JMSN and Jhene Aiko will appear on the upcoming solo project. On October 17, 2013, Stevens stated that he was close to finalizing the project. Then later that week, he confirmed that the project had been turned in for mixing and cleared up rumors that it was titled Black Lip Pastor. With the release of the 56th Annual Grammy Awards nominations, it was revealed Stevens was nominated for Album of the Year for his participation on Macklemore & Ryan Lewis' debut album, The Heist.
On January 2, 2014, Stevens revealed he had turned in two projects to his label Top Dawg, before the year 2013, was over: "I turned in 2 projects last year, yea I know what your thinking, let's see where this year takes me..." he tweeted. On January 6, 2014, in an interview with Bootleg Kev, when speaking on the album Stevens stated: "Ali is mixing it right now," and that they were waiting on the perfect way to present the project, as a result of creative releases such as Nipsey Hussle's Crenshaw. He also revealed the album is about progression and confirmed there would be appearances from his TDE label-mates, as well as production from hip hop producer Statik Selektah. On April 11, 2014, Stevens announced he was also working on the third installment in the Longterm series.

On May 5, 2014, Stevens took to Twitter to announce his third album would be titled These Days.... On May 30, 2014, Top Dawg management took to Twitter to reveal These Days..., is scheduled for a June 24 release date. That same day, TDE management also unveiled the cover art for the album and released a snippet of a music video for Stevens' song "Stigmata". On June 21, 2014, Stevens released a music video for a song titled "Closure", taken from These Days.... The album debuted at number 11 on the US Billboard 200 chart, with first-week sales of 21,812 copies in the United States and has received generally positive reviews from music critics.
In October 2014, in an interview with Montreality, Stevens revealed the title for his first in-store retail project would be Longterm 3. In February 2015, Ab-Soul premiered the song "47 Bars" online, produced by The Alchemist. In July 2015, Stevens tweeted that his next album was "almost done". In July 2015, Stevens gave an update on the album: "My album's almost done..." he wrote on Twitter, adding, "It's a love story". He completed the post with the hashtag "DWTW", presumably the album title acronym to which he kept alluding.
On June 8, 2016, via Twitter, Stevens revealed he had completed his upcoming album and turned it in for mixing. The album, titled Do What Thou Wilt., was released December 9, 2016.
In 2018, Stevens appeared on the song Bloody Waters with Anderson .Paak & James Blake from Black Panther: The Album


=== 2019–present: Herbert ===

On November 3, 2019, Stevens performed his set at the Day N Vegas music festival and revealed that he "been cookin' the bird up slow", referring to his album. He then ended his set by freestyling and promising a new album in 2020.
On April 20, 2020, to celebrate Top Dawg Entertainment founder and CEO Anthony Tiffith's birthday, as well as start off TDE's Fan Appreciation Week, Stevens released the single "Dangerookipawaa Freestyle".
On April 22, 2022, Stevens released the single "Hollandaise", which was produced by TDE in-house producer Kal Banx.
On November 18, 2022, alongside the release of the single "Gang'Nem", Stevens announced his fifth studio album Herbert, would be released on December 16, 2022.
Herbert was released on December 16, 2022, featuring guest appearances from Joey Bada$$, Big Sean, Jhené Aiko, Russ, Fre$h, Ambré, Alemeda, SiR, Punch, Zacari, and Lance Skiiiwalker.
In February 2023, Stevens performed an NPR Tiny Desk Concert.
In June 2023, These Days was removed from Apple Music and Spotify in the United States for currently unknown reasons. However, the album returned to most streaming platforms in July 2023.
In November 2024, Stevens released his sixth studio album Soul Burger, an album dedicated to Doe Burger, who died in 2021.


== Artistry ==


=== Influences ===
Ab-Soul cites fellow American rappers Twista, Canibus, Eminem, Nas and Lupe Fiasco as major influences, with Jay-Z being his biggest influence. He stated: "There are so many others, but those are the ones that came to my mind at this time. Those artists are basically the template to my format as an MC. They all capture me with their music, whether it be the vibe, delivery, cadence, story, or just the lyrics in general."


== Personal life ==
Stevens has cited the book The Autobiography of Malcolm X (1964) as being highly influential to him.
Stevens dated fellow label mate Alori Joh (born Loriana Johnson) from high school until her death in 2012. Joh died of suicide after jumping from a radio tower in Compton. Stevens references the relationship and loss on his song "The Book of Soul" from his 2012 album, Control System. Since then, Stevens has reportedly dated model Yaris Sanchez. 
In 2022, he attempted suicide by jumping from a highway overpass, but survived when a car broke his fall. He revealed in an interview with Charlamagne Tha God that his suicidal thoughts were drug-induced and that he would normally not have such feelings.

'''UK underground rap''' (also referred to as '''UK underground''', '''UK UG''', or '''Overground''') is a [[hip-hop]] [[music genre]], [[counterculture]] and [[Indie music scene|scene]] of [[Experimental music|experimental]] [[UK rap]] that emerged in [[London]] during the early 2020s. It has been called "the UK's rap revolution".<ref name="Dazed" /> The scene differs from earlier waves of [[Underground hip-hop|underground]] [[UK rap|UK hip-hop]] through its strong influence from [[Music of the United States|American]] [[internet rap]] genres such as [[cloud rap]], [[Plugg music|plugg]], [[Rage music|rage]] and [[Jerk (music genre)|jerk]].

The genre is known for its experimental and [[Eclecticism|eclectic]] sound, but is typically characterised by heavily [[Distortion (music)|distorted]], [[Bass (sound)|bass-heavy]] production built around clipped, burst [[Roland TR-808|808s]] and [[Snare drum|snare]]-heavy drum patterns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johri |first=Antonio |date=12 April 2026 |title=UK Underground Rap: Essential Projects of 2026 (So Far) |url=https://www.complex.com/music/a/antonio-johri/uk-underground-rap-projects-2026 |access-date=10 June 2026 |website=Complex |language=en}}</ref> Beats are usually 130 to 160 [[Beats per minute|BPM]] and frequently feature distorted [[Lo-fi music|lo-fi]] [[Texture (music)|textures]] and backward [[Loop (music)|loops]], alongside sparse [[Melody|melodic elements]] and glassy, [[rompler]]-style [[digital piano]] and skittering percussion.<ref name=":24">{{Cite web |date=21 January 2026 |title=The Sounds of UK Underground Rap #2 |url=https://tnam.uk/the-sounds-of-uk-underground-rap-pt-2-12-2025/ |access-date=10 June 2026 |website=TNAM.UK |language=en-GB}}</ref> Vocal delivery tends toward flat, monotone rapping over abrasive instrumentals, though some artists employ melodic, [[AutoTune]]d approaches.<ref name=":17">{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=15 December 2025 |title=‘UK Ug’: How Gen Z Brits reinvented rap in 2025 |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/69279/1/uk-ug-gen-z-brits-reinvented-rap-2025-fakemink-esdeekid-jim-legxacy |access-date=10 June 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> Lyrics are often introspective and vulnerable, and frequently mention pride in being [[Youth in the United Kingdom|young]] and British despite the [[United Kingdom cost-of-living crisis|difficult socioeconomic circumstances]] faced by [[Generation Z]].<ref name=":17" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=27 May 2026 |title=Opportunities shrinking for too many young people, says major report on 'lost generation' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cy026x9jpd0o |access-date=10 June 2026 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kollewe |first=Julia |date=9 June 2026 |title=UK’s biggest retailers urge government to act on youth unemployment |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/jun/09/uk-top-retailers-government-jobless-young-people |access-date=10 June 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Much like the [[Britpop]] and [[Punk subculture|punk]] movements, the scene places [[British national identity|Britishness]] at the forefront, with many artists of foreign backgrounds, especially [[Black British people|Black British]] artists, reclaiming [[Union Jack|the Union Jack]] and [[Culture of the United Kingdom|British cultural imagery]] as an act of defiance against the [[Far-right politics in the United Kingdom|far-right]]'s [[Operation Raise the Colours|use of the Union Jack]] and [[2024 United Kingdom riots|rising anti-immigration rhetoric]].<ref name=":0" /> Speaking with ''[[The Guardian]]'', director Lauzza added that young people were "creating our own Britain and our own culture that we can be proud of".<ref name=":0" />

Notable artists associated with the scene include [[EsDeeKid]],<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Shutler |first=Ali |date=18 May 2026 |title=EsDeeKid has arrived in ‘Fortnite’ |url=https://www.nme.com/news/gaming-news/esdeekid-fortnite-bundle-cost-items-skin-jam-tracks-3945916 |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=NME |language=en-GB}}</ref> [[Fakemink]],<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Suskind |first=Alex |date=11 May 2026 |title=Fakemink Announces Release Date for New Album Terrified |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/fakemink-announces-release-date-for-new-album-terrified/ |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=Pitchfork |language=en-US}}</ref> Rico Ace,<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=10 April 2026 |title=The rise of Rico Ace in 5 tracks |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/70068/1/the-rise-of-rico-ace-in-5-tracks-esdeekid-uk-ug |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> [[Fimiguerrero]],<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Wonderland |date=8 March 2024 |title=Fimiguerrero: Sorcerer of Rage |url=https://www.wonderlandmagazine.com/2024/03/08/fimiguerrero/ |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=Wonderland |language=en-GB}}</ref> [[Feng (rapper)|Feng]],<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=12 January 2026 |title=New year, new Feng |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/69391/1/new-year-same-feng-uk-ug-croydon-london-rap-cali-crazy-interview |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> [[Lancey Foux]],<ref name=":11">{{Cite web |date=20 April 2026 |title=Sounds of the Underground: Lancey Foux Is Rewriting the Rules of UK Rap |url=https://www.redbull.com/gb-en/theredbulletin/lancey-foux-underground-uk-rap |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=Red Bull |language=en-gb}}</ref> [[Jim Legxacy]],<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |date=8 January 2026 |title=Sound of 2026: Rap polymath Jim Legxacy is the runner-up |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj4lxz1yvddo |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> and [[YT (rapper)|YT]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=14 January 2026 |title=When did UK underground rap get so Christian? |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/69393/1/when-did-uk-underground-rap-get-so-christian-ug-yt |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> The scene has achieved significant [[critic]]al and commercial success, and much like the name "[[Indie rock|indie]]" rock, the term "underground" is often used to refer to the genre [[Musical style|stylistically]] rather than denoting popularity.<ref name="Dazed" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" />

== Characteristics ==
[[File:Collaborations Between UK Underground Artists 2026.png|thumb|The interconnected nature of the scene has been described as one of its defining features.<ref name=":4" />|200x200px]]
The interconnected and collaborative nature of the scene is one of its defining features. ''[[The Fader]]'' has stated that it separates the scene from previous British scenes such as [[Grime music|grime]], [[afrobeats]] and [[Drill music|drill]].<ref name=":4" /> [[Romford]] rapper [[YT (rapper)|YT]] added that most members of the scene are "legitimate friends, not simply coworkers."<ref>{{Cite web |title=GEN F: YT owns U.K. rap’s new swag |url=https://www.thefader.com/2025/05/12/yt-arcteryx-oi-jim-legxacy-uk-rap-interview |access-date=14 June 2026 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref> In 2026, ''Culted'' magazine stated that the scene was becoming "increasingly connected".<ref name=":21">{{Cite web |last=Lynch |first=Jack |date=2026-08-05 |title=The UK vs US underground music debate {{!}} Culted Music |url=https://culted.com/music/the-uk-vs-us-underground-music-debate/ |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Culted |language=en}}</ref>  

The scene draws heavily from American [[internet rap]],''<ref name=":4" />'' with artists often referencing American brands, [[Culture of the United States|pop culture]] and athletes.''<ref name=":4" />'' However, the scene maintains a strong regional British identity, with many artists rapping about everyday life in modern Britain and using their natural [[Regional accents of English|regional accents]] rather than adopting [[Americanization|Americanised]] accents historically used by some British acts. [[EsDeeKid]], for example, has been noted for rapping in a "thick" [[Scouse]] accent.''<ref name=":4" />'' Other artists have similarly embraced local identity, with [[Jim Legxacy]] and [[YT (rapper)|YT]] frequently expressing pride in being Londoners, and in their respective [[London boroughs]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Petridis |first=Alexis |date=17 July 2025 |title=Jim Legxacy: Black British Music review – London iconoclast catalyses chaos into a major mixtape |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2025/jul/17/jim-legxacy-black-british-music-review |access-date=27 May 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite web |title=GEN F: YT owns U.K. rap’s new swag |url=https://www.thefader.com/2025/05/12/yt-arcteryx-oi-jim-legxacy-uk-rap-interview |access-date=27 May 2026 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref>

British magazine ''[[Dazed]]'' noted that several artists in the scene were from [[Generation Z]] and had been robbed of their youth due to the impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="Dazed">{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=28 February 2025 |title=9 underground artists leading the UK’s rap revolution |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/66191/1/dazed-uk-rappers-cover-spring-2025-victory-lap-yt-niko-b-bxks-jim-legxacy-kwes-e |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> In 2025, 86% of UK underground listeners on [[SoundCloud]] were from Gen Z. Director Lauzza added that "[[Mass media in the United Kingdom|The news]] is just negative, negative, negative: it can be very draining for the average young person." and "We’re all just reaching for the last time we remember being truly happy, when you could come home from school and slap on [[FIFA (video game series)|FIFA]] and nothing else mattered."<ref name=":0" />

== Etymology ==
[[File:London_Underground_Roundel,_London_SW1_-_geograph.org.uk_-_4291435.jpg|thumb|The visual identity of the [[London Underground]] and [[London Overground|Overground]] networks has been adopted by some UK underground rap artists due to coincidences in naming.<ref name="RedBullOverground" /><ref name=":16" />|180x180px]]
The UK underground rap scene has been referred to by publications as "UK UG" and "the UK's rap revolution".<ref name="Dazed" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Dazed|date=29 December 2025|title=Zukovstheworld on the UK Ug scene: ‘It’s modern pop music’|url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/69346/1/its-modern-pop-music-zukovstheworld-on-the-uk-ug-scene|access-date=17 January 2026|website=Dazed|language=en}}</ref> The genre is sometimes simply referred to as "UK Underground".<ref>{{Cite web |last=and Jed Dixon |date=8 April 2026 |title=How did the UK underground go international? |url=https://epigram.org.uk/how-did-the-uk-underground-go-international/ |access-date=27 May 2026 |website=Epigram |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ceebo: "Art is part of an instrument for getting my beliefs out there" {{!}} Interview |url=https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/features/interviews/ceebo-on-the-rise |access-date=27 May 2026 |website=The Line of Best Fit |language=en-US}}</ref> Much like "[[Indie rock|indie]]" rock, the term "underground" is often used to refer to the genre [[Musical style|stylistically]] rather than denoting popularity.<ref name="Dazed" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" />

Some artists and publications have advocated for a new name for the scene to differentiate it from [[UK rap#Origins|other UK underground scenes]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rap It Up: The Underground Is Officially Overground |url=https://trenchtrenchtrench.com/features/rap-it-up-the-underground-is-officially-overground |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=trenchtrenchtrench.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=GEN F: YT owns U.K. rap’s new swag |url=https://www.thefader.com/2025/05/12/yt-arcteryx-oi-jim-legxacy-uk-rap-interview |access-date=27 May 2026 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> [[Lancey Foux]], a pioneer of the style,<ref name=":26">{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=2026-07-24 |title=Lancey Foux: The godfather of UK Ug is back |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/70692/1/lancey-foux-godfather-of-uk-ug-interview-the-time-of-our-lives |access-date=2026-08-13 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> has argued that "underground" as a label is "very restrictive", adding that "[[EsDeeKid]] is one of the biggest [[:Category:British musicians|UK artists]], so why would you call him underground?" Foux suggested the name "Overground" to describe the new scene and sound,<ref name=":0" /> the term being a reference to the [[London Overground]] train network.<ref name="RedBullOverground">{{Cite web |date=20 April 2026 |title=Sounds of the Underground: Lancey Foux Is Rewriting the Rules of UK Rap |url=https://www.redbull.com/gb-en/theredbulletin/lancey-foux-underground-uk-rap |access-date=28 April 2026 |website=Red Bull |language=en-gb |last=Mukhtar |first=Amel}}</ref> ''[[The Fader]]'' added that "[This] cohort has the goal of reshaping the overground in their distinct vision."<ref name=":16" />

== History ==

=== 2015–2023: Origins ===
[[File:Lancey Foux, Live in Glasgow (2023).jpg|thumb|[[Stratford, London|Stratford]] rapper [[Lancey Foux]] has been called "fundamental" to the scene's initial success and referred to as the "[[Crime boss|godfather]]" of the movement.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=2026-07-24 |title=Lancey Foux: The godfather of UK Ug is back |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/70692/1/lancey-foux-godfather-of-uk-ug-interview-the-time-of-our-lives |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref>|250x250px]]
According to ''[[The Guardian]]'', London rapper [[Lancey Foux]] was "fundamental" to the scene's initial growth and has been described as "The Godfather of UK UG".<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":26" /> British DJ [[Kenny Allstar]] stated "He started in 2015, and couldn't be boxed in: not [[Drill music|drill]], or [[Afroswing]], or [[Trap music|trap]]. He was more outlandish with his approach to the music, using heavy melodic vibes with distorted beats. It created a new wave."<ref name=":0" /> 

The scene began growing through the rising popularity of the [[plugg]] sound in 2021.<ref name=":4" /> The single "Arc'teryx" by [[Romford]] rapper [[YT (rapper)|YT]] has been cited as the song that "heralded the new scene's subsumption of American rap traditions mixed in with splashes of homegrown flavor".<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=9 key moments in the rise of U.K. rap’s new underground |url=https://www.thefader.com/2025/06/06/uk-rap-underground-timeline-key-artists-fakemink-yt |access-date=25 July 2025 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref> 

[[South London]] rapper [[Zukovstheworld]] has been called a pioneer of the style. British magazine ''[[Dazed]]'' stated that "Zuko was UK Ug ''before'' UK Ug"<ref name=":1" /> and added that he "gave [[Fakemink]] some of his first features... hopped on [[Wraith9]] beats long before [[Timothée Chalamet]] had ever heard of [[EsDeeKid]], and has been fusing [[DIY punk ethic|DIY punk]] and [[Indie rock|indie]] sensibilities with [[Trap music|trap]] and [[rage beats]] as far back as 2022."<ref name=":1" /> 

British rapper [[Phreshboyswag]] has been labelled as a key figure in the rise of the UK underground rap scene, although ''[[The Fader]]'' noted that he was more associated with the New York [[jerk revival]] scene.<ref name=":22">{{Cite web |title=9 key moments in the rise of U.K. rap’s new underground |url=https://www.thefader.com/2025/06/06/uk-rap-underground-timeline-key-artists-fakemink-yt |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref>
=== 2024–2026: Rise to mainstream ===
[[File:Fakemink performing in London, photographed by Teddy Westside.jpg|thumb|[[Essex]] rapper [[Fakemink]] has been called the [[Figurehead|face]] of the movement.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":21" />|250x250px]]
While rooted in the US, [[jerk music]] began to gain momentum in the UK in 2024. Led by artists like Fakemink,<ref name=":32">{{Cite web |last=Madden |first=Emma |title=fakemink: “Givenchy” |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/tracks/fakemink-givenchy/ |access-date=29 June 2025 |website=Pitchfork |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=fakemink Is The Hottest DIY Artist In The World Right Now |url=https://dmy.co/features/fakemink-is-the-hottest-diy-artist-in-the-world-right-now |access-date=25 July 2025 |website=dmy.co |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=8 July 2025 |title=The rise of Fakemink in 5 tracks |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/68204/1/londons-saviour-the-rise-of-fakemink-in-5-tracks-makka-blow-me |access-date=25 July 2025 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=A |first=Aron |date=30 March 2023 |title=Who Is Fakemink? The UK Rapper Winning Co-Signs From Drake, Playboi Carti, Frank Ocean & More |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/953474-fakemink-who-is-everything-to-know-hip-hop-news |access-date=15 November 2025 |website=HotNewHipHop |language=en}}</ref> as well as [[YT (rapper)|YT]] with his single "Black and Tan", whose music video made use of the [[Frutiger Metro]] aesthetic. The song was dubbed a "crowning jewel" of the jerk revival,<ref name=":4" /> with the release being quickly followed by the single "Prada or Celine".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rap Blog: YT and Lancey Foux count up foreign currency |url=https://www.thefader.com/2024/06/21/rap-blog-yt-and-lancey-foux-count-up-foreign-currency |access-date=25 July 2025 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Kyann-Sian |date=2 April 2025 |title=YT – ‘Oi!’ review: underground rap star makes his biggest bid for mainstream success yet |url=https://www.nme.com/reviews/yt-oi-review-3851183 |access-date=9 April 2026 |website=NME |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Selenou |first=Serge |title=YT: OI! |url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/yt-oi/ |access-date=29 June 2025 |website=Pitchfork |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=100 Best Songs of 2024 |url=https://pitchfork.com/features/lists-and-guides/best-songs-2024/ |website=Pitchfork}}</ref> English singer-songwriter [[PinkPantheress]] was later inspired by the music video's visual direction and collaborated with the video's director, Lauzza, for her future releases.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Monroe |first=Jazz |date=8 May 2026 |title=PinkPantheress Turns London Into a Moving Walkway in “Girl Like Me” Video |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/pinkpantheress-turns-london-into-a-moving-walkway-in-girl-like-me-video/ |access-date=27 May 2026 |website=Pitchfork |language=en-US}}</ref> YT's releases were followed by further major contributions in the genre by artists such as [[Jim Legxacy]], [[EsDeeKid]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 November 2025 |title=EsDeeKid – Rebel |url=https://theneedledrop.com/album-reviews/esdeekid-rebel-album-review/ |access-date=8 December 2025 |website=The Needle Drop |language=en}}</ref> [[Len (rapper)|Len]], and [[Fimiguerrero]].<ref name=":12" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=25 UK Rappers To Watch In 2025 |url=https://www.complex.com/music/a/joseph-jp-patterson/25-uk-rappers-to-watch-in-2025 |access-date=30 June 2025 |website=Complex |language=en}}</ref>

The scene was further popularised by English rapper Fakemink, described as the "man-of-the-moment" by ''[[Dazed]]''.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=2 March 2026 |title=fakemink: ‘I’m the Eminem of the UK underground’ |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/69785/1/fakemink-londons-saviour-terrified-interview-uk-ug-underground-spring-2026-issue |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> Fakemink titled his debut mixtape ''[[London's Saviour]]'' because he wanted to "change" the [[Music of London|London music scene]] which he had previously described as "all trash".<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 November 2024 |title=Fakemink's dropped yet another underground rap banger with Crush |url=https://theface.com/music/fakemink-london-rapper-playlist-best-new-songs-arca-addison-rae |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=The Face |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=D'Souza |first=Shaad |last2=Beaumont-Thomas |first2=Ben |date=22 August 2025 |title=Add to playlist: Fakemink’s sugar-high rap and the week’s best new tracks |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2025/aug/22/fakeminks-sugar-high-rap-and-the-weeks-best-new-tracks |access-date=10 April 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> He pioneered a microgenre dubbed "moody jerk" and has been labelled a "[[critic]]al darling".<ref name=":4" />
In 2025, the scene gained wider attention with the commercial breakthrough of [[EsDeeKid]], whose single "[[Phantom (EsDeeKid and Rico Ace song)|Phantom]]" reached the [[UK Top 20]] and whose debut On the music streaming service [[SoundCloud]], UK underground rap listens rose by "nearly 300%" throughout 2025,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Music Intelligence Report 2026 - UK Underground Rap Family Tree |url=https://soundcloud.com/company/music-intelligence-report-2026---uk-underground-rap-family-tree?ref=epigram.org.uk |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=soundcloud.com |language=en}}</ref> making it the platform's fastest-growing [[Rapping|rap]] movement in both [[United Kingdom|the United Kingdom]] and [[United States|the United States]].<ref name=":21" /> 

Several major publications, including ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' and ''[[The Guardian]]'' described the movement as a "new [[British Invasion]]",<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leight |first=Elias |date=18 February 2026 |title=Britain May Finally Have Its Next Big Pop Star |url=https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/music/british-pop-stars-olivia-dean-lola-young-sienna-spiro-3ca37efc |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> with the latter stating "with [[Hip-hop|US rap]] in the [[wiktionary:doldrums|doldrums]], the time is ripe for another British Invasion".<ref name=":0" /> English rapper YT added "We know that we’re undeniable and that this shift is inevitable."<ref name=":16" />

In January 2026, [[Christians|Christian]] rapper [[YT (rapper)|YT]] was ridiculed by fans online for redacting a lyric regarding pornographic actress [[Bonnie Blue (actress)|Bonnie Blue]] on American streamer [[PlaqueBoyMax]]'s [[Twitch (service)|Twitch]] livestream. YT's decision to redact the line was supported by fellow Christian rappers [[Dave (rapper)|Dave]] and Svn4vr.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=14 January 2026 |title=When did UK underground rap get so Christian? |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/69393/1/when-did-uk-underground-rap-get-so-christian-ug-yt |access-date=17 January 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> The publication ''[[Dazed]]'' argued that the scene had pushed for more inclusion of rappers' [[religious beliefs]] in British youth culture music.<ref name=":3" />

== Fashion and visual arts ==
The UK underground rap scene has been noted for having its own [[visual language]] and "cultural [[ecosystem]]." In 2026, ''Culted'' magazine stated that [[Luxury goods|luxury brands]] were increasingly looking towards British underground artists when "searching for the next face of [[youth culture]]."<ref name=":21" />[[File:UK Underground rap fans leaving a Fakemink pop-up concert (cropped).jpg|thumb|[[Concert|Concertgoers]] at a UK underground rap [[Pop-up exhibition|pop-up]] concert in [[London]], 2026|482x482px]]The movement emphasises [[openness]] and a "[[Punk fashion|punk]] approach" to creativity.<ref name=":23">{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=2023-07-20 |title=In pictures: the new faces of the UK’s underground rap scenes |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/art-photography/article/60401/1/mosy-mcdermott-inside-the-underground-uk-rap-scenes-manchester-london |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> Listeners of the genre typically wear dark, baggy outfits that take inspiration from the [[Cool Britannia]], [[Rage (music genre)|rage]], [[Scene (subculture)|scene]] and [[Grime music|grime]] movements. [[Tartan]] patterns are sometimes implemented, largely due to the popularity of [[Fimiguerrero]], [[Ledbyher]] and [[PinkPantheress|Pinkpantheress]], who all make use of the pattern in their artwork.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-14 |title=PinkPantheress Heard Plaid Was Back & Made It A Beauty Trend |url=https://www.nylon.com/beauty/pinkpantheress-tartan-lips |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=Nylon |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-09 |title=Meet Ledbyher, the UK rap scene’s most engaging new storyteller |url=https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/music/features/ledbyher-rapper-interview-esdeekid-skepta-b2915545.html |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Horvath |first=Zachary |date=2023-03-30 |title=Fimiguerrero & Reekz MB Ooze Swagger On "Tartan" |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/907579-fimiguerrero-tartan-stream |access-date=2026-08-06 |website=HotNewHipHop |language=en}}</ref> Photographer Mosy McDermott noted that "people in this [[subculture]] all have such diverse styles and looks" and that listeners and artists' outfits would often "represent a bit of their personality".<ref name=":23" /><ref name=":12" />

== Local scenes ==
{{expand section|date=August 2026}}

=== London ===
[[File:YT and Len Photographed by Correya (cropped).png|thumb|269x269px|[[YT (rapper)|YT]] (left) and [[Len (rapper)|Len]] (right) are UK UG rappers from London known for [[Jerk (music genre)|jerk]] and [[Afrobeats]] music, respectively.<ref name=":17" />]]
London is the most influential city within the UK underground scene, with many of its most significant contributions originating from [[South London|South]] and [[East London]]. However, the scene is notable for producing successful acts from across the city and from a wide range of [[Ethnicity|ethnic backgrounds]].<ref name=":0" /> Artists associated with the scene include [[Jim Legxacy]] from [[London Borough of Lewisham|Lewisham]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=3 October 2025 |title=‘Cold Lewisham nights’: Behind the scenes at Jim Legxacy’s debut UK tour |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/68817/1/cold-lewisham-nights-behind-the-scenes-at-jim-legxacys-debut-uk-tour |access-date=17 June 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> [[YT (rapper)|YT]] from [[London Borough of Havering|Havering]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=GEN F: YT owns U.K. rap’s new swag |url=https://www.thefader.com/2025/05/12/yt-arcteryx-oi-jim-legxacy-uk-rap-interview |access-date=17 June 2026 |website=The FADER |language=en}}</ref>, [[Fimiguerrero]] from [[Royal Borough of Greenwich|Greenwich]],{{Citation needed|date=June 2026|reason=Confirmed by artist in a YouTube video interview but has no reliable primary sources.}} and [[Ledbyher]] from [[London Borough of Newham|Newham]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2026|reason=Confirmed by artist in a YouTube video interview but has no reliable primary sources.}} 

Local identity is a recurring theme among London's artists, many of whom frequently reference their [[Culture of London|local culture]] and environment. This includes the [[London boroughs]],<ref name=":17" /> public transport systems such as the [[London Underground]] rail lines, the "London Look" by [[Rimmel|Rimmel London]], the city's [[Climate of London|weather]], and everyday life in the capital. Examples include Jim Legxacy's single ''Cold [[Lewisham]] Roses'',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Wonderland |date=7 October 2021 |title=Jim Legxacy Breaks Down A Relationship In "cold Lewisham Roses" |url=https://www.wonderlandmagazine.com/2021/10/07/premiere-jim-legxacy-cold-lewisham-roses/ |access-date=17 June 2026 |website=Wonderland |language=en-GB}}</ref> [[Fakemink]]'s mixtape ''[[London's Saviour]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dazed |date=3 March 2026 |title=fakemink 101: The rise of ‘London’s saviour’ in numbers |url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/69807/1/who-is-fakemink-londons-saviour-uk-ug-spotify-data-numbers |access-date=17 June 2026 |website=Dazed |language=en}}</ref> [[YT (rapper)|YT]]'s single ''Take Me Back To London Where It's Raining'',<ref name=":19" /> among others.

London is also a major hub in the [[counterculture]] movement associated with the UK underground, with major influences on the scene's fashion, [[graphic design]] and politics.<ref name=":20">{{Cite web |last=Hennell |first=Phoebe |date=9 June 2026 |title=Rock Will Be the ‘Next Wave’ After UK Underground Rap |url=https://thecoldmagazine.co.uk/underground-rock-london/ |access-date=17 June 2026 |website=The Cold Magazine |language=it}}</ref> "This is the time to be young in London" is a common sentiment among members of the movement.<ref name=":20" />

=== Leicester ===
[[Leicester]]'s most notable UK underground rapper is Snoa.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Beamount-Thomas |first=Ben |last2=Snapes |first2=Laura |date=5 September 2025 |title=Add to playlist: ultra-prolific Leicester rapper Snoa and the week’s best tracks |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2025/sep/05/add-to-playlist-ultra-prolific-leicester-rapper-snoa-plus-the-weeks-best-tracks |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> He has been labeled by ''[[The Guardian]]'' as "prolific even by the standards of [[underground rap]]", and noted him for releasing a considerable amount of music while keeping it at a "remarkably high level".<ref name=":2" /> He released the album ''2il De4th Du Us 7art'' in 2025 which became "a classic of the [[Cloud rap|cloud-rap]] genre".<ref name=":2" /> His music has been compared to [[Playboi Carti]], [[Che (rapper)|Che]], [[Bladee]] and [[OsamaSon]].<ref name=":2" />
