'''Marvin William Bailey''' (born 6 March 1994), known professionally as '''Fredo''', is a British rapper and singer from Mozart Estate, [[Kilburn, London]]. He rose to fame in 2016 from his track "They Ain't 100". Two years later he achieved his first UK number one single with fellow rapper [[Dave (rapper)|Dave]] titled "[[Funky Friday]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/51266/fredo/|title=Fredo | full Official Chart History | Official Charts Company|website=Officialcharts.com}}</ref> 

Fredo's first album ''[[Third Avenue (album)|Third Avenue]]'' (2019) was released through [[RCA Records]], and peaked at number 5 on the UK Albums Chart, later becoming [[Certified silver|certified Silver]] In 2021. Fredo's second album ''[[Money Can't Buy Happiness]]'' (2021) peaked at number two on the UK Albums Chart and was supported by the single "[[Money Talks (Fredo song)|Money Talks]]" with Dave, which reached number three on the [[UK singles chart|UK Singles Chart]]. The album later became certified Gold in 2025. Fredo followed up with his third album ''Independence Day'' (2021) which peaked at number nine on the UK Albums Chart. He later released the album ''Unfinished Business'' (2023) which also peaked at number nine on the UK Albums Chart, becoming his fourth top-ten album.

== Early life ==
Marvin Bailey grew up in [[Kilburn, London|West Kilburn, London]] to a [[Barbadians|Bajan]] father and [[Moroccans|Moroccan]] mother from [[Letchworth Garden City]] ([[Hertfordshire]]), and lived on West Kilburn's Mozart Estate where he was surrounded by gang violence and crime.<ref name="MEN" /><ref name="Vice" /> During Bailey's youth, he listened to [[Giggs (rapper)|Giggs]] and [[50 Cent]], stating "I remember I used to bang ''[[Get Rich or Die Tryin']]'' every day".<ref>{{Cite web|title=UK Rap Star Fredo Isn't Resting On His he Laurels|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2019/02/fredo-interview|access-date=29 April 2021|website=Complex}}</ref>

== Music career ==

=== 2016–2018: Initial success, ''Get Rich or Get Recalled'' and ''Tables Turn'' ===
Bailey released his first track "They Ain't 100" in March 2016. Three weeks later he went to prison, on a knife crime charge which was later dropped.<ref name="Vice">{{cite web | url = https://www.vice.com/en/article/fredo-third-avenue-album-interview-2019/ | title = Fredo: "I've Spent More Helping My Friends in Prison Than in Harrods" | work = [[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] | last = Thapar | first = Ciaran| date = 1 February 2019 | access-date = 16 December 2019 }}</ref> Whilst he was in prison, the track gained popularity, with radio play and millions of views. Inspired by its success, and despite a second stint in prison, he persisted in his newfound rapping and recording career, releasing two mixtapes, ''Get Rich or Get Recalled'' in 2017, and ''Tables Turn'' in 2018, the latter of which reached number five on the UK Albums Chart.<ref name="FT">{{Cite web |last=Hunter-Tilney |first=Ludovic |date=7 February 2019 |title=London rapper Fredo on the neighbourhood that shaped his music |url=https://www.ft.com/content/5355f564-288a-11e9-88a4-c32129756dd8 |url-access=subscription |access-date=15 February 2019 |website=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Get Rich Or Get Recalled by Fredo |url=https://genius.com/albums/Fredo/Get-rich-or-get-recalled |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=Genius |language=en}}</ref> He also appeared as a featured artist on tracks by [[Kojo Funds]] and [[Young T & Bugsey]], as well as on [[Dave (rapper)|Dave]]'s 2018 hit single "[[Funky Friday]]".

=== 2019–2021: ''Third Avenue'' and ''Money Can't Buy Happiness'' ===
Fredo's first full-length album, ''[[Third Avenue (album)|Third Avenue]]'', was released on 1 February 2019. Produced mostly by JB,<ref name="Vice" /> it marked Bailey's debut on [[RCA Records|RCA]]'s Since '93 imprint. It included "Love You for That", a track dedicated to his mother and apologising for not being the perfect son.<ref name="MEN">{{cite web | url = https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/whats-on/fredo-manchester-interview-o2-ritz-15860793 | title = UK rapper Fredo: "My mum's a really big part of my life" | work = [[Manchester Evening News]] | last = Sue | first = David| date = 2 February 2019 | access-date = 16 December 2019 }}</ref> The album takes its title from the West London housing estate he grew up on. In January 2021, Bailey released his second album, ''Money Can't Buy Happiness'', which contained features from [[Pop Smoke]], [[Dave (rapper)|Dave]], [[Summer Walker]] and [[D-Block Europe|Young Adz]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=29 January 2021|title=Fredo releases new album 'Money Can't Buy Happiness'|url=https://www.sonymusic.co.uk/fredo-releases-new-album-money-cant-buy-happiness/|access-date=29 April 2021|website=Sony Music UK}}</ref> It peaked at number two on the UK Albums Chart.<ref>{{Cite web|title=money can't buy happiness {{!}} full Official Chart History {{!}} Official Charts Company|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/search/albums/money-can%27t-buy-happiness/|access-date=9 August 2021|website=officialcharts.com}}</ref>

=== 2021–2023: ''Independence Day'' and ''Unfinished Business'' ===
On 24 June 2021, Fredo announced his third album, ''Independence Day'', which was released on 5 August 2021 and peaked at number nine on the UK Albums Chart. The album announced that his future music would be released independently.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stream Fredo's 'Independence Day' Album f/ Headie One, Potter Payper, Clavish & More|url=https://www.complex.com/music/fredo-independence-day-album-stream|access-date=9 August 2021|website=Complex}}</ref> On 11 August 2023, Bailey released his fourth album, ''Unfinished Business'', which again peaked at number nine on the UK Albums Chart.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Interviews |first=Clash Magazine Music News, Reviews & |last2=Murray |first2=Robin |date=2023-07-28 |title=Fredo Launches New Album 'Unfinished Business' {{!}} News |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/news/fredo-launches-new-album-unfinished-business/ |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=Clash Magazine Music News, Reviews & Interviews |language=en-GB}}</ref>

=== 2024–present: Single releases and "No Comment" ===
In March 2024, Fredo appeared on [[Clavish]]'s track "Uh Uh". Two months later, following his release from a Dubai prison, he released his first solo track in over a year, the single "Top G", which is a reference to controversial internet personality [[Andrew Tate]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fredo returns with the brand new single, "Top G" |url=https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news/fredo-returns-with-the-brand-new-single-top-g |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=The Line of Best Fit |language=en-US}}</ref> Following another year-long hiatus, Fredo released the track "No Comment" on 21 August 2025, which served as a response to recent Internet rumors, including claims that he was on the run from British authorities.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DAILY |first=GRM |date=2025-08-26 |title=Fredo Sets The Internet Alight With New Banger "No Comment" |url=https://grmdaily.com/fredo-no-comment/ |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=GRM Daily |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Fredo Strikes Back With "No Comment" Video |url=https://trenchtrenchtrench.com/news/fredo-no-comment |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=trenchtrenchtrench.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Business career ==

It was reported on 26 April 2021 on Kick Game's website, a retailer of footwear, that Bailey invested millions of pounds to become a shareholder of the Kick Game company. In 2021, Kick Game’s revenue over the last 12 months had grown from £2 million to £15 million. Kick Game has a YouTube channel with over 1,000,000 subscribers, which features celebrities purchasing footwear from Kick Game and discussing their preferred styles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kick Game Announces Fredo Partnership |url=https://www.kickgame.com/blogs/sneaker-news/kick-game-fredo-partnership |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=Kick Game |language=en}}</ref>

On 9 August 2022, Bailey founded the international clothing brand Parental Guidance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Khaki Combat Gilet |url=https://www.parentalguidance.store/products/cargo-gilet-khaki |access-date=2024-06-28 |website=PG London |language=en}}</ref>

==Legal issues==

=== 2016–2017: Stabbing charges ===
Bailey spent time in prison on remand in 2016 and 2017, both times for stabbing-related charges that were dropped before reaching court. He has also been the victim of a stabbing attack, having been stabbed four times on one occasion on his local high street.<ref>{{Cite news|title=London rapper Fredo on the neighbourhood that shaped his music|url=https://www.ft.com/content/5355f564-288a-11e9-88a4-c32129756dd8|access-date=29 April 2021|newspaper=Financial Times|date=7 February 2019|last1=Hunter-Tilney|first1=Ludovic}}</ref>

=== 2021–2023: Banned temporarily from Mozart Estate ===
In July 2021, the Westminster housing [[Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003|ASB]] team gained two direct injunctions with power of arrest granted against Bailey and fellow rapper Jayvon Tison, also known as Lil Dotz. They were both banned from entering or attempting to enter or remain on the Mozart Estate and the Lydford Estate. Bailey was arrested in July 2023, and the Westminster housing ASB team were successful in enforcing the breach of his injunction. Bailey was ordered to pay a fine of £5k plus court costs. The order was then extended in July 2023 until July 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Appendix H Housing ASB case studies |url=https://westminster.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s54344/Appendix%20H%20Housing%20ASB%20case%20studies.pdf |access-date=2024-08-26}}</ref>

Fredo (rapper).text:
Marvin William Bailey (born 6 March 1994), known professionally as Fredo, is a British rapper and singer from Mozart Estate, Kilburn, London. He rose to fame in 2016 from his track "They Ain't 100". Two years later he achieved his first UK number one single with fellow rapper Dave titled "Funky Friday". 
Fredo's first album Third Avenue (2019) was released through RCA Records, and peaked at number 5 on the UK Albums Chart, later becoming certified Silver In 2021. Fredo's second album Money Can't Buy Happiness (2021) peaked at number two on the UK Albums Chart and was supported by the single "Money Talks" with Dave, which reached number three on the UK Singles Chart. The album later became certified Gold in 2025. Fredo followed up with his third album Independence Day (2021) which peaked at number nine on the UK Albums Chart. He later released the album Unfinished Business (2023) which also peaked at number nine on the UK Albums Chart, becoming his fourth top-ten album.


== Early life ==
Marvin Bailey grew up in West Kilburn, London to a Bajan father and Moroccan mother from Letchworth Garden City (Hertfordshire), and lived on West Kilburn's Mozart Estate where he was surrounded by gang violence and crime. During Bailey's youth, he listened to Giggs and 50 Cent, stating "I remember I used to bang Get Rich or Die Tryin' every day".


== Music career ==


=== 2016–2018: Initial success, Get Rich or Get Recalled and Tables Turn ===
Bailey released his first track "They Ain't 100" in March 2016. Three weeks later he went to prison, on a knife crime charge which was later dropped. Whilst he was in prison, the track gained popularity, with radio play and millions of views. Inspired by its success, and despite a second stint in prison, he persisted in his newfound rapping and recording career, releasing two mixtapes, Get Rich or Get Recalled in 2017, and Tables Turn in 2018, the latter of which reached number five on the UK Albums Chart. He also appeared as a featured artist on tracks by Kojo Funds and Young T & Bugsey, as well as on Dave's 2018 hit single "Funky Friday".


=== 2019–2021: Third Avenue and Money Can't Buy Happiness ===
Fredo's first full-length album, Third Avenue, was released on 1 February 2019. Produced mostly by JB, it marked Bailey's debut on RCA's Since '93 imprint. It included "Love You for That", a track dedicated to his mother and apologising for not being the perfect son. The album takes its title from the West London housing estate he grew up on. In January 2021, Bailey released his second album, Money Can't Buy Happiness, which contained features from Pop Smoke, Dave, Summer Walker and Young Adz. It peaked at number two on the UK Albums Chart.


=== 2021–2023: Independence Day and Unfinished Business ===
On 24 June 2021, Fredo announced his third album, Independence Day, which was released on 5 August 2021 and peaked at number nine on the UK Albums Chart. The album announced that his future music would be released independently. On 11 August 2023, Bailey released his fourth album, Unfinished Business, which again peaked at number nine on the UK Albums Chart.


=== 2024–present: Single releases and "No Comment" ===
In March 2024, Fredo appeared on Clavish's track "Uh Uh". Two months later, following his release from a Dubai prison, he released his first solo track in over a year, the single "Top G", which is a reference to controversial internet personality Andrew Tate. Following another year-long hiatus, Fredo released the track "No Comment" on 21 August 2025, which served as a response to recent Internet rumors, including claims that he was on the run from British authorities.


== Business career ==
It was reported on 26 April 2021 on Kick Game's website, a retailer of footwear, that Bailey invested millions of pounds to become a shareholder of the Kick Game company. In 2021, Kick Game’s revenue over the last 12 months had grown from £2 million to £15 million. Kick Game has a YouTube channel with over 1,000,000 subscribers, which features celebrities purchasing footwear from Kick Game and discussing their preferred styles.
On 9 August 2022, Bailey founded the international clothing brand Parental Guidance.


== Legal issues ==


=== 2016–2017: Stabbing charges ===
Bailey spent time in prison on remand in 2016 and 2017, both times for stabbing-related charges that were dropped before reaching court. He has also been the victim of a stabbing attack, having been stabbed four times on one occasion on his local high street.


=== 2021–2023: Banned temporarily from Mozart Estate ===
In July 2021, the Westminster housing ASB team gained two direct injunctions with power of arrest granted against Bailey and fellow rapper Jayvon Tison, also known as Lil Dotz. They were both banned from entering or attempting to enter or remain on the Mozart Estate and the Lydford Estate. Bailey was arrested in July 2023, and the Westminster housing ASB team were successful in enforcing the breach of his injunction. Bailey was ordered to pay a fine of £5k plus court costs. The order was then extended in July 2023 until July 2025.


=== 2024: Dubai arrest ===
It was heavily rumoured on the internet via many Media Outlets that on 29 January 2024, that Bailey was sentenced to five years in prison in Dubai for cannabis possession after being arrested in late 2023. However, Bailey was released from the Dubai prison after three months and made a video clarifying about his time in prison.

Fredo Santana.text:
Derrick Antonio Coleman (July 4, 1990 – January 19, 2018), known professionally as Fredo Santana, was an American rapper. The older cousin of rapper Chief Keef, Santana began his career in 2011. His debut studio album, Trappin Ain't Dead (2013), peaked at number 45 on the US Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart. Santana died of a seizure on January 19, 2018.


== Career ==

Fredo's first mixtape, It's a Scary Site, was released on September 20, 2012. It featured production by TM88, Young Chop, 12Hunna, Leek E Leek, J-Hill, C-Sick, and Paris Bueller as well as guest appearances from Chief Keef, Lil Reese, King L, Gino Marley, Frenchie, Lil Herb, Lil Bibby, and Lil Durk. Santana's second mixtape, Fredo Kruger, was released on February 28, 2013, and featured production by 808 Mafia, Young Chop and Mike Will Made It, as well as guest appearances from Migos, Juelz Santana, Soulja Boy, Young Scooter, Fat Trel, Alley Boy, Lil Durk and Lil Reese among others. It would later be released for retail sale via iTunes on May 7, 2013.
On September 24, 2013, Fredo Santana made a cameo appearance in Drake's music video for "Hold On, We're Going Home", in which he portrayed a bad guy kidnapping Drake's "girlfriend".
His debut album, Trappin Ain't Dead, was released on November 20, 2013. The album featured guest appearances by Kendrick Lamar, Chief Keef, Peewee Longway and other members of Glory Boyz Entertainment. It's a Scary Site 2 was released on December 20, 2013.
On February 27, 2014, Santana announced that he and Keef were going to release a collaboration album Blood Thicker Than Water, which never came to fruition. On July 9, 2014, he revealed the track list for his upcoming album Walking Legend.


== Personal life ==
Santana was the older cousin of Chicago rapper Chief Keef.


=== Health problems ===
Santana was a heavy user of drugs, at one point being addicted to Xanax and Lean. Santana attributed his heavy drug use to trauma experienced during his childhood, admitting he had post-traumatic stress disorder and turned to drugs as a coping mechanism.
Santana was hospitalized in March 2017 after having a seizure, which he blamed on a heavy workload and his poor sleep schedule. After the seizures persisted, Santana was diagnosed with idiopathic epilepsy in May 2017 and was prescribed Keppra to treat it. Despite the medicine, Santana continued to have seizures, usually multiple in a row.
Santana was hospitalized once again in October 2017 after friend and fellow rapper Gino Marley found Santana mid-seizure on the floor of his house with blood coming from his mouth. He was rushed to hospital and diagnosed with both liver and kidney failure, with the main factors being his addiction to Xanax and Lean. Santana expressed interest in going to rehab while in the hospital.


== Death ==
On the evening of January 19, 2018, at around 11:30 p.m. local time, Santana's girlfriend discovered him unresponsive at their home in Reseda, Los Angeles. Shortly after, Santana was pronounced dead, aged 27. He had a fatal seizure, and an autopsy revealed he had developed cardiovascular disease in addition to the previous conditions he had.

'''Frederick Thomas''' (February 22, 1985 – April 23, 2020),<ref name="Times Obit">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/04/24/arts/music/fred-the-godson-dead-coronavirus.html|work=New York Times|title=Fred the Godson, Nimble New York Rapper, Dies at 41|first=Jon |last=Caramanica|date=April 24, 2020|accessdate=April 24, 2020}}</ref> known as '''Fred the Godson''', was an American DJ and rapper.<ref name="Billboard Obit">{{cite magazine |url= https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/obituary/9364643/fred-the-godson-dies-35-coronavirus-obituary|first=Gil|last=Kaufman|magazine=Billboard|title=Fred the Godson Dies at 35 From Coronavirus|date=April 23, 2020|accessdate=April 24, 2020}}</ref><ref name="NPR Obit">{{cite news |url= https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/04/24/843381098/fred-the-godson-new-york-hip-hop-fixture-dead-at-35-from-covid-19-complications |work= National Public Radio|title=Fred The Godson, New York Hip-Hop Fixture, Dead At 35 From COVID-19 Complication|first=Jon |last=Lewis|date=April 24, 2020 |accessdate=April 24, 2020}}</ref> He was the first high-profile [[hip hop music|hip hop]] personality to have died from [[COVID-19]] in April 2020; it was the early stages of the pandemic.<ref> https://abc7ny.com/covid-vaccine-fred-the-godson-frederick-thomas-street-renaming/10362768/ </ref>

==Early life==
Frederick Thomas was born on February 22, 1985, and grew up in [[the Bronx]], New York City. He gained an early nickname of "Big Bronx".<ref name="Times Obit" />

He started freestyling in the early 2000s.<ref name="Times Obit" />

==Career==
Thomas's music was characterized by his husky voice, humorous [[wordplay]], and creative rhymes.<ref name="Times Obit" /> In the early-2010s, he released two mixtapes; his debut was ''Armageddon'' in 2010, featuring samples of [[The Notorious B.I.G.]], [[Busta Rhymes]] and [[Cam'ron]].<ref name="NPR Obit" /> His second release, ''City of God'', was one of a series for DJ Drama's Gangsta Grillz,<ref name="Times Obit" /> and featuring [[Pusha T]] and [[Raekwon]].<ref name="Billboard Obit" />

In 2011, ''[[XXL (magazine)|XXL]]'' included him in its annual Freshman class of up-and-comers.<ref name="Billboard Obit" />

Between 2011 and 2020, Thomas released music and performed regularly, guest DJ-ing on New York radio station based in Hudson [[Hot 97]],<ref name="NPR Obit" /> and collaborated with artists including Pusha T, [[Jadakiss]], Cam'ron, and Raekwon, as well as releasing the [[answer song]], "Monique's Room".<ref name="Times Obit" /> He released two additional mixtapes in 2020, ''Training Day'' in January with [[Jay Pharoah]], and ''Payback'', released on March 20, 2020, which would be his last release before his death from COVID-19 one month later.<ref name="NPR Obit" />

==Personal life==
Thomas was married to LeeAnn Jemmott; they had two daughters.<ref name="Times Obit" /><ref name="Bronx12">{{cite news|url=http://bronx.news12.com/story/41988922/rapper-fred-the-godson-diagnosed-with-covid19-fighting-for-his-life|title=Rapper Fred The Godson diagnosed with COVID-19, fighting for his life|date=April 8, 2020|work=Bronx News 12|accessdate=April 24, 2020}}</ref>

Thomas was reported to be suffering from acute asthma and kidney problems, after contracting [[COVID-19]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)| early days of the pandemic]], and by April 6, 2020, his fever had abated in hospital, according to his publicist and his [[Instagram]] account.<ref name="Billboard Obit" /><ref name="Source">{{cite news|last=White|first=Roman|url=https://thesource.com/2020/04/22/source-fred-the-godsons-kidneys-not-working-but-fever-improvement-is-big/|title=Source: Fred The Godson's Kidneys 'Not Working' But Fever Improvement is 'Big'|date=April 22, 2020|work=Source (magazine)|accessdate=April 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/B-puaempK0f/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/instagram/fredthegodsonmusic/2281558815946353951 |archive-date=December 25, 2021 |url-access=registration|title=Fred the Godson's Instagram|author=Fred the Godson|date=April 6, 2020|work=Instagram|accessdate=April 24, 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref> His wife told media on April 9 that she was concerned he was going to die,<ref name="Bronx12" /> but the next day, said he was "going to make it", and was being weaned from a [[ventilator]].<ref name="Source" /><ref name="XXL Update">{{cite news|last=Woods|first=Aleia|url=https://www.xxlmag.com/news/2020/04/fred-the-godson-wife-coronavirus-diagnosis-update/|title=Fred the Godson's Wife Says He's Fighting for His Life After Coronavirus Diagnosis|date=April 9, 2020|work=XXL (magazine)|accessdate=April 24, 2020}}</ref>

Thomas died at [[Montefiore Medical Center]] in the Bronx, New York City, on April 23, 2020, due to complications of COVID-19.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fred The Godson, New York Hip-Hop Fixture, Dead At 35 From COVID-19 Complications|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/04/24/843381098/fred-the-godson-new-york-hip-hop-fixture-dead-at-35-from-covid-19-complications|access-date=2021-02-06|website=NPR.org|date=April 24, 2020 |language=en|last1=Lewis |first1=Jon }}</ref> He was 35.<ref name="Times Obit" /><ref name="Billboard Obit" /><ref name="NPR Obit" />

=== Legacy ===
On February 22, 2021, what would have been his 36th birthday, [[Bronx Borough President]] [[Rubén Díaz Jr.]] honored Fred by giving him his own street co-name on the block of his childhood home that he grew up in.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Thomas|first=Datwon|date=2021-02-22|title=Fat Joe, Jim Jones and Bronx Community Celebrate Fred The Godson's Street Naming On His Birthday|url=https://www.vibe.com/news/entertainment/fat-joe-jim-jones-celebrate-fred-the-godson-687174/|access-date=2021-02-22|website=VIBE.com|language=en-US}}</ref> Special appearances were made by [[Sway Calloway]], [[Fat Joe]], [[Jim Jones (rapper)|Jim Jones]], [[Jaquae]], Mysonne and [[Justina Valentine]].

Fred the Godson.text:
Frederick Thomas (February 22, 1985 – April 23, 2020), known as Fred the Godson, was an American DJ and rapper. He was the first high-profile hip hop personality to have died from COVID-19 in April 2020; it was the early stages of the pandemic.


== Early life ==
Frederick Thomas was born on February 22, 1985, and grew up in the Bronx, New York City. He gained an early nickname of "Big Bronx".
He started freestyling in the early 2000s.


== Career ==
Thomas's music was characterized by his husky voice, humorous wordplay, and creative rhymes. In the early-2010s, he released two mixtapes; his debut was Armageddon in 2010, featuring samples of The Notorious B.I.G., Busta Rhymes and Cam'ron. His second release, City of God, was one of a series for DJ Drama's Gangsta Grillz, and featuring Pusha T and Raekwon.
In 2011, XXL included him in its annual Freshman class of up-and-comers.
Between 2011 and 2020, Thomas released music and performed regularly, guest DJ-ing on New York radio station based in Hudson Hot 97, and collaborated with artists including Pusha T, Jadakiss, Cam'ron, and Raekwon, as well as releasing the answer song, "Monique's Room". He released two additional mixtapes in 2020, Training Day in January with Jay Pharoah, and Payback, released on March 20, 2020, which would be his last release before his death from COVID-19 one month later.


== Personal life ==
Thomas was married to LeeAnn Jemmott; they had two daughters.
Thomas was reported to be suffering from acute asthma and kidney problems, after contracting COVID-19 during the  early days of the pandemic, and by April 6, 2020, his fever had abated in hospital, according to his publicist and his Instagram account. His wife told media on April 9 that she was concerned he was going to die, but the next day, said he was "going to make it", and was being weaned from a ventilator.
Thomas died at Montefiore Medical Center in the Bronx, New York City, on April 23, 2020, due to complications of COVID-19. He was 35.


=== Legacy ===
On February 22, 2021, what would have been his 36th birthday, Bronx Borough President Rubén Díaz Jr. honored Fred by giving him his own street co-name on the block of his childhood home that he grew up in. Special appearances were made by Sway Calloway, Fat Joe, Jim Jones, Jaquae, Mysonne and Justina Valentine.

'''Karim Kharbouch''' ([[Moroccan Arabic|Arabic]]: {{lang|ar|كريم خربوش}} [[IPA pronunciation|[kæɾiːm χɑɾbuːʃ]]]; born 9 November 1984), known professionally as '''French Montana''', is a Moroccan and American rapper.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://thevogue.com/artists/french-montana/#bio|title=French Montana |website=Thevogue.com|access-date=November 9, 2024}}</ref> Born and raised in [[Morocco]], he immigrated to [[New York City]] with his family at the age of 13 and began his career as a [[Battle rap|battle rapper]] in the early 2000s — under the name '''Young French'''.<ref name="fader" /><ref name="SDinterview" /><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.musicconnection.com/qa-with-french-montana/ | title=#Post Title #Separator #Site Title | date=April 27, 2024 }}</ref> He first gained recognition hosting the locally-tailored [[DVD]] series ''Cocaine City'' during the 2000s, which centered around interviews of hip hop figures. He pursued a recording career while doing so, releasing several [[underground hip hop|underground]] projects before signing with [[Sean Combs]]'s [[Bad Boy Records]] and [[Rick Ross]]'s [[Maybach Music Group]], in a triple-joint venture with [[Interscope Records]] in 2012. 

Kharbouch's debut studio album, ''[[Excuse My French (album)|Excuse My French]]'' (2013), peaked at number four on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] despite critical failure; its lead single, "[[Pop That]]" (featuring Rick Ross, [[Drake (musician)|Drake]], and [[Lil Wayne]]), peaked within the top 40 of the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hotnewhiphop.com/french-montana-s-excuse-my-french-pushed-back-again-news.4388.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130209203632/http://www.hotnewhiphop.com/french-montana-s-excuse-my-french-pushed-back-again-news.4388.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 9, 2013 |title=French Montana's "Excuse My French" Pushed Back Again |date=February 8, 2013 |work=[[HotNewHipHop]] |access-date=March 8, 2013}}</ref> His 2017 single, "[[Unforgettable (French Montana song)|Unforgettable]]" (featuring [[Swae Lee]]), peaked within the chart's top 10, and received [[RIAA certification#List of certifications|diamond]] certification by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA). It preceded his second studio album ''[[Jungle Rules]]'' (2017), which was met with similar commercial success—peaking at number three on the ''Billboard'' 200—and a critical incline. His third and fourth albums, ''[[Montana (French Montana album)|Montana]]'' (2019) and ''[[They Got Amnesia]]'' (2021), were both met with lukewarm critical and commercial reception; the latter served as his final release on a [[major label]].<ref name=":0" />

Kharbouch founded the record label Coke Boys Records (previously known as Cocaine City Records) in 2008, which has signed Chicago rapper [[Lil Durk]], as well as fellow New York artists including [[Velous]], [[Chinx]], and record producer [[Harry Fraud]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/21970-french-montana-signs-velous-to-coke-boys-news | title=French Montana Signs Velous to
