Key Glock.text:
Markeyvius LaShun Cathey (born August 3, 1997), known professionally as Key Glock, is an American rapper, songwriter, and record producer. The cousin of late  Memphis rapper Young Dolph, Cathey signed with his record label, Paper Route Empire, to release his commercial mixtape, Glock Season (2017). His debut studio album, Yellow Tape (2020), peaked at number 14 on the Billboard 200 and received gold certification by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). His second album, Yellow Tape 2 (2021), peaked at number seven on the chart and spawned the multi-platinum-certified single "Ambition for Cash", as well as "Proud", which was released in the wake of Dolph's death and marked his first entry on the Billboard Hot 100. His third album, Glockoma 2 (2023), spawned the sleeper hit single "Let's Go"—his second entry on the chart.


== Early life ==
Markeyvius LaShun Cathey was born in South Memphis on August 3, 1997. When he was 20 months old, his mother Tameika Cathey was sent to prison, where she would be for the next 15 years. His father was in and out of his life, so he was raised by his grandmother and his aunt. According to Cathey, he and his grandmother occasionally visited his mother in prison during his youth. At 18 years old, he was charged with three counts of aggravated assault related to his involvement in a shooting. Music was a distraction from his oftentimes tumultuous life.
Cathey said he grew up listening to Gucci Mane, Lil Wayne, and cites Three 6 Mafia as his largest influence. He was also a big fan of Project Pat, whom he describes as the "Drake of Memphis". According to Glock, Pat's songs "If You Ain't From My Hood" and "Gorilla Pimp" changed his life. The latter's chorus inspired one of his breakout songs, "Dig That". The first track that Glock recorded himself was a freestyle of DJ Drama's 2011 song "Ain't No Way Around It".


== Career ==
Glock released his debut mixtape Whole Lotta Errthang in 2016. In 2017, Young Dolph signed Key Glock to the Paper Route Empire label. On January 25 of that year, Glock released his debut single "Racks Today" featuring American rapper Jay Fizzle. On June 16, 2017, Glock released his second mixtape, Glock Season, under the label. His collaborative album Dum and Dummer with Young Dolph reached number eight on the Billboard 200. Young Dolph's "Major" featuring Key Glock reached number 47 on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart.
Following the release of his collaborative album Dum and Dummer with Young Dolph, he went on a European tour across Manchester and London. The pair brought out UK rapper Blade Brown as a supporting act. The two proceeded to start the "No Rules" Tour in 2020, beginning on February 5 in Seattle.
On January 31, Key Glock released his debut studio album titled Yellow Tape, which debuted at number 14 on the Billboard 200. On May 22, 2020, Key Glock released his sixth mixtape, Son of a Gun, again with no features.
On March 5, 2021, Key Glock and Young Dolph released the single, "Aspen", and announced the release of their second collaborative album, Dum and Dummer 2, due for release on March 26, 2021. It is a sequel to 2019's Dum and Dummer. The project's cartoon artwork references Beavis & Butthead. On November 5, 2021, Glock released his second studio album Yellow Tape 2, a sequel to Yellow Tape.
On January 18, 2022, Key Glock released the song "Proud", a tribute to Young Dolph. It is included on the Dolph tribute compilation Long Live Young Dolph, released January 21, 2022.
On February 24, 2023, Key Glock released his third studio album, Glockoma 2. It is the sequel to his 2018 mixtape Glockoma.
On March 13, 2025, Key Glock signed to Republic Records.
On May 2, 2025, after facing several delays, Key Glock released his fourth studio album and major-label debut album, Glockaveli.


== Personal life ==
Key Glock is the cousin by marriage of Young Dolph, who was murdered in November 2021. Following Dolph's death, in a since-deleted Instagram post, Key Glock called him "my lefthand man, my brother, my cousin, and my mentor."  The same month Young Dolph died he got a tattoo of Young Dolph.

'''Michael Santiago Render''' (born April 20, 1975), known professionally as '''Killer Mike''', is an American rapper, singer, actor, and activist. He made his recording debut on [[Outkast]]'s fourth album ''[[Stankonia]]'' (2000), and guest appeared on the duo's [[Grammy Award]]-winning single "[[The Whole World]]" from their greatest hits album ''[[Big Boi and Dre Present... Outkast]]'' (2001). He signed with [[Big Boi]]'s [[Purple Ribbon Records]] (known then as Aquemini Records) and [[Columbia Records]] to release his debut studio album ''[[Monster (Killer Mike album)|Monster]]'' (2003), which was met with critical acclaim and peaked at number ten on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. He parted ways with the label and released two albums—''[[I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind]]'' (2006) and ''[[I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind II]]'' (2008)—before signing with [[T.I.]]'s [[Grand Hustle Records|Grand Hustle]] to release his fourth album, ''[[Pledge (album)|Pledge]]'' (2011), and later [[Williams Street Records|Williams Street]] to release his fifth album, ''[[R.A.P. Music]]'' (2012). His sixth album, ''[[Michael (Killer Mike album)|Michael]]'' (2023), was met with continued acclaim and won three awards at [[66th Annual Grammy Awards]], including [[Grammy Award for Best Rap Album|Best Rap Album]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.revolt.tv/article/2023-12-06/344921/killer-mike-speaks-on-possibility-of-winning-a-grammy/|title=Killer Mike Speakd on the Possibility of Winning a Grammy|website=Revolt.com}}</ref>

Following ''R.A.P. Music'', which was produced entirely by rapper and producer [[El-P]], he and Render subsequently formed the duo [[Run the Jewels]] in 2013. They signed with [[Fool's Gold Records]] and released their [[Run the Jewels (album)|self-titled debut]] in June of that year to critical acclaim. Its three sequels—''[[Run the Jewels 2]]'' (2014), ''[[Run the Jewels 3]]'' (2016) and ''[[RTJ4]]'' (2020)—were each met with continued critical praise, the latter of which matched his debut solo album in chart position on the ''Billboard'' 200. The duo made a guest appearance alongside Big Boi on [[Danger Mouse (musician)|Danger Mouse]]'s 2017 single "[[Baby Driver – Music from the Motion Picture|Chase Me]]", which received a Grammy Award nomination.

Outside of music, Render has been a social and political activist, focusing on subjects including [[social inequality]], [[police brutality]], and [[systemic racism]]. In addition to discussing related topics in his music, he has lectured about similar issues at colleges and universities, written about such matters for publications including ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'', and been the subject of interviews regarding police misconduct and race relations. He was a visible and vocal supporter of [[Bernie Sanders presidential campaign, 2016|Bernie Sanders' 2016 U.S. presidential campaign]], and supported Sanders once more in [[Bernie Sanders presidential campaign, 2020|his 2020 presidential campaign]]. Render has appeared in films such as ''[[Idlewild (film)|Idlewild]]'', ''[[Baby Driver]]'', ''[[ATL (film)|ATL]]'', and ''[[America: The Motion Picture]]''. His six episode docu-series, ''[[Trigger Warning with Killer Mike]]'', investigated social issues that affect [[African American middle class|Black Americans]], and premiered on [[Netflix]] in January 2019. His weekly interview program for the [[Public Broadcasting Service]] (PBS), ''Love & Respect'' (2021–present), won an [[Emmy Award]] in 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://hiphopdx.com/news/killer-mike-emmy-love-respect | title=Killer Mike 'Humbled & Honored' to Win First Emmy for 'Love & Respect' | date=June 18, 2023 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Michael Render was born in the [[Adamsville, Atlanta|Adamsville]] neighborhood of [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]], on April 20, 1975,<ref name="Allmusic">{{cite web |url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/killer-mike-mn0000771261 |title=Killer Mike Biography |website=AllMusic |author=Bush, John |access-date=April 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130125080842/http://www.allmusic.com/artist/killer-mike-mn0000771261 |archive-date=January 25, 2013 |url-status=live }}</ref> the son of a policeman father and a florist mother.<ref name="GuardianInterview">{{cite news |date=2022-07-04 |first=Ammar |last=Kalia |title='I will never be against the second amendment': Run the Jewels' Killer Mike on rap, racism and gun control |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2022/jul/04/i-smoke-weed-and-i-go-to-strip-clubs-but-i-care-about-people-killer-mike-on-rapping-politics-and-race |newspaper=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref name="biography1">{{cite web|url=https://www.biography.com/people/killer-mike-5102017|title=Killer Mike|website=Biography|access-date=January 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171129234215/https://www.biography.com/people/killer-mike-5102017|archive-date=November 29, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Because his parents were teenagers at the time of his birth, he was partly raised by his grandparents in the [[Collier Heights]] neighborhood of Atlanta, and attended [[Douglass High School (Atlanta)|Douglass High School]].<ref name="biography1" />

==Career==
===1995–2005: Early career===
In 1995, Render briefly attended Atlanta's [[Morehouse College]], where he met producers [[The Beat Bullies]], and soon met rapper [[Big Boi]] of [[Outkast]].<ref name=Grammy>{{cite web |url=https://www.grammy.com/grammys/awards/winners-nominees/208 |title=Best Rap Performance By A Duo Or Group |website=Grammy.com |access-date=February 7, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322203515/https://www.grammy.com/grammys/awards/winners-nominees/208 |archive-date=March 22, 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="GuardianInterview" /> His music debut was a feature appearance on Outkast's "Snappin' & Trappin'" from the 2000 album ''[[Stankonia]]'', followed by their 2001 single "[[The Whole World]]", which won the 2002 [[Grammy Award]] for [[Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group]].<ref name=Grammy /> He was featured on several other tracks that year, including the [[Jay-Z]]'s song "Poppin' Tags" from his album ''[[The Blueprint 2]]'', where he guest performed alongside both Big Boi and Chicago rapper [[Twista]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hiphopdx.com/news/killer-mike-jay-z-poppin-tags-verse|title=Killer Mike Claims JAY-Z's 'Poppin' Tags' Was Changed Because He Was 'Rapping His Ass Off'|date=August 15, 2023 }}</ref>

In 2003, Render released his debut studio album, ''[[Monster (Killer Mike album)|Monster]]'', while being managed by Dayo Adebiyi and Al Thrash of Own Music. The album's lead single, "Akshon (Yeah!)", featured both Outkast members as guest performers. A remix of the song was included on the soundtrack of [[EA Sports]] video game ''[[Madden NFL 2004]]''.<ref name=Madden04>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1473241/blink-182-outkast-bone-crusher-joe-budden-score-tracks-on-madden-2004/|title=Blink-182, Outkast, Bone Crusher, Joe Budden Score Tracks On 'Madden 2004'|website=MTV.com|date=June 24, 2003|author=D'Angelo, Joe|access-date=April 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150410104020/http://www.mtv.com/news/1473241/blink-182-outkast-bone-crusher-joe-budden-score-tracks-on-madden-2004/|archive-date=April 10, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> The album's second single was "[[A.D.I.D.A.S. (Killer Mike song)|A.D.I.D.A.S]]"., featuring [[Big Boi]] and [[Sleepy Brown]], which peaked at number 60 on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. It remains Render's only single to enter the chart as a lead artist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/305859/killer-mike/chart?f=379&sort=position|title=Killer Mike - Chart history|newspaper=Billboard|access-date=April 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160503075924/http://www.billboard.com/artist/305859/killer-mike/chart?f=379&sort=position|archive-date=May 3, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the release of his own material, he appeared on "Flip Flop Rock" and "Bust" on the ''Speakerboxx'' half of OutKast's ''[[Speakerboxxx/The Love Below]]'' double album. He appeared on "Southern Takeover" with [[Pastor Troy]] on [[Chamillionaire]]'s album ''[[The Sound of Revenge]]''. Render appeared alongside [[T.I.]] on the song "[[Never Scared (song)|Never Scared]]" by [[Bone Crusher (rapper)|Bone Crusher]] on his album ''[[AttenCHUN!]]''. It peaked at #26 on the Hot 100, becoming Mike's second top 40 hit ("The Whole World" being the first). The song was used on the ''Madden NFL 2004'' game soundtrack<ref name=Madden04/> and by the [[Atlanta Braves]] for their [[2003 Atlanta Braves season|2003 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2013/01/the-30-best-so-so-def-songs/bone-crusher-killer-mike-ti-never-scared|title=Bone Crusher f/ Killer Mike & T.I. "Never Scared" (2003) - The 30 Best So So Def Songs|website=Complex|date=January 29, 2013|author=Drake, David|access-date=April 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826173227/http://www.complex.com/music/2013/01/the-30-best-so-so-def-songs/bone-crusher-killer-mike-ti-never-scared|archive-date=August 26, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2006–2012: ''Pledge'' series and ''R.A.P. Music''===
{{main|I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind|I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind II|Pledge (album)|R.A.P. Music}}

Render was introduced to rapper-producer [[El-P]] by [[Cartoon Network]] executive Jason DeMarco in 2011.<ref name=RollingStone_RTJ>{{cite web |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/run-the-jewels-how-2014s-hardest-rap-duo-came-back-from-oblivion-20141024 |title=Run the Jewels: 2014's Brashest Rap Duo Comes Back From Oblivion |newspaper=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=October 24, 2014 |author=Weingarten, Christopher R. |access-date=May 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141025163522/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/features/run-the-jewels-how-2014s-hardest-rap-duo-came-back-from-oblivion-20141024 |archive-date=October 25, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> The following year, El-P produced Mike's album ''[[R.A.P. Music]]'' and guested on the song "Butane (Champion's Anthem)". That same year, Render guested on El-P's album ''[[Cancer 4 Cure]]''. When ''R.A.P. Music'' and ''Cancer 4 Cure'' were released within weeks of each other, the two rappers decided to tour together. The success of the tour eventually led to the decision to record as a duo, which they named [[Run the Jewels]].<ref name=RTJ_NPR>{{cite news |url=https://www.npr.org/blogs/microphonecheck/2014/11/11/363125142/run-the-jewels-im-taking-this-life |title=Run The Jewels: 'I'm Taking This Life' |newspaper=NPR |date=November 11, 2014 |author=Kelley, Frannie |access-date=May 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150425223749/http://www.npr.org/blogs/microphonecheck/2014/11/11/363125142/run-the-jewels-im-taking-this-life |archive-date=April 25, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Killer Mike WHTA interview 2024.png|thumb|Killer Mike in an interview with [[WHTA]] in 2024]]

Run the Jewels released a free [[Run the Jewels (album)|eponymous album]] on June 26, 2013.<ref name=RTJ_releasedate/> The next year, on October 28, 2014, Run the Jewels released their second free album, ''[[Run the Jewels 2]]''.<ref name=RTJ2_release/> On September 25, 2015, the duo released a re-recorded version of ''Run the Jewels 2'' made entirely with [[cat communication|cat sounds]], titled ''[[Meow the Jewels]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.spin.com/2015/09/meow-the-jewels-run-the-jewels-killer-mike-el-p-review-cat-sound-remix/ |title=Five Thoughts About 'Meow the Jewels,' Because How the Hell Would You Actually Review This? |website=Spin.com |author=Grebey, James |date=September 29, 2015 |access-date=October 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005181832/http://www.spin.com/2015/09/meow-the-jewels-run-the-jewels-killer-mike-el-p-review-cat-sound-remix/ |archive-date=October 5, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> A third album, ''[[Run the Jewels 3]]'', was released on December 24, 2016.<ref name=BB_RTJ3>{{cite web |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/run-the-jewels-new-album-rtj3-early-release-listen-7633335/ |title=Run the Jewels' New Album, 'RTJ3,' Released Early: Listen |website=Billboard.com |date=December 26, 2016 |author=DiMeglio, Mary J. |access-date=December 28, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161228094947/http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/hip-hop/7633335/run-the-jewels-new-album-rtj3-early-release-listen |archive-date=December 28, 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> Their fourth album, ''[[RTJ4]]'', was released on June 3, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Strauss|first=Matthew|title=Run the Jewels Surprise Release New Album RTJ4|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/run-the-jewels-surprise-release-new-album-rtj4-listen/|access-date=June 3, 2020|website=Pitchfork|date=June 3, 2020|language=en}}</ref>

The album released August 2nd.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Paul |first=Larisha |date=2024-07-29 |title=Killer Mike Will Close 'Michael' Album Era With 'Songs for Sinners & Saints' |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/killer-mike-songs-for-sinners-and-saints-1235069721/ |access-date=2024-07-29 |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2025, Killer Mike appeared on the [[De La Soul]] album [[Cabin in the Sky (De La Soul album)|''Cabin in the Sky'']], on the song “A Quick 16 For Mama”.

===Graffitis SWAG barbershop===
Mike and his wife, Shana, opened a barbershop in [[Atlanta, Georgia|Atlanta]] on November 1, 2011. The two acquired and reworked a barbershop and named it Graffitis SWAG (shave, wash, and groom). He had waited nine years before choosing to open the barbershop, after having an early business manager advise him against the plan. It took his wife advising him to do it now while he had the time and money to pursue his lifelong dream. He eventually plans to open 150 shops across the United States over time, predominantly in cities with large Black communities.<ref name=BarberSchools>{{cite web |last=Physioc |first=Heather E. |url=http://www.barber-schools.org/blog/killer-mikes-barber-shop-in-atlanta-ga-graffiti-swag |title=Killer Mike's Barbershop in Atlanta, GA - Graffiti's SWAG |website=Barber-Schools.org |date=July 2, 2012 |access-date=July 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120705210418/http://www.barber-schools.org/blog/killer-mikes-barber-shop-in-atlanta-ga-graffiti-swag |archive-date=July 5, 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref>

The barbershop is decorated with artwork on the walls honoring historic Black leaders, including [[Martin Luther King Jr.]] Mike said that he hopes to "lift up men in the community who are out of work and help move them toward sustainable, lifelong careers" and give his employees "opportunity for real economic elevation". As of 2012, the shop employed six barbers, with plans to add four to six more licensed barbers to the team. Mike said that he hoped to pursue his own barber license in the winter of 2012.<ref name=BarberSchools/>

The enterprise has been successful and the shop has become a gathering place for the community, in addition to hosting events such as a season premiere for ''[[The Boondocks (TV series)|The Boondocks]]'' and serving as the setting for several music videos. A second location in [[Tampa, Florida]] was planned for 2014.<ref name=SWAG_Bevel>{{cite web |url=http://bevelcode.com/inside-the-shop/graffitis-swag |title=Killer Mike's Graffiti's SWAG Barbershop |website=Bevel Code |date=November 17, 2014 |author=Howard, Marcia |access-date=April 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304050447/http://bevelcode.com/inside-the-shop/graffitis-swag |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=SWAG_BE>{{cite web |url=http://www.blackenterprise.com/small-business/kille-mike-interview-swag-barbershop-airport-atlanta/ |title=Rapper Killer Mike Redefines 'SWAG' with Barbershop |website=Black Enterprise |date=June 30, 2013 |author=Garland, Maurice |access-date=April 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150523021403/http://www.blackenterprise.com/small-business/kille-mike-interview-swag-barbershop-airport-atlanta/ |archive-date=May 23, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Greenwood bank===
In October 2020, Render, [[Bounce TV]] founder Ryan Glover, and former Atlanta mayor [[Andrew Young]] founded [[Greenwood (bank)|Greenwood]], an online bank targeting "Black and Latinx communities and anyone else who wants to support Black-owned businesses".<ref name="CNN-Greenwood">{{cite web|title=Killer Mike's new Black-owned bank receives 'tens of thousands' of account requests in less than 24 hours|last1=Alcorn|first1=Chauncey|publisher=CNN Money|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/10/10/business/killer-mike-greenwood-bank/index.html|date=October 10, 2020|access-date=October 15, 2020}}</ref><ref name="Greenwood-About">{{cite web|title=About Us: Bank Greenwood. Modern Banking for the Culture.|url=https://bankgreenwood.com/about/|publisher=Greenwood|access-date=October 15, 2020}}</ref> According to Glover "tens of thousands" of people were on its waitlist for accounts within a day,<ref name="CNN-Greenwood" /> and on January 26 Greenwood reported 500,000 people were waiting for accounts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Greenwood reaches 500,000 sign-ups, announces partnership and donation to King Center and Drum Major Institute|work=Greenwood |date=January 26, 2021 |url=https://bankgreenwood.com/press-release/greenwood-reaches-500000-sign-ups-announces-partnership-and-donation-to-king-center-and-drum-major-institute/|accessdate=January 26, 2021 }}</ref> The bank was originally expected to open in January 2021,<ref name="CNN-Greenwood" /> but delayed its opening first to July, and then to the end of 2021, due to "unanticipated high demand".<ref name="CNN-GreenwoodDelays">{{cite news|last1=Alcorn|first1=Chauncey|title=Killer Mike's bank has to postpone its launch again to catch up to high customer demand|work=CNN Business|date=June 24, 2021|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/06/24/business/greenwood-killer-mike-delayed/index.html|access-date=August 11, 2021}}</ref>

==Activism==

Mike is an outspoken social activist focusing on subjects including [[social equality]], [[police brutality]], and [[systemic racism]].<ref name=activism>{{cite web |url=http://theurbandaily.com/2015/04/20/killer-mike-mit-mike-brown/ |title=How Killer Mike Became Rap's Most Influential Political Leader |website=The Urban Daily |date=April 20, 2015 |author=Balfour, Jay |access-date=May 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421215904/http://theurbandaily.com/2015/04/20/killer-mike-mit-mike-brown/ |archive-date=April 21, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> His views are reflected in his music, as well as in interviews with the media. As a publicly viewed figure, Mike feels it is his responsibility to represent African-Americans: "I feel I have to be politically active and I have to be a credit to my race".<ref>{{cite web |title=Killer Mike, Venerable Rapper/Activist, Talks New Album, Drug War, and Maybe Running for Office |url=http://www.alternet.org/story/155338/killer_mike%2C_venerable_rapper_activist%2C_talks_new_album%2C_drug_war%2C_and_maybe_running_for_office?page=0%2C2 |website=Alternet |author=Shepherd, Julianne Escobedo |date=May 8, 2012 |access-date=November 19, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129023524/http://www.alternet.org/story/155338/killer_mike,_venerable_rapper_activist,_talks_new_album,_drug_war,_and_maybe_running_for_office?page=0,2 |archive-date=November 29, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> He has been vocal on the subject of police misconduct, his father being a former police officer. His anti-brutality sentiment can be found on the song "[[Reagan (song)|Reagan]]" from his album ''[[R.A.P. Music]]'',<ref>{{cite book |title=Reagan - R.A.P Music |author=Killer Mike |date=May 15, 2012 |publisher=Williams Street Records}}</ref> and the song "Early" on ''[[Run the Jewels 2]]''.<ref>{{cite book |author=Run The Jewels |title=Early - RTJ2 |date=October 28, 2014 |publisher=Mass Appeal Records}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.avclub.com/article/run-jewels-release-dark-stark-new-video-early-219504 |title=Run The Jewels release dark, stark new video for "Early" |website=The A.V. Club |date=May 15, 2015 |author=Eakin, Marah |access-date=May 18, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150517235850/http://www.avclub.com/article/run-jewels-release-dark-stark-new-video-early-219504 |archive-date=May 17, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In response to the 2014 [[killing of Michael Brown]] in [[Ferguson, Missouri]], Mike said:

{{blockquote|I'm appalled that regular Americans are apathetic. I'm appalled that people choose to use the word "thug" as a code word for "[[nigger]]". I'm appalled at everyday citizens... when will we, as an American constituency, tell our politicians enough's enough? Enough mayors supporting murderous police departments. Enough police chiefs having to give excuses for murderous police officers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Killer Mike, J. Cole, and Hip-Hop's Response to Ferguson|url=http://grantland.com/hollywood-prospectus/killer-mike-j-cole-and-hip-hops-response-to-ferguson/|website=Grantland|author=Barshad, Amos|date=August 21, 2014|access-date=November 19, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141108123115/http://grantland.com/hollywood-prospectus/killer-mike-j-cole-and-hip-hops-response-to-ferguson/|archive-date=November 8, 2014|url-status=live}}</ref>}}

In an [[op-ed]] published in ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine, Render stated that "there is no reason that Mike Brown and also [[Death of Eric Garner|Eric Garner]] are dead today—except bad policing, excessive force, and the hunt-and-capture-prey mentality many thrill-seeking cops have adapted".<ref name=Billboard_op-ed>{{cite web |url=https://www.billboard.com/biz/articles/6221888/op-ed-killer-mike-on-the-problems-underlying-the-chaos-in-ferguson |title=Op-Ed: Killer Mike on the Problems Underlying the Chaos in Ferguson |newspaper=Billboard |date=August 19, 2014 |author=Killer Mike |access-date=April 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150502045520/http://www.billboard.com/biz/articles/6221888/op-ed-killer-mike-on-the-problems-underlying-the-chaos-in-ferguson |archive-date=May 2, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Mike and El-P performed at The Ready Room in [[St. Louis, Missouri]] on November 24, 2014, the same night that the Grand Jury verdict was announced stating that Darren Wilson would not be charged with a crime in the shooting of Michael Brown. Mike opened the set, which began about two hours after the announcement was made, with a heartfelt speech.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MQs7CWKHM9w |title=Killer Mike's pre-show Ferguson Grand Jury speech |publisher=YouTube |date=November 24, 2014 |access-date=April 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421233953/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MQs7CWKHM9w |archive-date=April 21, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> Fan-shot footage of the speech later went viral.<ref name=RTJ_Ferguson>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2015/feb/26/run-the-jewels-on-hip-hops-golden-age-playing-ferguson-and-americas-civil-rights-problem |title=Run the Jewels on hip-hop's golden age, playing Ferguson and America's civil rights problem |newspaper=The Guardian |date=February 26, 2015 |author=Petridis, Alexis |access-date=April 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150509070524/http://www.theguardian.com/music/2015/feb/26/run-the-jewels-on-hip-hops-golden-age-playing-ferguson-and-americas-civil-rights-problem |archive-date=May 9, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Mike, in an op-ed, defended rap lyrics as freedom of speech.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/opinion/2014/11/28/poetic-injustice-rap-supreme-court-lyrics-violence-trial-column/19537391/|title=Rap's poetic (In)justice: Flashback|website=[[USA Today]]|access-date=September 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170928193234/https://www.usatoday.com/story/opinion/2014/11/28/poetic-injustice-rap-supreme-court-lyrics-violence-trial-column/19537391/|archive-date=September 28, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Mike gave a keynote address on free speech, and particularly with respect to the criminalization of rap music (he has a particular interest in championing the expressive rights of artists, and led the way in a successful campaign against the use of lyrics as criminal evidence in California), at the inaugural gala for the [[Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression]] in New York City in April 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SPEAKERS - Free Speech Makes Free People: Celebrating a New Era of FIRE |url=https://web.cvent.com/event/82b6e2cf-6fce-4e4e-8586-e3d7147fdf99/websitePage:bfd9922f-b4e1-4b60-9f4a-081a5414df7b |access-date=2023-04-22 |website=web.cvent.com}}</ref>

Commenting on the [[2015 Baltimore uprising]] related to the [[death of Freddie Gray]], Render noted that he understood the frustrations leading to violent demonstrations, but encouraged protesters to use their energy to organize for lasting change. In a ''Billboard'' op-ed, Mike stated:

{{blockquote|For the people of Baltimore—I don't criticize rioting because I understand it. But after the fires die down: organize, strategize, and mobilize. Like Ferguson, you have an opportunity to start anew. I don't have a solution because whoever's there will have to come up with it. But we need community relations: riots are the language of the unheard.<ref name=KM_BaltimoreOpEd>{{cite web |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6553719/killer-mike-baltimore-op-ed-correspondents-dinner-freddie-gray |title=Killer Mike Baltimore Op-Ed: 'I've Watched Geraldo Rivera and Wolf Blitzer Pander to the Audiences of Oppression' |newspaper=Billboard |date=May 1, 2015 |author=Killer Mike |access-date=May 1, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150503201758/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6553719/killer-mike-baltimore-op-ed-correspondents-dinner-freddie-gray |archive-date=May 3, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>}}

He made similar points in an interview with the ''[[Harvard Political Review]]'': "Baltimore is an opportunity for us to do something different. As society, there's a real opportunity to organize there, and if we do not take full advantage of the opportunity to organize, then the riots truly meant nothing".<ref name=KM_HPR>{{cite web |url=http://harvardpolitics.com/interviews/killer-mike-baltimore-riots-police/ |title=Killer Mike on the Baltimore Riots |newspaper=Harvard Political Review |date=April 29, 2015 |author=Mulholland, Quinn |access-date=May 1, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150502063847/http://harvardpolitics.com/interviews/killer-mike-baltimore-riots-police/ |archive-date=May 2, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Mike has given lectures about race relations in the United States at several American universities, including Northwestern University, [[New York University]]<ref name=NYU_lecture>{{cite web |url=http://nyulocal.com/on-campus/2015/03/24/killer-mike-oklahoma-fraternity-systemic-racism/ |title=Killer Mike Talks Oklahoma Fraternity, Systemic Racism |website=NYU Local |date=March 24, 2015 |author=Proctor, Bertram |access-date=May 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150420023105/http://nyulocal.com/on-campus/2015/03/24/killer-mike-oklahoma-fraternity-systemic-racism/ |archive-date=April 20, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> and the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name=lectures>{{cite web |url=http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/posts/la-et-ms-killer-mile-to-lecture-on-race-at-mit-20150420-story.html |title=Rapper Killer Mike to lecture on race at MIT |newspaper=LA Times |date=April 20, 2015 |author=Brown, August |access-date=April 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150420231919/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/posts/la-et-ms-killer-mile-to-lecture-on-race-at-mit-20150420-story.html |archive-date=April 20, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=MIT_lecture>{{cite web |url=https://www.boston.com/news/local/massachusetts/2015/04/27/here-killer-mike-mit-talk-race-video/5iCBdm1hAKHwAhzKKEMHTN/story.html |title=Here's Killer Mike's MIT Talk on Race |website=Boston.com |date=April 27, 2015 |author=Loftus, Jamie |access-date=May 1, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150430004818/http://www.boston.com/news/local/massachusetts/2015/04/27/here-killer-mike-mit-talk-race-video/5iCBdm1hAKHwAhzKKEMHTN/story.html |archive-date=April 30, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His activism work was featured in a 2019 episode of ''[[The Real World: Atlanta]]''.<ref>''The Real World''. Season Atlanta, episode Who Will Hook Up First?, Facebook Watch, 20 June 2019.</ref>

===Political involvement===
[[File:Killer Mike Introduces Bernie Sanders in Atlanta.webm|thumb|Render introduces [[Bernie Sanders]] at a November 2015 [[Bernie Sanders presidential campaign, 2016|campaign rally]] in Atlanta]]
In June 2015, Mike briefly ran as a [[write-in candidate]] to become the representative for Georgia's 55th district in the [[Georgia House of Representatives]]. Despite encouraging voters to write in his real name, Michael Render, any votes he received would not have been considered valid due to his failure to previously register as an official candidate in the election.<ref name=KM_writein_AJC>{{cite web |url=http://www.ajc.com/news/news/local/rapper-killer-mike-runs-for-georgia-state-represen/nmdSW/ |title=Rapper Killer Mike wanted to run for Georgia state representative |newspaper=Atlanta Journal-Constitution |date=June 15, 2015 |author=Funke, Daniel |access-date=June 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150619032123/http://www.ajc.com/news/news/local/rapper-killer-mike-runs-for-georgia-state-represen/nmdSW/ |archive-date=June 19, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=KM_writein_CNN>{{cite web |url=http://www.cnn.com/2015/06/16/us/killer-mike-write-in-candidate/ |title=Killer Mike to Georgia voters: Pick me! ... Oh wait |website=CNN |date=June 16, 2015 |author=Lacey-Bordeaux, Emma |access-date=July 26, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806144740/http://www.cnn.com/2015/06/16/us/killer-mike-write-in-candidate |archive-date=August 6, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> He said his purpose in running was to raise awareness of the special election, and to demonstrate that political outsiders can and should run against established politicians.<ref name=KM_writein_Guardian>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2015/jun/16/killer-mike-plots-political-agenda-ahead-georgia-state-election |title=Killer Mike plots political agenda ahead of Georgia state election |newspaper=The Guardian |date=June 16, 2015 |access-date=June 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622222837/http://www.theguardian.com/music/2015/jun/16/killer-mike-plots-political-agenda-ahead-georgia-state-election |archive-date=June 22, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Mike announced his support of Democratic U.S. presidential candidate [[Bernie Sanders]] in June 2015 after Sanders announced his intention to restore the [[Voting Rights Act of 1965]].<ref name=KM_Sanders>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2015/jun/29/killer-mike-bernie-sanders-president-run-the-jewels |title=Killer Mike Endorses Bernie Sanders for President |newspaper=The Guardian |date=June 29, 2015 |author=Holpuch, Amanda |access-date=July 13, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150714085336/http://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2015/jun/29/killer-mike-bernie-sanders-president-run-the-jewels |archive-date=July 14, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> After introducing Sanders at a rally held in Atlanta November 23, 2015,<ref name=RS_Bernie_Rally>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/watch-killer-mike-introduce-bernie-sanders-with-moving-speech-at-atlanta-rally-20151123|title=Watch Killer Mike Introduce Bernie Sanders With Moving Speech at Atlanta Rally|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=November 23, 2015|author=Kreps, Daniel|access-date=December 16, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218012434/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/watch-killer-mike-introduce-bernie-sanders-with-moving-speech-at-atlanta-rally-20151123|archive-date=December 18, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> Mike spent time recording an interview with the presidential candidate at Mike's barbershop. In February 2016, Mike received criticism during his activism for Sanders for quoting American anti-racism and LGBT advocate [[Jane Elliott]] regarding [[Hillary Clinton]], which was criticized as misogynistic and mistakenly attributed as being his original phrasing online and in the press.<ref>{{cite web|last1=McCarthy|first1=Tom|title=Sanders campaign defends Killer Mike using 'uterus' quote about Clinton|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2016/feb/17/killer-mike-uterus-hillary-clinton-bernie-sanders-jane-elliott|date=February 17, 2016|website=The Guardian|access-date=February 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220035644/http://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2016/feb/17/killer-mike-uterus-hillary-clinton-bernie-sanders-jane-elliott|archive-date=February 20, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> Following Sanders' exit from the race, Mike refused to support Clinton, citing her pro-war record.<ref name=HillaryNope>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/news/killer-mike-says-donald-trump-and-hillary-clinton-are-exactly-the-same|title=Killer Mike says Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton are exactly the same|publisher=CBS News|date=August 12, 2016|author=Ehrbar, Ned|access-date=October 26, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011094925/http://www.cbsnews.com/news/killer-mike-says-donald-trump-and-hillary-clinton-are-exactly-the-same/|archive-date=October 11, 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

Mike has been an advocate for investment in [[African-American businesses|black-owned banks]]; in July 2016, he called for people to transfer their money to black-owned [[Atlanta]] bank Citizens Trust, stating, "We don't have to burn our city down. But what we can do is go to your banks tomorrow. You can go to your bank tomorrow. And you can say, 'Until you as a corporation start to speak on our behalf, I want all my money. And I'm taking all my money to Citizens Trust".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://pitchfork.com/news/66804-killer-mike-prompts-huge-influx-into-black-owned-bank|title=Killer Mike Prompts 'Huge Influx' Into Black-Owned Bank|last=Hogan|first=Mark|website=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]|date=July 14, 2016|access-date=July 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709105418/http://pitchfork.com/news/66804-killer-mike-prompts-huge-influx-into-black-owned-bank/|archive-date=July 9, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2016/07/15/black-owned-banks-credit-unions/87118624/|title=Black-owned banks get rush of new depositors|author=Bomey, Nathan|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170727202509/https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/2016/07/15/black-owned-banks-credit-unions/87118624/|archive-date=July 27, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

In June 2017, at [[Glastonbury Festival|Glastonbury]] festival, Mike endorsed [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] leader [[Jeremy Corbyn]] in the [[2017 United Kingdom general election|2017 UK general election]].<ref name="theguardian">{{cite news|last=Beaumont-Thomas|first=Ben|url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/jun/16/jeremy-corbyn-pyramid-stage-glastonbury-festival-2017|title=Jeremy Corbyn to appear on Pyramid stage at Glastonbury festival 2017|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=June 16, 2017|access-date=June 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622181716/https://www.theguardian.com/music/2017/jun/16/jeremy-corbyn-pyramid-stage-glastonbury-festival-2017|archive-date=June 22, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 22, 2018, Mike appeared on [[NRATV]] with host [[Colion Noir]] defending Black gun ownership. He says it had been filmed a week prior to the [[March for Our Lives]] yet released the weekend of the protest. He stated that he told his children that if they participated in the [[2018 United States gun violence protests|National School Walkout]] that he would expect them to leave the family home. On March 26, 2018, he posted a video stating that the NRA used his interview out of context, saying he actually supports March for Our Lives while simultaneously advocating for Black gun ownership. During this same video he gave his endorsement for gun ownership alternatives, listing the [[Socialist Rifle Association]] by name.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/killer-mike-defends-gun-ownership-in-nratv-interview-w518353#|title=Run the Jewels' Killer Mike Defends Gun Ownership in NRATV Interview|magazine=Rolling Stone|access-date=March 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324235607/https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/killer-mike-defends-gun-ownership-in-nratv-interview-w518353|archive-date=March 24, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/therecord/2018/03/26/596988606/killer-mike-apologizes-for-interview-with-nra-claims-it-was-misused|title=Killer Mike Apologizes For Interview With NRA, Claims It Was Misused|newspaper=NPR|date=March 26, 2018|access-date=March 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180326191617/https://www.npr.org/sections/therecord/2018/03/26/596988606/killer-mike-apologizes-for-interview-with-nra-claims-it-was-misused|archive-date=March 26, 2018|url-status=live|last1=Flanagan|first1=Andrew}}</ref>

On May 29, 2020, Mike spoke during a press conference with Atlanta mayor [[Keisha Lance Bottoms]] in response to the [[murder of George Floyd]] and the ensuing protests.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rapper Killer Mike addresses Atlanta protesters|url=https://www.cnn.com/2020/05/30/us/killer-mike-atlanta-protest-rapper-trnd/index.html|first=Jay |last=Croft|website=CNN|date=May 30, 2020 |access-date=May 31, 2020}}</ref><ref name="mclaughlin">{{cite web | title = How Atlanta rappers helped flip the White House | last = McLaughlin | first = Eliott C. | website = CNN | url = https://edition.cnn.com/2020/12/29/politics/atlanta-hip-hop-flip-election-senate-white-house/index.html | date = 29 December 2020}}</ref>

In 2020, Mike supported both [[Raphael Warnock]] and [[Jon Ossoff]] in the [[2020–2021 United States Senate special election in Georgia]], both of whom won. He again endorsed Warnock in the [[2022 United States Senate election in Georgia]], although he interviewed his opponent, [[Herschel Walker]], in May of that year on his ''Love & Respect'' series.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bet.com/article/vvmf3o/killer-mike-stirs-controversy-with-herschel-walker-interview | title=Killer Mike Stirs Controversy with Herschel Walker Interview | website=[[BET]] }}</ref><ref name="zaru2021">{{cite web | title = In 'mecca of hip-hop,' rappers rally for Georgia Democrats ahead of Senate runoffs | last = Zaru | first = Deena | website = Good Morning America | date = 5 January 2021 | url = https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/news/story/rappers-rally-georgia-democrats-ahead-high-stakes-senate-74966943}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | website = Bloomberg | title = Hip Hop Star Killer Mike on Raphael Warnock's Reelection | date = 7 December 2022 | url = https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2022-12-07/hip-hop-star-killer-mike-on-raphael-warnock-s-reelection-video}}</ref>

On October 3, 2026, Mike will appear at the Power to the People Festival at [[Merriweather Post Pavilion]] in [[Columbia, MD]]. The festival, which is being put on by [[Tom Morello]], will also feature performances by Morello, [[Bruce Springsteen]], [[Foo Fighters]] and many others. The festival is being held in response to [[President Donald Trump]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/music/2026/05/28/bruce-springsteen-tom-morello-foo-fighters-power-to-the-people-festival-ticket-lineup/90290898007/|title=Springsteen, Foo Fighters, Morello more set for Power to the People|first=Chris|last=Jordan|publisher=USA Today|date=May 28, 2026|access-date=May 28, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mike married his wife, Shana, in 2006.<ref name=CNBC>{{cite web |date=2019-03-20 |first=Joan |last=McDonald |title=Rapper and Netflix star Killer Mike says this was his best business decision—and Warren Buffett agrees |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/03/19/netflix-star-killer-mike-says-marriage-was-his-best-business-decision.html |work=[[CNBC]]}}</ref> They have four children.<ref name=CNBC /><ref name="GuardianInterview" />

Mike was arrested and booked for [[misdemeanor battery]] following an altercation with a security guard on February 4, 2024, shortly after he won three [[Grammy Awards]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://apnews.com/article/killer-mike-arrest-grammys-7c95ddb7a5180de4dd13b6b2cd415bb7 |title=Killer Mike says arrest at Grammys stems from altercation with an 'over-zealous' security guard|website=[[Associated Press News]] |date=February 6, 2024}}</ref> He completed a community service requirement, thus avoiding charges.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://people.com/killer-mike-wont-face-charges-2024-grammys-arrest-8670480 |title=Killer Mike Will Not Face Charges Over 2024 Grammys Arrest|website=People.com |date=June 27, 2024}}</ref>

Mike has five sisters, including LaShunda and Lovie.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rb-hip-hop/killer-mike-michael-church-new-album-1235354111/|title=Inside the Making of Killer Mike's 'Michael' and His Midnight Revival|magazine=Billboard|date=June 14, 2023|access-date=August 22, 2024}}</ref>

Killer Mike.text:
Michael Santiago Render (born April 20, 1975), known professionally as Killer Mike, is an American rapper, singer, actor, and activist. He made his recording debut on Outkast's fourth album Stankonia (2000), and guest appeared on the duo's Grammy Award-winning single "The Whole World" from their greatest hits album Big Boi and Dre Present... Outkast (2001). He signed with Big Boi's Purple Ribbon Records (known then as Aquemini Records) and Columbia Records to release his debut studio album Monster (2003), which was met with critical acclaim and peaked at number ten on the Billboard 200. He parted ways with the label and released two albums—I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind (2006) and I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind II (2008)—before signing with T.I.'s Grand Hustle to release his fourth album, Pledge (2011), and later Williams Street to release his fifth album, R.A.P. Music (2012). His sixth album, Michael (2023), was met with continued acclaim and won three awards at 66th Annual Grammy Awards, including Best Rap Album.
Following R.A.P. Music, which was produced entirely by rapper and producer El-P, he and Render subsequently formed the duo Run the Jewels in 2013. They signed with Fool's Gold Records and released their self-titled debut in June of that year to critical acclaim. Its three sequels—Run the Jewels 2 (2014), Run the Jewels 3 (2016) and RTJ4 (2020)—were each met with continued critical praise, the latter of which matched his debut solo album in chart position on the Billboard 200. The duo made a guest appearance alongside Big Boi on Danger Mouse's 2017 single "Chase Me", which received a Grammy Award nomination.
Outside of music, Render has been a social and political activist, focusing on subjects including social inequality, police brutality, and systemic racism. In addition to discussing related topics in his music, he has lectured about similar issues at colleges and universities, written about such matters for publications including Billboard, and been the subject of interviews regarding police misconduct and race relations. He was a visible and vocal supporter of Bernie Sanders' 2016 U.S. presidential campaign, and supported Sanders once more in his 2020 presidential campaign. Render has appeared in films such as Idlewild, Baby Driver, ATL, and America: The Motion Picture. His six episode docu-series, Trigger Warning with Killer Mike, investigated social issues that affect Black Americans, and premiered on Netflix in January 2019. His weekly interview program for the Public Broadcasting Service (PBS), Love & Respect (2021–present), won an Emmy Award in 2022.


== Early life ==
Michael Render was born in the Adamsville neighborhood of Atlanta, Georgia, on April 20, 1975, the son of a policeman father and a florist mother. Because his parents were teenagers at the time of his birth, he was partly raised by his grandparents in the Collier Heights neighborhood of Atlanta, and attended Douglass High School.


== Career ==


=== 1995–2005: Early career ===
In 1995, Render briefly attended Atlanta's Morehouse College, where he met producers The Beat Bullies, and soon met rapper Big Boi of Outkast. His music debut was a feature appearance on Outkast's "Snappin' & Trappin'" from the 2000 album Stankonia, followed by their 2001 single "The Whole World", which won the 2002 Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group. He was featured on several other tracks that year, including the Jay-Z's song "Poppin' Tags" from his album The Blueprint 2, where he guest performed alongside both Big Boi and Chicago rapper Twista.
In 2003, Render released his debut studio album, Monster, while being managed by Dayo Adebiyi and Al Thrash of Own Music. The album's lead single, "Akshon (Yeah!)", featured both Outkast members as guest performers. A remix of the song was included on the soundtrack of EA Sports video game Madden NFL 2004. The album's second single was "A.D.I.D.A.S"., featuring Big Boi and Sleepy Brown, which peaked at number 60 on the US Billboard Hot 100. It remains Render's only single to enter the chart as a lead artist.
Following the release of his own material, he appeared on "Flip Flop Rock" and "Bust" on the Speakerboxx half of OutKast's Speakerboxxx/The Love Below double album. He appeared on "Southern Takeover" with Pastor Troy on Chamillionaire's album The Sound of Revenge. Render appeared alongside T.I. on the song "Never Scared" by Bone Crusher on his album AttenCHUN!. It peaked at #26 on the Hot 100, becoming Mike's second top 40 hit ("The Whole World" being the first). The song was used on the Madden NFL 2004 game soundtrack and by the Atlanta Braves for their 2003 season.


=== 2006–2012: Pledge series and R.A.P. Music ===

What was to be his second album, Ghetto Extraordinary, had its release date pushed back several times due to disputes between Big Boi and Sony Music. Originally recorded in 2005, the album was eventually self-released as a mixtape in 2008. Render confirmed in January 2008 that he had officially left Purple Ribbon Records.
Render's second album, I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind, was released on his own Grind Time Official label in 2006, followed by I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind II in 2008.
T.I. announced that he and Render had been in talks about bringing Mike to his Grand Hustle imprint on Atlantic, and Render confirmed that he had signed in December 2008. He released his fourth album, PL3DGE, on Grand Hustle in 2011. His fifth album, R.A.P. Music, followed in 2012.
In 2013, Render announced that he was working to release two albums in 2014, I Pledge Allegiance to the Grind IV and R.A.P. Music II, both of which were to feature production by El-P. Although neither album was released as planned, 2013 and 2014 did see the release of two Run the Jewels albums, both collaborative efforts between Render and El-P.
Render announced in 2013 that his next solo album would be titled Elegant Elephant, a project he described as his "Moby Dick". He did not specify a timeline for its release.


=== 2013–present: Run the Jewels, Michael and Songs for Sinners & Saints ===

Render was introduced to rapper-producer El-P by Cartoon Network executive Jason DeMarco in 2011. The following year, El-P produced Mike's album R.A.P. Music and guested on the song "Butane (Champion's Anthem)". That same year, Render guested on El-P's album Cancer 4 Cure. When R.A.P. Music and Cancer 4 Cure were released within weeks of each other, the two rappers decided to tour together. The success of the tour eventually led to the decision to record as a duo, which they named Run the Jewels.

Run the Jewels released a free eponymous album on June 26, 2013. The next year, on October 28, 2014, Run the Jewels released their second free album, Run the Jewels 2. On September 25, 2015, the duo released a re-recorded version of Run the Jewels 2 made entirely with cat sounds, titled Meow the Jewels. A third album, Run the Jewels 3, was released on December 24, 2016. Their fourth album, RTJ4, was released on June 3, 2020.
On July 4, 2022, Mike released a solo single, "Run". This track would subsequently appear on Michael, a solo album that Mike released on June 16, 2023.
On July 29, 2024, Mike announced his seventh studio album, Songs for Sinners & Saints, with his gospel group, Michael & The Mighty Midnight Revival. The album released August 2nd.
In 2025, Killer Mike appeared on the De La Soul album Cabin in the Sky, on the song “A Quick 16 For Mama”.


== Other ventures ==


=== Acting ===
Mike has been featured in the films 20 Funerals, Idlewild (2006), and ATL (2006). He has performed as a voice actor, playing a rapper/actor-turned-U.S. President named Taqu'il in the Adult Swim cartoon Frisky Dingo from 2006 to 2008. Mike guest-voiced a Boost Mobile phone in an episode of the same name of Adult Swim's Aqua Teen Hunger Force. He appeared twice on an Adult Swim surreal comedy series The Eric Andre Show, once in 2012, where he acted as a hype man for a female opera singer, and again in 2014, where he performed a rap battle with Action Bronson while the two were forced to walk on treadmills. He appeared as himself in Ozark (season 4 episode 8). On January 18, 2019, Netflix released Trigger Warning with Killer Mike, a docuseries which Mike hosts.


=== Graffitis SWAG barbershop ===
Mike and his wife, Shana, opened a barbershop in Atlanta on November 1, 2011. The two acquired and reworked a barbershop and named it Graffitis SWAG (shave, wash, and groom). He had waited nine years before choosing to open the barbershop, after having an early business manager advise him against the plan. It took his wife advising him to do it now while he had the time and money to pursue his lifelong dream. He eventually plans to open 150 shops across the United States over time, predominantly in cities with large Black communities.
The barbershop is decorated with artwork on the walls honoring historic Black leaders, including Martin Luther King Jr. Mike said that he hopes to "lift up men in the community who are out of work and help move them toward sustainable, lifelong careers" and give his employees "opportunity for real economic elevation". As of 2012, the shop employed six barbers, with plans to add four to six more licensed barbers to the team. Mike said that he hoped to pursue his own barber license in the winter of 2012.
The enterprise has been successful and the shop has become a gathering place for the community, in addition to hosting events such as a season premiere for The Boondocks and serving as the setting for several music videos. A second location in Tampa, Florida was planned for 2014.


=== Greenwood bank ===
In October 2020, Render, Bounce TV founder Ryan Glover, and former Atlanta mayor Andrew Young founded Greenwood, an online bank targeting "Black and Latinx communities and anyone else who wants to support Black-owned businesses". According to Glover "tens of thousands" of people were on its waitlist for accounts within a day, and on January 26 Greenwood reported 500,000 people were waiting for accounts. The bank was originally expected to open in January 2021, but delayed its opening first to July, and then to the end of 2021, due to "unanticipated high demand".


== Activism ==
Mike is an outspoken social activist focusing on subjects including social equality, police brutality, and systemic racism. His views are reflected in his music, as well as in interviews with the media. As a publicly viewed figure, Mike feels it is his responsibility to represent African-Americans: "I feel I have to be politically active and I have to be a credit to my race". He has been vocal on the subject of police misconduct, his father being a former police officer. His anti-brutality sentiment can be found on the song "Reagan" from his album R.A.P. Music, and the song "Early" on Run the Jewels 2.
In response to the 2014 killing of Michael Brown in Ferguson, Missouri, Mike said:

I'm appalled that regular Americans are apathetic. I'm appalled that people choose to use the word "thug" as a code word for "nigger". I'm appalled at everyday citizens... when will we, as an American constituency, tell our politicians enough's enough? Enough mayors supporting murderous police departments. Enough police chiefs having to give excuses for murderous police officers.
In an op-ed published in Billboard magazine, Render stated that "there is no reason that Mike Brown and also Eric Garner are dead today—except bad policing, excessive force, and the hunt-and-capture-prey mentality many thrill-seeking cops have adapted".
Mike and El-P performed at The Ready Room in St. Louis, Missouri on November 24, 2014, the same night that the Grand Jury verdict was announced stating that Darren Wilson would not be charged with a crime in the shooting of Michael Brown. Mike opened the set, which began about two hours after the announcement was made, with a heartfelt speech. Fan-shot footage of the speech later went viral.
Mike, in an op-ed, defended rap lyrics as freedom of speech. Mike gave a keynote address on free speech, and particularly with respect to the criminalization of rap music (he has a particular interest in championing the expressive rights of artists, and led the way in a successful campaign against the use of lyrics as criminal evidence in California), at the inaugural gala for the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression in New York City in April 2023.
Commenting on the 2015 Baltimore uprising related to the death of Freddie Gray, Render noted that he understood the frustrations leading to violent demonstrations, but encouraged protesters to use their energy to organize for lasting change. In a Billboard op-ed, Mike stated:

For the people of Baltimore—I don't criticize rioting because I understand it. But after the fires die down: organize, strategize, and mobilize. Like Ferguson, you have an opportunity to start anew. I don't have a solution because whoever's there will have to come up with it. But we need community relations: riots are the language of the unheard.
He made similar points in an interview with the Harvard Political Review: "Baltimore is an opportunity for us to do something different. As society, there's a real opportunity to organize there, and if we do not take full advantage of the opportunity to organize, then the riots truly meant nothing".
Mike has given lectures about race relations in the United States at several American universities, including Northwestern University, New York University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. His activism work was featured in a 2019 episode of The Real World: Atlanta.


=== Political involvement ===

In June 2015, Mike briefly ran as a write-in candidate to become the representative for Georgia's 55th district in the Georgia House of Representatives. Despite encouraging voters to write in his real name, Michael Render, any votes he received would not have been considered valid due to his failure to previously register as an official candidate in the election. He said his purpose in running was to raise awareness of the special election, and to demonstrate that political outsiders can and should run against established politicians.
Mike announced his support of Democratic U.S. presidential candidate Bernie Sanders in June 2015 after Sanders announced his intention to restore the Voting Rights Act of 1965. After introducing Sanders at a rally held in Atlanta November 23, 2015, Mike spent time recording an interview with the presidential candidate at Mike's barbershop. Mike released his interview with Sanders as a six-part video series the following month. In the following months, he remained an active and vocal supporter of Sanders, delivering speeches at rallies, voicing support in televised interviews and on social media, and traveling with the campaign. Sanders introduced Run the Jewels before their appearance at the 2016 Coachella music festival.
In February 2016, Mike received criticism during his activism for Sanders for quoting American anti-racism and LGBT advocate Jane Elliott regarding Hillary Clinton, which was criticized as misogynistic and mistakenly attributed as being his original phrasing online and in the press. Following Sanders' exit from the race, Mike refused to support Clinton, citing her pro-war record.
Mike has been an advocate for investment in black-owned banks; in July 2016, he called for people to transfer their money to black-owned Atlanta bank Citizens Trust, stating, "We don't have to burn our city down. But what we can do is go to your banks tomorrow. You can go to your bank tomorrow. And you can say, 'Until you as a corporation start to speak on our behalf, I want all my money. And I'm taking all my money to Citizens Trust".
In June 2017, at Glastonbury festival, Mike endorsed Labour Party leader Jeremy Corbyn in the 2017 UK general election.
On March 22, 2018, Mike appeared on NRATV with host Colion Noir defending Black gun ownership. He says it had been filmed a week prior to the March for Our Lives yet released the weekend of the protest. He stated that he told his children that if they participated in the National School Walkout that he would expect them to leave the family home. On March 26, 2018, he posted a video stating that the NRA used his interview out of context, saying he actually supports March for Our Lives while simultaneously advocating for Black gun ownership. During this same video he gave his endorsement for gun ownership alternatives, listing the Socialist Rifle Association by name.
On May 29, 2020, Mike spoke during a press conference with Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms in response to the murder of George Floyd and the ensuing protests.
In 2020, Mike supported both Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff in the 2020–2021 United States Senate special election in Georgia, both of whom won. He again endorsed Warnock in the 2022 United States Senate election in Georgia, although he interviewed his opponent, Herschel Walker, in May of that year on his Love & Respect series.
On October 3, 2026, Mike will appear at the Power to the People Festival at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, MD. The festival, which is being put on by Tom Morello, will also feature performances by Morello, Bruce Springsteen, Foo Fighters and many others. The festival is being held in response to President Donald Trump.


== Personal life ==
Mike married his wife, Shana, in 2006. They have four children.
Mike was arrested and booked for misdemeanor battery following an altercation with a security guard on February 4, 2024, shortly after he won three Grammy Awards. He completed a community service requirement, thus avoiding charges.
Mike has five sisters, including LaShunda and Lovie.

Reloaded (Roc Marciano album).text:
Reloaded is the second studio album by American hip-hop recording artist Roc Marciano, released on November 13, 2012, by Decon Records. Marciano produced most of the album and was assisted by The Alchemist, Ray West, Q-Tip, and The Arch Druids. The album features guest contributions by rappers Ka and Knowledge the Pirate.


== Critical reception ==

At Metacritic, which assigns a normalized rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream critics, the album received an average score of 83, which indicates "universal acclaim", based on 13 reviews. Nick de Molina of XXL praised its production as "bold and experimental", and called Reloaded "a thrilling upgrade of signature East Coast delivery in the new age and one of the best albums of the year to date." Phillip Mlynar of Spin felt that "Marciano's writing style elevates [the album] to a great one" and stated, "he's written perhaps the most vivid rap album of the year — and possibly of his lifetime." Peter Marrack of Exclaim! called it "a sequel nonpareil in its originality and craftsmanship ... a humbling exhibit of spoken poetry knitted to orchestral magic, mixed and beautified by Q-Tip himself." Although he found it thematically "narrow", Pitchfork's Ian Cohen found Marciano's "lyrical genius ... so captivating on a second-by-second basis that these criticisms feel misplaced or even irrelevant", and stated, "Reloaded improves on Marcberg in every conceivable way."
About.com ranked the album #4 on its list of the "Top 10 Rap Albums of 2012." Spin ranked the album #6 on its list of the "40 Best Hip-Hop Albums of 2012."
