'''Corey Miller''' (born March 9, 1971),<ref name="allmusic">{{cite web |url={{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p278648|pure_url=yes}}|title=C-Murder Biography|last=Erlewine|first=Stephen Thomas|publisher=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=July 27, 2009}}</ref> better known by his stage name '''C-Murder''', is an American rapper. He initially gained fame in the mid-1990s as a part of his brother [[Master P]]'s label [[No Limit Records]], primarily as a member of the label's supergroup, [[TRU (band)|TRU]]. Miller went on to release several solo albums of his own through the label, including 1998's [[Music recording sales certification|platinum]] ''[[Life or Death (C-Murder album)|Life or Death]]''. C-Murder has released nine albums altogether on six different labels, [[No Limit Records]], TRU Records, [[Koch Records]], [[Asylum Records]], [[RBC Records]], and Venti Uno.

In 2002, Miller was arrested in connection with the murder of 16-year-old Steve Thomas, and was sentenced to [[Life imprisonment|life in prison]] on August 14, 2009. Miller is serving his sentence at the [[Louisiana State Penitentiary]].<ref name="mtv2003">{{cite news |last=Kaufman |first=Gil |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/1479444/c-murder-found-guilty-of-second-degree-murder-receives-life-sentence/ |title=C-Murder Found Guilty Of Second-Degree Murder, Receives Life Sentence |publisher=MTV News |date=October 1, 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031002183849/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1479444/10012003/c_murder.jhtml |archive-date=October 2, 2003 |access-date=May 4, 2016 }}</ref><ref name="auto">{{cite news|title=Rapper C-Murder sentenced to life in prison|url=http://www.today.com/id/32418793|publisher=MSN Music|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=August 14, 2009|access-date=November 17, 2019|archive-date=November 6, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191106234634/http://www.today.com/id/32418793}}</ref> Controversy surrounding witnesses involved in Miller's trial came to light in 2018 when two key witnesses recanted their statements, stating they had been pressured into testifying against Miller by authorities. Miller maintains his innocence, and he, his brothers, and his [[Romeo Miller|nephew]] have all called for a [[new trial]] numerous times.<ref name="auto1">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/c-murder-witness-recants-testimony-pressured-shooter/|title=C-Murder Witness Recants Testimony, Says He Was Pressured Into Identifying Rapper as Shooter|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=June 27, 2018|access-date=June 27, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/112622-c-murders-lawyer-wants-conviction-reversed-after-2nd-witness-recants-testimony-news|title=C-Murder's Lawyer Wants Conviction Reversed After 2nd Witness Recants Testimony.|website=HNHH|date=July 4, 2018|access-date=July 7, 2018}}</ref>

==Early life==
Corey Miller was born in [[Uptown New Orleans]], [[Louisiana]] on March 9, 1971.<ref name="allmusic" /> He grew up in the [[Calliope Projects]] in the [[3rd Ward of New Orleans]] with his sister Germaine, and brothers [[Silkk the Shocker]] and [[Master P]] and Kevin Miller.

==Military service==
After graduating from high school, Corey Miller enlisted in the [[United States Army]]. He served as a [[combat medic]] and was deployed to the [[Persian Gulf]] during the [[Gulf War]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The Rise & Fall Of C-Murder: A Complete History |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/299121-the-rise-of-c-murder-a-complete-history-news |website=HotNewHipHop |date=May 19, 2020 |access-date=June 3, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=C-Murder |url=https://invocation.co/people/person/c-murder |website=Shefik presents Invocation |access-date=June 3, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Kim Kardashian teams up with Monica to #FreeCoreyMiller |url=https://www.theloop.ca/kim-kardashian-teams-up-with-monica-to-freecoreymiller/ |website=Etalk |date=August 17, 2020 |access-date=June 3, 2025}}</ref>

== Music career ==
In 1998, Miller released his first album ''[[Life or Death (C-Murder album)|Life or Death]]''<ref name="allmusic"/> which peaked at No. 3 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]<ref name="allmusic-awards">{{cite web|url={{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p278648|pure_url=yes}}|title=C-Murder > Charts & Awards > Billboard Albums|website=AllMusic|access-date=July 27, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131031071717/http://www.allmusic.com/artist/c-murder-mn0000527773/awards |archive-date=2013-10-31}}</ref> and was eventually certified platinum.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}  He also was featured on the theme for the [[nWo Wolfpac]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lambert |first1=Jeremy |title=Jimmy Hart Discusses His Role In Creating The nWo Wolfpac Theme |url=https://www.fightful.com/wrestling/jimmy-hart-discusses-his-role-creating-nwo-wolfpa |website=Fightful}}</ref>

In 1999, he released ''[[Bossalinie]]'' which peaked at No. 2 on the ''Billboard'' 200<ref name="allmusic-awards"/> and was certified gold.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

In 2000, he released ''[[Trapped in Crime]]'' which peaked at No. 9 on the ''Billboard'' 200.<ref name="allmusic-awards"/> The album included the single "[[Down for My N's]]"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/c-murder-mn0000527773/biography|title=C-Murder Biography|website=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=May 13, 2023}}</ref>

In 2001, he released ''[[C-P-3.com]]'', his last album with [[No Limit Records]]. It peaked at No. 45 on the ''Billboard'' 200<ref name="allmusic-awards"/> and included the singles "What U Gonna Do" and "Im Not Just".{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

In 2003, he was convicted of the murder of fan Steve Thomas.<ref name="mtv2003"/> He recorded three hit albums while under house arrest awaiting re-trial: ''[[The Truest Shit I Ever Said]]'' (2005) which reached No. 41 on the ''Billboard'' 200, ''[[Screamin' 4 Vengeance]]'' (2008) which reached No. 130, and ''[[Calliope Click Volume 1|Calliope Click]]'' (2009) which peaked at No. 68 on the ''Billboard'' R&B Albums chart.<ref name="allmusic-awards"/>

In 2009, he lost his appeal<ref name="nola"/> and pleaded no contest to two counts of attempted murder in an unrelated incident.<ref name="wafb"/> While in prison he self-released a mixtape ''Ricochet'' (2013) and four albums, ''[[Tomorrow (C-Murder album)|Tomorrow]]'' (2010), ''Ain't No Heaven in the Pen'' (2015), ''Give Me Freedom Or Give Me Death'' (2021), and the compilation ''Oldies but Goodies'' (2018).{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

In 2016, he released a diss track accusing rapper [[2 Chainz]] of using the slogan and name style of his former group TRU<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S-jKzjYLyNs|title=C-Murder Disses 2 Chainz On "2 Stainz;" 2 Chainz Responds|date=January 12, 2016|access-date=December 12, 2017|publisher=[[YouTube]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R3fPlX6Ijf8|title=@CartoonTutorBabi - C Murder 2 Stainz (2 Chainz Diss)|publisher=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> and record label TRU Global Records.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LKBonE7FZ88|title=C-Murder speaks on the return of TRU Records Part 2|date=September 17, 2016|access-date=December 12, 2017|publisher=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>

== Other ventures ==
Miller acted in the [[No Limit Records|No Limit]] films ''[[Da Game of Life (film)|Da Game of Life]]'', ''[[I Got the Hook-Up]]'', and ''[[Hot Boyz (film)|Hot Boyz]]''.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}} He is the author of the novel ''Death Around The Corner'', published by ''[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]''.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

== Legal issues ==
{{too detailed|section|date=March 2024}}
=== Steve Thomas case ===
In September 2003, Miller was convicted of second degree murder in connection with the January 12, 2002 beating and fatal shooting of a fan, 16-year-old Steve Thomas, at the Platinum Club, a now-closed nightclub in [[Harvey, Louisiana]].<ref name="mtv2003"/> Miller was arrested in the early hours of January 18 for causing a disturbance at the [[House of Blues]] in New Orleans, and shortly after charged in Thomas' murder.<ref name="2002 arrest">{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020822015138/http://www.nola.com/news/t-p/frontpage/index.ssf?%2Fnewsstory%2Fcmurder19.html|archive-date=August 22, 2002|title=Gangsta rapper booked in teen killing|author=Nelson, Rob|url=http://www.nola.com:80/news/t-p/frontpage/index.ssf?/newsstory/cmurder19.html|work=The Times-Picayune|date=January 19, 2002|access-date=June 11, 2017}}</ref> He was indicted on February 28, 2002.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nola.com:80/news/t-p/frontpage/index.ssf?/newsstory/cmurder19.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030506160352/http://www.nola.com/news/t-p/frontpage/index.ssf?%2Fnewsstory%2Fcmurder19.html|archive-date=May 6, 2003|title=Rapper indicted in Harvey shooting|work=[[The Times-Picayune]]|location=New Orleans|author=Darby, Joe|date=March 1, 2002|access-date=June 11, 2017}}</ref> Judge Martha Sassone granted a new trial in April 2004 based on the claim that prosecutors improperly withheld criminal background information on three of their witnesses.{{citation needed|date=August 2020}}

On March 20, 2006, Miller was released on a $500,000 bond and placed under house arrest.<ref>{{cite news |author=Gil Kaufman |title = C-Murder Released From Prison, Placed On House Arrest|url = https://www.mtv.com/news/mclas7/c-murder-released-from-prison-placed-on-house-arrest|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20221002141140/https://www.mtv.com/news/mclas7/c-murder-released-from-prison-placed-on-house-arrest|url-status = dead|archive-date = October 2, 2022|work=MTV|date = March 21, 2006|access-date = March 18, 2024}}</ref> Sassone allowed Miller to promote his new, yet-to-be-titled CD and his novel, ''Death around the Corner'', while under house arrest, but ruled that a [[gag order]] pertaining to the case would remain in effect. The terms of the house arrest required Sassone's permission for all visitors, including reporters.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://infoweb.newsbank.com/resources/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info:sid/iw.newsbank.com:NewsBank:CPDB&rft_val_format=info:ofi/fmt:kev:mtx:ctx&rft_dat=117A0F3B27386F90&svc_dat=InfoWeb:aggregated5&req_dat=0D0CB579A3BDA420&p_openurl=NewsBank|title=Judge lets rapper promote CD, novel|author=Purpura, Paul|work=The Times-Picayune|location=New Orleans|date=March 2, 2007|access-date=June 16, 2017}}</ref>

On March 13, 2007, Sassone granted Miller's request to work on his music career on a per-request basis, but denied his request for a 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. curfew.<ref name="leave house">{{cite news|work=The Times-Picayune|location=New Orleans |date=March 13, 2007 |title=Rapper may leave house |url=http://infoweb.newsbank.com/resources/openurl?ctx_ver=z39.88-2004&rft_id=info:sid/iw.newsbank.com:NewsBank:CPDB&rft_val_format=info:ofi/fmt:kev:mtx:ctx&rft_dat=117E00401DD6AC00&svc_dat=InfoWeb:aggregated5&req_dat=0D0CB579A3BDA420&p_openurl=NewsBank |author=Purpura, Paul}}</ref> Sassone's rulings in the case became an issue in her failed 2008 bid for re-election. Sassone was defeated by Judge Ellen Kovach; prosecutors subsequently renewed a request to have Miller returned to jail.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nola.com/news/index.ssf/2009/08/rapper_being_retried_in_2002_k.html|title=C-Murder's retrial in 2002 killing set to open Monday|author=Purpura, Paul|work=The Times-Picayune|location=New Orleans|date=August 2, 2009|access-date=June 16, 2017}}</ref> During January 2009, Miller was confined to his residence on house arrest, and could only leave for a documented medical emergency.

On May 27, 2009, Miller pleaded [[Nolo contendere|no contest]] to two counts of attempted second degree murder. These charges stem from a 2001 incident in [[Baton Rouge]] in which Miller fired one shot, after which it jammed, from a semi-automatic pistol at the owner and bouncer of a night club who refused to allow Miller to enter the business with the gun. Miller was sentenced to ten years with credit for time served.<ref name="wafb">{{cite news|url=http://www.wafb.com/Global/story.asp?s=10431228|title=C-Murder pleads no contest to attempted murder|last=Gates|first=Paul|date=May 27, 2009|publisher=[[WAFB]]|access-date=August 27, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090612104725/http://www.wafb.com/Global/story.asp?s=10431228|archive-date=June 12, 2009}}</ref> A surveillance video of the incident was posted on [[YouTube]].{{citation needed|date=August 2020}}

[[File:LSPEntrance-.jpg|thumb|upright|The [[Louisiana State Penitentiary]] in November 2009]]

On August 5, 2009, the murder trial began. The father of the victim spoke of his son being a fan of C-Murder before the incident. A bouncer also testified against Miller, saying he witnessed the shooting. He expressed fear of repercussions for his testimony. Prosecutors also charged C-Murder's associates with [[witness tampering]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://allhiphop.com/stories/news/archive/2009/08/06/21882487.aspx|title=Bouncer Says C-Murder Guilty of Killing Teen|last=AbduSalaam|first=Ishmael|date=August 6, 2009|publisher=AllHipHop.com|access-date=August 27, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101129135231/http://allhiphop.com/stories/news/archive/2009/08/06/21882487.aspx|archive-date=November 29, 2010}}</ref>

On August 10, 2009, the jury reported being deadlocked, but Judge Hans Liljeberg instructed them to attempt to resolve the deadlock. Three hours later, the jury returned to announce it reached a 10–2 guilty verdict. The judge suspected that, given the deadlock announced earlier followed by the quick reversal, one of the jurors decided to switch under pressure to end the trial and instructed the jury to go back and deliberate on the case longer.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lin|first=C.J.|url=http://www.nola.com/news/index.ssf/2009/08/cmurder_verdict.html|title=C-Murder guilty verdict not valid, judge says, and sends jury back for more deliberations|work=The Times-Picayune|location=New Orleans|date=August 11, 2009|access-date=December 12, 2010}}</ref>

When they returned with the same 10–2 verdict, Miller was convicted of second-degree murder.<ref name="nola">{{cite news|url=http://www.nola.com/news/index.ssf/2009/08/cmurder_verdict_1.html|title=C-Murder guilty of second-degree murder after topsy-turvy jury action|last=Purpura|first=Paul|author2=Lin, C. J.|date=August 11, 2009|work=The Times-Picayune|location=New Orleans|access-date=August 27, 2009}}</ref> During sentencing, the victim's father said, "I'm not rejoicing. I feel bad for [Miller's] family. But at least they can see him. What have we got but a gravesite and a photograph?"<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.sky.com/skynews/Home/World-News/US-Rapper-Corey-C-Murder-Miller-Found-Guilty-Of-Second-Degree-Murder/Article/200908215359098?lpos=World_News_First_Home_Article_Teaser_Region_5&lid=ARTICLE_15359098_US_Rapper_Corey_C-Murder_Miller_Found_Guilty_Of_Second_Degree_Murder_|title= Rapper C-Murder Shot 16-Year-Old Fan In Club|date=August 12, 2009|publisher=[[Sky News]]|access-date=August 27, 2009}}</ref> C-Murder was sentenced on August 14 by District Judge Hans Liljeberg to mandatory life imprisonment.<ref name="auto"/>

On August 27, 2009, Ernest Johnson, president of the Louisiana [[NAACP]], requested an investigation into the jury deliberations.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nola.com/crime/index.ssf/2009/08/la_naacp_wants_state_supreme_c.html|title=C-Murder jury deliberation needs investigation, Louisiana NAACP president says|last=Purpura|first=Paul|date=August 27, 2009|work=The Times-Picayune|location=New Orleans|access-date=August 27, 2009}}</ref> C-Murder's financial woes reportedly landed him the help of two Harvard attorneys, one of them Ronald Sullivan, who have agreed to assist with his appeal. One of the jurors, Mary Jacob, said that both she and a fellow juror, a 20-year-old student at [[Xavier University of Louisiana]], were verbally abused by fellow jurors for their decision to acquit. According to Jacob, the abuse resulted in her switching her verdict, saying, "They literally made this 20-year-old girl so violently ill, she was shaking so bad. She ran into the bathroom. She was throwing her guts up. She couldn't function anymore. That's when I decided, the judge don't want to listen to me, doesn't want to listen to us? I told them, 'You want him to be guilty? He's guilty; now let's get the hell out of here.{{'"}} This account was partially confirmed by another juror. At the time, a 10–2 consensus was sufficient for conviction in Louisiana but a 9–3 consensus would result in a mistrial.<ref>{{cite news|title=C-Miller, rap star, kills a young fan|url=http://www.trutv.com/library/crime/notorious_murders/celebrity/corey_miller/32.html/|publisher=[[TruTV]]|date=August 14, 2009}}</ref>

On December 28, 2011, his conviction was upheld.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kunzelman|first=Michael|title=Rapper C-Murder's Conviction, Sentence Upheld|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/wireStory/rapper-murders-conviction-sentence-upheld-15255638#.Tv2EeymNr4s|work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]}}</ref>

On February 19, 2013, the Supreme Court rejected Miller v. Louisiana, which was Miller's final appeal of his conviction. After a jury voted 10–2 to convict Miller, Miller's attorneys argued that because federal juries must reach unanimous verdicts in criminal cases, Miller should have not been convicted in Louisiana.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.22985/title.supreme-court-rejects-c-murder-s-appeal-of-murder-conviction|title=Supreme Court Rejects C-Murder's Appeal Of Murder Conviction|publisher=HipHopDX.com|access-date=December 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130221162703/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.22985/title.supreme-court-rejects-c-murder-s-appeal-of-murder-conviction/|archive-date=February 21, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nola.com/crime/index.ssf/2013/02/supreme_court_rejects_appeal_f.html|title=Supreme Court rejects appeal from rapper C-Murder|newspaper=The Times-Picayine|location=New Orleans|access-date=December 12, 2017}}</ref>

On April 2, 2014, Miller's attorney, Rachel Conner, filed a [[post-conviction]] relief application in state court in [[Gretna, Louisiana|Gretna]]. She raised 10 points to support her assertion that her client received no fair trial. Conner said she plans to raise additional points. Primary among the assertions is what she described as irregularities during the jury's deliberations, stating, "One juror cast a guilty vote not based on the evidence but because she wanted to end deliberations to protect another juror who refused to convict Miller but was targeted by other jurors to change her mind, Conner wrote."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sohh.com/c-murder-says-this-cant-be-life-wants-another-shot-at-freedom/|title=C-Murder Says This Can't Be Life, Wants Another Shot At Freedom|date=April 2, 2014|publisher=Sohh.com|access-date=December 12, 2017|last1=Samuel|first1=S.|archive-date=December 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213010612/https://www.sohh.com/c-murder-says-this-cant-be-life-wants-another-shot-at-freedom/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://hiphopnews24-7.com/profiles/blogs/c-murder-seeks-new-trial-in-teen-s-death-saying-this-can-t-be-lif|title=TMZ BREAKING|publisher=HipHopNews24-7.com|access-date=December 12, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |url=http://www.hiphopweekly.com/c-murder-hopes-to-escape-prison-through-new-trial/ |title=C-Murder Hopes to Escape Prison Through New trial|magazine=Hip Hop Weekly |access-date=March 15, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402133856/http://www.hiphopweekly.com/c-murder-hopes-to-escape-prison-through-new-trial/ |archive-date=April 2, 2015 }}</ref>

In August 2021, Miller went on [[hunger strike]] to protest his conditions, which he feared would result in him getting [[COVID-19]], and the status of his trial, saying he believed the district attorney had withheld evidence.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wdsu.com/article/louisiana-rapper-c-murder-on-hunger-strike-over-covid-19-trial-evidence/37243934 |title=Louisiana rapper C-Murder on hunger strike over COVID-19, trial evidence |date=August 6, 2021 |website=[[WDSU]] |access-date=August 7, 2021}}</ref> That month, he hired civil rights attorney [[Benjamin Crump]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/361760-c-murder-adds-civil-rights-attorney-ben-crump-to-legal-counsel-news |title=C-Murder Adds Civil Rights Attorney Ben Crump To Legal Counsel |date=August 7, 2021 |website=Hot New Hip Hop |access-date=August 7, 2021}}</ref>

=== ''Investigation Discovery Reasonable Doubt'' ===
In June 2018, Miller's case was highlighted on an episode of ''Investigation Discovery Reasonable Doubt'', in which Kenneth Jordan recanted and discussed his false testimony.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nola.com/news/crime_police/article_2a24afd9-f3eb-5ca2-87b9-3bf5d25e66a8.html|title=C-Murder witness recants testimony that rapper fatally shot teen in Harvey nightclub|author=Michelle Hunter |newspaper=The Times-Picayune |date=June 26, 2018 |access-date=October 13, 2021}}</ref> Jordan stated he was pressured by detectives to testify against Miller or he himself would have faced a 10-year prison sentence for unrelated criminal charges.<ref name="auto1"/> On July 6, another witness, Darnell Jordan, recanted his testimony, saying he was detained and locked in a hotel room by the police for refusing to testify against Miller.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/c-note-shooting-murder-witness-tricked-testimony/|title=Second Witness Says Detectives 'Tricked' Him Into Identifying C-Murder in Nightclub Shooting|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date= July 7, 2018}}</ref>

C-Murder.text:
Corey Miller (born March 9, 1971), better known by his stage name C-Murder, is an American rapper. He initially gained fame in the mid-1990s as a part of his brother Master P's label No Limit Records, primarily as a member of the label's supergroup, TRU. Miller went on to release several solo albums of his own through the label, including 1998's platinum Life or Death. C-Murder has released nine albums altogether on six different labels, No Limit Records, TRU Records, Koch Records, Asylum Records, RBC Records, and Venti Uno.
In 2002, Miller was arrested in connection with the murder of 16-year-old Steve Thomas, and was sentenced to life in prison on August 14, 2009. Miller is serving his sentence at the Louisiana State Penitentiary. Controversy surrounding witnesses involved in Miller's trial came to light in 2018 when two key witnesses recanted their statements, stating they had been pressured into testifying against Miller by authorities. Miller maintains his innocence, and he, his brothers, and his nephew have all called for a new trial numerous times.


== Early life ==
Corey Miller was born in Uptown New Orleans, Louisiana on March 9, 1971. He grew up in the Calliope Projects in the 3rd Ward of New Orleans with his sister Germaine, and brothers Silkk the Shocker and Master P and Kevin Miller.


== Military service ==
After graduating from high school, Corey Miller enlisted in the United States Army. He served as a combat medic and was deployed to the Persian Gulf during the Gulf War.


== Music career ==
In 1998, Miller released his first album Life or Death which peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200 and was eventually certified platinum.  He also was featured on the theme for the nWo Wolfpac.
In 1999, he released Bossalinie which peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and was certified gold.
In 2000, he released Trapped in Crime which peaked at No. 9 on the Billboard 200. The album included the single "Down for My N's"
In 2001, he released C-P-3.com, his last album with No Limit Records. It peaked at No. 45 on the Billboard 200 and included the singles "What U Gonna Do" and "Im Not Just".
In 2003, he was convicted of the murder of fan Steve Thomas. He recorded three hit albums while under house arrest awaiting re-trial: The Truest Shit I Ever Said (2005) which reached No. 41 on the Billboard 200, Screamin' 4 Vengeance (2008) which reached No. 130, and Calliope Click (2009) which peaked at No. 68 on the Billboard R&B Albums chart.
In 2009, he lost his appeal and pleaded no contest to two counts of attempted murder in an unrelated incident. While in prison he self-released a mixtape Ricochet (2013) and four albums, Tomorrow (2010), Ain't No Heaven in the Pen (2015), Give Me Freedom Or Give Me Death (2021), and the compilation Oldies but Goodies (2018).
In 2016, he released a diss track accusing rapper 2 Chainz of using the slogan and name style of his former group TRU and record label TRU Global Records.


== Other ventures ==
Miller acted in the No Limit films Da Game of Life, I Got the Hook-Up, and Hot Boyz. He is the author of the novel Death Around The Corner, published by Vibe.


== Legal issues ==


=== Steve Thomas case ===
In September 2003, Miller was convicted of second degree murder in connection with the January 12, 2002 beating and fatal shooting of a fan, 16-year-old Steve Thomas, at the Platinum Club, a now-closed nightclub in Harvey, Louisiana. Miller was arrested in the early hours of January 18 for causing a disturbance at the House of Blues in New Orleans, and shortly after charged in Thomas' murder. He was indicted on February 28, 2002. Judge Martha Sassone granted a new trial in April 2004 based on the claim that prosecutors improperly withheld criminal background information on three of their witnesses.
On March 20, 2006, Miller was released on a $500,000 bond and placed under house arrest. Sassone allowed Miller to promote his new, yet-to-be-titled CD and his novel, Death around the Corner, while under house arrest, but ruled that a gag order pertaining to the case would remain in effect. The terms of the house arrest required Sassone's permission for all visitors, including reporters.
On March 13, 2007, Sassone granted Miller's request to work on his music career on a per-request basis, but denied his request for a 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. curfew. Sassone's rulings in the case became an issue in her failed 2008 bid for re-election. Sassone was defeated by Judge Ellen Kovach; prosecutors subsequently renewed a request to have Miller returned to jail. During January 2009, Miller was confined to his residence on house arrest, and could only leave for a documented medical emergency.
On May 27, 2009, Miller pleaded no contest to two counts of attempted second degree murder. These charges stem from a 2001 incident in Baton Rouge in which Miller fired one shot, after which it jammed, from a semi-automatic pistol at the owner and bouncer of a night club who refused to allow Miller to enter the business with the gun. Miller was sentenced to ten years with credit for time served. A surveillance video of the incident was posted on YouTube.

On August 5, 2009, the murder trial began. The father of the victim spoke of his son being a fan of C-Murder before the incident. A bouncer also testified against Miller, saying he witnessed the shooting. He expressed fear of repercussions for his testimony. Prosecutors also charged C-Murder's associates with witness tampering.
On August 10, 2009, the jury reported being deadlocked, but Judge Hans Liljeberg instructed them to attempt to resolve the deadlock. Three hours later, the jury returned to announce it reached a 10–2 guilty verdict. The judge suspected that, given the deadlock announced earlier followed by the quick reversal, one of the jurors decided to switch under pressure to end the trial and instructed the jury to go back and deliberate on the case longer.
When they returned with the same 10–2 verdict, Miller was convicted of second-degree murder. During sentencing, the victim's father said, "I'm not rejoicing. I feel bad for [Miller's] family. But at least they can see him. What have we got but a gravesite and a photograph?" C-Murder was sentenced on August 14 by District Judge Hans Liljeberg to mandatory life imprisonment.
On August 27, 2009, Ernest Johnson, president of the Louisiana NAACP, requested an investigation into the jury deliberations. C-Murder's financial woes reportedly landed him the help of two Harvard attorneys, one of them Ronald Sullivan, who have agreed to assist with his appeal. One of the jurors, Mary Jacob, said that both she and a fellow juror, a 20-year-old student at Xavier University of Louisiana, were verbally abused by fellow jurors for their decision to acquit. According to Jacob, the abuse resulted in her switching her verdict, saying, "They literally made this 20-year-old girl so violently ill, she was shaking so bad. She ran into the bathroom. She was throwing her guts up. She couldn't function anymore. That's when I decided, the judge don't want to listen to me, doesn't want to listen to us? I told them, 'You want him to be guilty? He's guilty; now let's get the hell out of here.'" This account was partially confirmed by another juror. At the time, a 10–2 consensus was sufficient for conviction in Louisiana but a 9–3 consensus would result in a mistrial.
On December 28, 2011, his conviction was upheld.
On February 19, 2013, the Supreme Court rejected Miller v. Louisiana, which was Miller's final appeal of his conviction. After a jury voted 10–2 to convict Miller, Miller's attorneys argued that because federal juries must reach unanimous verdicts in criminal cases, Miller should have not been convicted in Louisiana.
On April 2, 2014, Miller's attorney, Rachel Conner, filed a post-conviction relief application in state court in Gretna. She raised 10 points to support her assertion that her client received no fair trial. Conner said she plans to raise additional points. Primary among the assertions is what she described as irregularities during the jury's deliberations, stating, "One juror cast a guilty vote not based on the evidence but because she wanted to end deliberations to protect another juror who refused to convict Miller but was targeted by other jurors to change her mind, Conner wrote."
In August 2021, Miller went on hunger strike to protest his conditions, which he feared would result in him getting COVID-19, and the status of his trial, saying he believed the district attorney had withheld evidence. That month, he hired civil rights attorney Benjamin Crump.


=== Investigation Discovery Reasonable Doubt ===
In June 2018, Miller's case was highlighted on an episode of Investigation Discovery Reasonable Doubt, in which Kenneth Jordan recanted and discussed his false testimony. Jordan stated he was pressured by detectives to testify against Miller or he himself would have faced a 10-year prison sentence for unrelated criminal charges. On July 6, another witness, Darnell Jordan, recanted his testimony, saying he was detained and locked in a hotel room by the police for refusing to testify against Miller.

List of X-Men film series cast members.text:
The following is a list of cast members who have portrayed characters appearing in 20th Century Fox's X-Men film series, based upon the Marvel Comics superhero team of the same name and its related characters.
The first three films in the series are X-Men (2000), X2 (2003), and X-Men: The Last Stand (2006), starring Hugh Jackman as James "Logan" Howlett / Wolverine, Patrick Stewart as Charles Xavier / Professor X, Ian McKellen as Erik Lehnsherr / Magneto, Famke Janssen as Jean Grey, Halle Berry as Ororo Munroe / Storm, Anna Paquin as Marie D'Ancanto / Rogue, James Marsden as Scott Summers / Cyclops, Shawn Ashmore as Bobby Drake / Iceman, and Rebecca Romijn as Raven Darkhölme / Mystique. Daniel Cudmore portrays Piotr Rasputin / Colossus in the last two films, while Elliot Page and Kelsey Grammer star as Kitty Pryde and Hank McCoy / Beast, respectively, in the latter. Jackman also stars in a trilogy of films centered on Wolverine, consisting of X-Men Origins: Wolverine (2009), The Wolverine (2013), and Logan (2017), where he is joined by Stewart as Xavier.
James McAvoy, Michael Fassbender, Jennifer Lawrence, and Nicholas Hoult star in X-Men: First Class (2011) as younger versions of Xavier, Lehnsherr, Darkhölme, and McCoy, respectively, while Lucas Till appears as Alex Summers / Havok. X-Men: Days of Future Past (2014) features both the original cast (except for Romijn) and the new actors, while also introducing Evan Peters as Peter Maximoff / Quicksilver. McAvoy, Fassbender, Lawrence, Hoult, Till, and Peters reprise their roles in X-Men: Apocalypse (2016), where Sophie Turner, Tye Sheridan, Kodi Smit-McPhee, and Alexandra Shipp portray younger versions of Grey, Scott Summers, Kurt Wagner / Nightcrawler, and Munroe. Except for Till, all new actors return in Dark Phoenix (2019).
Ryan Reynolds portrays Wade Wilson in X-Men Origins: Wolverine before starring as a new version of the character in the titular role in Deadpool (2016), which also features a new version of Colossus played by Stefan Kapičić, replacing Cudmore. Reynolds reprises his role in the short film No Good Deed (2017), and in Deadpool 2 (2018), in which Kapičić also reprises his role. Maisie Williams, Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Heaton, Blu Hunt, and Henry Zaga star as the titular team members Rahne Sinclair, Illyana Rasputin, Samuel Guthrie, Danielle Moonstar, and Roberto da Costa in The New Mutants (2020).
Reynolds, Jackman, Kapičić, Morena Baccarin, Rob Delaney, Brianna Hildebrand, Dafne Keen, Shioli Kutsuna, Tyler Mane, Karan Soni, Aaron Stanford, Lewis Tan, and Leslie Uggams reprise their respective roles in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) media franchise; the film Deadpool & Wolverine (2024) serves as a sequel to the Deadpool films.

|[[Clapton, London|Clapton]], London

A passenger then dismounted and shot him several times.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Thompson|first=Tony|title=Two more die on 'murder mile'|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2001/apr/22/tonythompson.theobserver1|website=The Guardian|date=22 April 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125104432/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2001/apr/22/tonythompson.theobserver1|archive-date=25 January 2021|access-date=7 September 2021}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>
|-
|July 2000
|Mark Corley
|Near [[Bolam, County Durham|Bolam]], County Durham
|Corley, a 23-year-old from [[Grantham]] in Lincolnshire, disappeared on 7 July 2000, and his remains were discovered in a rural area of County Durham in December. He had been shot in the head. Five men were due to go on trial in early 2002, but a judge called off the trial after finding that police had unlawfully bugged conversations between those men and their solicitors.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Murder trial five freed over police bugging|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2002/jan/30/3|website=The Guardian|date=30 January 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221018141040/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2002/jan/30/3|archive-date=18 October 2022|access-date=10 January 2021}}</ref>
|-
|July 2000
|Iwona Kaminska
|Body not found
|Kaminska, a 20-year-old Polish woman, disappeared after leaving her workplace in [[Hammersmith]], London, on 13 July 2000,<ref>{{Cite news|title=Emotional appeal for Iwona's return|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6469660.emotional-appeal-for-iwonas-return/|work=News Shopper|date=28 July 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250529211842/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6469660.emotional-appeal-for-iwonas-return/|archive-date=29 May 2025|access-date=29 May 2025}}</ref> and investigators came to believe she had been murdered.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Information about missing Iwona Kamińska who disappeared in July 2000|url=https://www.met.police.uk/foi-ai/metropolitan-police/d/february-2022/information-about-missing-iwona-kamiska-who-disappeared-in-july2000/|website=Metropolitan Police|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241013034721/https://www.met.police.uk/foi-ai/metropolitan-police/d/february-2022/information-about-missing-iwona-kamiska-who-disappeared-in-july2000/|archive-date=13 October 2024|access-date=29 May 2025}}</ref> Two other young women had disappeared from the street in [[Ealing]] four miles away over the previous 15 months,<ref name=Independent/> and Polish serial sex offender and suspected serial killer [[Andrzej Kunowski]], who died in 2009 and, in 1997, had murdered a 12-year-old girl near where Kaminska was last seen, was to become the prime suspect in those cases.<ref name=Journal/>
|-
|July 2000
|Beatrice Wilson
|[[Poole]], Dorset
|74-year-old Wilson was knifed to death in her sheltered accommodation on 21 July 2000. A boy who was 15 at the time of the killing was charged with her murder. The prosecution claimed at the subsequent trial that he killed Wilson while burgling her flat and later confessed to a friend.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Boy 'slit pensioner's throat', court hears|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/1917479.stm|work=BBC News|date=8 April 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200915204447/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/1917479.stm|archive-date=15 September 2020|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref> The jury acquitted him.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Son's plea to reopen Beatrice murder case|url=https://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/news/5413709.sons-plea-to-reopen-beatrice-murder-case/|work=Dorset Echo|date=18 March 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200915204725/https://www.dorsetecho.co.uk/news/5413709.sons-plea-to-reopen-beatrice-murder-case/|archive-date=15 September 2020|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref>
|-
|August 2000
|Jonathan Bristow
|[[Sheerness]], Kent
|39-year-old Bristow was last seen as he left a pub in [[Chatham, Kent|Chatham]], Kent, on 4 August 2000. His body was discovered floating in the [[River Medway]] a week later, having separated from weights that had been attached to keep it down. He had been shot in the head.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bennetto|first=Jason|title=Who lured Mr Nice Guy to his death then dumped his body?|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/this-britain/who-lured-mr-nice-guy-to-his-death-then-dumped-his-body-710868.html|website=The Independent|date=29 August 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706170539/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/this-britain/who-lured-mr-nice-guy-to-his-death-then-dumped-his-body-710868.html|archive-date=6 July 2022|access-date=30 January 2026}}</ref> Although Bristow was believed to have had over £20,000 in cash on him and police thought it could have been accumulated through drugs or bootlegging, it was also acknowledged that they had not found any evidence of illegal dealings on his part.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police try to break 'wall of silence'|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/1043160.stm|website=BBC News|date=27 November 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130175027/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/1043160.stm|archive-date=30 January 2026|access-date=30 January 2026}}</ref>
|-
|August 2000
|Paul Rogers
|Liverpool
|27-year-old Rogers was shot at his flat near [[Liverpool Cathedral]] by an intruder wearing a mask resembling the one in the film ''[[Scream (1996 film)|Scream]]'' on 5 August 2000. The intruder had an accomplice, and Rogers, shot in front of his nine-year-old son, died the next day. A woman had let the culprits in through a communal door after suggesting to them that they rob Rogers because she had had a dispute with him over a bicycle. She was jailed for conspiracy to rob in November 2001, though the judge passing the four-year sentence accepted that she had not been aware that either of the culprits was going to be armed with a gun or kill their victim.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Roughley|first=Lynda|title=STUDENT JAILED OVER ROBBERY; VICTIM KILLED IN FRONT OF SON|url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/STUDENT+JAILED+OVER+ROBBERY%3B+VICTIM+KILLED+IN+FRONT+OF+SON.-a079930960|website=The Free Library|date=10 November 2001|access-date=29 May 2026}}</ref>
|-
|August 2000
|Greg Watson
|Attacked in [[North Kensington]], London, died in hospital
|21-year-old Watson was knifed in Kensal Road on 28 August 2000 when his female cousin was accosted and he tried to defuse the situation. He died soon after the nighttime stabbing, which ''[[Crimewatch]]'' later showed low-quality CCTV footage of and which occurred at the time of the [[Notting Hill Carnival]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Carnival murder footage released|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/967787.stm|website=BBC News|date=11 October 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205232220/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/967787.stm|archive-date=5 February 2022|access-date=5 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Greg Watson|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2065|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230617211543/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2065|archive-date=17 June 2023|access-date=17 June 2023}}</ref>
|-
|August 2000
|Ronald Fuller
|Attacked in [[Grays, Essex|Grays]], died in hospital in Basildon (both in Essex)
|30-year-old Fuller was shot twice in the head and twice in the chest outside his bungalow on 29 August 2000 by a man who left the scene on a motor scooter.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police hunt L-plate gunman|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/901482.stm|website=BBC News|date=29 August 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200915211338/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/901482.stm|archive-date=15 September 2020|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Grays: Woman's terror at gun slaying|url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/5478199.grays-womans-terror-at-gun-slaying/|website=Daily Gazette|date=23 November 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200915205512/https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/5478199.grays-womans-terror-at-gun-slaying/|archive-date=15 September 2020|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref>
|-
|August 2000
|Abdul Bhatti
|Attacked in [[Notting Hill]], London, died in hospital
|28-year-old Bhatti was punched and kicked at the Notting Hill Carnival at around 7:30 p.m. on 28 August 2000 after intervening when a friend was being assaulted by a mob, and died on the evening of 29 August.<ref>{{Cite web|title='RACIST MOB' KILLED ASIAN|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6461073.racist-mob-killed-asian/|website=News Shopper|date=6 September 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205232212/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6461073.racist-mob-killed-asian/|archive-date=5 February 2022|access-date=5 February 2022}}</ref> Nine men were jailed for taking part in the violence that culminated in the fatal attack, but no one has been convicted of Bhatti's murder.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cheston|first=Paul|title=Gang jailed for carnival rampage|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/hp/front/gang-jailed-for-carnival-rampage-6303924.html|website=Evening Standard|date=2 May 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160913065356/https://www.standard.co.uk/news/gang-jailed-for-carnival-rampage-6303924.html|archive-date=13 September 2016|access-date=5 February 2022}}</ref>
|-
|September 2000
|Susan Kelly
|[[Liverpool]]
|38-year-old Kelly was a sex worker in Liverpool when she was murdered on the night of 3–4 September 2000. Her body was found in an alley off Blessington Road, [[Anfield (suburb)|Anfield]], and she had suffered a number of violent injuries, including a cut throat, six broken ribs and a broken nose. A man was cleared of Kelly's murder in 2003 and others have since been arrested and released.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police probe Crossbow Cannibal links to Merseyside murders|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/police-probe-crossbow-cannibal-links-3404019|website=Liverpool Echo|date=14 June 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214162107/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/police-probe-crossbow-cannibal-links-3404019|archive-date=14 December 2019|access-date=14 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Man arrested over murder of Liverpool woman Susan Kelly in 2000|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-merseyside-18264043|website=BBC News|date=30 May 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160320053014/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-merseyside-18264043|archive-date=20 March 2016|access-date=14 December 2019}}</ref>
|-
|September 2000
|Clifford Clarke
|[[Uppingham]], [[Rutland]]
|56-year-old Clarke, a former plumber and hospital porter, was stabbed in the chest and neck, and it was noted at his inquest that the attack could have occurred between two and four days prior to his body being found in his flat by his brother on 10 September 2000.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police re-open murder inquiry after 15 years|url=https://www.stamfordmercury.co.uk/news/police-re-open-murder-inquiry-after-15-years-1-6819769/|website=Rutland & Stamford Mercury|date=26 June 2015|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200102205830/https://www.stamfordmercury.co.uk/news/police-re-open-murder-inquiry-after-15-years-1-6819769/|archive-date=2 January 2020|access-date=2 January 2020}}</ref> Two men were arrested in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Clifford Clarke murder: Men arrested after 15 years|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leicestershire-33315077|website=BBC News|date=29 June 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220419222515/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-leicestershire-33315077|archive-date=19 April 2022|access-date=2 January 2020}}</ref>
|-
|September 2000
|Thomas Ramsey
|Manchester
|16-year-old Ramsey was shot twice – once in the head, once in the neck – in a park in [[Levenshulme]], Manchester, on 19 September 2000.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Teenager gunned down in park|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/teenager-gunned-down-in-park-1197724|website=Manchester Evening News|date=20 September 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711180815/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/teenager-gunned-down-in-park-1197724|archive-date=11 July 2021|access-date=11 July 2021}}</ref> His crime boss was acquitted of his murder but convicted of the murder of a man from another gang.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Day|first=Rebecca|title=Woman tied naked to radiator during two years of hell at hands of gangster ex|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/woman-tied-naked-radiator-during-14181763|website=Mirror Online|date=25 March 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711213353/https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/woman-tied-naked-radiator-during-14181763|archive-date=11 July 2021|access-date=11 July 2021}}</ref> Ramsey had been acquitted himself of the October 1999 murder of Judah Dewar – a murder linked to Ramsey due to the discovery of one of his fingerprints at the scene.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Teenager 'executed in revenge'|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/teenager-executed-in-revenge-1197740|website=Manchester Evening News|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711181133/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/teenager-executed-in-revenge-1197740|archive-date=11 July 2021|access-date=11 July 2021}}</ref>
|-
|September 2000
|Vicky Glass
|[[Danby, North Yorkshire|Danby]], North Yorkshire
|21-year-old Glass went missing from [[Middlesbrough]] town centre on 24 September 2000. Her body was found 20 miles away in a stream on the [[North York Moors]] approximately six weeks later. Glass was a sex worker at the time of her death. In 2018, a specialist police team was set up to revisit the murders of Glass, [[Donna Keogh]] and Rachel Wilson. A [[Home Office]] review of all three cases said: "It is generally accepted that initial enquiries and investigations were inadequate."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Corrigan|first=Naomi|title=Detectives in new appeal for help in finding Vicky Glass' killer ahead of 40th birthday|url=https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/news/teesside-news/detectives-new-appeal-help-finding-16954991|website=Teesside Live|date=20 September 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191114201711/https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/news/teesside-news/detectives-new-appeal-help-finding-16954991|archive-date=14 November 2019|access-date=29 November 2019}}</ref> [[Cleveland Police]] believe there could be a link to serial prostitute killer [[Steve Wright (serial killer)|Steve Wright]], whose known victims were all found in streams or near water.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Addley|first1=Esther|last2=McVeigh|first2=Karen|title=Motive still unknown as serial killer faces rest of life in prison|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2008/feb/22/suffolkmurders.ukcrime|website=The Guardian|date=22 February 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170516163148/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2008/feb/22/suffolkmurders.ukcrime|archive-date=16 May 2017|access-date=21 September 2021}}</ref> In September 2021, police announced a re-investigation by a historical crimes unit into Glass's murder. This announcement came two months after Wright's arrest for another historical murder: that of Victoria Hall in 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Evans|first=Martin|title=Exclusive: Suffolk Strangler Steve Wright arrested over unsolved murder of 17-year-old Victoria Hall|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/07/29/exclusive-suffolk-strangler-steve-wright-arrested-unsolved-murder/|website=The Telegraph|date=29 July 2021|issn=0307-1235|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210729161915/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/07/29/exclusive-suffolk-strangler-steve-wright-arrested-unsolved-murder/|archive-date=29 July 2021|access-date=29 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Davies|first=Caroline|title=Police to re-examine unsolved UK murder case after 21 years|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/sep/24/police-to-re-examine-unsolved-uk-case-after-21-years-vicky-glass|website=The Guardian|date=24 September 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924112019/https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/sep/24/police-to-re-examine-unsolved-uk-case-after-21-years-vicky-glass|archive-date=24 September 2021|access-date=24 September 2021}}</ref>
|-
|October 2000
|[[Murder of Alan Decabral|Alan Decabral]]
|[[Ashford, Kent|Ashford]], Kent
|40-year-old Decabral was shot dead on 5 October as he sat in the passenger seat of a car in a busy car park. It happened six months after he gave evidence that helped convict [[Kenneth Noye]] of a fatal road-rage attack, and the idea that the gunman was acting on Noye's orders was considered. However, it has also been noted by detectives investigating the case that the shooting could have been carried out because of a disagreement with an associate in the criminal world.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Williams|first=Sam|title=Murder of Alan Decabral, who gave evidence against Kenneth Noye, still being investigated|url=https://www.kentonline.co.uk/ashford/news/case-still-open-in-noye-witness-murder-205440/|work=KentOnline|date=28 May 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190528071934/https://www.kentonline.co.uk/ashford/news/case-still-open-in-noye-witness-murder-205440/|archive-date=28 May 2019|access-date=29 December 2020}}</ref>
|-
|October 2000
|Raymond Isaacs
|Attacked in [[Hounslow]], London, died in hospital
|Isaacs, 21, was set upon by about 10 people after leaving a Hounslow café on 16 October 2000. He was punched, kicked, stabbed in the leg, and fatally stabbed in the heart. Some of those people were found guilty of offences relating to the incident, but nobody has been found guilty of Isaacs's killing.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ashford|first=Jenny|title=Raymond Isaacs|url=https://crimeimmemorial.com/2024/03/18/raymond-isaacs/|website=Crime Immemorial|date=18 March 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250827214238/https://crimeimmemorial.com/2024/03/18/raymond-isaacs/|archive-date=27 August 2025|access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref>
|-
|October 2000
|Clay Benjamin
|Liverpool
|24-year-old Benjamin was stabbed in the heart while at a blues party in [[Toxteth]] on 21 October 2000. A man in his 30s was cleared of his murder.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Carter|first=Helen|title=Girl, 6, shot in gang feud|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2003/nov/04/ukguns.helencarter|work=The Guardian|date=4 November 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226002007/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2003/nov/04/ukguns.helencarter|archive-date=26 December 2024|access-date=22 May 2021}}</ref>

|October/November 2000
|Manokumar Kumar
|[[Edmonton, London|Edmonton]], London
|31-year-old Kumar's arm was almost severed in a fatal axe attack at his home on North Road, Edmonton, at some point between 29 October and 1 November 2000. Described as a gangster, he and a man who was to be charged with his murder had been using stolen credit cards to buy things at petrol stations. When that man was on trial, the prosecution advanced the theory that the attack had been committed because the two had fallen out over their fraudulent activities, but the trial was halted and the man had the charges against him dropped.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Manokumar Kumar|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2096|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725222040/https://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2096|archive-date=25 July 2025|access-date=25 July 2025}}</ref>

|November 2000
|Kenneth Beagle
|[[Romford]], London
|55-year-old Beagle was from [[Billericay]] in Essex and had convictions for drug dealing and kidnapping. He was shot in the head at point-blank range while paying for a parking ticket in the car park of a hospital in Romford at about 10:05 p.m. on 1 November 2000, and was thought to have gone there after taking a telephone call made solely for the purpose of luring him to the spot to kill him.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Billericay, Romford: Shooting witness pleas renewed|url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/5501272.billericay-romford-shooting-witness-pleas-renewed/|website=Daily Gazette|date=9 November 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241228224447/https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/5501272.billericay-romford-shooting-witness-pleas-renewed/|archive-date=28 December 2024|access-date=28 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Billericay, Romford: Call lured man to killers|url=https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/5493069.billericay-romford-call-lured-man-to-killers/|website=Daily Gazette|date=29 March 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241228224855/https://www.gazette-news.co.uk/news/5493069.billericay-romford-call-lured-man-to-killers/|archive-date=28 December 2024|access-date=28 December 2024}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>
|-
|November 2000
|Wade Hewitt
|Attacked in [[Barking, London|Barking]], London, died in hospital
|26-year-old Hewitt was stabbed in the abdomen when two youths approached him on the upper deck of a bus travelling through Barking in the early hours of 3 November 2000. The youths then alighted and ran off, and Hewitt died the following day.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Can you help catch bus killers?|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6445309.can-you-help-catch-bus-killers/|website=News Shopper|date=9 November 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250116213220/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6445309.can-you-help-catch-bus-killers/|archive-date=16 January 2025|access-date=16 January 2025}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>
|-
|November 2000
|Garfield Nandram
|Attacked in [[Tottenham]], London, died in hospital
|27-year-old Nandram, a hairdresser from [[Stamford Hill]], was shot once in the face in Croydon House just before 10 p.m. on 5 November 2000.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Killing will not affect estate|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6445435.killing-will-not-affect-estate/|website=News Shopper|date=9 November 2000|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250921173407/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6445435.killing-will-not-affect-estate/|archive-date=21 September 2025|access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>

|November 2000
|Steve Jindu
|[[Greenford]], London
|25-year-old Jindu, a warehouse driver, was found stabbed to death on Horsenden Hill on 14 November 2000. He had last been seen three days previously, when he visited a wine bar in [[Ealing]] by himself and went outside to use his mobile phone several times whilst at the establishment.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Murder hunt: fresh appeal|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6286643.murder-hunt-fresh-appeal/|website=News Shopper|date=7 November 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719213212/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6286643.murder-hunt-fresh-appeal/|archive-date=19 July 2024|access-date=19 July 2024}}</ref>
|-
|November 2000
|Vincent Clay
|[[Salford]], Greater Manchester
|Two men shot 27-year-old Clay while he was talking to his girlfriend in Amersham Street, Salford, on 14 November 2000. The victim had been charged with leading a prison riot and acquitted in 1999 of an attempted murder with a [[samurai sword]]. A man was put on trial for Clay's murder, it being claimed that he had taken part in the crime in revenge for Clay stealing his car, but the court was informed on the second day of the hearing that the prosecution would not be offering any more evidence.<ref>{{Cite web|title='Hail of bullets' street murder trial collapses|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/hail-of-bullets-street-murder-trial-1187921|website=Manchester Evening News|date=17 February 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205230147/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/hail-of-bullets-street-murder-trial-1187921|archive-date=5 February 2022|access-date=5 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Unsolved Murder: Shootings around Greater Manchester|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/unsolved-murder-shootings-around-greater-862448|website=Manchester Evening News|date=7 June 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151017022505/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/unsolved-murder-shootings-around-greater-862448|archive-date=17 October 2015|access-date=5 February 2022}}</ref>

|December 2000
|[[Murder of Zoe Parker|Zoe Parker]]
|Chelsea Harbour, [[River Thames]], London
|24-year-old Parker was last seen with two men in [[Hounslow]], west London, on 6 December 2000. She had learning difficulties and no fixed address, staying with friends and at hostels in various places such as [[London]], [[Colchester]] and [[Bournemouth]]. Parker was known to engage in sex work. Shortly before her death she changed her name to Cathy Dennis.<ref name=Parker>{{Cite web|last=Branigan|first=Tania|title=Police reveal chaotic life of murder victim|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2001/feb/14/taniabranigan|website=The Guardian|date=13 February 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140510131019/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2001/feb/14/taniabranigan|archive-date=10 May 2014|access-date=30 November 2019}}</ref>

The upper part of Parker's body was discovered in the River Thames on 17 December; her body had been sawn in half before being dumped in the river, and it is not known what happened to the lower half.<ref name=Parker/> Police suspect she could have been a victim of [[Anthony Hardy]] (the "Camden Ripper"), who dismembered his known victims after killing them in a nearby area between January and December 2002.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Bourgoin|first=Stéphane|year=2015|title=La Bible du crime|language=French|publisher=MARTINIERE BL|page=401}}</ref>

|December 2000
|Anthony Rose-Windon
|[[Clapton, London|Clapton]], London
|25-year-old Rose-Windon was shot after leaving a nightclub on Lower Clapton Road, Clapton, on 16 December 2000, and died after crawling to neighbouring Kenninghall Road.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Anthony Rose-Windon|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=405&termRef=Anthony%20Rose-Windon|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319214658/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=405&termRef=Anthony%20Rose-Windon|archive-date=19 March 2023|access-date=19 March 2023}}</ref>

|December 2000
|Douglas McPherson
|Attacked in [[Hackney, London|Hackney]], London, died in hospital
|42-year-old McPherson died four days after a Boxing Day attack in which he was battered with a baseball bat in the London Tavern when four men wearing balaclavas entered the Hackney pub. A man who was evicted from there earlier that day for hogging the punch was arraigned on a murder charge for allegedly being one of the assailant's accomplices. Only one witness could place him at the crime scene, however, and his mother – a judo expert – testified that she was holding him down at home at the time of the beating to prevent him from going back out to cause further trouble. The defendant was cleared and claimed that his missing half-brother was involved in the killing.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Boxing Day murder suspect leaves court as a free man|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6392190.boxing-day-murder-suspect-leaves-court-as-a-free-man/|website=News Shopper|date=19 October 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240428201202/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6392190.boxing-day-murder-suspect-leaves-court-as-a-free-man/|archive-date=28 April 2024|access-date=28 April 2024}}</ref>

|January 2001
|Andrew Williams
|[[Peckham]], London
|On 29 January 2001, 30-year-old Williams was killed in Peckham and a friend was seriously injured there in an early hours street shooting preceded by an altercation with a group of other men. The victims had just left a nightclub in the vicinity when the trouble began.<ref name=SouthwarkNews>{{Cite news|last=Pugh|first=Oliver|title=UNSOLVED|url=http://www.southwarknews.co.uk/00,news,19759,185,00.htm|work=Southwark News|date=10 June 2010|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140603001633/http://www.southwarknews.co.uk/00,news,19759,185,00.htm|archive-date=3 June 2014|access-date=4 August 2020}}</ref>

|February 2001
|Akbal Brar
|Attacked in [[Hayes, Hillingdon|Hayes]], London, died in hospital
|On 3 February 2001, 21-year-old Brar was in his parked car with a male friend in the passenger seat when a man appeared suddenly on foot and shot him after the passenger had started talking to another unknown man. No motive behind the incident was established.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Ashford|first=Jenny|title=Akbal Brar|url=https://crimeimmemorial.com/2025/04/11/akbal-brar/|website=Crime Immemorial|date=11 April 2025|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251107221355/https://crimeimmemorial.com/2025/04/11/akbal-brar/|archive-date=7 November 2025|access-date=7 November 2025}}</ref>

|February 2001
|Peter Beaumont-Gowling
|Newcastle
|Beaumont-Gowling was shot dead in a Valentine's Day attack at his flat in [[Jesmond]] not long after serving a prison sentence for money laundering. Two suspects caught on CCTV were never identified. A theory developed that the 52-year-old was killed for refusing to compensate people for money not received as a consequence of over £500,000 in drug money being seized when he was arrested.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Doughty|first=Sophie|title=Murderous Valentine's Day: A look back at the unsolved slaying of Peter Beaumont-Gowling|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/north-east-news/peter-beaumont-gowling-jesmond-murder-15815997|work=Chronicle Live|date=14 February 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190215114547/https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/north-east-news/peter-beaumont-gowling-jesmond-murder-15815997|archive-date=15 February 2019|access-date=3 December 2020}}</ref>

|March 2001
|Ian Dowling
|[[Grantham]], Lincolnshire
|39-year-old Dowling, a road maintenance worker, was shot in the heart and lungs on the doorstep of his home in Grantham on 15 March 2001. In 2003, his lover's husband was imprisoned for conspiracy to murder after standing accused of recruiting contract killers, but in 2005, judges at the Appeal Court deemed his conviction unsafe and quashed it because police had bugged conversations between him and his solicitor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Two in court over shooting|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/1103718.stm|website=BBC News|date=16 June 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250731190451/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/1103718.stm|archive-date=31 July 2025|access-date=31 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Husband cleared of plot to kill|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/lincolnshire/4513115.stm|website=BBC News|date=4 May 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250731190807/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/lincolnshire/4513115.stm|archive-date=31 July 2025|access-date=31 July 2025}}</ref>
|-
|March 2001
|David Williamson
|Attacked in North Yorkshire, died in hospital in Leeds
|On 26 March 2001, 58-year-old Williamson was found unconscious with a fractured skull a few hundred yards from his home in [[Sutton-on-the-Forest]] after he was struck from behind with a blunt instrument following a visit to a pub at nearby [[Huby, Hambleton|Huby]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fresh appeal in Williamson investigation|url=https://www.gazetteherald.co.uk/news/6662606.fresh-appeal-in-williamson-investigation/|website=Gazette & Herald|date=31 March 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250929210744/https://www.gazetteherald.co.uk/news/6662606.fresh-appeal-in-williamson-investigation/|archive-date=29 September 2025|access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref> Although a judge deemed a man's murder confession inadmissible, a later threat by that man to kill a garage attendant resulted in him being sent to [[Rampton Secure Hospital]] for an indefinite period in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Murder suspect sent to Rampton|url=https://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/7974064.murder-suspect-sent-to-rampton/|website=York Press|date=5 October 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250929211150/https://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/7974064.murder-suspect-sent-to-rampton/|archive-date=29 September 2025|access-date=29 September 2025}}</ref>
|-
|March 2001
|[[Stuart Lubbock]]
|[[Roydon, Essex|Roydon]], Essex
|Lubbock, 31, died during a party at the home of entertainer [[Michael Barrymore]] on 31 March 2001. Initially his death was treated as an accidental drowning, but an inquest found he had suffered injuries consistent with sexual assault. In a documentary, ''Barrymore: The Body in the Pool'', shown on [[Channel 4]] on 6 February 2020, Detective Chief Inspector Stephen Jennings of [[Essex Police]] stated that mistakes had been made in the original investigation and that he believed Lubbock had been raped and murdered.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Sommerlad|first=Joe|title=Stuart Lubbock: What happened to the man found dead in Michael Barrymore's swimming pool?|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/michael-barrymore-stuart-lubbock-death-body-pool-injuries-channel-4-documentary-a9317281.html|website=The Independent|date=6 February 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813004438/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/michael-barrymore-stuart-lubbock-death-body-pool-injuries-channel-4-documentary-a9317281.html|archive-date=13 August 2022|access-date=7 February 2020}}</ref>

|April 2001
|[[Murder of Rebecca Hall|Rebecca Hall]]
|[[Bradford]], West Yorkshire
|19-year-old Hall, a sex worker with a four-month-old son, went missing from her home in Little Horton, Bradford, on 13 April 2001. Her body was found in Thornton Street on 26 April; she had suffered severe head injuries. In January 2019, police arrested a 37-year-old woman and then released her under investigation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Woman arrested in Rebecca Hall cold case murder inquiry|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leeds-46890873|website=BBC News|date=16 January 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190116112351/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-leeds-46890873|archive-date=16 January 2019|access-date=30 November 2019}}</ref> Hall's murder has also been linked to Bradford serial killer [[Bradford murders|Stephen Griffiths]], who lived {{convert|800|m|yd|0}} from where she was found dead. He was interviewed by police about her murder in 2010 but refused to answer any of their questions.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Carter|first=Helen|title=Bradford murders: Stephen Griffiths questioned about teenager's death|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2010/jun/01/bradford-murders-stephen-griffiths|website=The Guardian|date=1 June 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921113933/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2010/jun/01/bradford-murders-stephen-griffiths|archive-date=21 September 2021|access-date=21 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|author=David Wilson|author-link=David Wilson (criminologist)|title=Killers Behind Bars: The Untold Story – Stephen Griffiths|url=https://ok.ru/video/1631886445103|format=TV documentary|website=OK|publisher=Channel 5|date=21 March 2013|access-date=29 October 2021}}</ref>

|April 2001
|Corey Wright and Wayne Henry
|[[Clapton, London|Clapton]], London
|20-year-old Wright was a passenger in 19-year-old Henry's car when shots were fired at the vehicle as it was being driven away from the Chimes nightclub in Clapton on Saturday 21 April 2001, killing both of them. Wright had been convicted along with five other youths of conspiracy to commit grievous bodily harm against Kingsley Iyasara, a 16-year-old boy beaten and fatally shot in the [[Finsbury Park (area)|Finsbury Park]] district of London in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bartholomew|first=Emma|title='My heartache 17 years on': Corey Wright's mother holds London Fields vigil on anniversary of 'Murder Mile' shooting|url=https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/22936536.my-heartache-17-years-on-corey-wrights-mother-holds-london-fields-vigil-anniversary-murder-mile-shooting/|website=Hackney Gazette|date=19 April 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410115752/https://www.hackneygazette.co.uk/news/my-heartache-17-years-on-corey-wright-s-mother-holds-3590818|archive-date=10 April 2021|access-date=7 September 2021}}</ref>

|May 2001
|[[Murder of Don Banfield|Don Banfield]]
|Body not found
|63-year-old Banfield went missing from his home in the northwest London suburb of [[Harrow, London|Harrow]] on 11 May 2001. In April 2012 his wife and daughter, having earlier pleaded guilty to forgery, conspiracy to defraud and conspiracy to pervert the course of justice, were convicted of his murder after being accused of lying about seeing him in 2008 and being found to have gained financially from his disappearance. However, they were released on appeal in July 2013 – even though a lawyer representing the mother at that hearing acknowledged that the likelihood was that Banfield was murdered by one or other of the women – as they were convicted under [[joint enterprise]] and the appeal judges ruled that there was insufficient evidence to prove that they acted together to kill him.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Shirley and Lynette Banfield's murder convictions quashed|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-23522195|work=BBC News|date=31 July 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230205230435/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-23522195|archive-date=5 February 2023|access-date=18 August 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=R V (1) SHIRLEY BANFIELD (2) LYNETTE BANFIELD (2013)|url=https://www.lccsa.org.uk/r-v-1-shirley-banfield-2-lynette-banfield-2013/|website=London Criminal Courts Solicitors' Association|date=31 July 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404013358/https://www.lccsa.org.uk/r-v-1-shirley-banfield-2-lynette-banfield-2013/|archive-date=4 April 2023|access-date=18 August 2022}}</ref>

|May 2001
|Andre Jan Aylward
|London
|27-year-old Aylward was driving his black E28 5 Series BMW along Valleyfield Road in [[Streatham]] at around 2:10 a.m. on 12 May 2001 when six bullets were fired at it from a handgun. After the shooting, he lost control of the car and crashed. He had been hit twice in the head and neck and was taken to [[King's College Hospital]], where he died at around 4:00 a.m.

A grey 7 Series BMW had been seen next to Aylward's vehicle a few minutes before he was shot and the police said that they were seeking to identify it. It was thought that the attack might have been a case of road rage or mistaken identity. The police also said that they had found nothing in Aylward's background to suggest that he had been involved in any criminal activity. The murder was featured on ''[[Crimewatch]]'' in July 2001.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Williams|first=Nino|title=Road rage link to car shooting|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6405177.road-rage-link-to-car-shooting/|website=News Shopper|date=1 August 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414080659/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6405177.road-rage-link-to-car-shooting/|archive-date=14 April 2019|access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Crimewatch U.K - July 2001 (18.07.01)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w-a1CL-QDC4|website=YouTube|date=18 July 2001|access-date=22 November 2019}}</ref>

|May 2001
|Stephen Lawlor
|Liverpool
|34-year-old Stephen Lawlor was shot dead close to his residence in [[Netherley, Liverpool|Netherley]], Liverpool, as he left a party on 19 May 2001. Peter Clarke was convicted of Stephen's murder in December 2001 but found not guilty after being retried at Manchester Crown Court.<ref name=ECHO2>{{Cite web|last=Edrich|first=Patrick|title=Tidal wave of violence saw three men shot dead and innocent boy caught in crossfire|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/tidal-wave-violence-saw-three-30121633|website=Liverpool Echo|date=12 October 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207211753/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/tidal-wave-violence-saw-three-30121633.amp|archive-date=7 December 2024|access-date=7 December 2024}}</ref>

|May 2001
|Richard Rayner
|[[Bow, London|Bow]], London
|43-year-old Rayner, a plumber from [[Millwall]] (east London), was shot at the River Bank Cafe, Bow, on 25 May 2001. |Keith Rogers
|Died in hospital in [[Harlow]] in Essex from the effects of a fire in [[Sawbridgeworth]], Hertfordshire
|40-year-old Rogers managed to escape the fire at his first-floor flat by jumping from a window but died in hospital four weeks later from organ failure caused by smoke inhalation. The fire had been started in the early hours of 29 April by igniting petrol that had been poured through the flat's letterbox.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Murder probe follows arson attack|url=https://www.watfordobserver.co.uk/news/5769620.murder-probe-follows-arson-attack/|website=Watford Observer|date=6 June 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108220243/https://www.watfordobserver.co.uk/news/5769620.murder-probe-follows-arson-attack/|archive-date=8 January 2025|access-date=19 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Murder investigations|url=https://www.herts.police.uk/assets/FOI-Herts/FOI-2017/FOI-Herts-FOI201701107-Nov2017.pdf|website=Hertfordshire Constabulary|date=23 November 2017|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612211043/https://www.herts.police.uk/assets/FOI-Herts/FOI-2017/FOI-Herts-FOI201701107-Nov2017.pdf|archive-date=12 June 2020|access-date=19 October 2021}}</ref>

|May 2001
|Hasan Mamali and Sami Mustafa
|[[Islington]], London
|23-year-old Mamali was shot in the back of a car and 26-year-old Mustafa was shot after getting out of it in a bid to escape on 27 May 2001. Police are yet to trace the driver or the front seat passenger, both of whom abandoned the vehicle a short distance away with Mamali still in the back. Mamali and Mustafa were Turkish Cypriots who investigators thought might have been hoping to secure a drug deal.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Hasan Mamali|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=1824|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230925222501/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=1824|archive-date=25 September 2023|access-date=25 September 2023}}</ref>

|June 2001
|Donovan Williams
|[[Streatham]], London
|23-year-old Williams was found shot dead at a flat in Barrow Road, Streatham, on 7 June 2001. A man said to have been involved in a gang fight that the shooting was part of – John Dickinson – was found fatally stabbed approximately an hour after that fight, and nobody has been charged with either murder.<ref name=NewsShopper>{{Cite web|title=Man left to die in Mayday grounds|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6411387.man-left-to-die-in-mayday-grounds/|website=News Shopper|date=18 June 2001|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260324222037/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6411387.man-left-to-die-in-mayday-grounds/|archive-date=24 March 2026|access-date=24 March 2026}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>

|June 2001
|John Dickinson
|[[Thornton Heath]], London
|35-year-old Dickinson was found with a fatal stab wound to the leg in the grounds of [[Mayday University Hospital]], Thornton Heath, on 7 June 2001. He was thought to be connected to the death of Donovan Williams, a man murdered earlier on that date.<ref name=NewsShopper/><ref name=MetFOI/>

|June 2001
|Christopher Hewitt
|[[Bristol]]
|18-year-old Hewitt, a Jamaican who had recently arrived in Britain, was stabbed outside a pub on All Hallows Road, [[Easton, Bristol|Easton]], Bristol, on 10 June 2001 in an incident thought to have involved up to several assailants. |June 2001
|Jody Burns
|Attacked in [[Runcorn]], Cheshire, died at [[Whiston Hospital]]
|27-year-old Burns sustained a fatal head injury during a disturbance in Runcorn town centre in the early hours of 15 June 2001. The disturbance involved up to 60 people and he was said to have been trying to act as peacemaker. Police charged five men with violent disorder relating to the brawl, but nobody has been charged with Burns's murder.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Clay|first=Oliver|title=Killer who struck during taxi rank mass brawl 20 years ago still walking the streets|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/cold-case-still-open-20-20712690|website=Liverpool Echo|date=1 June 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003185150/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/cold-case-still-open-20-20712690|archive-date=3 October 2021|access-date=3 October 2021}}</ref>
