|July 2001
|Mithat Lleshi
|[[Northampton]]
|23-year-old Albanian Lleshi and a 28-year-old friend from the same country were set upon by a group of six men and stabbed in Northampton town centre on 7 July 2001. The older victim survived his injuries. It was believed that the group was made up of fellow Albanians and three men were arrested in Albania in 2005, but a ''Northamptonshire Telegraph'' article from 2017 has Lleshi's murder as one of the county's still-unsolved crimes.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Mithat Lleshi|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=1829&termRef=Mithat%20Lleshi|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230325215220/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=1829&termRef=Mithat%20Lleshi|archive-date=25 March 2023|access-date=25 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Police committed to seeking justice in Northamptonshire's unsolved murders|url=https://www.northantstelegraph.co.uk/news/police-committed-to-seeking-justice-in-northamptonshires-unsolved-murders-849288|website=Northamptonshire Telegraph|date=17 August 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231111014453/https://www.northantstelegraph.co.uk/news/police-committed-to-seeking-justice-in-northamptonshires-unsolved-murders-849288|archive-date=11 November 2023|access-date=25 March 2023}}</ref>

|July 2001
|Oguzhin Ozdemir
|[[South Tottenham]], London
|Ozdemir was kidnapped before being found shot dead next to the [[River Lea]] on 14 July 2001. His phone had been used earlier that day to warn friends of his that the 26-year-old, a small-time drug dealer who owed money, would be killed if the people holding him hostage did not receive money or goods. Three men involved in the kidnap were handed sentences of between 10 and 14 years in 2005, but none of the sentences was for murder because it had not been determined who had shot Ozdemir.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dealers kidnappers jailed for 36 years|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/565597.dealers-kidnappers-jailed-for-36-years/|website=Enfield Independent|date=31 January 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230911195906/https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/565597.dealers-kidnappers-jailed-for-36-years/|archive-date=11 September 2023|access-date=11 September 2023}}</ref>

|July 2001
|Daniel Dale
|Manchester
|18-year-old Dale was killed and another youth hit in the hand when shots were fired at their group as they chatted in the street in [[Miles Platting]] on the evening of 25 July 2001. |7 November 2001
|Sellathurai Balasingham
|Attacked in [[Mitcham]], London, died in hospital
|36-year-old Balasingham was dragged from his car and beaten in [[Pollards Hill]] at around 11:00 p.m. on 6 November 2001, and pronounced dead shortly after midnight as a result of a fractured skull. Other injuries included bruising and five broken ribs. Several men were charged, one of whom – a man said to have driven a [[Suzuki Swift]] away from the scene – agreed ahead of trial to give evidence against the others and plead guilty to conspiracy to assault. In 2004, four of them were convicted of murder and three of conspiracy to assault, but in 2007, their convictions were quashed when the putative Suzuki Swift driver, who disappeared before the 2004 trial and claimed later that threats against him and his family were the reason, was found to lack credibility. At a 2008 retrial, two were convicted of murder and two of manslaughter, but fresh witness evidence in 2011 caused these convictions to be quashed as well. Balasingham was alleged to have insulted an uncle of two of the defendants (who were brothers), and bad feeling stemming from the insult was advanced as a motive for killing him.<ref>{{Cite web|title=[2007] EWCA Crim 2687|url=https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Crim/2007/2687.html|website=BAILII|date=24 July 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250905183026/https://www.bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Crim/2007/2687.html|archive-date=5 September 2025|access-date=5 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Burnett|first=Craig|title=Brothers released after serving eight years for murder|url=https://www.yourlocalguardian.co.uk/news/8987146.brothers-released-after-serving-eight-years-for-murder/|website=Your Local Guardian|date=21 April 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250905183304/https://www.yourlocalguardian.co.uk/news/8987146.brothers-released-after-serving-eight-years-for-murder/|archive-date=5 September 2025|access-date=5 September 2025}}</ref>

|March 2002
|[[Exmoor Body mystery|Exmoor Body in the Bag]]
|Winsford Hill, [[Winsford, Somerset|Winsford]], Somerset
|The man's badly decomposed corpse was found wrapped in bin bags, a single green bed sheet and a single duvet on 13 March 2002. Also present were a white pillowcase and a stereo wire, which a detective said the victim might have been tied up with. He is thought to have died two to three years before being found, and it is not clear if the body was brought into the UK from overseas. Clay and computer-generated reconstructions of the man's head were shown on ''Crimewatch'' in May 2002 in the hope that someone would recognise him, but without success. He was 26 to 36 years old and possibly of Turkish or Indian origin, and a gold chain he was wearing when discovered had a pendant with a verse from the [[Koran]] inscribed across it. A funeral for the mystery victim was arranged in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Alder|first=Chris|title=Mystery body to be laid to rest|url=https://www.somersetcountygazette.co.uk/news/920591.mystery-body-to-be-laid-to-rest/|website=Somerset County Gazette|date=17 September 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180812053340/http://www.somersetcountygazette.co.uk/news/920591.mystery_body_to_be_laid_to_rest|archive-date=12 August 2018|access-date=13 October 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Head 'reconstructed' in body inquiry|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/1987020.stm|website=BBC News|date=14 May 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224192448/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/1987020.stm|archive-date=24 February 2020|access-date=24 February 2020}}</ref>

|[[Newcastle upon Tyne|Newcastle]]
|44-year-old Baldwin's body was found in the kitchen of his home in [[Heaton, Newcastle upon Tyne|Heaton]] by a window cleaner the day after he was bludgeoned to death in the property. Because the assailant appeared not to have gained access using force, detectives believed that it was someone the victim knew.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Victim probably knew his attacker - police|url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/7072879.victim-probably-knew-attacker---police/|website=The Northern Echo|date=24 May 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220116012300/https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/7072879.victim-probably-knew-attacker---police/|archive-date=16 January 2022|access-date=15 January 2022}}</ref> A suspect was arrested but died in a road traffic collision before the evidence was sufficient to charge him.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Freedom of Information Act 2000 (FOIA) Request 1183/15 - Unsolved murders|url=https://www.northumbria.police.uk/media/6832741/foi-1183-15.pdf|website=Northumbria Police|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231101214556/https://www.northumbria.police.uk/media/6832741/foi-1183-15.pdf|archive-date=1 November 2023|access-date=15 January 2022}}</ref>
|-
|23 May 2002
|Zennen Blackburn
|Manchester
|A man got out of a car and shot 27-year-old Blackburn dead in [[Moston, Manchester|Moston]] late in the afternoon. Investigators still do not know why the crime was committed, but rumour has it that it was to settle a debt owed to a criminal with whom Blackburn had fallen out.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Thompson|first=Dan|title=Zennen Blackburn unsolved murder: Mother's plea 13 years on for people to come forward|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/zennen-blackburn-unsolved-murder-mothers-9311688|website=Manchester Evening News|date=23 May 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917153813/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/zennen-blackburn-unsolved-murder-mothers-9311688|archive-date=17 September 2021|access-date=29 March 2021}}</ref>

|June 2002
|Geoffrey Windsor
|[[Beaulieu Heights]], London
|57-year-old Windsor was beaten to death with a car aerial in Beaulieu Heights, a park between the districts of [[Upper Norwood]] and [[South Norwood]], on 26 June 2002. Homophobia was suspected to have motivated the attack.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Menhinnitt|first=Daniel|title=World Cup murder unsolved|url=https://www.yourlocalguardian.co.uk/news/502559.world-cup-murder-unsolved/|website=Your Local Guardian|date=23 June 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226002117/https://www.yourlocalguardian.co.uk/news/502559.world-cup-murder-unsolved/|archive-date=26 December 2024|access-date=10 October 2022}}</ref>
|-
|June 2002
|Alexander Blue
|[[Glasgow]]
|41-year-old Blue, a businessman who co-owned a taxi company, was found with head injuries outside his home in [[Dowanhill]], in Glasgow's west end, on 25 June 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Murder of Alexander Blue|url=http://www.strathclyde.police.uk/whats_happening/feature_cases/murder_of_alexander_blue/|website=Strathclyde Police|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120901023007/http://www.strathclyde.police.uk/whats_happening/feature_cases/murder_of_alexander_blue/|archive-date=1 September 2012|access-date=22 August 2012}}</ref> He died at the Southern General Hospital two days later.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Burns|first=Janice|title=The killer of Alexander Blue will be caught|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/13283702.the-killer-of-alexander-blue-will-be-caught/|website=Glasgow Times|date=24 June 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200623195719/https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/13283702.the-killer-of-alexander-blue-will-be-caught/|archive-date=23 June 2020|access-date=23 June 2020}}</ref>
|-
|July 2002
|Joseph Byrne
|Attacked in Oxford, died in hospital in [[Aylesbury]], Buckinghamshire
|Paramedics attending a flat in [[Littlemore]] on 7 May 2002 were told by 61-year-old Byrne that he had had a liquid thrown at him. The liquid was a chemical that had caused his skin to become tightly stretched and his head to swell to twice its normal size, and he died at [[Stoke Mandeville Hospital]] on 1 July after breathing difficulties brought on by swelling in his airways triggered a heart attack. At Byrne's inquest, the assistant deputy coroner and a detective were critical of hospital staff for not informing the police of the assault sooner.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man's head swelled to twice normal size|url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/732588.mans-head-swelled-twice-normal-size/|website=Oxford Mail|date=13 April 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108084403/https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/732588.mans-head-swelled-twice-normal-size/|archive-date=8 January 2025|access-date=12 May 2021}}</ref>
|-
|July 2002
|Jonathan McMurray
|Attacked in [[Wood Green]], London, died in hospital
|20-year-old McMurray had left a pub to walk home when he was stabbed during a clash between the people he was with and another group. The incident happened at nighttime on 17 July 2002, and McMurray died at [[North Middlesex Hospital]], Edmonton, about two hours later.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man stabbed to death|url=https://www.guardian-series.co.uk/news/197511.man-stabbed-to-death/|website=East London & West Essex Guardian|date=25 July 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221000319/https://www.guardian-series.co.uk/news/197511.man-stabbed-to-death/|archive-date=21 December 2021|access-date=21 December 2021}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>
|-
|July 2002
|Damian Cope
|London
|22-year-old Cope was shot in the abdomen outside Browns, a nightclub on [[Great Queen Street]] in central London, on 29 July 2002. According to two friends, he told them who the shooter was before dying, and though one of them would not reveal that person's identity to detectives, the other gave the police a name. The alleged shooter was acquitted because Cope's friends refused to testify and two doctors independently concluded that the nature of his injuries made it highly unlikely that Cope would have been able to communicate by speech seven minutes after sustaining them, as claimed by one of his friends.<ref>{{Cite web|title=£10,000 reward offered in murder case|url=https://www.thisislocallondon.co.uk/news/397669.10000-reward-offered-in-murder-case/|website=This Is Local London|date=29 July 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208220756/https://www.thisislocallondon.co.uk/news/397669.10000-reward-offered-in-murder-case/|archive-date=8 February 2023|access-date=8 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=McGowan|first=Patrick|title=Old Bailey murder trial collapses|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/hp/front/old-bailey-murder-trial-collapses-6954525.html|website=Evening Standard|date=15 August 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624003513/https://www.standard.co.uk/hp/front/old-bailey-murder-trial-collapses-6954525.html|archive-date=24 June 2021|access-date=8 February 2023}}</ref> The acquitted man was himself murdered in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Summers|first=Chris|title=Victim who will be mourned by few|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/7605761.stm|website=BBC News|date=17 October 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208225631/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/7605761.stm|archive-date=8 February 2023|access-date=8 February 2023}}</ref>
|-
|August 2002
|Monica Flaherty
|[[Bradford]], West Yorkshire
|62-year-old Flaherty, a grandmother who had discovered her murdered daughter's body in 1990, was stabbed in the chest during a street brawl on 3 August 2002 and managed to make her way to her home in [[Manningham, Bradford|Manningham]]'s Priestman Street before dying there. [[West Yorkshire Police]] charged a 35-year-old man over the stabbing but later dropped the charge.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Murdered gran's daughter was stab victim|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/8025099.murdered-grans-daughter-was-stab-victim/|website=Telegraph & Argus|date=5 August 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208221138/https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/8025099.murdered-grans-daughter-was-stab-victim/|archive-date=8 February 2023|access-date=8 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Man 'made up two claims of attacks'|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/7996828.man-made-up-two-claims-of-attacks/|website=Telegraph & Argus|date=25 November 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208223422/https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/7996828.man-made-up-two-claims-of-attacks/|archive-date=8 February 2023|access-date=8 February 2023}}</ref>
|-
|August 2002
|Thomas Breen
|Attacked in [[Camden Town]], London, died in hospital
|50-year-old Breen, a builder from [[Downpatrick]] in Northern Ireland, was stabbed in the chest outside a pub in Camden High Street on 10 August 2002. Although the street was covered by CCTV cameras, none filmed the incident because all were pointing away from where it was taking place.<ref>{{Cite web|last=McLennan|first=William|title=Exclusive: Scotland Yard to re-open files on 2002 Camden Town murder|url=https://www.camdennewjournal.co.uk/article/exclusive-scotland-yard-to-re-open-files-on-2002-camden-town-murder|website=Camden New Journal|date=23 February 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260406184339/https://www.camdennewjournal.co.uk/article/exclusive-scotland-yard-to-re-open-files-on-2002-camden-town-murder|archive-date=6 April 2026|access-date=6 April 2026}}</ref>
|-
|August 2002
|Nikolaos Pittakis
|[[West Green, London|West Green]]<!--source says Belmont Road is in Hornsey, but this is not so-->, London
|Police found the body of Greek-born Pittakis, 60, in his Belmont Road flat on 23 August 2002 after being informed by a neighbour that a foul smell was emanating from there. He had died from stab wounds up to two weeks earlier.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Schroder|first=Johnathan|title=Body find sparks a police murder hunt|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/205551.body-find-sparks-a-police-murder-hunt/|website=Enfield Independent|date=29 August 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114231052/https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/205551.body-find-sparks-a-police-murder-hunt/|archive-date=14 January 2026|access-date=14 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Nikolaos Pittakis|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=463|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114231356/https://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=463|archive-date=14 January 2026|access-date=14 January 2026}}</ref>
|-
|August 2002
|Lorraine Turner
|[[Norwich]], Norfolk
|37-year-old Turner's 10-year-old son and eight-year-old daughter found her murdered at her home in [[Old Catton]] on 17 August 2002. A 21-year-old roofer was charged with the killing of the former newspaper journalist before being cleared in May 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Murder inquiry over N-E woman|url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/7062607.murder-inquiry-n-e-woman/|website=The Northern Echo|date=20 August 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917083559/https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/7062607.murder-inquiry-n-e-woman/|archive-date=17 September 2021|access-date=5 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Roofer cleared of killing woman|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/norfolk/3013697.stm|website=BBC News|date=9 May 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305211234/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/norfolk/3013697.stm|archive-date=5 March 2021|access-date=5 March 2021}}</ref>
|-
|August 2002
|Darren Birt
|Glasgow
|Birt, 22, died from injuries sustained in an attack in Barlanark on 28 August 2002. He was chased from Edinburgh Road to Burnett Road and was found lying in the road in Calvay Place. In March 2022, police announced that they were reinvestigating the case.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police to reinvestigate 2002 murder of Darren Birt in Glasgow|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-60877701|website=BBC News|date=25 March 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230412150619/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-60877701|archive-date=12 April 2023|access-date=23 July 2022}}</ref>
|-
|September 2002
|Kevin Nunes
|[[Pattingham]], Staffordshire
|On 19 September 2002, 20-year-old Nunes's body was found dumped in a country lane about two miles from the outskirts of his home city of [[Wolverhampton]] after he had been shot five times. Although five men went to prison in 2008 for the drug dealer and amateur footballer's murder, they were released in 2012 because of failures to do with disclosure to the defence. The disclosure failures concerned information relating to the key prosecution witness.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Five men jailed for murder of Wolverhampton drug dealer Kevin Nunes have convictions overturned|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/local-news/five-men-jailed-murder-wolverhampton-180683|website=Birmingham Live|date=8 March 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200625004712/https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/local-news/five-men-jailed-murder-wolverhampton-180683|archive-date=25 June 2020|access-date=23 June 2020}}</ref>
|-
|September 2002
|Gordon Ross
|Glasgow
|36-year-old Ross was stabbed to death outside a pub on Shettleston Road, Glasgow, on 24 September 2002, possibly because of an attack on a gangland rival earlier in the month. A close associate of gangster [[Tam McGraw]], Ross was an enforcer and drug supplier who, in 1998, had walked free from a trial where he had been accused of smuggling 220lb of cannabis resin.<ref>{{Cite web|last=McGivern|first=Mark|title=Gangland enforcer stabbed to death|url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Gangland+enforcer+stabbed+to+death.-a092009342|website=The Free Library|date=25 September 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=25 December 2025}}</ref>

|October 2002
|Julie Dorsett
|[[Walthamstow]], London
|Dorsett, a 33-year-old sex worker, vanished in early October 2002, and her skull and upper body were discovered buried in an allotment in 2008. It is believed her remains were placed there shortly after she disappeared. In 2012 Dorsett's former partner was cleared of killing her and burying her body.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Binns|first=Daniel|title=Sinclair Lewis has been cleared of killing his ex-partner Julie Dorsett and burying her body in a Walthamstow allotment|url=https://www.guardian-series.co.uk/news/9838993.walthamstow--man-cleared-of-allotment-body-murder/|website=Guardian-Series|date=26 July 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250210121433/https://www.guardian-series.co.uk/news/9838993.walthamstow--man-cleared-of-allotment-body-murder/|archive-date=10 February 2025|access-date=16 August 2012}}</ref>
|-
|October 2002
|Billy Sibbald
|[[Edinburgh]]
|Father-of-three Sibbald, 48, went missing from [[Joppa, Edinburgh|Joppa]], Edinburgh, on 8 October 2002 after telling his wife he was meeting business associates. Three months later his decomposing body was found in woodland next to a lay-by near the outskirts of the city. There have been various theories for the pub landlord's murder, including that it was a [[gangland killing]]. Little information came through to the police in their hunt for the culprit(s).<ref>{{Cite news|title=Photo hope in hunt for landlord's killer|url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/photo-hope-in-hunt-for-landlord-s-killer-1-873942|work=[[The Scotsman]]|publisher=[[Johnston Press]]|date=26 March 2003|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160424104406/https://www.scotsman.com/news/photo-hope-in-hunt-for-landlord-s-killer-1-873942|archive-date=24 April 2016|access-date=7 January 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Unsolved murder files that stay open|url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/unsolved-murder-files-that-stay-open-2508608|work=[[The Scotsman]]|publisher=[[Johnston Press]]|date=16 November 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230926203751/https://www.scotsman.com/news/unsolved-murder-files-that-stay-open-2508608|archive-date=26 September 2023|access-date=7 January 2012}}</ref>
|-
|October 2002
|David Draycott
|[[Sutton-in-Ashfield]], Nottinghamshire
|40-year-old Draycott was shot when he pulled up outside his Sutton-in-Ashfield home on 7 October 2002, and died four days later at [[King's Mill Hospital]] in the town. A man who may be linked to the case was convicted of drug trafficking and smuggling by a French court in December 2018 and handed a 22-year jail sentence.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Whitfield|first=David|title=Widow of David Draycott says she is hopeful his killers can still be found following conviction of Robert Dawes|url=https://www.nottinghampost.com/news/local-news/widow-david-draycott-says-hopeful-2369065|website=Nottinghamshire Live|date=28 December 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111204640/https://www.nottinghampost.com/news/local-news/widow-david-draycott-says-hopeful-2369065|archive-date=11 January 2020|access-date=11 January 2020}}</ref>

|October 2002
|Devon Brown
|[[Shepherd's Bush]], London
|39-year-old Brown, a Jamaican-born father-of-two, was shot dead in Shepherd's Bush on the afternoon of 15 October 2002. [[Operation Trident (Metropolitan Police)|Operation Trident]] investigated the murder.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Devon Omaro Brown|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=464|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210522185609/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=464|archive-date=22 May 2021|access-date=22 May 2021}}</ref>

|October 2002
|Thomas Scott
|Attacked in [[Kentish Town]], London, died in hospital
|On the night of 19/20 October 2002, 34-year-old Scott and his 28-year-old half-brother debarked at [[Kentish Town tube station]] to change trains after taking the wrong branch of the [[northern line]], walked out of the station because the last train had gone, and were attacked by a gang. Scott was beaten with a knuckleduster and a bread crate. Four people aged 16 to 20 were found guilty of violent disorder, but there were no convictions for murder or manslaughter.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Family's anger at Tube death sentencing|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/3135579.stm|website=BBC News|date=8 August 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260313232203/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/3135579.stm|archive-date=13 March 2026|access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Morris|first=Steven|title=18 months for gang in fatal beating|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2003/aug/09/ukcrime.stevenmorris1|website=The Guardian|date=9 August 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420192315/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2003/aug/09/ukcrime.stevenmorris1|archive-date=20 April 2021|access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref>
|-
|7 November 2002
|John Shippam
|[[Nottingham]]
|25-year-old Shippam was found shot dead in his flat in [[Bestwood]], Nottingham. He had been assaulted at The Anchor Inn in [[Gunthorpe, Nottinghamshire|Gunthorpe]] two days previously, and police believed the incidents were probably linked.<ref>{{Cite web|title=John Shippam murder: Appeal 10 years after shooting|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-nottinghamshire-20228787|website=BBC News|date=7 November 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110015621/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-nottinghamshire-20228787|archive-date=10 November 2012|access-date=4 January 2020}}</ref>

|7/8 November 2002
|Andrew Brown
|[[Streatham]], London
|28-year-old Brown ran a scooter shop in Westcote Road, Streatham, and was found stabbed to death in his nearby flat after his girlfriend had a locksmith open its door because nobody had seen or heard from him since the previous evening.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Girlfriend finds body of murdered shopkeeper|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6284721.girlfriend-finds-body-of-murdered-shopkeeper/|website=News Shopper|date=15 November 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240229230018/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6284721.girlfriend-finds-body-of-murdered-shopkeeper/|archive-date=29 February 2024|access-date=29 February 2024}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>

|9 November 2002
|Theresa Jacobs
|Nottingham
|In front of about 40 people and within minutes of leaving a [[Radford, Nottingham|Radford]] nightclub in the early hours, 33-year-old Jacobs was shot point-blank in a crime thought to have been drug-related. She was pronounced dead at the [[Queen's Medical Centre]] later that day.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Theresa Jacobs|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=1875|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230716204732/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=1875|archive-date=16 July 2023|access-date=16 July 2023}}</ref>

|Alisan Dogan
|[[Harringay]], London
|43-year-old Dogan was stabbed to death and others were injured when a café on Green Lanes was stormed by a gang. |10 November 2002
|Martin Gorman
|Attacked in [[Tottenham]], London, died in hospital
|24-year-old Gorman and a friend were outside [[White Hart Lane railway station]] when Gorman was stabbed by a man with whom he had been arguing. |13 November 2002
|Jason Spence
|Attacked in [[Great Barr]], Birmingham, died in hospital in [[West Bromwich]]
|31-year-old Spence was shot by an occupant of a silver [[Mitsubishi Galant]] estate car travelling along Cardington Avenue. |23 November 2002
|Martin Simpson
|[[Leicester]]
|59-year-old Simpson, a well-liked regular at various Leicester pubs, bars and betting shops, was assaulted in Leicester city centre on the night of 22–23 November 2002. |30 November 2002
|Tony Nicholls
|[[Brixton]], London
|44-year-old Nicholls was shot as he sat in a stationary car near the junction of Tulse Hill and Brixton Water Lane, Brixton. He had no fixed address at the time.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police appeal for murder witnesses|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6278752.police-appeal-for-murder-witnesses/|website=News Shopper|date=11 December 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210914173915/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/6278752.police-appeal-for-murder-witnesses/|archive-date=14 September 2021|access-date=14 September 2021}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>

|1 December 2002
|Susan McDonald
|[[Broughton Astley]], Leicestershire
|A fire that was started in a wheelie bin outside 47-year-old McDonald's house resulted in her death when it trapped her in her bedroom, having spread to that room via the hall and stairway after burning through the front door.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Appeal 10 years after death of Broughton Astley mum|url=https://www.hinckleytimes.net/news/local-news/appeal-10-years-after-death-6032326|work=The Hinckley Times|date=28 December 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200103191052/https://www.hinckleytimes.net/news/local-news/appeal-10-years-after-death-6032326|archive-date=3 January 2020|access-date=3 January 2020}}</ref>
|-
|5 December 2002
|Wayne Trotter
|Attacked in [[Borehamwood]], Hertfordshire, died in hospital in London
|30-year-old Trotter was walking home from work just after midnight on 5 December 2002 when he was doused with petrol and set on fire. |7 December 2002
|Debbie Remorozo
|[[Oldham]], Lancashire
|26-year-old Remorozo was stabbed to death in her flat in Oldham on 7 December 2002. Remorozo was a nurse who worked at the Royal Oldham Hospital and was originally from the Philippines.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Scheerhout|first=John|title=Family of murdered nurse Debbie Remorozo say GMP have not been in touch for more than TEN years|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/family-murdered-nurse-debbie-remorozo-12100513|website=Manchester Evening News|date=30 October 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161030190016/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/family-murdered-nurse-debbie-remorozo-12100513|archive-date=30 October 2016|access-date=24 November 2019}}</ref>
|-
|12 December 2002
|Daniel Regan
|[[Haydock]], Merseyside
|25-year-old Regan was found dead in his house on Station Road with a gunshot wound to the chest. Nearby was the burnt-out shell of the vehicle the killer is thought to have arrived in: a stolen grey or silver Rover.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Summers|first=Chris|title='I dreamed about my son's murder'|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/6938309.stm|website=BBC News|date=14 November 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090203095635/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/6938309.stm|archive-date=3 February 2009|access-date=20 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Unsolved 2002 - Daniel Regan|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uKqerbSHjMY|website=YouTube|date=18 March 2023|access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref>

|15 December 2002
|Selorn Gbesemete and Mohamed Korneh
|[[Southall]], London
|Gbesemete, 21, was shot in the neck and Korneh, also 21, was shot in the head at the Tudor Rose nightclub in Southall during an event whose aim was to discourage young black men from carrying guns. Rapper [[Dizzee Rascal]] performed at the event. A suspect was acquitted in May 2009 – 13 months after another suspect was himself shot dead.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man not guilty of double murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/8037532.stm|website=BBC News|date=7 May 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240918214209/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/8037532.stm|archive-date=18 September 2024|access-date=18 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Reggae star's son jailed for 30 years over murder|url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/default_content/12391700.reggae-stars-son-jailed-30-years-murder/|website=The Herald|date=16 July 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240918214640/https://www.heraldscotland.com/default_content/12391700.reggae-stars-son-jailed-30-years-murder/|archive-date=18 September 2024|access-date=18 September 2024}}</ref>
|-
|15 December 2002
|Carl Seaton
|Liverpool
|28-year-old Seaton was shot after leaving [[Edge Hill, Liverpool|Edge Hill]]'s Weighing Machine pub.<ref name=Seaton>{{Cite web|title=Shooting victim starred in gun film|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/2581411.stm|website=BBC News|date=16 December 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210820184905/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/2581411.stm|archive-date=20 August 2021|access-date=20 August 2021}}</ref> A man was charged but his trial was stopped because too many witnesses were absent.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Witness jailed for not testifying|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/merseyside/4337855.stm|website=BBC News|date=10 March 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210820181540/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/merseyside/4337855.stm|archive-date=20 August 2021|access-date=20 August 2021}}</ref> Seaton had appeared in a 1998 film about the increase in gun crime in inner-city areas of Britain, in which he portrayed a man who practised with a gun bought for self-defence.<ref name=Seaton/>
|-
|26 December 2002
|Mario O'Brien Clarke
|[[Hackney, London|Hackney]], London
|25-year-old Clarke, an off-duty soldier, was shot outside his home in Morning Lane, Hackney. Police believed him to have been a victim of mistaken identity.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Off-duty soldier shot 'in error'|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/2749449.stm|work=BBC News|date=11 February 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200620215750/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/2749449.stm|archive-date=20 June 2020|access-date=20 June 2020}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI>{{Cite web|title=Response to FOI request re undetected homicides in London|url=http://www.met.police.uk/foi/pdfs/disclosure_2011/october/2011090004192.pdf|website=Metropolitan Police|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425030126/http://www.met.police.uk/foi/pdfs/disclosure_2011/october/2011090004192.pdf|archive-date=25 April 2012|access-date=21 June 2020}}</ref>
|-
|3 January 2003
|Edward Byrne
|Attacked in [[Knotty Ash]], Liverpool, died at [[Whiston Hospital]]
|A lone gunman shot 66-year-old Byrne in a pub where about 40 drinkers were present.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Pensioner was shot 'by mistake'|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/2632615.stm|work=BBC News|date=6 January 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030207184348/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/2632615.stm|archive-date=7 February 2003|access-date=22 May 2021}}</ref> Investigators believed that someone other than him was meant to be targeted.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Killer robbed us of a lovely man|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/killer-robbed-lovely-man-3547883|work=Liverpool Echo|date=7 January 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151204143153/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/killer-robbed-lovely-man-3547883|archive-date=4 December 2015|access-date=22 May 2021}}</ref>
|-
|13 January 2003
|David Warrilow
|[[Chelmsley Wood]], West Midlands
|The 37-year-old welder and father-of-two suffered serious head injuries when he was run over as he tried to stop thieves taking his van from outside GB Singh's newsagents in Willow Way, Chelmsley Wood. His murder was featured on ''[[Crimewatch]]'' in February 2003.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Charges dropped over van death|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/west_midlands/3168202.stm|work=BBC News|date=6 October 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160804030715/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/west_midlands/3168202.stm|archive-date=4 August 2016|access-date=16 January 2019}}</ref>

|14 January 2003
|Brenda Wynne
|[[Liverpool]]
|63-year-old Wynne died three days after being pushed over in a robbery on Castlefield Road, West Derby, Liverpool, on 11 January 2003. The attackers were two men in their early 20s and Wynne's handbag was stolen.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pensioner dies after robbery|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/2664865.stm|website=BBC News|date=16 January 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210914175801/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/2664865.stm|archive-date=14 September 2021|access-date=26 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Kirwin|first=Ellen|title=175 unsolved Merseyside murders detectives want to crack|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/175-unsolved-merseyside-murders-detectives-25784733|website=Liverpool Echo|date=31 December 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725013135/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/175-unsolved-merseyside-murders-detectives-25784733|archive-date=25 July 2025|access-date=8 July 2023}}</ref>

|18 January 2003
|Kevin Clark
|[[Glasgow]]
|22-year-old Clark was discovered dead on waste ground in [[Carntyne]] with his head slashed and a gunshot wound to his back. In February of the following year a 24-year-old man was acquitted of murder and his father of cutting up the murder suspect's clothes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Appeal by murdered man's mother|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/scotland/2702183.stm|website=BBC News|date=28 January 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130210619/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/2702183.stm|archive-date=30 November 2023|access-date=30 November 2023}}</ref><ref name=Campbell>{{Cite web|title='Bugged' murder suspects walk free|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/3460435.stm|website=BBC News|date=4 February 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170531112841/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/scotland/3460435.stm|archive-date=31 May 2017|access-date=30 November 2023}}</ref>

|29 January 2003
|Domicela Skiera
|[[Ealing]], London
|85-year-old Skiera, a Polish widow, was beaten to death at her house in Ranelagh Road, Ealing, and the property was ransacked. |3 February 2003
|Margaret Muller
|[[Victoria Park, Tower Hamlets|Victoria Park]], London
|Muller, 27, was fatally stabbed while jogging in the park. Police suspect she may have been killed in a robbery gone wrong.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Victoria Park murder: Reward over Margaret Muller death|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-12351391|work=BBC News|date=3 February 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130627122122/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-12351391|archive-date=27 June 2013|access-date=3 February 2011}}</ref>

|4 February 2003
|Paul Savage
|Attacked in [[Mold, Flintshire|Mold]], Flintshire, died in hospital in [[Wrexham]]
|Postman Savage, 30, died after being attacked while on his round in Mold, Flintshire. He was beaten with a wooden baton and found lying in a pool of blood on Clayton Road. The police later said that they knew the reason Savage was killed, but did not divulge it. There is a £100,000 reward for information.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mold postman murder appeal renewed seven years on|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/wales/north_east/8498037.stm|website=[[BBC News]]|date=4 February 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180812083313/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/wales/north_east/8498037.stm|archive-date=12 August 2018|access-date=13 October 2011}}</ref>

|6 February 2003
|Beverley Brinkley
|Attacked in [[Harlow]], Essex, died at [[Addenbrooke's Hospital]] in Cambridge
|Brinkley, a 35-year-old woman with three children, died four days after being severely assaulted by two men in the lobby of the third floor of the block of flats she lived in.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Who murdered Harlow woman Beverley Brinkley in 2003?|url=https://www.yourharlow.com/2016/02/01/who-murdered-harlow-woman-beverley-brinkley-in-2003/|website=Your Harlow|date=1 February 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628160503/https://www.yourharlow.com/2016/02/01/who-murdered-harlow-woman-beverley-brinkley-in-2003/|archive-date=28 June 2020|access-date=28 June 2020}}</ref>

|14 February 2003
|Mohammed Mahmood
|[[Slough]], Berkshire
|25-year-old Mahmood died at [[Wexham Park Hospital]] after a police car took him there because he was seen in an injured state as the vehicle was passing through the area. The cause of his death was a stab wound to the chest inflicted during the theft of his friend's car by a group of four men.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Mohammad Mahmood|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=634|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240106213144/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=634|archive-date=6 January 2024|access-date=6 January 2024}}</ref>

|March 2003
|Billy McPhee
|Glasgow
|McPhee, a 38-year-old who was gangster [[Tam McGraw]]'s right-hand man, was fatally attacked as he sat on a stool in a family-friendly pub in [[Baillieston]], Glasgow, on 8 March 2003. The assailant entered the pub, walked up to him and stabbed him a number of times before walking out of the building. Lack of evidence against a man arraigned for murder led to the collapse of his trial the day after it began.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Silvester|first=Norman|title=Glasgow Crime Stories: Billy McPhee murdered in Brewers Fayre pub|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/23791805.glasgow-crime-stories-billy-mcphee-murdered-brewers-fayre-pub/|website=Glasgow Times|date=17 September 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231211024510/https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/23791805.glasgow-crime-stories-billy-mcphee-murdered-brewers-fayre-pub/|archive-date=11 December 2023|access-date=6 August 2025}}</ref>
|-
|March 2003
|Andrew Jones
|Liverpool
|On 9 March 2003, 18-year-old Jones was punched to the ground in Hanover Street in Liverpool when he encountered a group of people there at night after becoming separated from friends. A man who was in that group was acquitted of his manslaughter.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Siddle|first=John|title=Parents of Liverpool teenager Andrew Jones reveal they know who killed their son 10 years ago|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/parents-liverpool-teenager-andrew-jones-3009176|website=Liverpool Echo|date=8 March 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220624175725/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/parents-liverpool-teenager-andrew-jones-3009176|archive-date=24 June 2022|access-date=24 June 2022}}</ref>

|March 2003
|Thilipan Thangavadivel
|[[Ilford]], London
|24-year-old Thangavadivel's murder in Ilford on 19 March 2003 apparently took place in the context of gangland conflicts between Tamil people.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Thilipan Thangavadivel|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=205|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251110191720/https://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=205|archive-date=10 November 2025|access-date=10 November 2025}}</ref>

|March 2003
|Shaham Ali
|Birmingham
|Ali, 30, was shot on 17 March 2003 whilst using a public telephone in [[Small Heath]], and died seven days later in hospital. Four men charged over his death were accused at their trial of targeting him because of his support for the secretary of Birmingham's main mosque, who was suspected of impregnating the wife of its imam. The two accused of Ali's murder were both found not guilty of that charge, although one of them was, along with the two other defendants, convicted of assaulting and unlawfully imprisoning him.<ref>{{Cite web|last=McCarthy|first=Ross|title=Two men cleared of drive-by shooting after sex row at mosque|url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Two+men+cleared+of+drive-by+shooting+after+sex+row+at+mosque.-a0114113949|website=The Free Library|date=11 March 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220913211041/https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Two+men+cleared+of+drive-by+shooting+after+sex+row+at+mosque.-a0114113949|archive-date=13 September 2022|access-date=13 September 2022}}</ref> A second man injured in the same shooting – Azmat Yaqub – was shot dead in July 2004 in a murder that is also yet to be solved.
|-
|March 2003
|Peter Singleton
|[[Wirral Peninsula|Wirral]], Merseyside
|A masked gunman shot 26-year-old Singleton in front of his girlfriend and young son as they got out of a car in Column Road, [[West Kirby]], on 27 March 2003. Singleton suffered injuries to his head and stomach and died at Arrowe Park Hospital in [[Woodchurch, Merseyside|Woodchurch]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Thomas|first=Joe|title=Family of man gunned down on Merseyside street appeal for help on 11th anniversary of his death|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/family-man-gunned-down-merseyside-6883236|website=Liverpool Echo|date=27 March 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200226180732/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/family-man-gunned-down-merseyside-6883236|archive-date=26 February 2020|access-date=26 February 2020}}</ref>
|-
|April 2003
|Stephen Colby
|[[Great Yarmouth]], Norfolk
|47-year-old Colby was battered to death in the terraced house in which he lived on his own. His two sons said they discovered his body there on 11 April 2003 – nothing was missing – and the following year, one of them was tried for his murder but not found guilty. Because there were claims that Colby told people he was now wealthier thanks to money left to him in his aunt's will, an early line of inquiry pursued the theory that the murder was a result of a bungled burglary.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Burglary theory in seaside murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/norfolk/2959297.stm|work=BBC News|date=18 April 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009191700/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/norfolk/2959297.stm|archive-date=9 October 2020|access-date=9 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Man is cleared of father's murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/norfolk/3868213.stm|work=BBC News|date=5 July 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803102618/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/norfolk/3868213.stm|archive-date=3 August 2020|access-date=9 October 2020}}</ref>
|-
|May 2003
|Viola Mead
|Attacked in [[Wendover]], died in hospital in [[Aylesbury]] (both in Buckinghamshire)
|Mead, 85, of Dobbins Lane in Wendover, was attacked in her home by two men in late April 2003. She was found semi-conscious in her kitchen by a family friend on 28 April and died on 13 May in [[Stoke Mandeville Hospital]]. Mead gave a description of one of her attackers before she died: he was {{convert|5|ft|10|in}} tall, slim, had a narrow face with a dark yellowish complexion, and was wearing a black jumper with a yellow motif on the left.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wareham|first=Stephanie|title=Unsolved murders in Bucks: Who killed these women?|url=https://www.bucksfreepress.co.uk/news/18341323.unsolved-murders-bucks-killed-women/|website=Bucks Free Press|date=28 March 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240106214214/https://www.bucksfreepress.co.uk/news/18341323.unsolved-murders-bucks-killed-women/|archive-date=6 January 2024|access-date=6 January 2024}}</ref>
|-
|May 2003
|Otis Taylor
|[[Peckham]], London
|On 21 May 2003, 33-year-old Taylor was shot in the head at around 1:00 a.m. in Sassoon House, a block of flats on St Mary's Road in Peckham. It happened in the stairwell and the month before he and his pregnant fiancée were due to get married.<ref name=SouthwarkNews/>
|-
|June 2003
|Balkaran Deep Singh
|[[Southall]], London
|On 7 June 2003, 25-year-old Singh was beaten about the head and stabbed six times in Western Road, Southall, after crouching down – apparently to retrieve something from his inside pocket – while he and four companions were being chased by a larger group. Verbal hostility between the two groups had preceded the chase. Nobody was charged with Singh's murder, but four people were found guilty of threatening behaviour.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Balkaran Deep Singh|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2262|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240906211422/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2262|archive-date=6 September 2024|access-date=6 September 2024}}</ref>

|June 2003
|Partheepan Balasingham and Kishokumar Balachandiran
|London
|23-year-old Balasingham and 18-year-old Balachandiran suffered separate attacks on 8 June 2003, but both were thought to have been perpetrated by the same 12-strong gang. The attack on Balasingham, who died four days later, occurred outside a restaurant in [[Wembley]] at about 1:00 a.m., while that on Balachandiran, who died a week later, occurred after he was abducted from outside a bar in [[Ilford]] at about 2:00 a.m. Balachandiran was beaten, tortured and thrown into the [[River Roding]], and had hypothermia and numerous injuries when found there. The crimes were linked to Tamil gang warfare and apparently followed a bar fight involving Balachandiran earlier that night.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Partheepan Balasingham|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=4538|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250711182107/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=4538|archive-date=11 July 2025|access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Kishokumar Balachandiran|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=4539|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250423142020/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=4539|archive-date=23 April 2025|access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>

|June 2003
|Neil Nortrop (a.k.a. Neil McGarthland)
|Body not found
|32-year-old Nortrop left his home town of [[Brixham]], Devon, on 10 June 2003 to visit a friend in [[Greenwich]] or [[Dartford]]. He made a telephone call two days later but was never heard from again. The case was investigated as a murder by police, and a man and a woman from Greenwich were arrested in 2005, but no charges were brought. Nortrop's blue [[Ford Mondeo]] disappeared with him.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Chandler|first=Mark|title=DARTFORD & GREENWICH: Mum's seven-year search for 'murdered' son|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/8207918.dartford-greenwich-mums-seven-year-search-for-murdered-son/|work=News Shopper|date=9 June 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221023160410/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/8207918.dartford-greenwich-mums-seven-year-search-for-murdered-son/|archive-date=23 October 2022|access-date=23 October 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Arrests over death of fisherman|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/devon/4507192.stm|work=BBC News|date=7 December 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221023160408/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/devon/4507192.stm|archive-date=23 October 2022|access-date=23 October 2022}}</ref>

|August 2003
|Frank Bayley
|[[Stoke-on-Trent]], Staffordshire
|Three men went to court for alleged complicity in the murder of 66-year-old Bayley, but all of them were acquitted. Bayley had been asphyxiated at his Hartshill Road off-licence on 18 August 2003.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Three charged over shop killing|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/staffordshire/3508042.stm|work=BBC News|date=13 March 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226002603/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/staffordshire/3508042.stm|archive-date=26 December 2024|access-date=20 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|author=Staffordshire Police|title=FOI ref no: 8209|url=https://www.whatdotheyknow.com/request/unsolved_murders_29/response/984008/attach/3/Paul%20Jones%208209.doc|format=response to Freedom of Information request|website=WhatDoTheyKnow|date=25 May 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250429141948/https://www.whatdotheyknow.com/request/unsolved_murders_29/response/984008/attach/3/Paul%20Jones%208209.doc|archive-date=29 April 2025|access-date=10 November 2023}}</ref>

|August 2003
|Naveed Saleem
|Birmingham
|32-year-old Saleem's fiancée found him stabbed to death in his [[Range Rover]] early on 26 August 2003. Two men were cleared of his murder in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Balloo|first=Stephanie|title=I found the love of my life dead in his Range Rover a month before our wedding - but his killer is still free|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/i-found-love-life-dead-18994567|website=Birmingham Live|date=27 September 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201003125149/https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/i-found-love-life-dead-18994567|archive-date=3 October 2020|access-date=24 January 2023}}</ref>

|August 2003
|Justin Maynard
|[[Manchester]]
|19-year-old Maynard was fatally shot in Tugford Close, [[Moss Side]], Manchester, on 26 August 2003. He died of his injures at the scene.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Elise|title="My son's spirit walks the streets because the murderers are still out there"|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/my-sons-spirit-walks-streets-12799552|website=Manchester Evening News|date=26 March 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723173434/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/my-sons-spirit-walks-streets-12799552|archive-date=23 July 2021|access-date=28 February 2021}}</ref>

|September 2003
|Natalie Putt
|Body not found
|Putt, a 17-year-old mother of an 11-week-old baby, disappeared from her home in [[Lower Gornal]], [[Dudley]], West Midlands, on 1 September 2003, and police believe she was murdered. The father of her baby claimed that Putt, who had told him that she wanted a break from their relationship and was seeing another man at the time of her disappearance, went out to buy cigarettes and never returned, leaving him to care for their son. An inquest in January 2019 noted that a T-shirt with two tiny drops of Putt's blood on it had been found in her loft, and concluded that she had likely died at the address or nearby on 1 September 2003. The father has been interviewed by police a number of times, but there has never been sufficient evidence to charge anyone.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Natalie Putt: Missing mum's sister 'keeps campaigning'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-47867311|work=BBC News|date=9 April 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190409181043/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-birmingham-47867311|archive-date=9 April 2019|access-date=20 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Natalie Putt: Missing mum died 'at or near her home'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-46920650|work=BBC News|date=18 January 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190205073606/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-birmingham-46920650|archive-date=5 February 2019|access-date=20 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Deacon|first=Thomas|title=The mysterious disappearance of a teenager feared murdered after leaving behind her 11-week-old baby|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/wales-news/mysterious-disappearance-teenager-feared-murdered-16104988|work=Wales Online|date=10 April 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201123201933/https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/wales-news/mysterious-disappearance-teenager-feared-murdered-16104988|archive-date=23 November 2020|access-date=20 December 2021}}</ref>

|September 2003
|Shumin Hussain
|[[St Albans]], Hertfordshire
|Hussain, 29, fell to his death from a window of a ninth-floor flat on 7 September 2003 during a fracas in which a number of people were involved.<ref>{{Cite web|title=New plea over Shumin Hussain's 2003 St Albans flat plunge|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-beds-bucks-herts-24036049|website=BBC News|date=10 September 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206192309/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-beds-bucks-herts-24036049|archive-date=6 December 2021|access-date=6 December 2021}}</ref>

|September 2003
|Amir Abdula Bakir
|[[Nottingham]]
|27-year-old Bakir was stabbed to death and a 20-year-old man was stabbed and seriously wounded in a street battle in [[St Ann's, Nottingham|St Ann's]], Nottingham, on 8 September 2003. Described as "tribal warfare", the battle was thought to have been between Iraqi Kurds, and its participants (who possibly numbered as many as 100) had in some cases travelled there from places as far afield as [[Newcastle upon Tyne|Newcastle]], [[Coventry]] (Bakir's home city) and [[Peterborough]]. Two men were acquitted of Bakir's murder, but 28 were convicted of conspiracy to commit violent disorder.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Men jailed after mass brawl|work=Coventry Evening Telegraph|date=20 September 2005|page=3}}</ref>

|September 2003
|Stephen Henry
|[[Bristol]]
|32-year-old Henry was shot dead in an apparent contract killing during the early hours of 14 September 2003 as he was about to get into his car after leaving a nightclub. He was said to have been an underworld enforcer. Nine people were acquitted in 2005 of charges ranging from murder to perverting the course of justice.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wood|first=Alex|title=The mob family enforcer gunned down outside Bristol nightclub in 'contract killing'|url=https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/news/bristol-news/mob-family-enforcer-gunned-down-16509|website=Bristol Live|date=2 April 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210724065218/https://www.bristolpost.co.uk/news/bristol-news/mob-family-enforcer-gunned-down-16509|archive-date=24 July 2021|access-date=12 November 2023}}</ref>

|September/October 2003
|James Brodie
|Body not found
|Brodie was involved in a robbery at an [[Arnold, Nottinghamshire|Arnold]] jewellery shop in which Marian Bates, the woman who co-owned the shop with her husband, was shot dead. Brodie, who was 19 and is believed to have been the one who pulled the trigger, disappeared soon afterwards, and it is thought that his criminal associates killed him because the robbery had not gone as planned.<ref name=Brodie>{{Cite news|title=Marian Bates' widower 'will not find closure'|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-nottinghamshire-24329085|work=BBC News|date=30 September 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131003090209/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-nottinghamshire-24329085|archive-date=3 October 2013|access-date=30 September 2020}}</ref> Brodie had an accomplice when he was in the shop, and in 2005 that man went to prison for Bates's murder, as well as for conspiracy to rob, possession of a firearm with intent to use it and beating her husband with a crowbar.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Teenager guilty of Bates murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/nottinghamshire/4354467.stm|work=BBC News|date=21 March 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091207062200/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/nottinghamshire/4354467.stm|archive-date=7 December 2009|access-date=30 September 2020}}</ref>

In February 2013, another man who had been jailed for conspiring to rob the shop was charged with Brodie's murder,<ref>{{Cite news|title=Man charged over James Brodie murder|url=https://www.itv.com/news/central/update/2013-02-08/man-charged-over-james-brodie-murder|work=ITV News|date=8 February 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140121124046/https://www.itv.com/news/central/update/2013-02-08/man-charged-over-james-brodie-murder|archive-date=21 January 2014|access-date=30 September 2020}}</ref> but failure to gather enough evidence against him led to the charge being dropped in late April of that year.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Murder charge dropped in case of man accused of killing Bulwell man James Brodie|url=https://www.chad.co.uk/news/murder-charge-dropped-in-case-of-man-accused-of-killing-bulwell-man-james-brodie-2343148|work=Chad|date=2 May 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200930211443/https://www.chad.co.uk/news/murder-charge-dropped-case-man-accused-killing-bulwell-man-james-brodie-2343148|archive-date=30 September 2020|access-date=30 September 2020}}</ref>

Police made unsuccessful searches for Brodie's remains at a farm and in a canal in Lincolnshire.<ref name=Brodie/>

|Michael Jones
|[[Bermondsey]], London
|53-year-old Jones received 13 gunshot wounds in the early hours of 16 October 2003 at Bromleigh House, Abbey Street, Bermondsey – apparently after answering the door to his home there. He was shot in the head and abdomen and died at the scene.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Abbey Street murder: renewed appeal|url=https://www.london-se1.co.uk/news/view/1036|website=London SE1 Community Website|date=8 June 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430194441/https://www.london-se1.co.uk/news/view/1036|archive-date=30 April 2024|access-date=30 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Lambert|first=Luke|title=Canvey Island's Mike Jones: 'My criminal father was gunned down and I spent years in foster care...football was my only constant'|url=https://www.echo-news.co.uk/sport/11721219.canvey-islands-mike-jones-my-criminal-father-was-gunned-down-and-i-spent-years-in-foster-carefootball-was-my-only-constant/|website=Basildon Canvey Southend Echo|date=14 January 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430195159/https://www.echo-news.co.uk/sport/11721219.canvey-islands-mike-jones-my-criminal-father-was-gunned-down-and-i-spent-years-in-foster-carefootball-was-my-only-constant/|archive-date=30 April 2024|access-date=30 April 2024}}</ref>

|Eamonn Bloodworth
|Leicester
|46-year-old Bloodworth died on 18 October 2003 after being kicked and stamped on, and his body was found at the junction of Ravensbridge Drive and Blackbird Road. |Ronald Kerr
|Glasgow
|49-year-old Kerr was removed from his home and pronounced dead after firefighters arrived following an arson attack on the property in Lamberton Drive, [[Cardonald]], Glasgow, on 21 October 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Find our dad's killer to end our 4 years of agony|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/12849319.Find-our-dad-apos-s-killer-to-end-our-4-years-of-agony/|website=Glasgow Times|date=23 October 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516213311/https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/12849319.Find-our-dad-apos-s-killer-to-end-our-4-years-of-agony/|archive-date=16 May 2026|access-date=16 May 2026}}</ref>

|[[Charlene Downes]]
|Body not found
|14-year-old Downes went missing from [[Blackpool]] town centre on the night of 1 November 2003. Police believe she was a victim of local grooming and child sexual exploitation. |November 2003
|Jason Stock
|[[Kingston upon Hull|Hull]], East Yorkshire
|33-year-old Stock was found with 66 separate injuries in a ground floor flat on Alexandra Road, Hull, in the early hours of 2 November 2003. |November 2003
|[[Perch Garage murders|Graham and Carol Fisher]]
|Near [[Wadebridge]], Cornwall
|60-year-old Graham Fisher and his 53-year-old wife Carol were bludgeoned and shot – apparently during a failed burglary – at their bungalow near Wadebridge on 5 November 2003. |November 2003
|Omar Watson
|[[Nottingham]]
|Watson, 24, was shot in a [[Radford, Nottingham|Radford]] hair salon and died at the [[Queen's Medical Centre]] on 7 November 2003. |November 2003
|Erkan Konakli
|[[Clapton, London|Clapton]], London
|23-year-old Konakli, a Turkish Cypriot involved in drug trafficking, was last seen in [[Stoke Newington]] on the evening of 7 November 2003 and then killed in a gangland execution, suffering a single bullet wound to the back of the head. His body was found in a barrel in the canal at Clapton later that month.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Schroder|first=Johnathan|title=Missing man found executed|url=https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/434665.missing-man-found-executed/|website=Enfield Independent|date=20 November 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251021173354/https://www.enfieldindependent.co.uk/news/434665.missing-man-found-executed/|archive-date=21 October 2025|access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref> The drug dealer who dumped it there was jailed for four years for attempting to pervert the course of justice, and it was accepted that he played no part in the murder itself. He claimed to have discovered the victim's body in his flat and to have got rid of it because the thought of a police investigation concerned him.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jail for drug dealer who hid body|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4254107.stm|website=BBC News|date=10 February 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251021173801/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4254107.stm|archive-date=21 October 2025|access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref>

|November 2003
|Sandra Gant
|Body not found
|Mother-of-four Gant was last seen leaving an address in Hayes Road, [[Clacton]], Essex, on 15 November 2003. Although she has not been found, [[Essex Police]] believe the 48-year-old was murdered. |Attacked in [[West Kensington]], London, died in hospital

|Peter Stone
|Attacked in [[Cottenham]], Cambridgeshire, died in hospital
|37-year-old Stone, a postman and father-of-two from Cottenham, was attacked near the Chequers pub, where he had been drinking, on the night of 29/30 November 2003. |[[Renton, West Dunbartonshire|Renton]], West Dunbartonshire
|18-year-old Broome was last seen on 3 December 2003. |December 2003
|Leon Forbes
|Attacked in [[Clapham]], London, died in hospital
