|Evelyn Jackson
|Manchester
|97-year-old Jackson was punched and kicked at her flat in the [[Longsight]] area of Manchester on 28 November 2003, and her Christmas savings of £1,000 were stolen. She died from her injuries at a hospital in the city 12 days later.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Family angry after 'revolting' murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/manchester/3309983.stm|website=BBC News|date=11 December 2003|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031213002959/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/manchester/3309983.stm|archive-date=13 December 2003|access-date=20 October 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Fitzgerald|first=Todd|title=Fresh plea to catch 'coward' killer of 97-year-old widow Evelyn Jackson|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/evelyn-jackson-appeal-killer-murder-10812231|website=Manchester Evening News|date=31 January 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160131140339/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/evelyn-jackson-appeal-killer-murder-10812231|archive-date=31 January 2016|access-date=20 October 2023}}</ref>
|-
|December 2003
|Robin Williams
|[[Tottenham]], London
|47-year-old Williams was killed at his home in Lordship Lane, Tottenham, on 31 December 2003. He was battered and stabbed and then left in the bath. Williams was the landlord of a woman who would be acquitted of his murder after two juries could not settle on a verdict, but she was jailed in 2011 for a murder that occurred in December 2010. The second murder was of her ex-partner's 91-year-old father, whose head she battered with a bottle of wine at another property in Tottenham before leaving the residence with money stolen from it.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Robin Williams|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2302|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260520182409/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2302|archive-date=20 May 2026|access-date=20 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Raif|first=Shenai|title=Woman jailed for life for murdering OAP with wine bottle|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/woman-jailed-for-life-for-murdering-oap-with-wine-bottle-2341969.html|website=The Independent|date=22 August 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260210155250/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/woman-jailed-for-life-for-murdering-oap-with-wine-bottle-2341969.html|archive-date=10 February 2026|access-date=20 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Islington woman jailed for murdering pensioner with bottle|url=https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/21245545.islington-woman-jailed-murdering-pensioner-bottle/|website=Islington Gazette|date=25 August 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260520192945/https://www.islingtongazette.co.uk/news/21245545.islington-woman-jailed-murdering-pensioner-bottle/|archive-date=20 May 2026|access-date=20 May 2026}}</ref>
|-
|January 2004
|Richard Barrington
|Attacked in [[Brundall]], Norfolk, died at the Norfolk and Norwich Hospital
|Barrington was pushed into a brick pillar and received a fatal blow to the head or chest as he and some friends were returning to a New Year's Eve party, although it was not witnessed by his companions. The friends claimed that they and Barrington were first set upon by another group of youths after leaving the party to get some tobacco from his home, and that they took a rake, a copper pipe and a baseball bat from there too in case they needed them to defend themselves whilst heading back. The death of 17-year-old Barrington sparked a murder inquiry, but the police later decided that because he was carrying the rake when assaulted, the inquiry would have to be dropped. His inquest, however, found that he was unlawfully killed nonetheless.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Teenager killed in street fight|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/norfolk/3667343.stm|website=BBC News|date=28 April 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904180800/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/norfolk/3667343.stm|archive-date=4 September 2022|access-date=4 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Youth was 'unlawfully killed'|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/norfolk/3669937.stm|website=BBC News|date=29 April 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904180752/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/norfolk/3669937.stm|archive-date=4 September 2022|access-date=4 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Unsolved murders and suspicious deaths in Norfolk|url=https://www.suffolk.police.uk/sites/suffolk/files/002294-18_-_data.xlsx|website=Suffolk Constabulary|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720221627/https://www.suffolk.police.uk/sites/suffolk/files/002294-18_-_data.xlsx|archive-date=20 July 2023|access-date=20 July 2023}}</ref>
|-
|January 2004
|Danny McDonald
|Liverpool
|20-year-old McDonald, a key member of a gang known as the Crocky Crew or the Crocky Young Guns, was in a pub in [[West Derby]] on New Year's Day when a masked man walked over to him and shot him and a 19-year-old friend, who survived.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bona|first=Emilia|title=Hooded gunman blasted 'Crocky Crew leader' in the middle of a busy pub|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/hooded-gunman-blasted-crocky-crew-19612022|website=Liverpool Echo|date=16 January 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302172341/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/hooded-gunman-blasted-crocky-crew-19612022|archive-date=2 March 2021|access-date=17 October 2022}}</ref> Joey Thompson, himself now the victim of an unsolved murder, was a suspect.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Siddle|first=John|title=Murdered Strand Gang henchman Joseph Thompson was a prime suspect into the unsolved killing of a rival gang leader|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/murdered-strand-gang-henchman-joseph-3342291|website=Liverpool Echo|date=15 June 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210119083936/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/murdered-strand-gang-henchman-joseph-3342291|archive-date=19 January 2021|access-date=17 October 2022}}</ref>
|-
|January 2004
|Nureni Sheikh
|Manchester
|Sheikh, a 19-year-old London student on a visit to Manchester for a wedding, was shot in the upper body outside a [[Moss Side]] café on 10 January 2004, likely as a result of being mistaken for another youth.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Akwagyiram|first=Alexis|title=Murder inquiry after man dies in shooting attack|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2004/jan/12/ukguns|website=The Guardian|date=12 January 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226002344/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2004/jan/12/ukguns|archive-date=26 December 2024|access-date=3 May 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Crook|first=Amanda|title=Why was my son left dying in the street?|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/why-was-my-son-left-dying-in-the-street-1031042|website=Manchester Evening News|date=15 February 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503195914/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/why-was-my-son-left-dying-in-the-street-1031042|archive-date=3 May 2022|access-date=3 May 2022}}</ref>
|-
|January 2004
|Orville Donovan Gordon
|[[Beachy Head]], East Sussex
|39-year-old Gordon's body was discovered on 17 January 2004 in a barrel which had been pushed off the cliffs at Beachy Head. Gordon was from south London; he had been stabbed and his blood was found in a disused restaurant in [[Brixton]]. Police believed his murder was revenge for a robbery and three men were arrested, but getting information from witnesses proved very difficult.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Barrel death 'unlawful killing'|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/4166487.stm|website=BBC News|date=11 January 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200102164656/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/4166487.stm|archive-date=2 January 2020|access-date=2 January 2020}}</ref>
|-
|February 2004
|John Luper
|[[Leeds]]
|57-year-old Luper was walking his dog near his home in Alwoodley, Leeds, late on 16 February 2004 when a four- or five-strong gang forced him into the property before stealing about £100,000 worth of cash and valuables. Luper, whose wife, daughter and au pair were tied up during the burglary, was a businessman and died from asphyxiation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cold case detectives review John Luper murder enquiry|url=https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2017-02-16/cold-case-detectives-review-john-luper-murder-enquiry|website=ITV News|date=16 February 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180416232138/https://www.itv.com/news/calendar/2017-02-16/cold-case-detectives-review-john-luper-murder-enquiry|archive-date=16 April 2018|access-date=11 September 2023}}</ref>
|-
|February 2004
|Craig Eaton
|[[Liverpool]]
|22-year-old Eaton worked at [[Alder Hey Children's Hospital]] and was shot shortly after getting off a bus in Molyneux Road, [[Kensington, Liverpool|Kensington]], Liverpool, on 24 February 2004. Merseyside Police believe his murder was a case of mistaken identity.<ref name=ECHO/>
|-
|March 2004
|Camille Gordon
|[[London]]
|23-year-old Gordon was stabbed at her workplace, the Blue Bunny Club in [[Archer Street]], [[Soho]], on 1 March 2004. A man had visited the [[clip joint]] and become involved in a dispute about the payment of his bill, after which he attacked Gordon in the doorway of the club and ran away. She died later that evening at [[University College Hospital]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Reward over club hostess murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/london/4190389.stm|website=BBC News|date=20 January 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130108110343/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4190389.stm|archive-date=8 January 2013|access-date=30 November 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Unsolved 2004 - Camille Gordon|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=be1czbstLOI|website=YouTube|date=3 February 2023|access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref>
|-
|March 2004
|Anton Hyman
|[[River Brent]], London
|17-year-old Hyman's body was found in the River Brent between [[Greenford]] and [[Hanwell]] on 21 March 2004. He had been beaten, shot in the back, slashed across the throat and fatally stabbed in the heart the night before. Police thought the attack had not been committed at random, despite Hyman's criminal record describing only small-scale offending on his part.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Anton Jermaine Hyman|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=223|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240623213118/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=223|archive-date=23 June 2024|access-date=22 August 2026}}</ref>
|-
|April 2004
|Justyn Morgan
|Attacked in [[Walworth]], London, died in hospital
|24-year-old Morgan was shot outside Bagel King (an all-night café on Walworth Road) in the early hours of 13 April 2004 during a disturbance that started inside. Up to 20 youths were involved in the disturbance, and Morgan was shot several times in the chest. A murder trial ground to a halt after it was found that witnesses were unreliable and much of the evidence against the accused man was hearsay or second-hand.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Justyn Morgan|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2398|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009003727/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2398|archive-date=9 October 2024|access-date=10 July 2026}}</ref>
|-
|April 2004
|Ursula Caddock
|Mugged in [[Wanstead]], London, died in hospital
|82-year-old Caddock died on 27 April 2004 from acute [[peritonitis]] triggered by a fall she suffered during a street robbery near her Wanstead residence on 8 April. The mugger stole her handbag and went away before coming back and stealing her bus pass too.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mortlock|first=James|title=Son's heartbreak at mother's murder|url=https://www.eadt.co.uk/news/21314271.sons-heartbreak-mothers-murder/|website=East Anglian Daily Times|date=3 May 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260126201422/https://www.eadt.co.uk/news/21314271.sons-heartbreak-mothers-murder/|archive-date=26 January 2026|access-date=26 January 2026}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>
|-
|May 2004
|Elijah Fagan
|Birmingham
|24-year-old Fagan was punched to the ground and shot in the abdomen on 2 May 2004 after getting involved in an argument with a fellow cyclist in Foxglove Way, [[Handsworth, West Midlands|Handsworth]]. The gunman was then seen riding off in the direction of Alexandra Avenue.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man shot after row with cyclist|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/west_midlands/3679959.stm|website=BBC News|date=3 May 2004|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211223193002/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/west_midlands/3679959.stm|archive-date=23 December 2021|access-date=23 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Balloo|first1=Stephanie|last2=Coussins|first2=Jordan|title=Full list of Birmingham's horrifying unsolved murders over 60 years|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/full-list-birminghams-horrifying-unsolved-18849727|website=Birmingham Live|date=20 September 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201001163759/https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/midlands-news/full-list-birminghams-horrifying-unsolved-18849727|archive-date=1 October 2020|access-date=23 December 2021}}</ref>
|-
|May 2004
|Cheung Shing Cheung
|[[Birkenhead]], Merseyside
|51-year-old Cheung Shing Cheung was officially unemployed but made a living by lending money and charging interest. He left a casino in Liverpool on 13 May 2004 and later spoke to a neighbour before his strangled and battered body was found in his flat on 15 May. Raised voices and a scream were said to have been heard coming from the property during the early hours of 14 May. Two men alleged to have argued with the victim that night were cleared of murder in December 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pair cleared by Liverpool crown court jury over 2004 murder of Cheung Shing Cheung in his Birkenhead flat|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/pair-cleared-liverpool-crown-court-3437273|website=Liverpool Echo|date=23 December 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306141606/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/pair-cleared-liverpool-crown-court-3437273|archive-date=6 March 2021|access-date=9 February 2025}}</ref>
|-
|June 2004
|Adrian Marriott
|[[Brixton]], London
|20-year-old Marriott was shot five times in the head in a park off Barrington Road, Brixton, on 9 June 2004. It was claimed at the trial of three gang members accused of plotting to murder him that they did so because of his refusal to convert to Islam, but the trial came to a premature end when a prosecutor revealed that new evidence meant there was no longer a realistic prospect of any convictions for conspiracy to murder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Trio cleared of conversion killing|url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/article/trio-cleared-of-conversion-killing-9wnx9w3jxn2|url-access=subscription|website=[[The Times]]|date=10 September 2005|access-date=7 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Student killed 'for refusing to convert to Islam'|url=http://www.lse.co.uk/ShowStory.asp?story=LJ421202D&news_headline=student_killed_for_refusing_to_convert_to_islam|website=Life Style Extra|date=4 January 2006|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070819205347/http://www.lse.co.uk/ShowStory.asp?story=LJ421202D&news_headline=student_killed_for_refusing_to_convert_to_islam|archive-date=19 August 2007|access-date=7 April 2024}}</ref>
|-
|June 2004
|Nicholas Davies
|[[Clapham]]<!--source says his body was found in Stockwell, but the alley where the discovery was made appears to be nearer the Clapham end of Landor Road-->, London
|A single bullet had penetrated 25-year-old Davies's lungs and heart when he was found lifeless in an alley off Landor Road, Clapham, on 12 June 2004. A man who was to be acquitted of murder said that the crime had been committed because the victim had developed a habit of attacking and robbing other drug dealers.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Nicholas Davies|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2309|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240407213234/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2309|archive-date=7 April 2024|access-date=7 April 2024}}</ref>
|-
|June 2004
|Kevin Lavelle
|[[Banbury]], Oxfordshire
|29-year-old Lavelle, a father-of-two from [[Bootle]] on Merseyside, was in Banbury on a work contract when he was beaten with a dumbbell at a pub on 24 June 2004. In 2006, a trial was halted and a man found not guilty after the judge had come to the conclusion that it had not been demonstrated that any fatal blows had been delivered by him.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Appeal over 2004 Kevin Lavelle dumbbell killing|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-wales-south-east-wales-27761170|website=BBC News|date=9 June 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140612150356/http://www.bbc.com/news/uk-wales-south-east-wales-27761170|archive-date=12 June 2014|access-date=10 February 2023}}</ref>
|-
|June 2004
|Martin Toner
|[[Langbank]], Renfrewshire
|34-year-old Toner went missing in late June 2004, and his body was discovered by a farmer using a tractor to remove bales of hay from a field on 13 July. Toner had been stabbed about 12 times and had his throat cut, and two men were acquitted of his murder in 2015. A drug-related motive is suspected.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Silvester|first=Norman|title=The Glasgow Crime Story of the murder of Martin Toner|url=https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/19688889.glasgow-crime-story-murder-martin-toner/|website=Glasgow Times|date=3 November 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211106183147/https://www.glasgowtimes.co.uk/news/19688889.glasgow-crime-story-murder-martin-toner/|archive-date=6 November 2021|access-date=21 March 2023}}</ref>
|-
|July 2004
|Azmat Yaqub
|Birmingham
|Yaqub, 35, was in a gym in [[Sparkhill]] on 29 July 2004 when two men with machine guns entered the building and one of them shot him dead. Detectives were unable to find a link between this incident and a shooting in March 2003 that Yaqub survived.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Unsolved: New dad shot dead as he worked out at his gym|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/local-news/unsolved-new-dad-shot-dead-124301|website=Birmingham Live|date=6 May 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002143310/https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/local-news/unsolved-new-dad-shot-dead-124301|archive-date=2 October 2020|access-date=13 September 2022}}</ref>
|-
|July 2004
|Richard Clarke
|[[Leeds]]
|Clarke, 32, was shot at point-blank range as he slept at his home in Moorland Avenue, Leeds, on the night of 29 July 2004. The weapon used was a 12-bore shotgun. Clarke's girlfriend was sleeping next to him at the time of the attack and her three teenage sons were also in the house.<ref>{{Cite web|title=New appeal after man shot in head|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/west_yorkshire/4731125.stm|website=BBC News|date=30 July 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201207222110/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/west_yorkshire/4731125.stm|archive-date=7 December 2020|access-date=20 November 2020}}</ref>
|-
|August 2004
|Tom Brown
|[[Southgate, London|Southgate]], London
|27-year-old Brown, a BBC library assistant, was stabbed as he walked home along Southgate High Street in the early hours of 21 August 2004, but none of his belongings were stolen. An e-fit of the suspected perpetrator was issued.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/3603878.stm|title=Reward offered in BBC murder case|date=27 August 2004|website=BBC News|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200626202722/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/3603878.stm|archive-date=26 June 2020|access-date=26 June 2020}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>
|-
|August/September 2004
|[[Lamduan Armitage]]
|Near [[Pen-y-ghent]], North Yorkshire
|The body of Armitage, a Thai woman in her mid-30s, was found in a stream in the [[Yorkshire Dales]] on 20 September 2004. She had died in an undetermined manner a week to three weeks earlier. Armitage's husband was bailed in February 2025 after he had returned to the UK from Thailand and been arrested on suspicion of her murder.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Jones|first=Steve|title=Husband bailed over Thai woman's 2004 death|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3w83p86w25o|website=BBC News|date=4 February 2025|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251025205905/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3w83p86w25o|archive-date=25 October 2025|access-date=25 October 2025}}</ref>
|-
|c. September 2004
|Aivaras Danilevičius
|[[Bracknell]], Berkshire
|A body was found wrapped in bin bags and a blanket in Hawthorn Lane, Bracknell, on 24 July 2015. The skull was found to have two injuries indicating blunt-force trauma. The man was thought to have been 30–40 years old at the time of his death, but it is still not known how his body got to Hawthorn Lane or who put it there.<ref>{{Cite web|title=BBC One - Crimewatch, 14/12/2015 - Bracknell Body|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/profiles/2nvPV27X2mhY5ljYtkbj91X/bracknell-body|website=BBC|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160627190805/https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/profiles/2nvPV27X2mhY5ljYtkbj91X/bracknell-body|archive-date=27 June 2016|access-date=28 January 2016}}</ref> In July 2016 he was identified as Aivaras Danilevičius, a [[Lithuania]]n who had gone missing towards the end of the summer of 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Hill|first=Louise|title=Victim identified as Lithuanian man Aivaras Danilevicius who lived in UK for eight years before his murder in summer 2004|url=https://www.bracknellnews.co.uk/news/14636152.victim-identified-as-lithuanian-man-aivaras-danilevicius-who-lived-in-uk-for-eight-years-before-his-murder-in-summer-2004/|website=Bracknell News|date=22 July 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226002503/https://www.bracknellnews.co.uk/news/14636152.victim-identified-as-lithuanian-man-aivaras-danilevicius-who-lived-in-uk-for-eight-years-before-his-murder-in-summer-2004/|archive-date=26 December 2024|access-date=25 July 2016}}</ref>
|-
|September 2004
|Patrick Devine
|[[Claudy]], County Londonderry, [[Northern Ireland]]
|Devine was found shot dead in his home at Stranagalwilly on 13 September 2004. The 51-year-old was a sheep farmer and part-time nurse. He was shot six times through a window as he ate his dinner and then at point-blank range three times in the head with a .22 rifle.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Jackson|first=George|title=Inquest told farmer shot in head at point blank range|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/inquest-told-farmer-shot-in-head-at-point-blank-range-1.567775|newspaper=The Irish Times|date=10 March 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119121444/https://www.irishtimes.com/news/inquest-told-farmer-shot-in-head-at-point-blank-range-1.567775|archive-date=19 January 2019|access-date=19 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Patrick Devine murder: Brother offers £50,000 reward for information|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-northern-ireland-29157201|website=BBC News|date=12 September 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119182851/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-northern-ireland-29157201|archive-date=19 January 2019|access-date=19 January 2019}}</ref>
|-
|September 2004
|Daniel Blackett
|Attacked in [[Thorpe, Surrey|Thorpe Green]], died in hospital in [[Chertsey]] (both in Surrey)
|Blackett, a 36-year-old millionaire, was shot five times on his {{convert|4|acre|adj=on}} estate on 18 September 2004, despite having recently had a {{convert|10|ft|adj=on}} fence put up around the edge of it along with signs warning of guard dogs and CCTV. It was a murder believed to have been committed or ordered by someone keen for him to be eliminated as a rival in crime.<ref>{{Cite web|last=McKeon|first=Christopher|title=Unsolved murders in Surrey: Hitmen, gangsters, unexplained disappearances and miscarriages of justice|url=https://www.getsurrey.co.uk/news/surrey-news/unsolved-murders-surrey-hitmen-gangsters-14918873|website=Surrey Live|date=22 July 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210619084116/https://www.getsurrey.co.uk/news/surrey-news/unsolved-murders-surrey-hitmen-gangsters-14918873|archive-date=19 June 2021|access-date=13 May 2024}}</ref>
|-
|September 2004
|Mick Love
|[[Swindon]], Wiltshire
|40-year-old Love was stabbed to death in the street in Swindon's Old Town during the early hours of 27 September 2004 less than half an hour after the postal worker and a friend had parted company. When his body was discovered, money that he had had on him was now missing, as was his mobile phone. A man charged with Love's murder and with robbery was not found guilty of either.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Benke|first=Mike|title=Mick Love's widow speaks out 10 years after his tragic murder|url=https://www.swindonadvertiser.co.uk/news/11501076.mick-loves-widow-speaks-out-10-years-after-his-tragic-murder/|website=Swindon Advertiser|date=29 September 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200908205353/https://www.swindonadvertiser.co.uk/news/11501076.mick-loves-widow-speaks-out-10-years-after-his-tragic-murder/|archive-date=8 September 2020|access-date=8 September 2020}}</ref>
|-
|October 2004
|Warren Graham
|Attacked in [[Clapton, London|Clapton]], London, died in hospital
|18-year-old Graham was stabbed in Lower Clapton Road's Palace Pavilion nightclub on 26 October 2004 after a row about control of the microphone started between a friend of his and other youths on the stage.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Rasiah|first=Janine|title=Mother renews plea for help finding son's killer|url=https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/21446966.mother-renews-plea-help-finding-sons-killer/|website=Newham Recorder|date=21 October 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220424200816/https://www.newhamrecorder.co.uk/news/mother-renews-plea-for-help-finding-son-s-killer-3005472|archive-date=24 April 2022|access-date=24 April 2022}}</ref>
|-
|November 2004
|Paul Mooney
|Liverpool
|A gunshot fired from close range killed 35-year-old Mooney at a friend's bungalow in [[Croxteth]] on 13 November 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|title='Riddle' of why man shot dead|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/riddle-man-shot-dead-3520076|website=Liverpool Echo|date=21 April 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210530180334/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/riddle-man-shot-dead-3520076|archive-date=30 May 2021|access-date=30 May 2021}}</ref> Three men were found not guilty of murder or conspiracy to murder, and in October 2016, one of them – Blake Brown – was himself shot dead. The killing of Brown is likewise an unsolved murder at present.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Thomas|first=Joe|title=Murder victim was allowed to return home despite police fears it would lead to gangland trouble|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/murder-victim-allowed-return-home-18885273|website=Liverpool Echo|date=7 September 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002014221/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/murder-victim-allowed-return-home-18885273|archive-date=2 October 2020|access-date=30 May 2021}}</ref>
|-
|November 2004
|[[Murder of Alistair Wilson|Alistair Wilson]]
|Attacked in [[Nairn]], died in hospital in [[Inverness]] (both in the Scottish Highlands)
|30-year-old Wilson was shot on the doorstep of his home in Crescent Road, Nairn, near Inverness, in the evening of 28 November 2004 after his wife opened their front door to the killer. Police were not aware of a motive.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kelbie|first=Paul|title=One year on, who killed Alistair Wilson?|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/one-year-on-who-killed-alistair-wilson-517368.html|website=The Independent|date=29 November 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170831013919/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/one-year-on-who-killed-alistair-wilson-517368.html|archive-date=31 August 2017|access-date=12 August 2009}}</ref> Detectives remain puzzled by some peculiarities of the case. Prior to shooting Wilson, the killer asked for him by name, then handed him an empty envelope with "Paul" written on it. Wilson took it inside and showed it to his wife before returning to the door where he was gunned down. The envelope was taken away by the killer when he fled.<ref>{{Cite web|last=McAlinden|first=Mona|title=The mysterious envelope and the death of Alistair Wilson|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-highlands-islands-42056011|website=BBC News|date=27 November 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180604223634/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-highlands-islands-42056011|archive-date=4 June 2018|access-date=27 April 2022}}</ref> Police revealed that the weapon was a rare 1920s CG Haenel Waffen pistol, referred to as a "ladies' gun", and manufactured in [[Suhl]], Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|title=1920s East German pistol used in Nairn killing|url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/1920s-east-german-pistol-used-in-nairn-killing-2507122|website=[[The Scotsman]]|date=13 April 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160110204137/http://www.scotsman.com/news/1920s-east-german-pistol-used-in-nairn-killing-1-707687|archive-date=10 January 2016|access-date=20 May 2013}}</ref> In April 2022, Police Scotland announced that Wilson's involvement in a local planning dispute was a likely motive for his murder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police probe planning dispute in Nairn doorstep murder|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-highlands-islands-61215644|website=BBC News|date=26 April 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220427013907/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-highlands-islands-61215644|archive-date=27 April 2022|access-date=27 April 2022}}</ref>
|-
|December 2004
|Courtney Davies
|[[Forest of Dean]], Gloucestershire
|A burnt body discovered in the Forest of Dean on 20 December 2004 was that of 53-year-old Davies, a violent career criminal previously jailed for robbery. The body had over 70 stab wounds. A 32-year-old man was charged with murder following the discovery of his DNA on a cigarette end recovered at the scene, but proceedings ended and he was acquitted at a preliminary hearing in April 2006. He had admitted driving the deceased to the forest on 19 December 2004 but always denied involvement in his death.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bevan|first=Nathan|title=Gory gangland murder left my life in tatters|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/wales-news/gory-gangland-murder-left-life-2325236|website=Wales Online|date=2 July 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220409220519/https://www.walesonline.co.uk/news/wales-news/gory-gangland-murder-left-life-2325236|archive-date=9 April 2022|access-date=9 April 2022}}</ref>
|-
|December 2004
|Joey Peloe
|Attacked in [[Speke]], Liverpool, died at [[Whiston Hospital]]
|45-year-old Peloe was shot on 28 December 2004 at the front door of his house on Little Heath Road. In 2006, two men – one of whom had a girlfriend for whom Peloe was said to have been a love rival – were acquitted of his murder and a third of incitement to cause grievous bodily harm.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Siddle|first=John|title='We know the scumbags who killed our Joey' - Peloe brother speaks on 10th anniversary of unsolved Speke murder|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/we-know-scumbags-who-killed-8355399|website=Liverpool Echo|date=29 December 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230042419/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/we-know-scumbags-who-killed-8355399|archive-date=30 December 2014|access-date=14 March 2022}}</ref>
|-
|December 2004
|Solomon Martin
|[[Thornton Heath]], London
|24-year-old Martin died when the Renault Clio he was a backseat passenger in was shot at repeatedly on 31 December 2004. Police believed that the gunmen actually meant to kill the driver, who was not harmed in the attack.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Davenport|first=Justin|title=We must unite to stop guns|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/hp/front/we-must-unite-to-stop-guns-7167711.html|website=Evening Standard|date=7 February 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191102122247/https://www.standard.co.uk/news/we-must-unite-to-stop-guns-7167711.html|archive-date=2 November 2019|access-date=13 July 2020}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>

|January 2005
|Benjamin Onwuka
|Attacked in [[North Kensington]]<!--BBC News source incorrectly gives the location as Harlesden-->, London, died in hospital
|24-year-old Onwuka was shot in the head in Maxilla Walk, North Kensington, on the afternoon of 2 January 2005. Four arrests took place of men in London and Surrey and a reward of £10,000 was offered, but the case is still unsolved.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Reward offered after man's murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4552030.stm|website=BBC News|date=22 December 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816201900/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4552030.stm|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>
|-
|January 2005
|Khang Tho Nguyen
|[[Wembley]], London
|42-year-old Nguyen was stabbed in the neck about two weeks before being found dead on 15 January 2005 at a house that was used as a cannabis factory. The Vietnamese victim did not reside at the property but was believed to have had some involvement in the drug's cultivation there.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Khang Tho Nguyen|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=237|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816202431/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=237|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref>

|January 2005
|Sher "Lenny" Afzal
|[[Reading, Berkshire|Reading]], Berkshire
|Afzal, a 38-year-old drug dealer, died three days after being wounded in a drive-by shooting at [[Cemetery Junction, Reading|Cemetery Junction]] in Reading on 14 January 2005. Two men faced two trials for his murder, with the final trial coming to an end in July 2008 when no evidence was offered by the prosecution and the jury was ordered by the judge to find both suspects not guilty. The judge voiced concerns over the disclosure process, too.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cassell|first=Paul|title=Drug drive-by trial collapses|url=https://www.getreading.co.uk/news/local-news/drug-drive-by-trial-collapses-4250712|website=Berkshire Live|date=24 July 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022060349/https://www.getreading.co.uk/news/local-news/drug-drive-by-trial-collapses-4250712|archive-date=22 October 2020|access-date=19 May 2024}}</ref>
|-
|January 2005
|Junior Edwards
|[[Archway, London|Archway]], London
|30-year-old Edwards died at Whittington Hospital in Archway on the evening of 18 January 2005 about an hour after being found injured in nearby Spears Road following a fight with two men described as being in the 20–30 age bracket. A single stab wound was the cause of his death, but he had also been punched and knocked to the ground.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police name man stabbed in street|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4190225.stm|website=BBC News|date=20 January 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816202848/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4190225.stm|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Reward over street fight murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/london/4622686.stm|website=BBC News|date=17 January 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816203426/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4622686.stm|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref>

|January 2005
|[[Murder of Robert McCartney|Robert McCartney]]
|[[Belfast]], Northern Ireland
|On 30 January 2005, 33-year-old McCartney and a friend were followed outside from a bar in Belfast city centre and then beaten and stabbed in Market Street after a fight inside the establishment. McCartney died nine hours later, but his friend survived. Allegations have been made, particularly by relatives of McCartney, that members of the [[Irish Republican Army|IRA]] were involved in both the murder and a subsequent cover-up.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Breen|first=Suzanne|title=McCartney sisters say case closed: 'Jock Davison entered our lives uninvited and took Robert's life'|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/northern-ireland/mccartney-sisters-say-case-closed-jock-davison-entered-our-lives-uninvited-and-took-roberts-life-31202133.html|website=Belfast Telegraph|date=7 May 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211123184930/https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/northern-ireland/mccartney-sisters-say-case-closed-jock-davison-entered-our-lives-uninvited-and-took-roberts-life-31202133.html|archive-date=23 November 2021|access-date=23 November 2021}}</ref>
|-
|February 2005
|Justin Bernier
|[[Clapham]], London
|20-year-old Bernier was found stabbed to death at his flat in Clapham Road, Clapham, on Monday 21 February 2005. A police appeal three days later stressed the importance of speaking to those who had been in the area late the previous Saturday or early on the Sunday that followed.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Stern|first=James|title=Clapham man stabbed to death at home|url=https://www.london-now.co.uk/news/573197.clapham-man-stabbed-to-death-at-home/|website=London Now|date=24 February 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816213837/https://www.thisislocallondon.co.uk/news/573197.clapham-man-stabbed-to-death-at-home/|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>
|-
|March 2005
|Bruno Hrela
|[[Enfield, London|Enfield]], London
|33-year-old Hrela was shot twice in the head and discovered next to his Mercedes in Cedar Avenue, Enfield, on 5 March 2005. He was thought to have been murdered in a contract killing and to have been involved in the sale of stolen goods.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Bruno Hrela|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=242|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816211512/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=242|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref>
|-
|March 2005
|Shaun Stanislas
|[[Stonebridge, London|Stonebridge]], London
|24-year-old Stanislas was shot dead in Stonebridge on 22 March 2005. The attack was said to have been carried out because he was rumoured to have been responsible for the non-fatal shooting of a man the previous month. A man was sentenced to a minimum of 25 years in prison in September 2007 for being complicit in the fatal July 2006 shooting of a suspect in Stanislas's murder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man denies murdering Wembley father|url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/1571891.man-denies-murdering-wembley-father/|website=Harrow Times|date=25 July 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816214849/https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/1571891.man-denies-murdering-wembley-father/|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Man jailed for school-run murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6998200.stm|website=BBC News|date=17 September 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816213221/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6998200.stm|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref>
|-
|March 2005
|Orville Davidson
|[[New Cross]], London
|[[Purley, London|Purley]] resident Davidson, 25, was found in Knoyle Street, New Cross, on 27 March 2005 (Easter Sunday) after being shot through the heart. His death preceded by four months the murder of his friend Peter Buahin – another unsolved case.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Orville Davidson|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2208&termRef=Orville%20Davidson|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020105457/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=2208&termRef=Orville%20Davidson|archive-date=20 October 2020|access-date=31 December 2022}}</ref>

|April 2005
|Wayne Kelly
|[[West Hendon]], London
|21-year-old Kelly fell and hit his head outside the Harp pub in West Hendon on 10 April 2005 after being punched by a bouncer. He fell as he was being chased following his intervention in an argument between bouncers and two other men, and although three men were later arrested on suspicion of his murder, there was not enough evidence to try any of them.<ref>{{Cite web|last=King|first=Lorraine|title=Coroner rules Neasden man who died in pub fight was unlawfully killed|url=https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/22039541.coroner-rules-neasden-man-died-pub-fight-unlawfully-killed/|website=Brent & Kilburn Times|date=1 June 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240730213436/https://www.kilburntimes.co.uk/news/22039541.coroner-rules-neasden-man-died-pub-fight-unlawfully-killed/|archive-date=30 July 2024|access-date=30 July 2024}}</ref>
|-
|April 2005
|Chamlong Allen
|[[Notting Hill]], London
|Allen was found dead with multiple stab wounds in a lockup garage on Lonsdale Mews on 27 April 2005. The garage was close to the site of Portobello Market, where the 49-year-old Thai woman had sold food from a stall for a living. Allen's estranged husband, a retired actor who she had told people had abused her and whom she had been fighting for custody of their three daughters, was charged with her murder within days of the crime coming to the attention of the police, but he was acquitted at the [[Old Bailey]] after prosecutors had ceased to offer evidence.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bond actor is charged with murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/4502525.stm|website=BBC News|date=30 April 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240112233419/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/4502525.stm|archive-date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bond actor 'slit wife's throat'|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/london/4689550.stm|website=BBC News|date=7 February 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240112233413/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4689550.stm|archive-date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Former Bond villain cleared of murdering his wife|url=https://www.mi6-hq.com/news/index.php?itemid=3361|website=MI6 - The Home of James Bond 007|date=16 February 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240112233409/https://www.mi6-hq.com/news/index.php?itemid=3361|archive-date=12 January 2024|access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>
|-
|May 2005
|Vikki Preston and Rhona Schofield
|[[Salford]], Greater Manchester
|Preston and Schofield, both 19, were best friends who were killed by toxic fumes from a fire in the terraced house where they were staying in the early hours of 10 May 2005. The property was on King Street, Higher Broughton, Salford, and the victims were in an upstairs bedroom when the blaze was triggered by furniture being lit downstairs at around 4:00 a.m. Preston and another woman had a violent row the day before and that woman was said to have later uttered a threat against the pair, but she denied any role in the blaze when she attended their inquest hearing.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Keeling|first=Neal|title=The haunting images from an unsolved double murder which shattered two families|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/haunting-images-unsolved-double-murder-21115314|website=Manchester Evening News|date=2 August 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210802182946/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/haunting-images-unsolved-double-murder-21115314|archive-date=2 August 2021|access-date=14 March 2024}}</ref>
|-
|June 2005
|June Thrussell
|[[Dagenham]], London
|56-year-old Thrussell was found strangled to death in her home on Friday 17 June 2005 after one of her colleagues had notified the police that she had not turned up for her work as a secretary since Tuesday of that week.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Woman found strangled in own home|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4108362.stm|website=BBC News|date=19 June 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921102808/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4108362.stm|archive-date=21 September 2020|access-date=5 November 2021}}</ref> A man who had been convicted in 1976 of a murder committed the year before was cleared of Thrussell's murder but went back to prison despite that because there were concerns that he was still a danger to others.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Shirinian|first=Zjan|title=Man jailed for 1975 murder of Ilford neighbour appeals to be released|url=https://www.ilfordrecorder.co.uk/news/crime/21213016.man-jailed-1975-murder-ilford-neighbour-appeals-released/|website=Ilford Recorder|date=17 October 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211106133423/https://www.ilfordrecorder.co.uk/news/crime/man-jailed-for-1975-murder-of-ilford-neighbour-appeals-to-2933278|archive-date=6 November 2021|access-date=5 November 2021}}</ref>
|-
|June 2005
|Troy Robinson
|[[Stonebridge, London|Stonebridge]], London
|A group of people were standing outside James Dudson Court in Wyborne Way, Stonebridge, at around 9:45 p.m. on 19 June 2005 when one or more men got out of a car that had just pulled up and randomly fired bullets at them. 19-year-old Robinson was shot in the chest and pronounced dead on arrival at a hospital nearby; two other men in their late teens received gunshot wounds to their legs and survived.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Treanor|first=Tracey|title=Triple shooting: police appeal for witnesses|url=https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/609947.triple-shooting-police-appeal-for-witnesses/|website=Harrow Times|date=29 June 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114062638/https://www.harrowtimes.co.uk/news/609947.triple-shooting-police-appeal-for-witnesses/|archive-date=14 January 2025|access-date=14 January 2025}}</ref> A man was paralysed from the neck down a year later in a shooting suspected to have been a revenge attack for Robinson's murder.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Young gunman given life sentence|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6919354.stm|website=BBC News|date=27 July 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250114063136/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6919354.stm|archive-date=14 January 2025|access-date=14 January 2025}}</ref>
|-
|June 2005
|Bill Marney
|[[Crayford]], London
|39-year-old Marney lived in Mill Place in Crayford and was shot outside his home on 23 June 2005 by a man in a dark hatchback that was probably a Rover 45 or a Peugeot. There was another man in the vehicle besides the shooter.<ref>{{Cite web|title=New appeal over man's murder|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/1479629.new-appeal-over-mans-murder/|website=News Shopper|date=18 June 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230210222114/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/1479629.new-appeal-over-mans-murder/|archive-date=10 February 2023|access-date=10 February 2023}}</ref>
|-
|July 2005
|Peter Buahin
|[[New Cross]], London
|Buahin, 23, was shot in the head on 25 July 2005 after being approached by two men as he sat on his bicycle in Woodpecker Road, New Cross. The murder happened after that of Orville Davidson – a friend of his – in March 2005, and both remain unsolved.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Breakthrough hopes over murder|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6069994.stm|website=BBC News|date=20 October 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061107110819/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/london/6069994.stm|archive-date=7 November 2006|access-date=31 December 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Keel|first=Dan|title=NEW CROSS: Mother speaks out over Woodpecker estate unsolved murders|url=https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/5054914.new-cross-mother-speaks-out-over-woodpecker-estate-unsolved-murders/|website=News Shopper|date=11 March 2010|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190806064414/https://www.newsshopper.co.uk/news/5054914.new-cross-mother-speaks-out-over-woodpecker-estate-unsolved-murders/|archive-date=6 August 2019|access-date=31 December 2022}}</ref>

|July/August 2005
|Newton Thompson
|[[Paddington, London|Paddington]], London
|61-year-old Thompson, an Australian tourist, was found battered to death in his room at the Comfort Inn hotel on 1 August 2005. Property belonging to him had been taken, too. Because a child sex abuser who was also from Australia and had also recently come to the UK bore a strong resemblance to Thompson, it was believed that the murder might have been a case of mistaken identity.<ref>{{Cite web|title='Mistaken identity' murder clue|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/london/4165582.stm|website=BBC News|date=19 August 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240519184038/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/4165582.stm|archive-date=19 May 2024|access-date=19 May 2024}}</ref><ref name=MetFOI/>

|August 2005
|Lucy Hargreaves
|[[Liverpool]]
|Three masked men armed with a sawn-off shotgun forced their way into 22-year-old Hargreaves's house on Lambourne Road, [[Walton, Liverpool|Walton]], on 3 August 2005 while she was asleep on the living room sofa. She was then shot twice in the abdomen and once in the head at point-blank range before petrol was poured at various locations downstairs and ignited. Hargreaves's boyfriend, who it is thought might have been the intended target, escaped from the burning property by jumping with the couple's youngest daughter from an upstairs window. They were asleep upstairs when the perpetrators gained access.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Traynor|first=Luke|title=A young mum was shot dead on the sofa as her kids slept upstairs. Why has nobody ever been brought to justice?|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/young-mum-shot-dead-sofa-14956976|website=Liverpool Echo|date=3 August 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022102108/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/young-mum-shot-dead-sofa-14956976|archive-date=22 October 2020|access-date=19 January 2019}}</ref>

|August 2005
|James Tomlin
|[[Shipley, West Yorkshire|Shipley]], West Yorkshire
|36-year-old Tomlin went into cardiac arrest and died during the early hours of 15 August after jumping from a bedroom window at his home in [[Windhill and Wrose|Windhill]] to escape a fire that began when kerosene was poured through the letterbox and ignited. However, it was not heart failure or the fall that caused his death, but the inhaling of smoke and poisonous gasses. Also inside the property were Tomlin's pregnant 26-year-old partner and their two sons, who all escaped and survived. Because the arson attack was a seemingly motiveless crime against a family with no criminal ties, detectives considered it a possibility that the property was not the intended target.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wright|first=Steve|title=Detectives appeal for clues over unsolved arson murder|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/13599270.detectives-appeal-for-clues-over-unsolved-arson-murder/|website=Telegraph & Argus|date=15 August 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230613200054/https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/13599270.detectives-appeal-for-clues-over-unsolved-arson-murder/|archive-date=13 June 2023|access-date=13 June 2023}}</ref>

|September 2005
|Kenneth Nunn
|[[Whittlesford]], Cambridgeshire
|85-year-old Nunn died in an apparent arson attack on his home in Whittlesford on the night of 6–7 September 2005. |Attacked in [[Abermorddu]], Flintshire, died in hospital in [[Wrexham]]

|Anne Marie Foy
|Liverpool
|46-year-old Foy was killed at around 5:30 a.m. on 15 September 2005. Her body was found in bushes at the junction of Crown Street and West Derby Street in Liverpool; she had been battered to death. |September/October 2005
|George Willis
|[[Peckham]], London
|Willis's bus pass and flying jacket appeared to have been taken from his Torridge Gardens home when he was discovered tied up and dead from head injuries there on 6 October 2005. He was last seen alive eight days previously, arguing on his doorstep with a man thought to have been in his 20s. It came to be suspected that the murder of 84-year-old Willis, a bachelor who often tried to make friends by giving money to strangers, might have been a homophobic crime carried out by people who assumed that being a lifelong unmarried man meant he was gay.<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=George Edward Willis|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=252|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240627203604/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=252|archive-date=27 June 2024|access-date=27 June 2024}}</ref>

|October 2005
|Anthony Cavanagh
|Liverpool
|22-year-old Cavanagh was knocked to the ground in a single punch on Saturday 24 September 2005 after bumping into another man in a bar in central Liverpool earlier in the night, and his death occurred in hospital 11 days later. An arrest over Cavanagh's murder was made in 2015, but the arrested man was not charged.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Duffy|first=Tom|title=Young man killed outside Liverpool bar after accidentally spilling a drink|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/young-man-killed-outside-liverpool-21746705|website=Liverpool Echo|date=3 October 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003192551/https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/young-man-killed-outside-liverpool-21746705|archive-date=3 October 2021|access-date=15 January 2022}}</ref>

|October 2005
|Nora Tait
|[[Doncaster]], South Yorkshire
|Tait was 69 when she was bludgeoned at her home in Stone Close Avenue, [[Hexthorpe]], on 12 October 2005. She was murdered shortly after she had bought fish and chips, which were untouched on her dining table when a friend found her dead the following day. Police made a new appeal for information on the 10th anniversary of Tait's murder in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police renew appeal over murder of Doncaster grandmother Nora Tait|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-34516656|website=BBC News|date=13 October 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161213102552/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-south-yorkshire-34516656|archive-date=13 December 2016|access-date=2 February 2020}}</ref>

|October 2005
|Alexandre Marques
|[[Luton]], Bedfordshire
|Marques, 61, was last seen at his home in Clanricarde Gardens, [[Notting Hill]], London, on Sunday 16 October 2005. His remains were found on 2 January 2006 on the grass verge of Woodside Road, Luton. CCTV images showed a man using Marques's bank card in west and northwest London shortly after his disappearance. In January 2021, police reported that they had a new forensic lead and that a £20,000 reward was still available.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Shepka|first=Phil|title=London waiter murder: Man using cards 'critical' to inquiry|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-beds-bucks-herts-55681317|website=BBC News|date=24 January 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408161124/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-beds-bucks-herts-55681317|archive-date=8 April 2023|access-date=26 January 2021}}</ref>

|October 2005
|Isaiah Young-Sam
|Birmingham
|23-year-old Young-Sam and three companions were in a backstreet in [[Lozells]] on 22 October 2005 when a group of Asian men confronted them and one of them fatally stabbed him in the chest. Race riots were going on in the area at the time, triggered by an unsubstantiated rumour that Asians had gang-raped a black girl.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Britten|first=Nick|title=Asian race riot killers jailed for 25 years|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1519134/Asian-race-riot-killers-jailed-for-25-years.html|website=The Telegraph|date=23 May 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170610175920/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/1519134/Asian-race-riot-killers-jailed-for-25-years.html|archive-date=10 June 2017|access-date=15 March 2024}}</ref> Two trials resulted in four convictions for Young-Sam's murder, but each conviction was overturned by April 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Isaiah Young-Sam: Lozells riot murder accused cleared|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-13133782|website=BBC News|date=19 April 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240315233113/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-13133782|archive-date=15 March 2024|access-date=15 March 2024}}</ref>

|November 2005
|Andrea Daly
|[[Southend]], Essex
|40-year-old Daly died when her house on Rochford Road, Southend, was set alight at nighttime on 10 November 2005. Her sons, who were aged 17 and 20, managed to escape from the smoke and flames by jumping from a first-floor window. Police could not find a motive.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Kane|first=Hannah|title=Murder of Southend mum Andrea Daly still remains a mystery 12 years on|url=https://www.essexlive.news/news/essex-news/murder-southend-mum-andrea-daly-757706|work=Essex Live|date=10 November 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200828180614/https://www.essexlive.news/news/essex-news/murder-southend-mum-andrea-daly-757706|archive-date=28 August 2020|access-date=28 August 2020}}</ref>

|November 2005
|Michael Grey
|[[Newcastle upon Tyne|Newcastle]]
|45-year-old care worker Grey was walking to the home of an elderly person he cared for on 11 November 2005 when he was attacked on Ellesmere Road in Newcastle's West End at around 8:00 p.m. Grey's wallet was taken during the attack. He managed to get to his feet afterwards and sought treatment at [[Newcastle General Hospital]], but he fell into a coma and died 10 days later. Three people were charged with theft from Grey, but no one was charged with his murder.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Doughty|first=Sophie|title=Killers at large: The horrifying North East murder cases that remain unsolved|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/north-east-news/killers-large-horrifying-north-east-15463353|website=Chronicle Live|date=29 December 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181230114347/https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/north-east-news/killers-large-horrifying-north-east-15463353|archive-date=30 December 2018|access-date=24 November 2019}}</ref>

|Kamila Garsztka
|[[Bedford]]
|Garsztka was 26 when she went missing in mid-December 2005. Her body was found by canoeists in Priory Lake, Bedford, in January 2006. |[[Hallam Tennyson (radio producer)|Hallam Tennyson]]
|[[Highgate]], London
|85-year-old Tennyson, a retired author and former BBC employee, was stabbed to death in his home in Highgate on 21 December 2005 shortly after being filmed by CCTV at two London tube stations. He was the great-grandson of [[Alfred, Lord Tennyson]], a 19th-century [[poet laureate]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The unsolved murder of Hallam Tennyson|url=https://www.murdermap.co.uk/unsolved-murders/hallam-tennyson-murder-unsolved/|website=murdermap.co.uk|date=19 January 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240213225123/https://www.murdermap.co.uk/unsolved-murders/hallam-tennyson-murder-unsolved/|archive-date=13 February 2024|access-date=13 February 2024}}</ref>

|Barrington Williams-Samuels
|[[Clapton, London|Clapton]], London
|19-year-old Williams-Samuels was shot and killed in his car outside the Palace Pavilion, a nightclub on Lower Clapton Road, early on Monday 2 January 2006. |Ralph Platten
|Attacked in [[Sutton, Norfolk|Sutton]], Norfolk, died at the Norfolk and Norwich Hospital
|A group of men pushed past the 95-year-old war veteran and beat him when he opened his front door on 3 January 2006; he died of heart failure the next day. |[[Willesden]], London
|Likely the victim of a ritual killing, 44-year-old Sivakumar was found dead in his shop with a shoelace around his neck and wounds behind one of his ears on 5 January 2006.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Shopkeeper death still a mystery|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6214699.stm|work=BBC News|date=28 December 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081213042133/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6214699.stm|archive-date=13 December 2008|access-date=22 June 2020}}</ref>

|Joyce Sutton
|[[Skewen]], Wales
|Sutton, 65, was found dead in her bed at her home in Winifred Road, Skewen, on 11 January 2006. She had been beaten to death. |January 2006
|Rebwar Samin
|[[Leicester]]
|Samin, 21, was stabbed in Clyde Street, Leicester, at around 5:00 p.m. on 11 January 2006 when he and another man were involved in a confrontation with two men that had escalated. Police suspected early on in their investigation into his murder that the two people they most wanted to speak to about it (men who were Iraqi nationals, as was Samin) did not live in Leicestershire any longer.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Suspects sought over young man's murder|url=https://www.kentonline.co.uk/kent/news/suspects-sought-over-young-mans-a23365/|website=KentOnline|date=23 March 2006|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231104213955/https://www.kentonline.co.uk/kent/news/suspects-sought-over-young-mans-a23365/|archive-date=4 November 2023|access-date=4 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Watson|first=Hayley|title=5 mystery deaths in Leicester that have never been solved|url=https://www.leicestermercury.co.uk/news/leicester-news/deaths-leicester-unsolved-1375632|website=Leicestershire Live|date=22 August 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706215008/https://www.leicestermercury.co.uk/news/leicester-news/deaths-leicester-unsolved-1375632|archive-date=6 July 2020|access-date=4 November 2023}}</ref>

|Sukhwinder Singh
|[[Epsom]], Surrey
|27-year-old Singh was strangled and his body left in the car park of [[Epsom Downs Racecourse]], where it was found on the morning of 21 January 2006. |[[East Ham]], London
|On 3 February 2006, the 68-year-old widower was battered to death with a blunt object and then repeatedly stabbed at his house on Byron Avenue in East Ham, and an envelope containing approximately £200 was stolen. Because he was careful about whom he let in there and no signs of forced entry were found, police thought there was a strong possibility that he knew his attacker(s).<ref>{{Cite web<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|title=Mehar Singh Kataria|url=http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=156|website=Unsolved Murders<!--Deny Citation Bot-->|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428174355/http://www.unsolved-murders.co.uk/murder-content.php?key=156|archive-date=28 April 2022|access-date=28 April 2022}}</ref>

|March 2006
|Jamie Campbell
|[[Glasgow]]
|Four men were convicted in 2022 of the April 2018 gun murder of Kenneth Reilly in Glasgow's [[Maryhill]] area, but one of them was acquitted at the same trial of shooting dead 47-year-old Campbell in the [[Drumchapel]] area of the city on 4 March 2006. Lawyers acting for the man acquitted of this offence claimed that another murdered man – gangster Kevin Carroll, who died in 2010 – was Campbell's killer.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jamie Campbell murder: John Kennedy acquitted - but jailed for shooting of Kenny Reilly|url=https://www.clydebankpost.co.uk/news/19912141.jamie-campbell-murder-john-kennedy-acquitted---jailed-shooting-kenny-reilly/|website=Clydebank Post|date=9 February 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209173944/https://www.clydebankpost.co.uk/news/19912141.jamie-campbell-murder-john-kennedy-acquitted---jailed-shooting-kenny-reilly/|archive-date=9 February 2022|access-date=26 December 2023}}</ref> Campbell and his son were acquitted in 2004 over the January 2003 murder of Kevin Clark. At that trial, the son was accused of killing Clark and Campbell was accused of cutting up the son's football top and tracksuit bottoms.<ref name=Campbell/>

|March 2006
|Jordan Jackson and Leyla Djemal-Northcott
|[[Upper Norwood]], London
|20-year-old Jackson and 21-year-old Djemal-Northcott, Jackson's girlfriend, were shot dead in their flat in Menlo Gardens, Upper Norwood, on 7 March 2006 when Jackson, who was said to have stolen £5,000 from a violent drug dealer, answered the door to two men wearing ski masks. Jackson's brother was shot too but survived, and the girlfriend of this brother, who was likewise at the flat that day, hid from the gunmen and was not found by them. Four men were charged with murder in 2011. Two of the suspects were identical twins, with one alleged to have been one of the shooters and the other to have acted as a lookout, and the police tried to train witnesses to tell them apart by creating sets of virtual twins for those witnesses to study – a measure that a judge found "intelligent and imaginative" but "ultimately deficient", prompting him to throw the case out.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Unsolved Murders in London: 2006|url=https://www.murdermap.co.uk/unsolved-murders/unsolved-murders-london-2006-police/|website=murdermap.co.uk|date=28 January 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240810224227/https://www.murdermap.co.uk/unsolved-murders/unsolved-murders-london-2006-police/|archive-date=10 August 2024|access-date=10 August 2024}}</ref>

|March 2006
|Carlton Alveranga and Richard Austin
|[[Salford]], Greater Manchester
|Alveranga, 20, and Austin, 19, were recruited to murder David Totton, and entered Salford's Brass Handles pub on Sunday 12 March 2006 to carry out their task. Although Totton was shot, he survived. His assailants were then disarmed and shot dead with their own guns. Alveranga and Austin's clients were convicted of conspiracy to murder in 2007, but the killer or killers of their would-be hitmen remain unidentified.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Two guilty of pub execution plot|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/manchester/6475601.stm|work=BBC News|date=21 March 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070328192647/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/manchester/6475601.stm|archive-date=28 March 2007|access-date=30 June 2007}}</ref>

|March 2006
|Michael Shipton
|[[Sheering]], Essex

|Attacked in [[Battersea]], London, died in hospital
|On 17 April 2006 (Easter Monday), 18-year-old Ricketts was shot in the chest at The Battersea Bar in York Road after a friend of his made a signal to someone he thought he knew and the signal was mistaken for a gun gesture. |May 2006
|[[Luke Durbin]]
|Body not found
|19-year-old Durbin left an [[Ipswich]] nightclub on his own in the early hours of Friday 12 May 2006 when he had become separated from a friend, and later tried – unsuccessfully because he did not have any money on him – to get a taxi back to his home in the Suffolk village of [[Hollesley]]. |Ernest Gifford

|45-year-old Gifford, a small-time drug dealer, was shot in the thigh by one of three masked men during a robbery bid at his house in [[Moss Side]], Manchester, on 4 July 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Keegan|first=Mike|title=Drug dealer 'executed as children hid in fear' in Moss Side house, court told|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/local-news/drug-dealer-executed-as-children-hid-860523|website=Manchester Evening News|date=2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20251213221405/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/local-news/drug-dealer-executed-as-children-hid-860523|archive-date=13 December 2025|access-date=13 December 2025}}</ref> A man convicted of murder in 2007 was acquitted at a 2011 retrial after arguing that the presence of his DNA on a glove print in the house might have been due to someone borrowing his gloves, and that footprints there that matched the tread of a pair of trainers he owned could not have been his because he did not buy the trainers until after the killing.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man cleared after four years in jail for murder of drug dealer in Moss Side|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/man-cleared-after-four-years-860919|website=Manchester Evening News|date=18 May 2011|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921204159/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/man-cleared-after-four-years-860919|archive-date=21 September 2021|access-date=21 September 2021}}</ref>

|Jim Stanton
|[[Liverpool]]
|At around 6:00 p.m. on Monday 24 July 2006, two armed men in balaclavas went into Aintree Commercial Vehicles, Ormskirk Road, [[Aintree]], and shot 58-year-old Stanton, an office worker, in the head and back as he sat at his desk. |[[Oxford]]

|November 2006

|Birmingham
|Bernard-Brown was shot to death in a cul-de-sac off Melbourne Avenue, [[Lozells]], Birmingham, on 13 November 2006 (his 20th birthday). |Atiyebi Omuaru
|[[Barking, London|Barking]], London
|25-year-old Omuaru went to a garage on River Road, Barking, to pick up his serviced car on 2 January 2007 and was shot dead in the reception after diving behind the counter following earlier shots and a struggle.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CCTV of ambush suspects released|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6264052.stm|website=BBC News|date=3 July 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816223940/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6264052.stm|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref> The dark Vauxhall Omega saloon in which the two culprits left had arrived at the garage nearly two hours before Omuaru did.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Garage murder hunt goes on|url=https://www.barkinganddagenhampost.co.uk/news/20910842.garage-murder-hunt-goes/|website=Barking & Dagenham Post|date=14 January 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816221000/https://www.barkinganddagenhampost.co.uk/news/20910842.garage-murder-hunt-goes/|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref>

|January 2007
|Robert Pride-McLeod
|[[Harrogate]], North Yorkshire
|Pride-McLeod's body was found in the cellar of a homeless hostel on 21 January 2007 following a severe assault on the 49-year-old. The assault probably took place within a few days of his arrival at the hostel on 12 January.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Police to reopen ten-year case into the five-stone man 'left to die' in a Harrogate hostel cellar|url=https://www.harrogateadvertiser.co.uk/news/crime/police-to-reopen-ten-year-case-into-the-five-stone-man-left-to-die-in-a-harrogate-hostel-cellar-749677|website=Harrogate Advertiser|date=11 January 2017|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210531183504/https://www.harrogateadvertiser.co.uk/news/crime/police-reopen-ten-year-case-five-stone-man-left-die-harrogate-hostel-cellar-749677|archive-date=31 May 2021|access-date=31 May 2021}}</ref>

|January 2007
|Dean Tully
|[[Brentford]], London
|37-year-old Tully died and another man and a Staffordshire bull terrier were wounded when two men burst into the Brentford flat they were in on 25 January 2007 and sprayed it with bullets from a submachine gun for about three minutes. A nearby CCTV camera captured the gunmen leaving the scene, but the footage was of very poor quality. The shooting was believed to have been part of a turf war between an established drug-dealing gang and one trying to move in on its territory. Tully's background suggested he was not an intended target but was simply in the wrong place at the wrong time.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dean Tully murder: new suspect|url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/local-news/dean-tully-murder-new-suspect-6011899|website=My London|date=23 January 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816223942/https://www.mylondon.news/news/local-news/dean-tully-murder-new-suspect-6011899.amp|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Dean Tully police no closer to arresting killer|url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/local-news/dean-tully-police-no-closer-6007614|website=My London|date=9 June 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240816223945/https://www.mylondon.news/news/local-news/dean-tully-police-no-closer-6007614.amp|archive-date=16 August 2024|access-date=16 August 2024}}</ref>

|January 2007
|John Iveson
|Body not found
|The 36-year-old's wife was pregnant with his fifth child when he vanished from [[Nantwich]], Cheshire, on 30 January 2007, and his disappearance is being treated as murder. |February 2007
|James Andre Smartt-Ford
|London
|At approximately 10:55 p.m. on 3 February 2007, the [[Metropolitan Police]] received a call about a shooting at an ice-skating rink known as Streatham Ice Arena. Although there were multiple witnesses, the killer has not been identified.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Appeal over teenager shot dead during Streatham ice rink disco|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/hp/front/appeal-over-teenager-shot-dead-during-streatham-ice-rink-disco-6562875.html|website=The Standard|date=12 April 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220917143244/https://www.standard.co.uk/hp/front/appeal-over-teenager-shot-dead-during-streatham-ice-rink-disco-6562875.html|archive-date=17 September 2022|access-date=14 October 2023}}</ref>
|-
|February 2007
|Chamberlain Igwemba
|[[Peckham]], London
|Drug baron Igwemba, 47, and his accountant were shot at a flat on Clayton Road in Peckham on 4 February 2007, but the accountant survived. Two Jamaican men were acquitted.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Teenage boy shot dead in bedroom|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/london/6335483.stm|website=BBC News|date=6 February 2007|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220730210140/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/london/6335483.stm|archive-date=30 July 2022|access-date=30 July 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=JONES:JAMAICAN PAIR CLEARED OF SHOOTING DRUGS BARON DEAD|url=https://courtnewsuk.co.uk/jonesjamaican-pair-cleared-of-shooting-drugs-baron-dead/|website=Court News UK|date=12 March 2009|access-date=30 July 2022}}</ref>

|February 2007
|Sajid Saddique
|Body not found
|32-year-old Saddique, a father-of-three, met a friend in the car park of an Asda supermarket in [[Shipley, West Yorkshire|Shipley]], West Yorkshire, on 14 February 2007 and was never seen again. He was declared dead in 2014 and his disappearance began to be treated as murder later that same year. Saddique had been involved in disputes over money at the time of his disappearance and the investigation has seen two men arrested but not charged. A second inquest into his death in December 2020 ruled that he had been unlawfully killed, and the murder investigation remains ongoing.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sajid Saddique: Inquest returns unlawful killing verdict|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leeds-55317676|website=BBC News|date=21 December 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516184350/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-leeds-55317676|archive-date=16 May 2021|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Winrow|first=Jo|title=INQUEST: Bradford man Sajid Saddique, who went missing in 2007 was 'unlawfully killed'|url=https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/18944464.inquest-bradford-man-sajid-saddique-went-missing-2007-unlawfully-killed/|website=Telegraph & Argus|date=15 December 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220430015844/https://www.thetelegraphandargus.co.uk/news/18944464.inquest-bradford-man-sajid-saddique-went-missing-2007-unlawfully-killed/|archive-date=30 April 2022|access-date=9 January 2021}}</ref>

|February 2007
|Billy Cox
|[[Clapham]], London
|Cox's 13-year-old sister arrived home from school and found the 15-year-old dying from bullet wounds in his bedroom on 14 February 2007. |March 2007
|Terry McSpadden
|Body not found
|24-year-old McSpadden told people prior to vanishing on 2 March 2007 that he feared he was going to be murdered because he had recently woken up on the sofa in a friend's cottage to find himself encased in industrial-style cling film before being rescued from suffocation by his friend coming home and cutting through the material. The cottage was in [[Elm, Cambridgeshire|Elm]], a village on the Cambridgeshire/Norfolk border. |March 2007
|Tyno Kavuala
|[[College Park, London|College Park]], London
|Kavuala, a 20-year-old [[Kilburn, London|Kilburn]] man, was shot in his car near the northern end of Scrubs Lane, College Park, on 4 March 2007. The killing appeared to have been a gangland crime.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Welham|first=Jamie|title=Appeal over drive-by shooting|url=http://www.thecnj.com/westend/2008/030708/wnews030708_13.html|website=Camden New Journal|date=7 March 2008|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080828225540/http://www.thecnj.com/westend/2008/030708/wnews030708_13.html|archive-date=28 August 2008|access-date=16 May 2021}}</ref> A 22-year-old man murdered in London in May 2010 – Daniel Smith – was thought to have been targeted because he looked like Kavuala's suspected assailant.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Men cleared of Daniel Smith 'mistaken identity' murder|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-18793431|website=BBC News|date=11 July 2012|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170318005827/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-18793431|archive-date=18 March 2017|access-date=16 August 2012}}</ref>
