Aasis Beats.text:
Aasis Giri, professionally known as Aasis Beats, is a Nepalese record producer, songwriter, and sample maker from Kathmandu, Nepal. He is the first music producer from Nepal who has productions that have charted at number one on the Billboard charts. Aasis's samples have been the melodic foundation for hit songs for Central Cee, Lil Baby, Suicideboys, Dave East, Sofaygo and more. He worked with Suicideboys to co-produce their first number one charting album, New World Depression. He also worked with rapper Central Cee and Lil Baby to co-produce their 2024 hit song "Band4Band", and collaborated with Tommy Richman to produce the lead single "Thought You Were the One" from Richman's debut album, coyote. 
Aasis has contributed to connecting the Nepali music scene with the global hip-hop industry through a combination of technical production work and collaborations with artists from different regions, he has received Diamond and Gold certifications, appeared on Billboard charts, and worked with several well-known hip-hop artists, making him a notable music producer from South Asia.


== Early life ==
Aasis Giri was born on August 17, 1996, in Kathmandu, Nepal. He began producing at the age of 17, he cites Nick Mira, Metro Boomin, Drake, Juice Wrld & Noah 40 as an influence. Aasis describes his musical style as "synthetic", "melodic" and "nostalgic". Spending countless days and nights in front of his laptop producing music on FL Studio, Giri, more widely known as Aasis Beats in the music industry, immersed himself in the art of sample making and music production.


== Career ==
While Aasis began his producing career by selling beats online, he noticed that making samples might give him more opportunity so he started uploading loops and samples on Looperman.
In 2024, he got his first major placement in Central Cee's Lil Baby-assisted single "Band4Band", Giri created a loop several years ago that would later find its way into the hit song, Giri had nearly forgotten about the loop when it was unexpectedly picked up by Central Cee’s producers. The song went on to make waves, landing at number 18 on the US Billboard Hot 100, number 12 on the Billboard Global 200, and number 1 on UK Hip Hop/R&B Official Charts. Currently, the song has over 300 Million streams on Spotify and over 100 Million streams on YouTube. The record is also RIAA Certified Platinum in the US, selling over 1 million units. It also went platinum in Canada  and Gold on United Kingdom.
Later that year, Aasis began working with the American hip-hop duo Suicideboys on their album New World Depression, which charted at number one on Billboard's Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart. The album also reached number one on the Billboard US Independent Albums chart and number 5 on the US Billboard 200.
Aasis Beats also produced the hit single "Chandigarh Ka Chokra" for Indian singer and actress Sunanda Sharma, which peaked at number 35 on Asian Music Chart. The song currently has over 50 million streams on Spotify and over 40 million views on YouTube.
Later in his career, Aasis Beats collaborated with Million Dollar Baby artist Tommy Richman to produce the lead single, "THOUGHT YOU WERE THE ONE" from Richman's debut album Coyote. The album peaked at number 10 on the US Heatseekers Albums (Billboard).
Aasis Beats reached a career milestone in 2025 by producing the hit single “AVM” for French artist YG Pablo. The track earned a Diamond certification from the Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique (SNEP) in France.

==Life and career==
===UGK===
{{Main|UGK}}
In the late 1980s, [[Pimp C]] started the rap duo [[UGK]]. He first released a demo tape titled "Underground King" which didn't feature Bun B on the track. Instead, it featured Pimp C's friend Mitchell Queen. Bun B and friend Jalon Jackson had their own group called P.A. Militia. Both groups joined forces and formed the group 4 Black Ministers. Queen and Jackson later left the group leaving Pimp C and Bun B so they decided to revert to UGK.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2011/03/greatest-hip-hop-demos/ugk|title=The 30 Greatest Hip Hop demos|website=[[Complex Networks]]|access-date=December 28, 2012}}</ref> The demo Pimp C recorded with Mitchell Queen, ''Underground King'', caught the attention of an independent label in [[Houston]] called Bigtyme Records. They then released an [[extended play]] titled ''[[The Southern Way]]''. The release of this record caught the attention of [[Jive Records]]. While recording their debut album, ''[[Too Hard to Swallow]]'', many of the songs had content too explicit for the album, so Bigtyme Records released an extended play titled ''[[Banned (EP)|Banned]]'' before the album was released, including all the songs that were too explicit for ''Too Hard to Swallow''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.straightgangsterism.com/2008/11/30/songs-no-one-should-here-ugks-banned/|title=Songs No One Should Hear: UGK's Banned|access-date=November 2, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216021413/http://www.straightgangsterism.com/2008/11/30/songs-no-one-should-here-ugks-banned/|archive-date=December 16, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> The song "Pocket Full of Stones" became the first UGK song to get major airplay throughout the United States. Their second album, ''[[Super Tight]]...'', followed in 1994. Their third album, ''[[Ridin' Dirty]]'', peaked at number 2 on the R&B Charts in 1996, and at number 15 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. After releasing their fourth studio album, ''[[Dirty Money (album)|Dirty Money]]'', Pimp C got sentenced to jail.<ref name="allmusic2012">{{cite web|last=Bush|first=John|title=UGK > Biography|url={{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p413944|pure_url=yes}}|publisher=Allmusic|date=May 20, 2008|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref>

===''Trill'' and beginning of solo career===
{{Main|Trill (album)}}
When Bun B's [[UGK]] partner, the late [[Pimp C|Chad "Pimp C" Butler]], entered a jail sentence on an aggravated gun assault charge in 2002, Bun B made guest appearances on numerous albums by other rappers and released a 2005 [[Mixtape#Mixtapes in hip hop|mixtape]] titled ''Legends''.<ref name="Allmusic">{{cite web|last=Jeffries|first=David|title=Bun B > Biography|url={{AllMusic|class=artist|id=p133449|pure_url=yes}}|publisher=Allmusic|date=May 20, 2008|access-date=July 19, 2008}}</ref> Singles featuring a Bun B guest appearance included "They Don't Know" by [[Paul Wall]], "Gimme That" by [[Webbie]] and "I'm A G" by [[Yung Joc]]. Bun B also appeared in a documentary titled ''Screwed In Houston'' produced by VBS/''[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]'' that details the history of the Houston rap scene.

In October 2005, Bun B's debut solo album ''[[Trill (album)|Trill]]'' was released.<ref name="New Releases">{{cite news|last=Orzeck|first=Kurt|title=New Releases: Ashlee Simpson, Depeche Mode, Bun B, Stevie Wonder, Thrice, M.O.P. & More|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1511604/20051017/simpson_ashlee.jhtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051217135500/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1511604/20051017/simpson_ashlee.jhtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 17, 2005|work=MTV News|date=October 17, 2005|access-date=July 19, 2008}}</ref> Singles included "[[Draped Up]]",<ref name="New Releases" /> "[[Git It]]", and "[[Get Throwed]]".<ref>{{cite news|last=Reid|first=Shaheem|title=25 Best Tracks of 2005|work=Mixtape Monday|publisher=MTV News|url=http://www.mtv.com/bands/m/mixtape_monday/year_end_05/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060107143714/http://www.mtv.com/bands/m/mixtape_monday/year_end_05/|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 7, 2006|date=January 3, 2006|access-date=July 19, 2008}}</ref> The album peaked at the number 6 spot on the American [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] chart and number 1 on the [[Top R&B/Hip Hop Albums]] chart.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trill – Billboard Albums|url={{AllMusic|class=album|id=r789095|pure_url=yes}}|publisher=Allmusic}}</ref>

===''II Trill''===
{{Main|II Trill}}
After Pimp C died in 2007, Bun B returned to a solo career. In 2008, he released his second album, ''[[II Trill]]''.<ref name="Allmusic" /> The first single was "[[That's Gangsta]]" featuring Jamaican American artist [[Sean Kingston]]. It debuted at number 2 on the Billboard 200, selling 98,000 copies.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Hasty|first=Katie|title=3 Doors Down Cruisees To No. 1 On Album Chart|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1045267/3-doors-down-cruises-to-no-1-on-album-chart|magazine=Billboard|date=May 28, 2008}}</ref> Other singles were "Damn I'm Cold" featuring [[Lil Wayne]] and "[[You're Everything]]" featuring [[Rick Ross]], [[David Banner]], DJ Corbett and [[8Ball & MJG]], the latter of which was dedicated to the late Pimp C.

===''Trill OG''===
{{Main|Trill OG}}
[[File:Bun B's Set @ The Loft, Atlanta (cropped).jpg|thumb|Bun B performing in 2008]]
Bun B's third album is ''[[Trill OG]]''. In an interview with MTV Live, Bun B stated that [[2Pac]] was set to feature on the album, claiming "It's a brand new verse."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wordofsouth.com/online/?p=1557|archive-url=https://archive.today/20090318012123/http://www.wordofsouth.com/online/?p=1557|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 18, 2009|title=UGK: The Trill OG'z|date=March 15, 2009|work=WordofSouth.com|access-date=July 1, 2009}}</ref> The album was released under [[Universal Music Group]]<ref>[http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.10725/title.bun-b-moves-from-asylum-to-universal-still-with-rap-a-lot Paine, Jake, "Bun B Moves From Asylum To Universal Music Group, Still With Rap-A-Lot," Feb. 27, 2010] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100420055625/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.10725/title.bun-b-moves-from-asylum-to-universal-still-with-rap-a-lot |date=April 20, 2010 }}, accessed December 20, 2010.</ref> on August 3, 2010.<ref>[http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.11274/title.tuesday-rap-release-dates-crooked-i-nerd-young-buck Hanna, Mitchell, "Tuesday Rap Release Dates,"hiphopdx.com, May 18, 2010] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100603074917/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.11274/title.tuesday-rap-release-dates-crooked-i-nerd-young-buck |date=June 3, 2010 }}, accessed December 20, 2010.</ref>

===''Trill OG: The Epilogue''===
{{Main|Trill OG: The Epilogue}}
On October 28, 2011, a song titled "The Life" and produced by 14KT was leaked. On March 3, 2012, Bun B leaked a song featuring [[Royce da 5'9"]] and [[Redman (rapper)|Redman]] titled "Stop Playin'" after he reached 400,000 followers on Twitter. He has not announced the song's appearance on his upcoming album<ref>[http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/singles/id.17420/title.bun-b-the-life-prod-14kt Bun B "The Life [Prod. 14KT]"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150510005822/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/singles/id.17420/title.bun-b-the-life-prod-14kt |date=May 10, 2015 }}, accessed October 28, 2011.</ref>

[[File:Bun B (2013) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Bun B performing in 2013]]

His fourth studio album was rumored to be titled, ''Trill 4 Life'' and scheduled for a 2013 release.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xxlmag.com/hip-hop-today/2013/03/today-in-hip-hop-bun-b-celebrates-hi-40th-birthday/|title=Today In Hip-Hop: Bun B Celebrates His 40th Birthday – XXL|date=March 19, 2013 }}</ref> On August 22, 2013, [[Rap-A-Lot Records]] revealed that his Sony distributed fourth studio album will be released in October 2013. The album is to feature guest appearances from [[Rick Ross]] and [[2 Chainz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.25165/title.rap-a-lot-records-signs-distribution-deal-with-sony-red-plans-bun-b-album|title=Rap-A-Lot Records Signs Distribution Deal With Sony RED, Plans Bun B Album|author=HipHopDX|date=August 23, 2013|work=HipHopDX|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150216004940/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.25165/title.rap-a-lot-records-signs-distribution-deal-with-sony-red-plans-bun-b-album|archive-date=February 16, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 4, 2013, the album was then officially announced to be titled ''[[Trill OG: The Epilogue]]'' and be released on November 12, 2013. The album was revealed to contain primarily leftover tracks from the ''Trill O.G.'' recording sessions. It was also confirmed to feature Pimp C, 2 Chainz, Rick Ross, [[Lil Boosie]], [[Kirko Bangz]], [[Big K.R.I.T.]], [[Raekwon]], Z-Ro and [[Devin The Dude]].<ref name="rapradar.com">{{cite web|url=http://rapradar.com/2013/10/04/bun-b-announces-new-album/|title=Bun B Announces New Album – Rap Radar|work=Rap Radar|date=October 4, 2013 |access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/news/bun-b-closes-the-trill-chapter-20131004|title=Bun B Closes the 'Trill' Chapter|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=October 4, 2013|access-date=March 9, 2015}}</ref>

Bun B announced "The Trillest Tour" in January 2014. On January 30, the Houston native revealed the tour dates, where he was accompanied by fellow Houston native [[Kirko Bangz]]. The tour ran from March 6 until April 17, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://revolt.tv/video/exclusive-bun-b-and-kirko-bangz-announce-the-trillest-tour/E8B2B803-E32F-4617-9614-BE6E1635604F|title=Exclusive: Bun B & Kirko Bangz Announce The Trillest Tour|work=Revolt|access-date=March 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218200634/http://revolt.tv/video/exclusive-bun-b-and-kirko-bangz-announce-the-trillest-tour/E8B2B803-E32F-4617-9614-BE6E1635604F|archive-date=December 18, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2025, Freeman provided skits on [[JackBoys (rap group)|JackBoys]] and [[Travis Scott]]'s second compilation album ''[[JackBoys 2]]''.

==Other ventures==
===Awards===
On June 24, 2014, Bun B made a guest appearance to the Htown Beatdown concert hosted by local radio station [[KKHH|Hot 95.7]]. He was awarded the 360 Legend Award for his successful music career and his impact on the local community.

===Teaching===
At the start of the Spring 2011 semester, Bun B joined the faculty of [[Rice University]] as a Distinguished Lecturer. He taught a course in the School of the Humanities on [[Hip hop]] and [[Religion]].<ref name="AOL Music">[http://www.theboombox.com/2010/06/22/bun-b-to-teach-hip-hop-and-religion-class-at-rice-university/ Alexis, Nadeska, "Bun B to Teach Hip-Top and Religion Class at Rice University," 2010-06-22], Theboombox.com, accessed December 20, 2010.</ref> Into 2013 Bun B continues to teach the course twice a week.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2013/11/bun-b-says-elders-didnt-raise-young-mcs-correctly/|title=Bun B Says The Elders May Have Not Raised Upcoming MCs Correctly – XXL|date=November 13, 2013 }}</ref>

===Coloring book===
On September 17, 2013, Freeman released a coloring book titled "''Bun B's Rap Coloring Book''" along with author [[Shea Serrano]]. Freeman and Serrano had previously talked about working together to make a book. At first they agreed on a "hip hop survival guide", but both agreed against the project. Later on, Serrano drew coloring pages of rappers that he posted on [[Tumblr]]. The pages quickly went viral. Freeman and Serrano then decided to make a whole coloring book.<ref name="Rolling Stone – Rap Coloring book">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/qa-bun-b-on-the-incredible-journey-of-creating-his-hip-hop-coloring-book-242934/|title=Q&A: Bun B on the 'Incredible Journey' of Creating His Hip-Hop Coloring Book|first1=Danielle|last1=Bacher|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=June 18, 2013}}</ref>

===Trill Burgers===
Bun B opened up Trill Burgers located on South Shepherd and Richmond Avenue in [[Houston, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stewart |first=Kayla |date=2023-07-10 |title=Trill Burgers Is as 'Houston' as a Restaurant Can Get |url=https://www.texasmonthly.com/food/trill-burgers/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Texas Monthly |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bun B has been married to Angela "Queenie" Wells since 2003 and has two stepchildren and seven step-grandchildren.<ref name="urblife.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.urblife.com/the-life/bun-b-talks-married-bliss/|title=Bun B Talks Married pBliss! Peer Pressure, Family Values and More|work=UrbLife.com|date= July 8, 2010}}</ref> His stepson is American rapper Young-B, who is a member of the rap group Youngest N Charge, which is Bun B's opening act.<ref>{{cite book|last=Coleman II|first=C. Vernon|title=Down With The King|edition=September 2010|year=2010|location=[[XXL (magazine)]]|page=62}}</ref>

Since 2013, he has been a guest lecturer at [[Houston]]'s [[Rice University]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.houstonpress.com/bestof/2011/award/best-new-professor-2674689/|title=Bun B, Rice University|date=2011|newspaper=[[Houston Press]]|access-date=October 14, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cercl.rice.edu/|title=Center for Engaged Research and Collaborative Learning (CERCL)|website=CERCL}}</ref>

On April 24, 2019, Bun B shot an armed intruder who was attempting to rob his Houston home. The intruder fled on foot. The suspect, DeMonte Jackson, was taken into custody by Houston police after arriving at the hospital.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/bun-b-shoots-intruder-houston-robbery-826776/|title=Bun B Shoots Armed Intruder During Robbery Attempt at Houston Home|last=Kreps|first=Daniel|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=April 24, 2019|language=en-US|access-date=April 26, 2019}}</ref>

Bun B.text:
Bernard James Freeman (born March 19, 1973), known professionally as Bun B is an American rapper. He is best known as one half of the Southern rap duo UGK (Underground Kingz), which he formed in 1987 alongside Pimp C. Aside from his work with UGK, Bun B has released five solo albums, including 2010's Trill OG, which received the rare 5-mic rating from The Source.


== Life and career ==


=== UGK ===

In the late 1980s, Pimp C started the rap duo UGK. He first released a demo tape titled "Underground King" which didn't feature Bun B on the track. Instead, it featured Pimp C's friend Mitchell Queen. Bun B and friend Jalon Jackson had their own group called P.A. Militia. Both groups joined forces and formed the group 4 Black Ministers. Queen and Jackson later left the group leaving Pimp C and Bun B so they decided to revert to UGK. The demo Pimp C recorded with Mitchell Queen, Underground King, caught the attention of an independent label in Houston called Bigtyme Records. They then released an extended play titled The Southern Way. The release of this record caught the attention of Jive Records. While recording their debut album, Too Hard to Swallow, many of the songs had content too explicit for the album, so Bigtyme Records released an extended play titled Banned before the album was released, including all the songs that were too explicit for Too Hard to Swallow. The song "Pocket Full of Stones" became the first UGK song to get major airplay throughout the United States. Their second album, Super Tight..., followed in 1994. Their third album, Ridin' Dirty, peaked at number 2 on the R&B Charts in 1996, and at number 15 on the Billboard 200. After releasing their fourth studio album, Dirty Money, Pimp C got sentenced to jail.


=== Trill and beginning of solo career ===

When Bun B's UGK partner, the late Chad "Pimp C" Butler, entered a jail sentence on an aggravated gun assault charge in 2002, Bun B made guest appearances on numerous albums by other rappers and released a 2005 mixtape titled Legends. Singles featuring a Bun B guest appearance included "They Don't Know" by Paul Wall, "Gimme That" by Webbie and "I'm A G" by Yung Joc. Bun B also appeared in a documentary titled Screwed In Houston produced by VBS/Vice that details the history of the Houston rap scene.
In October 2005, Bun B's debut solo album Trill was released. Singles included "Draped Up", "Git It", and "Get Throwed". The album peaked at the number 6 spot on the American Billboard 200 chart and number 1 on the Top R&B/Hip Hop Albums chart.


=== II Trill ===

After Pimp C died in 2007, Bun B returned to a solo career. In 2008, he released his second album, II Trill. The first single was "That's Gangsta" featuring Jamaican American artist Sean Kingston. It debuted at number 2 on the Billboard 200, selling 98,000 copies. Other singles were "Damn I'm Cold" featuring Lil Wayne and "You're Everything" featuring Rick Ross, David Banner, DJ Corbett and 8Ball & MJG, the latter of which was dedicated to the late Pimp C.


=== Trill OG ===

Bun B's third album is Trill OG. In an interview with MTV Live, Bun B stated that 2Pac was set to feature on the album, claiming "It's a brand new verse." The album was released under Universal Music Group on August 3, 2010.


=== Trill OG: The Epilogue ===

On October 28, 2011, a song titled "The Life" and produced by 14KT was leaked. On March 3, 2012, Bun B leaked a song featuring Royce da 5'9" and Redman titled "Stop Playin'" after he reached 400,000 followers on Twitter. He has not announced the song's appearance on his upcoming album

His fourth studio album was rumored to be titled, Trill 4 Life and scheduled for a 2013 release. On August 22, 2013, Rap-A-Lot Records revealed that his Sony distributed fourth studio album will be released in October 2013. The album is to feature guest appearances from Rick Ross and 2 Chainz. On October 4, 2013, the album was then officially announced to be titled Trill OG: The Epilogue and be released on November 12, 2013. The album was revealed to contain primarily leftover tracks from the Trill O.G. recording sessions. It was also confirmed to feature Pimp C, 2 Chainz, Rick Ross, Lil Boosie, Kirko Bangz, Big K.R.I.T., Raekwon, Z-Ro and Devin The Dude.
Bun B announced "The Trillest Tour" in January 2014. On January 30, the Houston native revealed the tour dates, where he was accompanied by fellow Houston native Kirko Bangz. The tour ran from March 6 until April 17, 2014.
In 2025, Freeman provided skits on JackBoys and Travis Scott's second compilation album JackBoys 2.


== Other ventures ==


=== Awards ===
On June 24, 2014, Bun B made a guest appearance to the Htown Beatdown concert hosted by local radio station Hot 95.7. He was awarded the 360 Legend Award for his successful music career and his impact on the local community.


=== Teaching ===
At the start of the Spring 2011 semester, Bun B joined the faculty of Rice University as a Distinguished Lecturer. He taught a course in the School of the Humanities on Hip hop and Religion. Into 2013 Bun B continues to teach the course twice a week.


=== Coloring book ===
On September 17, 2013, Freeman released a coloring book titled "Bun B's Rap Coloring Book" along with author Shea Serrano. Freeman and Serrano had previously talked about working together to make a book. At first they agreed on a "hip hop survival guide", but both agreed against the project. Later on, Serrano drew coloring pages of rappers that he posted on Tumblr. The pages quickly went viral. Freeman and Serrano then decided to make a whole coloring book.


=== Trill Burgers ===
Bun B opened up Trill Burgers located on South Shepherd and Richmond Avenue in Houston, Texas.


== Personal life ==
Bun B has been married to Angela "Queenie" Wells since 2003 and has two stepchildren and seven step-grandchildren. His stepson is American rapper Young-B, who is a member of the rap group Youngest N Charge, which is Bun B's opening act.
Since 2013, he has been a guest lecturer at Houston's Rice University.
On April 24, 2019, Bun B shot an armed intruder who was attempting to rob his Houston home. The intruder fled on foot. The suspect, DeMonte Jackson, was taken into custody by Houston police after arriving at the hospital.

He is a member of the [[UK drill]] group [[OFB (rap group)|OFB]]. Beginning his career in 2018 alongside fellow OFB rappers SJ and [[Double Lz]], Bandokay gained prominence in 2019 after release of ''[[Frontstreet (album)|Frontstreet]]''. The mixtape peaked at number 36 on the [[UK Albums Chart]] and was followed by ''Drill Commandmants'', released in 2021. == Early life == Kemani Tutti Kane Duggan was born on 9 May 2001, in [[Tottenham]], [[London]], England. He is the son of [[Shooting of Mark Duggan|Mark Duggan]], who was fatally shot by armed police in 2011. After his father's death, Duggan was looked after by Marcus Knox-Hooke, one of his father's friends. This would lead Knox-Hooke to form a program to look after vulnerable youth in Tottenham.{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/meeting-marcus-knox-hooke-the-man-who-started-the-london-riots/|title=Meeting Marcus Knox-Hooke, the Man Who "Started the London Riots"|first=Shannon|last=Mahanty|date=13 July 2016|website=vice.com|access-date=10 November 2021}} Sometime afterwards, Duggan began secondary school; however, he was kicked out three months after beginning due to his inability to control his behaviour. == Career == ===2018-19: Early career and ''Frontstreet''=== In a 2022 video showcasing his daily life, Bandokay stated that Kash, a member of OFB, was the main reason that he would take a career in music seriously; according to Bandokay, Kash would call him in order to write lyrics.{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/ofb-bandokay-daily-lifestyle/|title=OFB BANDOKAY GIVES US AN INSIGHT INTO HIS DAILY LIFESTYLE IN NEW 'DAY IN THE LIFE' VID|first=Jamal|last=Wilson|date=20 January 2022|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=25 January 2022}} Bandokay began his musical career in early 2018 with the release of "Bruck It" alongside Kash, Ys, [[Double Lz]] and Boogie B.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} In late 2018, he released "Bad B on the Nizz" alongside Double Lz and [[SJ (rapper)|SJ]]; according to an interview with [[Complex Networks]], the song gained one million views in a week. In the same interview, Double Lz said that the first song that he and Bandokay made was created in 2017; however, it was never released.{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/ofb-bandokay-double-lz-interview|title=Get To Know Bandokay & Double Lz, The Fresh-Faced Stars Of OFB|first=Ajay|last=Rose|date=1 April 2021|website=complex.com|access-date=12 November 2021}} The three would, for sometime, adopt the name Y.OFB ("Young OFB"); the "Y." prefix would later be dropped in 2019.{{Cite web|url=https://www.passionweiss.com/2019/11/14/the-drop-the-best-uk-drill-of-november-2019/|title=The Drop: The Best UK Drill of November 2019|date=14 November 2019|website=Passion of the Weiss|language=en-US|access-date=12 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191215182618/https://www.passionweiss.com/2019/11/14/the-drop-the-best-uk-drill-of-november-2019/|archive-date=15 December 2019|url-status=live|quote=Frontstreet is mostly composed of Bandokay, Double Lz and SJ, a triplet of steel-mouthed musketeers (fka Y.OFB and later became OFB)…}} On 14 November 2019, The group released their debut mixtape ''[[Frontstreet (album)|Frontstreet]]''; the mixtape peaked at number 36 on the [[UK Albums Chart]]. The mixtape also included "Ambush", Which was certified silver by the [[British Phonographic Industry]]. ===2019-21: ''Drill Commandments''=== Following the release of ''Frontstreet'', Bandokay would appear on [[Kenny Allstar]]'s ''Mad About Bars'' freestyle series in 2019 and release "Lightwork Freestyle" in 2020, both of which featured Double Lz.{{Cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/thepitch/bandokay-double-lz-mad-about-bars-new-song-listen/|title=The Ones: Bandokay and Double Lz's "Mad About Bars"|first=Alphonse|last=Pierre|date=7 October 2019|work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]|access-date=2 April 2022}}{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/double-lz-bandokay-lightwork-freestyle/|title=OFB'S BANDOKAY & DOUBLE LZ TEAM UP FOR NEW 'LIGHTWORK' FREESTYLE|first=Gloria|last=Bikolo|date=23 January 2020|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=10 November 2021}} In 2020, he would release "OT Bopping" with Double Lz,{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/bandokay-double-lz-ot-bopping/|title=PREMIERE: BANDOKAY & DOUBLE LZ HIT US WITH VIDEO FOR "OT BOPPING"|first=Courtney|last=W|date=30 January 2020|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=10 November 2021}} which peaked at number 91 on the UK Singles Chart. In the beginning of 2020, Bandokay was named within the top 20 British MCs to watch in 2020 by [[Complex Networks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2020/01/20-british-emcees-to-watch-in-2020/|title=20 British Emcees To Watch In 2020|first1=Joseph|last1=Patterson|first2=James|last2=Keith|first3=Tobi|last3=Oke|first4=Ethan|last4=Herlock|first5=Elle|last5=Evans|date=23 January 2020|website=complex.com|access-date=12 November 2021}} In March 2020, Bandokay would appear alongside Double Lz on [[iLL BLU]]'s "Magic" and on [[War (Mastermind song)|"War"]] by Mastermind,{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/ill-blu-bandokay-double-lz-magic/|title=PREMIERE: BANDOKAY & DOUBLE LZ JOIN ILL BLU ON NEW HIT "MAGIC"|first=Courtney|last=W|date=12 March 2020|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=10 November 2021}}{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/mastermind-bandokay-war/|title=PREMIERE: MASTERMIND ENLISTS OFB'S BANDOKAY FOR NEW DROP "WAR"|first=Courtney|last=W|date=19 March 2020|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=10 November 2021}} which would peak at number 46 and number 39 on the UK Singles Chart, respectively. In May, he would release "Patient",{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/bandokay-patient/|title=OFB'S BANDOKAY KEEPS IT GREAZY IN FRESH "PATIENT" VISUALS|first=Jade|last=Dadalica|date=7 May 2020|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=10 November 2021}} which would peak at number 92. In July, Bandokay would appear on [[Deno (singer)|Deno]]'s "Circles", also featuring Double Lz;{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/deno-bandokay-double-lz-circles/|title=PREMIERE: DENO ENLISTS OFB'S BANDOKAY & DOUBLE LZ ON LATEST DROP "CIRCLES"|first=Courtney|last=W|date=2 July 2020|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=10 November 2021}} the song peaked at number 36. In October, Bandokay would release "BLM" with Double Lz and [[Abra Cadabra (rapper)|Abra Cadabra]],{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/bandokay-double-lz-abra-cadabra-blm/|title=BANDOKAY, DOUBLE LZ & ABRA CADABRA CONNECT ON POWERFUL TRACK "BLM"|first=Courtney|last=W|date=8 October 2020|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=10 November 2021}} which peaked at number 63. During a 2020 interview with Vice regarding "BLM", Double Lz and Bandokay teased that another mixtape was in the works, which included features from [[Loski]], Abra Cadabra, and others.{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/blm-bandokay-double-lz-abra-cadabra-interview/|title='BLM' Is the Poignant New UK Drill Tribute to Mark Duggan and Black Lives Matter|first=Abubakar|last=Finiin|date=14 October 2020|website=vice.com|access-date=11 November 2021}} The mixtape, named ''Drill Commandments'', was released by the two on 19 March 2021; it would peak at number 53 on the UK Albums Chart. ===2021-present: No Requests and solo album=== In June 2021, Bandokay released "Slide";{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/bandokay-slide/|title=PREMIERE: BANDOKAY HOSTS A LIT POOL PARTY IN BRAND-NEW "SLIDE" VISUALS|first=GRM|last=Daily|date=10 June 2021|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=10 November 2021}} it peaked at number 74. In January 2022, Bandokay announced in a video that he and Double Lz were to release solo albums. He would also release "Praise the Lord" in the same month.{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/bandokay-praise-the-lord/|title=PREMIERE: BANDOKAY OFFLOADS VIDEO FOR LATEST JOINT "PRAISE THE LORD"|first=Courtney|last=W|date=14 January 2022|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=14 January 2022}} In February, Bandokay was signed to No Requests, created by [[Tiffany Calver]] in collaboration with [[Polydor Records]]. In March, he would release "Tower Hill Freestyle", named after an area in [[Saint Andrew Parish, Jamaica]].{{Cite web|url=https://grmdaily.com/bandokay-tower-hill-freestyle/|title=BANDOKAY HEADS TO JAMAICA FOR FRESH "TOWER HILL FREESTYLE"|first=Naimah|last=Archibald-Powell|date=31 March 2022|website=grmdaily.com|access-date=2 April 2022}} ==Legal issues== In 2022, Bandokay, alongside [[Double Lz]], was charged with violent disorder following a 2021 incident at a [[Selfridges]] store where two people were stabbed.{{Cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/london/mark-duggan-brother-son-selfridges-stabbing-b979813.html|title=Mark Duggan's brother and son accused of being in Selfridges brawl where two people were stabbed|first=Tristan|last=Kirk|date=31 January 2022|website=standard.co.uk|access-date=6 February 2022}} On 15 January 2024, Bandokay was summoned at Thames Magistrates Court and charged with possession of a firearm and possession of ammunition without a license.{{Cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/crime/mark-duggan-rapper-son-arrested-gatwick-firearms-tottenham-hackney-metropolitan-police-b1133990.html|title=Mark Duggan's rapper son arrested at Gatwick Airport over firearms offences|first=Anthony|last=France|date=22 January 2024|work=[[Evening Standard]]|access-date=28 January 2024}} On 2 July 2024, BandoKay was due to face trial at the Old Bailey accused of possessing a Tokarev pistol and 22 bulleted cartridges with intent to endanger life last year. Just before his trial was due to start, however, he pleaded guilty to lesser offences of possession with intent to cause fear of violence. The court was told that the minimum sentence for possession of an illegal firearm was five years in prison. Judge Philip Katz KC remanded the defendants into custody to be sentenced on 5 July 2024.{{Cite web|url=https://news.sky.com/story/son-of-mark-duggan-whose-death-sparked-london-riots-admits-having-a-gun-13162382|title=Kemani Duggan: Son of Mark Duggan admits having a gun|website=Sky News}} On 5 July 2024, Kemani Duggan was sentenced to five years in prison.{{Cite web|url=https://news.sky.com/story/drill-rapper-son-of-mark-duggan-jailed-for-gun-crime-13173696|title=Drill rapper son of Mark Duggan jailed for gun crime|website=Sky News}} == Discography == === Mixtapes === {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center" |+List of mixtapes, with selected details ! scope="col" rowspan="2" style="width:10em"| Title ! scope="col" rowspan="2" style="width:16em"| Details ! scope="col" colspan="2"| Peak chart positions ! scope="col" rowspan="2" style="width:12em"| Certifications |- ! scope="col" style="width:3em;font-size:85%;"| [[UK Albums Chart|UK]]

Bandokay.text:
Kemani Tutti Kane Duggan (born 9 May 2001), known professionally as Bandokay (formerly stylized as BandoKay), is a British rapper. He is a member of the UK drill group OFB.
Beginning his career in 2018 alongside fellow OFB rappers SJ and Double Lz, Bandokay gained prominence in 2019 after release of Frontstreet. The mixtape peaked at number 36 on the UK Albums Chart and was followed by Drill Commandmants, released in 2021.


== Early life ==
Kemani Tutti Kane Duggan was born on 9 May 2001, in Tottenham, London, England. He is the son of Mark Duggan, who was fatally shot by armed police in 2011. After his father's death, Duggan was looked after by Marcus Knox-Hooke, one of his father's friends. This would lead Knox-Hooke to form a program to look after vulnerable youth in Tottenham.
Sometime afterwards, Duggan began secondary school; however, he was kicked out three months after beginning due to his inability to control his behaviour.


== Career ==


=== 2018-19: Early career and Frontstreet ===
In a 2022 video showcasing his daily life, Bandokay stated that Kash, a member of OFB, was the main reason that he would take a career in music seriously; according to Bandokay, Kash would call him in order to write lyrics.
Bandokay began his musical career in early 2018 with the release of "Bruck It" alongside Kash, Ys, Double Lz and Boogie B. In late 2018, he released "Bad B on the Nizz" alongside Double Lz and SJ; according to an interview with Complex Networks, the song gained one million views in a week. In the same interview, Double Lz said that the first song that he and Bandokay made was created in 2017; however, it was never released. The three would, for sometime, adopt the name Y.OFB ("Young OFB"); the "Y." prefix would later be dropped in 2019. 
On 14 November 2019, The group released their debut mixtape Frontstreet; the mixtape peaked at number 36 on the UK Albums Chart. The mixtape also included "Ambush", Which was certified silver by the British Phonographic Industry.


=== 2019-21: Drill Commandments ===
Following the release of Frontstreet, Bandokay would appear on Kenny Allstar's Mad About Bars freestyle series in 2019 and release  "Lightwork Freestyle" in 2020, both of which featured Double Lz. In 2020, he would release "OT Bopping" with Double Lz, which peaked at number 91 on the UK Singles Chart.
In the beginning of 2020, Bandokay was named within the top 20 British MCs to watch in 2020 by Complex Networks.
In March 2020, Bandokay would appear alongside Double Lz on iLL BLU's "Magic" and on "War" by Mastermind, which would peak at number 46 and number 39 on the UK Singles Chart, respectively. In May, he would release "Patient", which would peak at number 92. 
In July, Bandokay would appear on Deno's "Circles", also featuring Double Lz; the song peaked at number 36. In October, Bandokay would release "BLM" with Double Lz and Abra Cadabra, which peaked at number 63. During a 2020 interview with Vice regarding "BLM", Double Lz and Bandokay teased that another mixtape was in the works, which included features from Loski, Abra Cadabra, and others. 
The mixtape, named Drill Commandments, was released by the two on 19 March 2021; it would peak at number 53 on the UK Albums Chart.


=== 2021-present: No Requests and solo album ===
In June 2021, Bandokay released "Slide"; it peaked at number 74.
In January 2022, Bandokay announced in a video that he and Double Lz were to release solo albums. He would also release "Praise the Lord" in the same month. In February, Bandokay was signed to No Requests, created by Tiffany Calver in collaboration with Polydor Records. In March, he would release "Tower Hill Freestyle", named after an area in Saint Andrew Parish, Jamaica.


== Legal issues ==
In 2022, Bandokay, alongside Double Lz, was charged with violent disorder following a 2021 incident at a Selfridges store where two people were stabbed.
On 15 January 2024, Bandokay was summoned at Thames Magistrates Court and charged with possession of a firearm and possession of ammunition without a license.
On 2 July 2024, BandoKay was due to face trial at the Old Bailey accused of possessing a Tokarev pistol and 22 bulleted cartridges with intent to endanger life last year. Just before his trial was due to start, however, he pleaded guilty to lesser offences of possession with intent to cause fear of violence. The court was told that the minimum sentence for possession of an illegal firearm was five years in prison. Judge Philip Katz KC remanded the defendants into custody to be sentenced on 5 July 2024. On 5 July 2024, Kemani Duggan was sentenced to five years in prison.

{{Use American English|date=July 2023}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2023}} {{Short description|American hip hop record label}} {{Redirect|CTE World}} {{Infobox record label | name = Corporate Thugz Entertainment | image = [[File:CTE World logo.png|alt=A black man with braids wearing a silver chain with an eagle on its end|center]] | parent = [[The Universal Music Group]] | founded = 2001 | founder = Kinky B
[[Young Jeezy]] | distributor = {{hlist|[[The Island Def Jam Music Group|Island Def Jam]]||[[Def Jam Recordings|Def Jam]]}} | genre = [[Hip Hop music|Hip hop]] | country = United States | location = [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], U.S. | website = {{URL|https://cteworld.com}} }} '''CTE New World''' (acronym for '''Corporate Thugz Entertainment''', formerly '''CTE World''') is an American [[record label]] founded by rapper [[Jeezy]] and his former business partner Kinky B in 2001. In December 2012, the label signed a joint venture deal with [[Atlantic Records|Atlantic]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rap-up.com/2012/12/11/young-jeezys-cte-world-inks-deal-with-atlantic-records/ |title=Young Jeezy's Corporate Thugz Inks Deal with Atlantic |publisher=Rap-Up.com |access-date=June 10, 2013}}{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/young-jeezy-releases-its-tha-world-mixtape-announces-cte-world-1481443/ |title=Young Jeezy Releases 'It's Tha World' Mixtape, Announces Corporate Thugz, Atlantic Deal |date=December 12, 2012 |publisher=Billboard |access-date=June 10, 2013}} The label has signed artists including [[YG (rapper)|YG]], [[Freddie Gibbs]], [[Blood Raw]], [[Scrilla]], and Jeezy's group, [[U.S.D.A. (band)|USDA]]. The group's member, Boo Rossini was appointed as the label's president in 2016.{{cite web | url=http://allhiphop.com/2016/07/23/young-jeezy-signs-boston-george-and-makes-boo-rossini-president-of-cte-world/ | title=Young Jeezy Signs Boston George and Makes Boo Rossini President Of CTE World | publisher=Allhiphop | date=July 23, 2016 | access-date=July 24, 2016}} ==History== Corporate Thugz was launched in 2001 by Young Jeezy and his business partner, Kinky B. The label independently released two albums in 2001 and 2003, [[Young Jeezy]]'s ''Thuggin' Under the Influence (T.U.I.)'' and ''Come Shop wit Me'', respectively. In May 2004, [[Jazze Pha]]'s manager, Henry 'Noonie' Lee, showed Jeezy's demo to his friend [[Shakir Stewart]], then Vice President Artist and Repertoire (VP A&R) at Def Jam.{{cite web|url=http://www.hitquarters.com/index.php3?page=intrview/opar/intrview_ShakirStewart.html|title=Interview With Shakir Stewart|date=November 14, 2005|publisher=[[HitQuarters]]|access-date=June 22, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111223118/http://www.hitquarters.com/index.php3?page=intrview%2Fopar%2Fintrview_ShakirStewart.html|archive-date=January 11, 2019|url-status=dead}} Stewart "fell in love with it [the demo] the first time [he] heard it" and took it to [[L.A. Reid]]. Reid recognized Jeezy's talent and gave Stewart the green light to sign him. Due to Young Jeezy's rising popularity, other [[record label]]s began pursuing him simultaneously to sign with them, most notably, [[Warner Music Group|Warner Music]] and [[Interscope Records|Interscope]]. Ultimately, Jeezy decided he wanted to be in business with Stewart and Reid and signed himself and Corporate Thugz to [[Def Jam Recordings]] and [[The Island Def Jam Music Group]]. The following year, he released his 1st major label studio album ''[[Let's Get It: Thug Motivation 101]]''. Then in 2006 he released his 2nd major label studio album ''[[The Inspiration]]'' and in 2007 formed the rap group [[United Streets Dopeboyz of America]] (USDA) and signed [[Slick Pulla]], [[Blood Raw]], 211, JW and Boo Rossini to Corporate Thugz and released his label's 3rd studio album and USDA's debut studio album ''[[Young Jeezy Presents USDA: Cold Summer]]''. In 2008 [[Young Jeezy]] released ''[[The Recession]]''. In 2011, Young Jeezy signed [[Freddie Gibbs]], [[Tone Trump]], and [[Scrilla]] to Corporate Thugz. Freddie Gibbs left Corporate Thugz in late 2012, and after leaving the label Gibbs said "Anything he (Young Jeezy) tells you is fake." This laid the groundwork for Gibbs's album ''[[ESGN]]'' and the diss records directed at Jeezy.{{cite web|url=http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2013/06/freddie-gibbs-blasts-young-jeezy-says-anything-he-tells-you-its-going-to-be-fake/ |title=Freddie Gibbs Blasts Young Jeezy, Says "Anything He Tells You, It's Going To Be Fake" - XXL |publisher=Xxlmag.com |date=June 10, 2013 |access-date=October 6, 2013}} On New Year's Eve 2012 Scrilla announced that he had asked for and received his release from Corporate Thugz, and that there were no hard feelings.{{cite web|url=http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.22381/title.scrilla-says-hes-leaving-young-jeezys-cte-imprint|title=Scrilla Says He's Leaving Young Jeezy's CTE Imprint|author=HipHopDX|date=December 31, 2012|work=HipHopDX|access-date=August 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921055427/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.22381/title.scrilla-says-hes-leaving-young-jeezys-cte-imprint|archive-date=September 21, 2013|url-status=dead}} First action in the new imprint deal with Atlantic, Craig Kallman and Jeezy named Steven "Steve-O" Carless as A&R of Atlantic and President of Corporate Thugz.{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6236431/young-jeezy-posts-bail|title=Young Jeezy Posts Bail|website=Billboard.com|date=August 29, 2014|access-date=November 1, 2017}} In early 2013 Young Jeezy signed Detroit hip hop group Doughboyz Cashout{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1707459/young-jeezy-signs-doughboyz-cashout-cte.jhtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607063451/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1707459/young-jeezy-signs-doughboyz-cashout-cte.jhtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 7, 2013 |title=Young Jeezy Signs 'Ghetto Superstars' Doughboyz Cashout To CTE: Watch Now! - Music, Celebrity, Artist News |publisher=MTV.com |date=May 16, 2013 |access-date=June 10, 2013}} and later that year West Coast rapper [[YG (rapper)|YG]] was added to the record label.{{cite web|url=http://www.complex.com/music/2013/06/yg-announces-that-hes-signing-to-young-jeezys-cte |title=YG Young Jeezy CTE |publisher=Complex |date=June 18, 2013 |access-date=October 6, 2013}} On August 13, 2013, the label released a compilation mixtape featuring Jeezy, Doughboyz Cashout, and YG titled ''[[Boss Yo Life Up Gang]]''.{{cite web|url=http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2013/08/young-jeezy-to-release-compilation-mixtape/ |title=Young Jeezy To Release Compilation Mixtape - XXL |publisher=Xxlmag.com |date=August 6, 2013 |access-date=October 6, 2013}} The mixtape was supported by the singles "[[My Nigga]]" by YG and "Mob Life" by Doughboyz Cashout, both featuring Young Jeezy. CTE New World.text:
CTE New World (acronym for Corporate Thugz Entertainment, formerly CTE World) is an American record label founded by rapper Jeezy and his former business partner Kinky B in 2001. In December 2012, the label signed a joint venture deal with Atlantic. The label has signed artists including YG, Freddie Gibbs, Blood Raw, Scrilla, and Jeezy's group, USDA. The group's member, Boo Rossini was appointed as the label's president in 2016.


== History ==
Corporate Thugz was launched in 2001 by Young Jeezy and his business partner, Kinky B. The label independently released two albums in 2001 and 2003, Young Jeezy's Thuggin' Under the Influence (T.U.I.) and Come Shop wit Me, respectively. 
In May 2004, Jazze Pha's manager, Henry 'Noonie' Lee, showed Jeezy's demo to his friend Shakir Stewart, then Vice President Artist and Repertoire (VP A&R) at Def Jam. Stewart "fell in love with it [the demo] the first time [he] heard it" and took it to L.A. Reid. Reid recognized Jeezy's talent and gave Stewart the green light to sign him.  Due to Young Jeezy's rising popularity, other record labels began pursuing him simultaneously to sign with them, most notably, Warner Music and Interscope. Ultimately, Jeezy decided he wanted to be in business with Stewart and Reid and signed himself and Corporate Thugz to Def Jam Recordings and The Island Def Jam Music Group. The following year, he released his 1st major label studio album Let's Get It: Thug Motivation 101. Then in 2006 he released his 2nd major label studio album The Inspiration and in 2007 formed the rap group United Streets Dopeboyz of America (USDA) and signed Slick Pulla, Blood Raw, 211, JW and Boo Rossini to Corporate Thugz and released his label's 3rd studio album and USDA's debut studio album Young Jeezy Presents USDA: Cold Summer. In 2008 Young Jeezy released The Recession.
In 2011, Young Jeezy signed Freddie Gibbs, Tone Trump, and Scrilla to Corporate Thugz. Freddie Gibbs left Corporate Thugz in late 2012, and after leaving the label Gibbs said "Anything he (Young Jeezy) tells you is fake." This laid the groundwork for Gibbs's album ESGN and the diss records directed at Jeezy. On New Year's Eve 2012 Scrilla announced that he had asked for and received his release from Corporate Thugz, and that there were no hard feelings. First action in the new imprint deal with Atlantic, Craig Kallman and Jeezy named Steven "Steve-O" Carless as A&R of Atlantic and President of Corporate Thugz. In early 2013 Young Jeezy signed Detroit hip hop group Doughboyz Cashout and later that year West Coast rapper YG was added to the record label. On August 13, 2013, the label released a compilation mixtape featuring Jeezy, Doughboyz Cashout, and YG titled Boss Yo Life Up Gang. The mixtape was supported by the singles "My Nigga" by YG and "Mob Life" by Doughboyz Cashout, both featuring Young Jeezy. On November 20, 2013 Young Jeezy and Corporate Thugz via Twitter announced he had signed the label to Roc Nation.

{{Short description|American inventor and businessman (1813–1874)}}
[[Image:Samuel Martin Kier 1813-1874.JPG|thumb|right|250px]]

'''Samuel Martin Kier''' (July 19, 1813 – October 6, 1874) was an American inventor and businessman who is credited with founding the American [[petroleum]] [[oil refinery|refining]] industry.  He was the first person in the United States to refine crude oil into [[kerosene]] lamp oil.<ref Name="Pioneer">{{cite book
  | title =Greater Pittsburgh and Allegheny County, Past, Present, Future; The Pioneer Oil Refiner
  | publisher =The American Manufacturer and Iron World 
  | year =1901
  | location =Original from the New York Public Library
  | url =https://books.google.com/books?id=lkcVAAAAYAAJ&q=refinery+kier+pittsburgh&pg=PT57
  }}</ref>  Kier has been dubbed the ''Grandfather of the American Oil Industry'' by historians.<ref Name="McInnis">{{cite web
  | last =McInnis
  | first =Karen 
  | title = Kier, Samuel Martin- Bio
  | work = biography
  | publisher =The Pennsylvania State University
  | url =http://www.pabook.libraries.psu.edu/palitmap/bios/Kier__Samuel_Martin.html
  | format =web
  | access-date = 2008-12-12 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Kier was born in [[Conemaugh Township, Indiana County, Pennsylvania|Conemaugh Township]], [[Indiana County, Pennsylvania]] near the town of [[Livermore, Pennsylvania|Livermore]].  He was the son of Thomas Kier and Mary Martin Kier.  The Kiers were [[Scotch-Irish American|Scots-Irish]] [[immigrants]] who owned several [[salt well]]s around Livermore and nearby [[Saltsburg, Pennsylvania|Saltsburg]].

In addition to the salt business, Samuel helped found Kier, Royer and Co., in 1838.  The company was a canal boat operation that shipped coal between [[Pittsburgh]] and [[Philadelphia]].  Kier also owned interest in several coal mines, a brickyard, and a pottery factory.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Croneis |first=Carey |date=1933 |title=Early History of Petroleum in North America |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/15591 |journal=The Scientific Monthly |volume=37 |issue=2 |pages=124–133 |jstor=15591 |bibcode=1933SciMo..37..124C |issn=0096-3771}}</ref>

He, along with several other investors including [[Benjamin Franklin Jones (industrialist)|Benjamin Franklin Jones]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last1=Fork |first1=Mailing Address: 733 Lake Road South |last2=Us |first2=PA 15956 Phone: 814 886-6171 Contact |title=Benjamin Franklin "B.F." Jones (1824-1903) - Johnstown Flood National Memorial (U.S. National Park Service) |url=https://www.nps.gov/jofl/learn/historyculture/benjamin-franklin-jones.htm |access-date=2024-05-05 |website=www.nps.gov |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Detre Library & Archives, Heinz History Center - Jones & Laughlin Steel Corporation Photographs |url=https://historicpittsburgh.org/islandora/object/pitt:MSP33.B006.F01.I03 |access-date=2024-05-05 |website=historicpittsburgh.org|title=Benjamin Franklin Jones, Sr. | Historic Pittsburgh}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Smerker |first=Nick |date=2015-06-08 |title=The Joneses |url=https://alleghenywest.org/the-joneses/ |access-date=2024-05-05 |website=Allegheny West |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Detre Library & Archives, Heinz History Center |first=Jones & Laughlin Steel Corporation Photographs |title=B. F. Jones in Old Warehouse Office |url=https://historicpittsburgh.org/islandora/object/pitt%3AMSP33.B006.F01.I04}}</ref> founded several iron foundries in west central Pennsylvania.  The iron business would be the forerunner of the [[Jones and Laughlin Steel Company]], one of the largest steel producers in America.

Kier married Nancy Eicher<ref>{{Cite web |title=Samuel Martin Kier, b.1813 d.1874 - Ancestry® |url=https://www.ancestry.com.au/genealogy/records/samuel-martin-kier-24-22t6368 |access-date=2024-05-05 |website=www.ancestry.com.au |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Jordan |first=John W |title=Encyclopedia of Pennsylvania - biography |publisher=NEW YORK LEWIS HISTORICAL PUBLISHING COMPANY |year=1914 |pages=1467 |trans-title=}}</ref> of [[Greensburg, Pennsylvania|Greensburg]], Pennsylvania in 1842.

== Business career  ==
Samuel Kier moved to Pittsburgh at the age of 21. In Pittsburgh, he found employment with a railway express company,<ref>{{Cite book |last=J. T. Henry |title=The Early and Later History of Petroleum: With Authentic Facts in Regard to Its Development in Western Pennsylvania. The Oil Fields of Europe and America. ... Fields. Also, Life Sketches of Pioneer... |publisher=J.B. Rodgers Company, Printers, 1873 |year=1872 |pages=28, 56, 61, 83, 87, 90, 94, 97}}</ref> where he recognized his business acumen. He soon became a partner in the expanding enterprise, but the business eventually collapsed during the economic downturn of the [[Panic of 1837]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Pennsylvania Center for the Book |url=https://pabook.libraries.psu.edu/literary-cultural-heritage-map-pa/bios/Kier__Samuel_Martin |access-date=2024-05-05 |website=pabook.libraries.psu.edu}}</ref>

Samuel Kier rebounded from the failure<ref>{{Cite journal |doi= 10.2118/1195-G|title= The First Oil Well|date= 1959|last1= Dickey|first1= Parke A.|journal= Journal of Petroleum Technology|volume= 11|pages= 14–26}}</ref> of his first business by exploring new opportunities. In 1838, he ventured into canal transportation, utilizing [[Pennsylvania Canal|Pennsylvania's extensive canal system]] connecting Lake Erie to Pittsburgh and Philadelphia. Kier hired several independent canal operators of the Pennsylvania Canal to establish a continuous route from Pittsburgh to Philadelphia and formed Kier, Roger, and Company to manage the operation. This enterprise proved financially successful, allowing Kier to settle any outstanding debts from his previous business.<ref name=":0" />

When the government began constructing the [[Pennsylvania Railroad]], which paralleled Kier's canal route, he adapted his canal business. In 1846, Kier, in partnership with [[James Buchanan|James Buchannan]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Alfred N. Mann |title=Some Petroleum Pioneers of Pittsburgh |url=https://www.heinzhistorycenter.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/4-Petroleum-Pioneers.pdf |journal=Western Pennsylvania History Magazine |issue=2009}}</ref> later President of the United States, established "Independent Line," working with special section where "amphibious" canal boats boats which could be taken apart and put on railroad cars where they were available, or put together and pulled along the canal system where there was no railroad.  When later partnered<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> with [[Benjamin Franklin Jones (industrialist)|Benjamin Jones]] (of [[Jones and Laughlin Steel Company]]), this canal boat company eventually became, the "Mechanics Line." This innovative transportation method thrived until the railroad's completion in 1854, at which point Kier ceased the production and operation of the hybrid boats. But by 1854 with expanded railroad competition, the canal boat Company was discontinued and Kier, Buchannan, and Jones went into the fire-brick business in [[Bolivar, Pennsylvania]] (later moved to [[Salina, Pennsylvania]]).  They, Kier and Jones, also purchased iron furnaces at [[Armagh, Pennsylvania|Armaugh]], near Johnstown, Pennsylvania.  By the time he terminated his canal business, Kier had diversified into several other ventures, including a [[Fire brick|firebrick]] and pottery factory,<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Washlaski |first=Raymond A. |title=KIER: Kier Mine (Kier Fire Brick Mine) (Salina Mine), Salina, Bell Township, Westmoreland Co., Pennsylvania, U.S.A. |url=https://www.academia.edu/44241785}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kemp |first=Emory |date=1996-01-01 |title=Review: ''"A Fine Substantial Piece of Masonry": Scranton's Historical Furnaces'', by Daniel K. Perry and ''Brickyard Towns: A History of Refractories Industry Communities in South-Central Pennsylvania'', by Kim E. Wallace |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2307/3377894 |journal=The Public Historian |volume=18 |issue=1 |pages=112–115 |doi=10.2307/3377894 |jstor=3377894 |issn=0272-3433|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tribliveoffers.com/welcome |access-date=2024-05-05 |website=www.tribliveoffers.com}}</ref> investments in steel and iron, and notably, his involvement in the oil industry.<ref name=":0" />

By the 1840s, Kier's [[salt well]]s were becoming fouled with petroleum.  At first, Kier simply dumped the useless oil into the nearby [[Pennsylvania Main Line Canal]], but after an oil slick caught fire, he saw a way to profit from this otherwise worthless byproduct. With no formal training in science or [[chemistry]], he began experimenting with several distillates of the crude oil along with a chemist from eastern Pennsylvania.   He developed a substance he named "Rock Oil" and later "Seneca Oil".  In 1848, he began packaging  the substance as a [[patent medicine]] charging $0.50 per bottle.<ref Name="Harper">{{cite web
 |last        = Harper
 |first       = J. A.
 |title       = Samuel Kier - Medicine Man & Refiner
 |work        = Excerpt from Yo-Ho-Ho and a Bottle of Unrefined Complex Liquid Hydrocarbons. Pennsylvania Geology, v. 26, No. 1, p. -
 |publisher   = Oil Region Alliance of Business, Industry & Tourism
 |year        = 1995
 |url         = http://www.oil150.com/essays/2007/02/samual-kier
 |format      = web
 |access-date  = 2008-12-12
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120315221502/http://www.oil150.com/essays/2007/02/samual-kier
 |archive-date = 2012-03-15
}}</ref> He also produced petroleum<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-21 |title=S.M. Kier. Petroleum Pittsburgh |url=https://fohbcvirtualmuseum.org/galleries/medicines/s-m-kier-petroleum-pittsburgh/ |access-date=2024-05-05 |website=fohbcvirtualmuseum.org |language=en-US}}</ref> butter ([[petroleum jelly]]) and sold it as a topical ointment.<ref Name="Welty">{{cite book 
|title= The 76 Bonanza: The Fabulous Life and Times of the Union Oil Company of California
|last= Welty
|author2=Earl M. Welty |author3=Frank J. Taylor
 |year= 1966
|publisher= Lane Magazine & Book Co
|location= Original from the University of Michigan
|page= 46
|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=xwE7AAAAMAAJ&q=Kier+%22petroleum+butter%22}}</ref>  Neither product proved to be a commercial success.

After further experimenting, he discovered an economical way to produce kerosene.  Kerosene had been known for some time but was not widely produced and was considered to have little economic value. But at the time [[whale oil]], the principal fuel for lamps in America, was becoming increasingly scarce and expensive.

Kier began selling the kerosene, named "Carbon Oil", to local miners in 1851.  He also invented a new lamp to burn his product.<ref name="Pioneer"/>  Kier never obtained a patent for his developments and many other inventors and businessmen would go on to improve upon his work yielding huge fortunes.  Even so, Kier's income at the time exceeded US$40,000 per year, a huge sum for the time.

Kier established America's first oil refinery in Pittsburgh on Seventh avenue near Grant Street, in 1853.<ref name="Pioneer"/>  A marker identifying the site reads "Kier Refinery – Using a five-barrel still, Samuel M. Kier erected on this site about 1854 the first commercial refinery to produce illuminating oil from petroleum. He used crude oil from salt wells at [[Tarentum, Pennsylvania|Tarentum]]."<ref>[http://www.waymarking.com/waymarks/WMGBM Kier Refinery, in Pennsylvania Historical Markers] at waymarking.com</ref> Kier consulted with [[Edwin Drake]] concerning Drake's experimental [[oil well]].<ref Name="Wright">{{cite book

Samuel Kier.text:
Samuel Martin Kier (July 19, 1813 – October 6, 1874) was an American inventor and businessman who is credited with founding the American petroleum refining industry.  He was the first person in the United States to refine crude oil into kerosene lamp oil.  Kier has been dubbed the Grandfather of the American Oil Industry by historians.


== Biography ==
Kier was born in Conemaugh Township, Indiana County, Pennsylvania near the town of Livermore.  He was the son of Thomas Kier and Mary Martin Kier.  The Kiers were Scots-Irish immigrants who owned several salt wells around Livermore and nearby Saltsburg.
In addition to the salt business, Samuel helped found Kier, Royer and Co., in 1838.  The company was a canal boat operation that shipped coal between Pittsburgh and Philadelphia.  Kier also owned interest in several coal mines, a brickyard, and a pottery factory.
He, along with several other investors including Benjamin Franklin Jones, founded several iron foundries in west central Pennsylvania.  The iron business would be the forerunner of the Jones and Laughlin Steel Company, one of the largest steel producers in America.
Kier married Nancy Eicher of Greensburg, Pennsylvania in 1842.


== Business career ==
Samuel Kier moved to Pittsburgh at the age of 21. In Pittsburgh, he found employment with a railway express company, where he recognized his business acumen. He soon became a partner in the expanding enterprise, but the business eventually collapsed during the economic downturn of the Panic of 1837.
Samuel Kier rebounded from the failure of his first business by exploring new opportunities. In 1838, he ventured into canal transportation, utilizing Pennsylvania's extensive canal system connecting Lake Erie to Pittsburgh and Philadelphia. Kier hired several independent canal operators of the Pennsylvania Canal to establish a continuous route from Pittsburgh to Philadelphia and formed Kier, Roger, and Company to manage the operation. This enterprise proved financially successful, allowing Kier to settle any outstanding debts from his previous business.
When the government began constructing the Pennsylvania Railroad, which paralleled Kier's canal route, he adapted his canal business. In 1846, Kier, in partnership with James Buchannan, later President of the United States, established "Independent Line," working with special section where "amphibious" canal boats boats which could be taken apart and put on railroad cars where they were available, or put together and pulled along the canal system where there was no railroad.  When later partnered with Benjamin Jones (of Jones and Laughlin Steel Company), this canal boat company eventually became, the "Mechanics Line." This innovative transportation method thrived until the railroad's completion in 1854, at which point Kier ceased the production and operation of the hybrid boats. But by 1854 with expanded railroad competition, the canal boat Company was discontinued and Kier, Buchannan, and Jones went into the fire-brick business in Bolivar, Pennsylvania (later moved to Salina, Pennsylvania).  They, Kier and Jones, also purchased iron furnaces at Armaugh, near Johnstown, Pennsylvania.  By the time he terminated his canal business, Kier had diversified into several other ventures, including a firebrick and pottery factory, investments in steel and iron, and notably, his involvement in the oil industry.
By the 1840s, Kier's salt wells were becoming fouled with petroleum.  At first, Kier simply dumped the useless oil into the nearby Pennsylvania Main Line Canal, but after an oil slick caught fire, he saw a way to profit from this otherwise worthless byproduct. With no formal training in science or chemistry, he began experimenting with several distillates of the crude oil along with a chemist from eastern Pennsylvania.   He developed a substance he named "Rock Oil" and later "Seneca Oil".  In 1848, he began packaging  the substance as a patent medicine charging $0.50 per bottle. He also produced petroleum butter (petroleum jelly) and sold it as a topical ointment.  Neither product proved to be a commercial success.
After further experimenting, he discovered an economical way to produce kerosene.  Kerosene had been known for some time but was not widely produced and was considered to have little economic value. But at the time whale oil, the principal fuel for lamps in America, was becoming increasingly scarce and expensive.
Kier began selling the kerosene, named "Carbon Oil", to local miners in 1851.  He also invented a new lamp to burn his product.  Kier never obtained a patent for his developments and many other inventors and businessmen would go on to improve upon his work yielding huge fortunes.  Even so, Kier's income at the time exceeded US$40,000 per year, a huge sum for the time.
Kier established America's first oil refinery in Pittsburgh on Seventh avenue near Grant Street, in 1853.  A marker identifying the site reads "Kier Refinery – Using a five-barrel still, Samuel M. Kier erected on this site about 1854 the first commercial refinery to produce illuminating oil from petroleum. He used crude oil from salt wells at Tarentum." Kier consulted with Edwin Drake concerning Drake's experimental oil well.

'''David R. Styles''' (born November 28, 1974), better known by his [[stage name]] '''Styles P''' (also known [[Mononymous person|mononymously]] as '''Styles'''),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hiphopdx.com/reviews/id.187/title.styles-a-gangsta-a-gentleman|title=Styles - A Gangsta & A Gentleman|date=July 12, 2002|website=HipHopDX.com|access-date=February 24, 2022}}</ref> is an American rapper, best known as a member of East Coast hip-hop group [[The Lox]]. Formed with fellow rappers [[Sheek Louch]] and [[Jadakiss]] in 1994, the group was also part of the [[Ruff Ryders Entertainment]] collective.

As a solo act, Styles signed with Ruff Ryders' parent label, [[Interscope Records]], to release his debut studio album, ''[[A Gangster and a Gentleman]]'' (2002). Its lead single, "[[Good Times (Styles P song)|Good Times]]," peaked at number 22 on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], while the album peaked at number six on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/rapper-heads-rock-pile-hip-hop-artist-styles-p-cusp-success-faces-jail-term-article-1.505291|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150101215400/http://www.nydailynews.com/rapper-heads-rock-pile-hip-hop-artist-styles-p-cusp-success-faces-jail-term-article-1.505291|archive-date = January 1, 2015|title = RAPPER HEADS FOR ROCK PILE Hip-hop artist Styles P., on the cusp of success, faces a jail term|website = [[New York Daily News]]| date=July 14, 2002 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.21892/title.styles-p-speaks-on-being-the-worlds-most-hardest-emcee-involvement-on-upcoming-wu-block-album/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121117132504/http://www.hiphopdx.com/index/news/id.21892/title.styles-p-speaks-on-being-the-worlds-most-hardest-emcee-involvement-on-upcoming-wu-block-album/|archive-date=November 17, 2012|title=Styles P Speaks on Being "The World's Most Hardest Emcee," Involvement on Upcoming "Wu-Block" Album|date=November 15, 2012}}</ref> He guest appeared alongside Jadakiss on [[Jennifer Lopez]]' 2002 single "[[Jenny from the Block]]," as well as Senegalese-American singer [[Akon]]'s 2004 single "[[Locked Up (song)|Locked Up]]" — both songs peaked within the top ten of the ''Billboard'' Hot 100.

He has since released the albums ''[[Time Is Money (Styles P album)|Time Is Money]]'' (2006), ''[[Super Gangster (Extraordinary Gentleman)]]'' (2007), ''[[Master of Ceremonies (Styles P album)|Master of Ceremonies]]'' (2011), ''[[The World's Most Hardest MC Project]]'' (2012), ''[[Float (Styles P album)|Float]]'' (2013), ''[[Phantom and the Ghost]]'' (2014), ''A Wise Guy and a Wise Guy'' (2015), and ''[[G-Host]]'' (2018).

== Early life ==

David R. Styles was born November 28, 1974, in [[Corona, Queens]] to a South African mother, a Zulu woman from [[Clermont, KwaZulu-Natal]], and a Jamaican father.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.last.fm/music/Styles+P/+wiki |title=Style P Bio |author=<!--Not stated--> |website= Last.fm |publisher= CBS Corporation}}</ref> After his parents' divorce, Styles and his younger brother Gary moved to [[Yonkers, New York|Yonkers]] with their mother. It was there he met lifelong friends [[Jadakiss]] and [[Sheek Louch]]. The trio bonded over their shared passion for [[hip-hop]] and eventually formed a group known as [[the Lox]] in 1994.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1995400/bio|title=Styles P.|website=IMDb|access-date=April 2, 2018}}</ref><ref name="complex1">{{cite web|last=Ortiz |first=Edwin |url=http://www.complex.com/music/2014/01/jadakiss-unhinged-the-combat-jack-show |title=Jadakiss Talks About Growing Up In Yonkers and The LOX's Relationship with Mary J. Blige – The Combat Jack Show |publisher=Complex |date=January 23, 2014 |access-date=August 14, 2015}}</ref>

== Career ==
=== 1994–2000: The Lox ===
[[File:Jadakiss Styles P.jpg|thumb|Styles P (left) performing with [[Jadakiss]]]]
As a trio, the Lox began rapping in the mid-1990s and started to build a steady underground following thanks to their performances and street freestyles. In their late teens, the trio met [[Mary J. Blige]] who was impressed with their lyrical content, and gave their demo to [[Sean Combs|Sean "Puffy" Combs]].<ref name="complex1" /> Combs immediately hired the trio to write for [[Bad Boy Records]]. After signing with Bad Boy, the Lox quickly started collaborating on hits with Combs, [[the Notorious B.I.G.]], Mary J. Blige and [[Mariah Carey]] which gave them instant notoriety and status within the hip-hop and mainstream charts.<ref name="complex1" /> In 1996 and 1997, the group wrote and performed on a number of Diddy hits, including "[[It's All About the Benjamins]]" and "I Got the Power", [[Mase]]'s "[[24 Hrs. to Live]]", Mariah Carey's "[[Honey (Mariah Carey song)|Honey]]", the Notorious B.I.G.'s "Last Day" and Mary J. Blige's "Can't Get You Off My Mind".<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web |author=Vibe |url=http://www.vibe.com/photo-galleries/story-time-sheek-louch-recalls-studio-sessions-dmx-biggie-jay-z |title=Story Time: Sheek Louch Recalls Studio Sessions With DMX, Biggie & Jay-Z |publisher=Vibe |date=September 28, 2010 |access-date=August 14, 2015 |archive-date=October 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002044729/http://www.vibe.com/photo-galleries/story-time-sheek-louch-recalls-studio-sessions-dmx-biggie-jay-z |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1997, the Lox received international acclaim when their tribute to the late Biggie Smalls, "We'll Always Love Big Poppa", was picked as the B-side track from Combs' ''[[No Way Out (Puff Daddy album)|No Way Out]]'' album (3× Platinum) with the number one hit, "[[I'll Be Missing You]]".<ref name="autogenerated1" /> This single was the most played hit in 1997, which opened the door for the Lox's to write more of their own songs and eventually release their first album in January 1998 titled ''[[Money, Power & Respect]]''.<ref>{{cite web|author=Stephen Thomas Erlewine |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/money-power-respect-mw0000031595 |title=Money, Power & Respect – The LOX | Songs, Reviews, Credits, Awards |publisher=AllMusic |date=January 13, 1998 |access-date=August 14, 2015}}</ref> The album went on to be certified platinum, and, although the album was a chart-topping success, the group grew to feel that the glossy image and production style of Bad Boy Records conflicted with their grimier rap aesthetic. After trying and failing to get Combs to grant them a release from their contract, the group confronted him in his office, with Styles P throwing a chair at his own boss. After this, the group was granted their release and left Bad Boy to sign with [[Ruff Ryders Entertainment]] and [[Interscope Records]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-jan-23-ca-56625-story.html |title=More Grime Than Shine, the LOX Moves On – latimes |publisher=Articles.latimes.com |date=October 14, 2006 |access-date=August 14, 2015 |first=Soren |last=Baker}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NLaUUWHA5q0  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211213/NLaUUWHA5q0 |archive-date=December 13, 2021 |url-status=live|title=Jadakiss Recalls Styles P Throwing A Chair At Diddy So "The LOX" Could Leave Bad Boy Records |date=February 5, 2020 |publisher=[[YouTube]] |access-date=March 12, 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

=== 2000–2007: Ruff Ryders and solo albums ===
After releasing another Lox album, ''[[We Are the Streets]]'' and appearing on albums with other Ruff Ryders artists, Styles released his first solo album, ''[[A Gangster and a Gentleman]]'', in 2002.<ref name="allmusic1">{{cite web|last=Birchmeier |first=Jason |url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/styles-p-p693696 |title=Styles P |publisher=AllMusic |date=November 28, 1974 |access-date=March 30, 2012}}</ref> The album was supported by the hit single, [[Good Times (Styles P song)|Good Times]], which peaked at number 22 on the US [[Billboard Hot 100]] and number 6 on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]]. The song also received widespread airplay on the radio throughout 2002. In 2004, Styles was featured on an alternate version of [[Akon]]'s hit debut single, [[Locked Up (song)|Locked Up]]. Two years later, he released his second album, ''[[Time Is Money (Styles P album)|Time is Money]]'' on Ruff Ryders. In 2007, Styles would leave Ruff Ryders and Interscope to independently release his third studio album ''[[Super Gangster (Extraordinary Gentleman)]]'' on D-Block Records and [[MNRK Music Group|Koch Records]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://hiphopdx.com/news/id.5038/title.styles-p-signs-to-koch|title= STYLES P SIGNS TO KOCH|website=[[HipHopDX]]|last=Cooper|first=Roman|date=March 27, 2007|access-date=October 15, 2023}}</ref><ref name="allmusic1" />

=== 2016–present: The Lox reunion ===
In 2016, the Lox released their first album in 16 years, ''[[Filthy America... It's Beautiful]]''. The album reached number 6 on the ''Billboard'' Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart. It was followed by the release of the albums, ''[[G-Host]]'' (2018), ''Dime Bag'' (2018), ''S.P. the GOAT: Ghost of All Time'' (2019) and ''Presence'' (2019). Styles P and [[Dave East]] also released a collab album titled ''Beloved'', in 2018. Holders receive discounts on brands, access to shows and events, and all the intellectual property associated with the NFT such as the instrumentals, acapellas, and stems.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=James |first=Benjamin |date=2023-01-02 |title=Here Are the Biggest Music NFTs in December as Year Ends 95% Down From January |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/biggest-music-nfts-in-december-armin-van-buuren-3lau/ |access-date=2023-12-07 |magazine=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref>
