Styles P.text:
David R. Styles (born November 28, 1974), better known by his stage name Styles P (also known mononymously as Styles), is an American rapper, best known as a member of East Coast hip-hop group The Lox. Formed with fellow rappers Sheek Louch and Jadakiss in 1994, the group was also part of the Ruff Ryders Entertainment collective.
As a solo act, Styles signed with Ruff Ryders' parent label, Interscope Records, to release his debut studio album, A Gangster and a Gentleman (2002). Its lead single, "Good Times," peaked at number 22 on the US Billboard Hot 100, while the album peaked at number six on the Billboard 200. He guest appeared alongside Jadakiss on Jennifer Lopez' 2002 single "Jenny from the Block," as well as Senegalese-American singer Akon's 2004 single "Locked Up" — both songs peaked within the top ten of the Billboard Hot 100.
He has since released the albums Time Is Money (2006), Super Gangster (Extraordinary Gentleman) (2007), Master of Ceremonies (2011), The World's Most Hardest MC Project (2012), Float (2013), Phantom and the Ghost (2014), A Wise Guy and a Wise Guy (2015), and G-Host (2018).


== Early life ==
David R. Styles was born November 28, 1974, in Corona, Queens to a South African mother, a Zulu woman from Clermont, KwaZulu-Natal, and a Jamaican father. After his parents' divorce, Styles and his younger brother Gary moved to Yonkers with their mother. It was there he met lifelong friends Jadakiss and Sheek Louch. The trio bonded over their shared passion for hip-hop and eventually formed a group known as the Lox in 1994.


== Career ==


=== 1994–2000: The Lox ===

As a trio, the Lox began rapping in the mid-1990s and started to build a steady underground following thanks to their performances and street freestyles. In their late teens, the trio met Mary J. Blige who was impressed with their lyrical content, and gave their demo to Sean "Puffy" Combs. Combs immediately hired the trio to write for Bad Boy Records. After signing with Bad Boy, the Lox quickly started collaborating on hits with Combs, the Notorious B.I.G., Mary J. Blige and Mariah Carey which gave them instant notoriety and status within the hip-hop and mainstream charts. In 1996 and 1997, the group wrote and performed on a number of Diddy hits, including "It's All About the Benjamins" and "I Got the Power", Mase's "24 Hrs. to Live", Mariah Carey's "Honey", the Notorious B.I.G.'s "Last Day" and Mary J. Blige's "Can't Get You Off My Mind". In 1997, the Lox received international acclaim when their tribute to the late Biggie Smalls, "We'll Always Love Big Poppa", was picked as the B-side track from Combs' No Way Out album (3× Platinum) with the number one hit, "I'll Be Missing You". This single was the most played hit in 1997, which opened the door for the Lox's to write more of their own songs and eventually release their first album in January 1998 titled Money, Power & Respect. The album went on to be certified platinum, and, although the album was a chart-topping success, the group grew to feel that the glossy image and production style of Bad Boy Records conflicted with their grimier rap aesthetic. After trying and failing to get Combs to grant them a release from their contract, the group confronted him in his office, with Styles P throwing a chair at his own boss. After this, the group was granted their release and left Bad Boy to sign with Ruff Ryders Entertainment and Interscope Records.


=== 2000–2007: Ruff Ryders and solo albums ===
After releasing another Lox album, We Are the Streets and appearing on albums with other Ruff Ryders artists, Styles released his first solo album, A Gangster and a Gentleman, in 2002. The album was supported by the hit single, Good Times, which peaked at number 22 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number 6 on the Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs. The song also received widespread airplay on the radio throughout 2002. In 2004, Styles was featured on an alternate version of Akon's hit debut single, Locked Up. Two years later, he released his second album, Time is Money on Ruff Ryders. In 2007, Styles would leave Ruff Ryders and Interscope to independently release his third studio album Super Gangster (Extraordinary Gentleman) on D-Block Records and Koch Records.


=== 2010–2014: The Green Ghost and various mixtapes ===

After recording many mixtapes Styles returned to the Hip-Hop scene by releasing two retail albums in 2010, The Green Ghost Project with DJ Green Lantern on Invasion Records and The Ghost Dub-Dime a retail mixtape on E1 Records (formally Koch Records). This began a string of annual retail releases with his fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh albums (2011's Master of Ceremonies, 2012's The World's Most Hardest MC Project, 2013's Float, and 2014's Phantom and the Ghost) all being released within a year of each other.


=== 2016–present: The Lox reunion ===
In 2016, the Lox released their first album in 16 years, Filthy America... It's Beautiful. The album reached number 6 on the Billboard Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart. It was followed by the release of the albums, G-Host (2018), Dime Bag (2018), S.P. the GOAT: Ghost of All Time (2019) and Presence (2019). Styles P and Dave East also released a collab album titled Beloved, in 2018. Styles P's 13th studio album, Styles David: Ghost Your Enthusiasm, was released on May 22, 2020.


== Personal life ==

Styles is a vegan.
Styles married his wife Adjua on July 31, 1995. Together, they have two children, Noah (born 1998) and Tai (1995–2015), whom Adjua had from a previous relationship. Styles served as Tai's stepfather for the majority of her life, until she committed suicide in 2015.
Styles' younger brother, Gary Quarles Styles, died in a car accident on May 13, 2001. Styles has made many references to Gary in his music, including the tribute song "My Brother", from his debut album A Gangster and a Gentleman.
In July 2002, Styles was involved in an altercation at a New York nightclub that led to him stabbing a man in the buttocks. Styles surrendered himself to authorities on November 26, 2002, and began serving his eight-month sentence in the Westchester County Jail in Valhalla, New York, the same day. Styles was released from prison on August 4, 2003.


== Business ventures ==
Both Styles and Jadakiss launched a local juice bar called "Juices for Life" in 2011, there are currently six locations in New York. In 2018, Styles and his wife Adjua launched a local health food store called "Farmacy for Life". Styles P launched a Web3 Music NFT project called "The Farmacy Fantoms" with Gregory Cohen known as MΞT∆DUTCH and Daniel Dapaah. Styles collaborated with artist Dino Belli to launch the project on his birthday in 2022. They sold out 6,666 Farmacy Fantoms in two weeks and have over 1,000 holders. Holders receive discounts on brands, access to shows and events, and all the intellectual property associated with the NFT such as the instrumentals, acapellas, and stems.


== Other projects ==
Styles P released his first novel, Invincible, in 2010 through Random House Publishing Group. In 2011 he opened up a juice bar in the Bronx called Juices for Life with his business partners Nyger Rollocks and Leo Galvez. He released his EP with Currensy titled, #The1st28 on February 28, 2012.
Styles P appeared on the sixteenth season of Marriage Boot Camp with his wife, Adjua in 2020.
In February 2022, he was cast in the documentary series Everything's Gonna Be All White, airing on Showtime.

'''Cedric Dormaine Hill''' (born June 3, 1974) better known by his stage name '''E.S.G.''' (which stands for '''E'''veryday '''S'''treet '''G'''angsta or '''E'''veryday '''S'''erving '''G'''od) is an American rapper from [[Houston]], [[Texas]], and is a member of the [[Screwed Up Click]].

==Career==
Born on June 3, 1974, in [[Bogalusa, Louisiana]], he moved to [[Houston]] in his mid-teens. He began rapping in 1991, but spent a year in prison for drug possession.{{Citation needed|date=September 2024}} After being released in late 1992, he resumed his rap career a year later. He joined the Screwed Up Click, headed by [[DJ Screw]], who helped to popularize the "chopped and screwed" style of rap music.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hall |first=Michael |date=2013-01-21 |title=The Slow Life and Fast Death of DJ Screw |url=https://www.texasmonthly.com/arts-entertainment/slow-life-and-fast-death-of-dj-screw/ |access-date=2024-09-23 |website=Texas Monthly |language=en}}</ref> His debut album, ''[[Ocean of Funk]],'' was released on February 1, 1994 under independent label Perrion Entertainment. It contained the popular single "Swangin' & Bangin'", which would later be remixed for his follow-up, ''[[Sailin' Da South]]'', released in September 1995 under [[Priority Records]]; the album was released while E.S.G. was serving another jail sentence for a murder charge.{{Citation needed|date=September 2024|reason=Sources support this claim, but they are not reliable.}} He has released 13 more studio albums since then, ranging from 1998's ''Return of the Living Dead'' and the collaborative album, 2022's ''Dippin & Swangin'' with Mac Mall.{{Citation needed|date=September 2024|reason=There are no reliable sources found to support this and it needs to be perceived for this edit.}}

==Health problems==
On July 1, 2022, E.S.G. was diagnosed with colon cancer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-02 |title=Houston Rap Icon ESG Diagnosed With Cancer |url=https://hiphopdx.com/news/id.71444/title.houston-rap-icon-esg-diagnosed-with-cancer |access-date=2024-09-23 |website=HipHopDX |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Provost |first=Rex |date=2022-07-02 |title=ESG Diagnosed With Cancer, Hospitalized For Emergency Surgery |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/411077-esg-diagnosed-with-cancer-hospitalized-for-emergency-surgery-news |access-date=2024-09-23 |website=HotNewHipHop |language=en}}</ref> In June 2023, he was hit by a car after leaving a club, which ultimately led to him having his leg amputated.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-06-03 |title=UPDATE: Houston’s heroic rap legend ‘ESG’ candidly reveals what led to leg amputation |url=https://bayoubeatnews.com/2023/06/houston-rapper-esg-candidly-reveals-what-led-to-amputation-of-his-leg/ |access-date=2024-09-23 |website=Bayou Beat News |language=en-US}}</ref>

Won't He Do It (album).text:
Won't He Do It is the third studio album by American rapper Conway the Machine. It was released through Drumwork Music Group and Empire Distribution on May 5, 2023.
The album was preceded by four singles, "Super Bowl", "Brucifix", "Quarters" and "The Chosen". It features notable guest appearances by Benny the Butcher, Dave East, Fabolous, Jozzy, Juicy J and Sauce Walka. It is his first studio album since his official departure from Shady Records and Griselda Records. Critics have characterized Won't He Do It as a highlight in Conway's catalog.


== Background ==
On February 21, 2022, Conway the Machine announced his departure from Shady Records and Griselda Records four days before the release of his second studio album, God Don't Make Mistakes, by the two labels. Shortly after that album's release, Conway revealed Won't He Do It as the planned title for his next album. Conway has described the album title as an acknowledgement of "all that God has blessed [him] with" during his career.
Throughout much of 2022, Conway prioritized the expansion of his Drumwork Music Group label over working on music, stating that rap was becoming "boring" to him due to the proliferation of Griselda-influenced musicians. However, after witnessing the development of the artists on his label, Conway found himself inspired once more. Conway traveled to Denver to record the album; he spent several months there, recording prolifically, and developed Won't He Do It by narrowing down that body of material.
In February 2023, Conway released the album's debut single, "Super Bowl", and announced a release date of March 31, 2023. However, the release date was subsequently delayed to May 5, 2023. Throughout April 2023, Conway released three additional singles: "Quarters", "Brucifix", and "The Chosen".
The album cover features a direct view of Conway's face, something he had not shown on any of his previous albums or mixtapes.


== Content ==
Conway has described the mood of Won't He Do It as more triumphant than his previous work, contrasting it in particular to his prior studio album, God Don't Make Mistakes: With Won't He Do It I wanted it to be the total opposite [of God Don't Make Mistakes]. I didn't wanna get too deep into the pain of the songs. I didn't want the sad story. We went from all that to a life of luxury! We're thankful, we're blessed, and it's all a positive mindset now.
Sonically, the album centers features like "opulent horns and soaring orchestral compositions", but has been described as refining his traditional boom bap production rather than changing it dramatically. Lyrically, the project features Conway continuing to provide his characteristic "grimy" rapping while also "embrac[ing] his status as a boss".
At various points in the album, Conway recalls interactions he has had with artists he looks up to; he discusses conversations with Kanye West on "Kanye" and with Jay-Z on "Monogram".

'''Ameer Emmanuel Vann''' (born September 22, 1996) is an American rapper. He is best known for being a member of music collective [[Brockhampton]], until he left Brockhampton in May 2018. After leaving Brockhampton, Vann started his solo career and released his first commercial EP, ''[[Emmanuel (EP)|Emmanuel]]'', in September 2019.

== Early life ==
Ameer Emmanuel Vann was born in [[Houston]], Texas, on September 22, 1996. He attended [[The Woodlands High School]] in Texas with future [[Brockhampton]] bandmates [[Kevin Abstract]], Joba, [[Matt Champion]], and [[Merlyn Wood]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://centralsauce.com/who-is-brockhampton|title=Meet Every Member of Brockhampton|date=2017-12-07|website=CentralSauce Collective|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-18}}</ref> He held various jobs before joining Brockhampton, including working in a slaughterhouse and as a trash collector. Vann has also revealed in several songs that he has had a pill addiction due to sleeping problems, and often sold drugs from his mother's house.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.stanforddaily.com/2017/11/14/a-look-at-brockhampton-a-hip-hop-anti-collective-all-american-boyband/|title=A look at Brockhampton, a hip-hop anti-collective All-American Boyband|last=Grosz|first=Dylan|date=2017-11-14|website=The Stanford Daily|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-18}}</ref>

== Career ==
Vann embarked on his career as a member of AliveSinceForever, a group that started on the forum KanyeToThe in 2010, from which [[Brockhampton]] would eventually form.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2018/03/brockhampton-explained/|title=Everything You Always Wanted to Know About Brockhampton (But Were Afraid to Ask)|website=Complex|language=en|access-date=2019-09-18}}</ref> He was featured on their only project, ''The ASF EP'', released on July 29, 2013, on the tracks "Silent Water" and "Rabbits", both with [[Kevin Abstract]].

Vann also released an eponymous EP, titled ''Ameer Vann EP'', on October 29, 2013. He was one of the founding members of Brockhampton in 2015, and along with Kevin Abstract, contributed to "a fair amount of the group's image and vision".<ref name=":1" /> Vann has been called, "the face of the ''Saturation'' trilogy", being featured on the covers of Brockhampton's 2017 albums, ''[[Saturation (Brockhampton album)|Saturation]]'', ''[[Saturation II]]'', and ''[[Saturation III]]''.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=pitchfork>{{Cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/brockhamptons-ameer-vann-accused-of-sexual-misconduct-responds/|title=Brockhampton's Ameer Vann Accused of Sexual Misconduct, Responds|last=Yoo|first=Noah|date=May 14, 2019|website=Pitchfork|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180515010110/https://pitchfork.com/news/brockhamptons-ameer-vann-accused-of-sexual-misconduct-responds/ |archive-date=2018-05-15 |access-date=September 18, 2019}}</ref>

However, the group decided to part ways with Vann on May 27, 2018, following sexual abuse allegations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/brockhampton-kick-ameer-vann-following-sexual-assault-allegations-2326510|title=Brockhampton kick Ameer Vann out following sexual and mental abuse allegations|last=Bowman|first=Lisa|date=2018-05-27|website=NME|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-18}}</ref> After a hiatus and disappearance from social media, Vann reemerged on September 16, 2019, to announce the release of his debut commercial project [[Emmanuel (EP)|''Emmanuel'']], the following night.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/ex-brockhampton-rapper-ameer-vann-releases-new-music-following-sexual-abuse-allegations-2549242|title=Ex-Brockhampton rapper Ameer Vann releases new music following sexual abuse allegations|last=Jones|first=Damian|date=2019-09-18|website=NME|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-18}}</ref> Vann's first solo live performance was at Sound Of Brazil (S.O.B.'s) in [[New York City]] on September 23, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eventbrite.com/e/ameer-vann-tickets-73478236383|title = Ameer Vann}}</ref> The setlist included tracks from ''Emmanuel'' and older tracks from 2017, as well as unreleased songs.

On October 15, 2020, Vann released the [[Brandon Bell (record producer)|Donut]]-produced single "Keep Your Distance" via Winston Wolf and [[RCA Records]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ameer Vann Wants You To "Keep Your Distance"|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/289355-ameer-vann-wants-you-to-keep-your-distance-new-song|access-date=2020-10-20|website=HotNewHipHop|date=15 October 2020 |language=en}}</ref> On January 14, 2021, Vann released a second single titled "IDFIATOK" (an acronym for "I Don't Fit In and That's OK").<ref>{{cite web |title=Ameer Vann Returns With Creative "IDFIATOK" Single & Video |website=HNHH |date=14 January 2021 |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/310733-ameer-vann-returns-with-creative-idfiatok-single-and-video-new-song |access-date=14 January 2021}}</ref>

On October 27, 2023, Vann released a collaborative album titled ''Slime in the Ice Machine'' with former Brockhampton bandmate [[Merlyn Wood]]. On August 9, 2024, Vann independently released his first studio album titled ''Woof''. In 2025, Vann was a featured artist on four songs on Kevin Abstract's album ''[[Blush (Kevin Abstract album)|Blush]]'', released on June 27.

== Artistry ==
Vann is best known for his laid back flow and his frequent use of themes of [[racism]], [[Cynicism (contemporary)|cynicism]], [[substance abuse]] and [[introspection]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stanforddaily.com/2017/11/14/a-look-at-brockhampton-a-hip-hop-anti-collective-all-american-boyband/|title=A look at Brockhampton, a hip-hop anti-collective All-American Boyband|last=Grosz|first=Dylan|date=2017-11-14|website=The Stanford Daily|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-19}}</ref>

== Controversies ==

=== Sexual misconduct allegations ===

In May 2018, Vann was the subject of sexual misconduct and abuse allegations, after two women detailed their experiences; some of which included him being, "emotionally manipulative, and mentally abusive."<ref name=pitchfork  /><ref name="Two Women Detail Abuse">{{cite magazine |last1=Aniftos |first1=Rania |title=Former Brockhampton Member Ameer Vann: Two Women Detail Abuse Allegations |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/8459953/ameer-vann-brockhampton-two-women-describe-sexual-misconduct-accusations |magazine=Billboard |date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> He later responded to the allegations, denying sexual misconduct or sexual relations with a minor, in a series of [[Twitter|tweets]].<ref name=pitchfork /><ref name="Two Women Detail Abuse"/>

{{Quote box|width=25%|quote="In response to the claims of emotional and sexual abuse: Although my behavior has been selfish, childish, and unkind, I have never criminally harmed anyone or disrespected their boundaries. I have never had relations with a minor or violated anybody's consent."<ref name=pitchfork />}}

As a result, Brockhampton delayed, and ultimately shelved the release of their then-upcoming fourth studio album ''Puppy'', which was scheduled to be released the following month, as well as cancelling their remaining tour dates.<ref name=":2" /> On May 27, a statement was issued by the group announcing Vann's departure.<ref name=kim>{{cite news |last1=Kim |first1=Michelle |title=Brockhampton Kick Out Ameer Vann Over Sexual Misconduct Allegations |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/brockhampton-kick-out-ameer-vann-over-sexual-misconduct-allegations/ |accessdate=June 5, 2018 |work=[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |date=May 27, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet|user=brckhmptn|number=1000705013747015680|title=pic.twitter.com/49lWbDcXzl|date=2018-05-27|access-date=2019-09-17}}</ref>

=== Robbery accusations ===

In December 2018, former bandmate Dom McLennon posted a tweet claiming he thinks that Vann had arranged for one of his friends to be robbed, and did not reveal his involvement until after the controversy that led to his departure.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Findlay |first1=Mitch |title=Dom McLennon Accuses Ameer Vann Of Setting His Friend Up To Be Robbed |url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/154419-dom-mclennon-accuses-ameer-vann-of-setting-his-friend-in-robbery-news |website=HotNewHipHop |date=13 December 2018 |access-date=5 April 2021}}</ref> McLennon later addressed this in Brockhampton's "Dearly Departed" from their 2019 album ''[[Ginger (Brockhampton album)|Ginger]]'', elaborating on the robbery and further criticising Vann's behaviour.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Yassin |first1=Diana |title='Dearly Departed:' A message to Ameer Van |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/arts/dearly-departed-message-ameer-van/ |website=The Michigan Daily |date=4 September 2019 |access-date=5 April 2021}}</ref> Vann denied the allegations in a freestyle he posted on his Instagram page in March 2021.<ref>{{Citation|title=GOSSIPY FLOW|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7SRRDTdhLMY|language=en|access-date=2021-04-10}}</ref>

'''Big Ghost''' is an anonymous online personality, [[hip hop]] writer and blogger,<ref name="gq" /> and [[music producer]].<ref name="complex">{{cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2018/09/ghostface-killah-big-ghost-done-it-again|title=Premiere: Ghostface Killah and Big Ghost "Done It Again" on New Collab|website=Complex|date=27 September 2018|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref> He was once best known for his witty writing style and satirical humor on his earlier hip hop album reviews and blog posts.<ref name="djbooth">{{cite news|url=https://djbooth.net/features/2016-09-13-big-ghost-hip-hops-anger-translator|title=Big Ghost: Hip Hop's Purist Anger Translator|website=DJBooth|date=13 September 2016|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref>

== History ==

''Big Ghost'' began as a parody of [[Wu Tang Clan]]'s [[Ghostface Killah]], which many believed to be Ghostface himself.<ref name="gq">{{cite web|url=https://www.gq.com/story/big-ghost-chronicles-ghostface-killah-drake-take-care-review|first=Rob|last=Harvilla|title=Getting to Know Big Ghostface|website=GQ|date=29 November 2011|accessdate=2 May 2020}}</ref>

He was interviewed by various online magazines including ''[[GQ]]'',<ref name="gq"/> [[Genius (website)|Genius]],<ref>[https://genius.com/posts/809-Rap-genius-of-the-month-big-ghostfase "Rap Genius of the Month: Big Ghostfase"] 17 January 2012</ref> and [[Complex (magazine)|''Complex'']]<ref name="complex2">{{cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/pop-culture/2013/10/best-hip-hop-parody-twitter/big-ghost-fase|title=Big Ghost FASE - The Best Hip-Hop Parody Twitter Accounts|website=Complex|date=4 October 2013|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref> and later began writing for and collaborating with major blogs and websites such as [[Okayplayer]]<ref name="okayplayer">{{cite web|url=https://www.okayplayer.com/author/big-ghost|website=okayplayer.com|title=Big Ghost Okayplayer Author" 2013 – present |accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref> and the Genius website.<ref name="genius">{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/Big-ghost-ltd-nothing-was-the-same-review-annotated|title=Big Ghost LTD. – Nothing Was The Same Review|website=Genius|date=23 September 2013|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref>

== Controversy ==
In early March 2011, rapper [[Wiz Khalifa]] publicly went on the air during an interview on The Star & Bucwild Morning Show, and made remarks about rapper [[Ghostface Killah]], saying that he was "corny", for allegedly commenting on Wiz's latest single "[[Roll Up (Wiz Khalifa song)|Roll Up]]" on his blog, further stating, "Him saying corny stuff makes him a corny individual".

The real Ghostface quickly responded stating it was not him, tweeting ''"tell the kid Wiz, its all love i respect him as a artist and got no issues wit him at all, Once again the website is fake, its not ya boy!"'', then later tweeting again, reaffirming that he had no affiliation with the [[blogger]].<ref>[http://www.laweekly.com/music/ghostface-killah-changes-mind-about-online-impersonator-ghostfase-shout-out-to-my-mini-muse-funny-ass-ninja-2407121 "Ghostface Killah Tweets - LA Weekly"], 3 March 2011</ref>

On 3 March 2011, legal action was taken by Wu Tang Corporate to shut the blog site down due to infringement violations but was later made operational once again.<ref name="abovegroundmagazine">{{cite web|url=http://abovegroundmagazine.com/news/culture-news/03/04/fake-ghostface-killah-blog-temporarily-shut-down-by-wu-tang/|title=Fake Ghostface Killah Blog Temporarily Shut Down By Wu-Tang|website=aboveGround Magazine|date=3 March 2011|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref>

== Music production ==
In late 2015, Big Ghost branched out into [[music production]], releasing a free project with production being credited solely to ''Big Ghost Ltd''.<ref name="therealhip-hop">{{cite web|url=https://therealhip-hop.com/a-conversation-with-big-ghost/|title=A Conversation with Big Ghost|website=The Real Hip-Hop|date=21 September 2015|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref> It has never been made publicly clear whether ''Big Ghost Ltd'' itself is a solo venture or a team of collaborating producers, although a '''''Hector Puente Colon Jr. & The Santiago Men's Basketball Philharmonic Orchestra''''' has been attributed to the instrumentation on all albums. The first release under the Big Ghost Ltd name, was a collaborative project with Buffalo rappers [[Westside Gunn]] and [[Conway the Machine]], entitled ''Griselda Ghost'', released on 11 September 2015.<ref name="insomniacmagazine">{{cite web|url=https://insomniacmagazine.com/big-ghost-ltd-westside-gunn-conway-drop-griselda-ghost/|title=Big Ghost Ltd, Westside Gunn & Conway Drop "Griselda Ghost"|website=Insomniac Magazine|date=21 September 2015|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref> On 5 October 2018, ''Big Ghost Ltd.'' was given full production credit on [[Ghostface Killah]]'s 2018 project called ''[[The Lost Tapes (Ghostface Killah album)|The Lost Tapes]]''.<ref>[https://exclaim.ca/music/article/ghostface_killah-the_lost_tapes "Ghostface Killah - The Lost Tapes" 09 October 2018].</ref><ref name="xxlmag">{{cite web|url=https://www.xxlmag.com/rap-music/new-music/2018/10/ghostface-killah-the-lost-tapes-album-snoop-dogg-raekwon/|website=xxlmag.com|title=THIS WEBSITE USES COOKIES|date=5 October 2018|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref><ref name="rollingstone">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/ghostface-killah-the-lost-tapes-review-732783/|author=Elias Leight|title=Review: Ghostface Killah Sticks to Basics on 'The Lost Tapes'|magazine=Rolling Stone|date=5 October 2018|accessdate=28 October 2018}}</ref>

Big Ghost.text:
Big Ghost is an anonymous online personality, hip hop writer and blogger, and music producer. He was once best known for his witty writing style and satirical humor on his earlier hip hop album reviews and blog posts.


== History ==
Big Ghost began as a parody of Wu Tang Clan's Ghostface Killah, which many believed to be Ghostface himself.
He was interviewed by various online magazines including GQ, Genius, and Complex and later began writing for and collaborating with major blogs and websites such as Okayplayer and the Genius website.


== Controversy ==
In early March 2011, rapper Wiz Khalifa publicly went on the air during an interview on The Star & Bucwild Morning Show, and made remarks about rapper Ghostface Killah, saying that he was "corny", for allegedly commenting on Wiz's latest single "Roll Up" on his blog, further stating, "Him saying corny stuff makes him a corny individual".
The real Ghostface quickly responded stating it was not him, tweeting "tell the kid Wiz, its all love i respect him as a artist and got no issues wit him at all, Once again the website is fake, its not ya boy!", then later tweeting again, reaffirming that he had no affiliation with the blogger.
On 3 March 2011, legal action was taken by Wu Tang Corporate to shut the blog site down due to infringement violations but was later made operational once again.


== Music production ==
In late 2015, Big Ghost branched out into music production, releasing a free project with production being credited solely to Big Ghost Ltd. It has never been made publicly clear whether Big Ghost Ltd itself is a solo venture or a team of collaborating producers, although a Hector Puente Colon Jr. & The Santiago Men's Basketball Philharmonic Orchestra has been attributed to the instrumentation on all albums. The first release under the Big Ghost Ltd name, was a collaborative project with Buffalo rappers Westside Gunn and Conway the Machine, entitled Griselda Ghost, released on 11 September 2015. On 5 October 2018, Big Ghost Ltd. was given full production credit on Ghostface Killah's 2018 project called The Lost Tapes.

Erick Arc Elliott.text:
Erick Elliott (born August 12, 1988), better known as Erick Arc Elliott or Erick the Architect, is an American rapper, singer, artist and record producer from Brooklyn, New York. A member of the hip hop trio Flatbush Zombies, Elliott has released multiple solo projects as well, including I've Never Been Here Before in February 2024.
Elliott plays multiple instruments including the keyboard, piano, and the guitar. He is the primary producer of Flatbush Zombies and has produced for other popular acts such as Joey Badass, James Blake, and more. He also scored the film The Choice Is Yours (2023) on Paramount+ starring Black Sheep and J Dilla. He's also featured on the track "Candle Flame" by Jungle that has over 100 million streams.
As the primary producer of Flatbush Zombies, the "architect" part of his name refers to constructing the groups' iconic sound.
In June 2026, he signed with Mass Appeal Records and announced an upcoming project.

Subsequently, Tsuji reintroduced the [[IWGP Heavyweight Championship]]—which had been retired in 2021 and succeeded by the World Heavyweight—to replace the World Heavyweight, retroactively merging the lineages of both titles as one, with all former IWGP World Heavyweight Champions recognized as former IWGP Heavyweight Champions. The [[IWGP Intercontinental Championship]] history—which had been unified with the Heavyweight in 2021 and also retired to create the World Heavyweight—would also later be amended with all former World Heavyweight Champions also recognized as former Intercontinental Champions, with Tsuji recognized as its final holder. **Also at [[Wrestle Kingdom 20]], [[Hiroshi Tanahashi]] lost to [[Kazuchika Okada]], ending his 25-year professional wrestling career. * January 6 – Backstage during [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]]'s [[New Year Dash!!#2026|New Year Dash]], [[Yota Tsuji]] announced that [[Bullet Club]] would be dissolved going forward, marking the end of the stable after 12 years. * January 8 – ''[[WWE Main Event]]'' premiered on [[YouTube]] in the United States, after streaming on [[Peacock (streaming service)|Peacock]] since 2021. * January 15 – ''[[TNA iMPACT!]]'' premiered on [[AMC (TV channel)|AMC]] and [[AMC+]], after airing on [[AXS TV]] since October 2019, [[TNA+]] since January 2024, and [[New England Sports Network]] since January 2025. * January 31 – At [[WWE]]'s [[Royal Rumble (2026)|Royal Rumble]], [[AJ Styles]] lost to [[Gunther (wrestler)|Gunther]] via [[technical submission]], ending his 27-year professional wrestling career. * March 9 – Outside of the United States and Canada, [[All Elite Wrestling]] (AEW), in partnership with [[Kiswe (company)|Kiswe]], launched [[MyAEW]], an [[over-the-top media services|over-the-top]] [[streaming service]] and [[digital television]] network, hosting all episodes of AEW's programs and all [[pay-per-view]] (PPV) events, live and on-demand, as well as hosting the archive for all prior programs and PPVs. It also hosts the archive for [[Ring of Honor]]. * March 15 – In the United States, [[NXT (WWE brand)|NXT]]'s livestreaming events were removed from [[Peacock (streaming service)|Peacock]] following the expiration of that portion of [[WWE]]'s contract with [[NBCUniversal]]. NXT's next livestreaming event, [[NXT Stand & Deliver (2026)|Stand & Deliver]], aired on [[YouTube]] on April 4, with NXT's livestreaming events subsequently going to [[The CW]] and [[ESPN Unlimited]] starting with [[NXT The Great American Bash (2026)|The Great American Bash]] on June 28. * March 31 – The [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] Board of Directors transferred all shares of [[World Wonder Ring Stardom]], which had operated under the [[trade name]] Stardom Co., Ltd. since their acquisition in April 2024, back to their parent company [[Bushiroad]]. * April 1 – The standalone [[WWE Network]] permanently shut down in its last remaining countries—Austria, Germany, Italy, and Switzerland—which transitioned to [[Netflix]], bringing a complete end to the service after 12 years. * April 28 – [[WWE]] announced that beginning with [[NXT The Great American Bash (2026)|NXT The Great American Bash]] on June 28, [[NXT (WWE brand)|NXT]]'s livestreaming events would begin airing on [[The CW]]'s linear channel in the United States under a multi-year agreement that includes 20 livestreaming events. The CW channel had already been airing the weekly ''[[WWE NXT|NXT]]'' program since October 2024. * April 29 – In the United States, [[ESPN]] revealed a deal with [[The CW]] that would include [[NXT (WWE brand)|NXT]]'s livestreaming events and the weekly ''[[WWE NXT|NXT]]'' program, with these events [[simulcast]] on The CW's linear channel and [[ESPN Unlimited]], later confirmed to begin on August 4. * May 1 – ''[[NWA Powerrr]]'' premiered on [[Comet (TV network)|Comet]], after airing on [[The Roku Channel]] since July 2025. This put the [[National Wrestling Alliance]] (NWA) back on over-the-air television for the first time in over 30 years. * May 26 – ** [[Nicola Glencross]] and [[Damian Mackle]] (best known as Nikki Cross and Killian Dain in [[WWE]], respectively) purchased both [[Progress Wrestling]] and [[DEFY Wrestling]]. ** [[Major League Wrestling]] (MLW) announced a partnership with [[Veeps]] to stream MLW's relaunched weekly series, ''[[MLW Fusion|Fusion]]'', starting May 30, as well as quarterly [[pay-per-view]] events, on the platform, with ''Fusion'' also available on [[YouTube]]. * May 27 – [[Bushiroad]] transferred all shares of [[New Japan Pro-Wrestling]] to a [[consortium]] between [[TV Asahi]] and [[CyberAgent]], after the promotion had been a consolidated subsidiary of the company since 2012. * May 30 – At [[Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide]]'s [[Noche de Los Grandes]], [[Ludwig Kaiser|El Grande Americano]] defeated [["The Original" El Grande Americano]] in a [[No Disqualification match|No Disqualification]] [[Mask vs. Mask match]], with "The Original" El Grande Americano being revealed to be [[Chad Gable]]. * June 24 – The [[National Wrestling Alliance]] (NWA) announced a partnership with [[Tubi]] to stream ''[[NWA Powerrr]]''. * June 28 – In the United States, [[WWE]]'s livestreaming events for [[NXT (WWE brand)|NXT]] began airing [[The CW]]'s linear channel, starting with that night's [[NXT The Great American Bash (2026)|The Great American Bash]]. These events were previously streamed on [[Peacock (streaming service)|Peacock]] until March, with one event streamed on [[YouTube]] in April. Outside the US, these events remain on [[Abema]] in Japan, [[SuperSport (South African broadcaster)|SuperSport]] in Sub-Saharan Africa, and [[Netflix]] everywhere else. * July 3 – ''[[WWE SmackDown]]'' returned to two hours after airing for three hours since January 2. * July 15 – [[Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling]]'s weekly series, ''[[MLP Mayhem (TV program)|Mayhem]]'', premiered on [[TSN2]]. * August 4 – [[WWE]]'s livestreaming events for [[NXT (WWE brand)|NXT]] as well as the weekly ''[[WWE NXT|NXT]]'' program began [[simulcasting]] on [[The CW]]'s linear channel and [[ESPN Unlimited]]. * August 30 – The [[WWE Women's Speed Championship]] was retired after it was [[Championship unification|unified]] with the [[NXT Women's North American Championship]] at [[NXT Heatwave (2026)|Heatwave]]. Women's North American Champion [[Zaria (wrestler)|Zaria]] defeated Women's Speed Champion [[Wren Sinclair]] and [[Kali Armstrong]] in a [[Winner Takes All match|Winner Takes All]] [[triple threat match]] to unify the titles, with Sinclair recognized as the final champion. * September 1 – The men's [[WWE Speed Championship]] was retired on ''[[WWE NXT|NXT]]'' after [[NXT (WWE brand)|NXT]] General Manager [[Robert Stone (wrestler)|Robert Stone]] had [[Lexis King]] relinquish the title. ==Accomplishments and tournaments== ===AAA=== {| class="wikitable" style="width:100%;" |- ! == Notable events ==
January 1 –
In the United States, the majority of WWE's archival content on Peacock was moved to Netflix, with Peacock maintaining NXT's livestreaming events until March 15 and the Saturday Night's Main Event specials and replays of recent episodes of WWE SmackDown until at least 2029, as well as exclusive documentaries.
Many of the select few countries that were still on the WWE Network in 2025 transitioned to Netflix, with only Austria, Germany, Italy, and Switzerland still on the WWE Network until April 1, while Sub-Saharan Africa and Japan remained on SuperSport and Abema, respectively.
January 2 – WWE SmackDown returned to three hours after airing for two hours since July 4, 2025.
January 4 –
At New Japan Pro-Wrestling's Wrestle Kingdom 20, IWGP Global Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji defeated IWGP World Heavyweight Champion Konosuke Takeshita in a Winner Takes All match. Subsequently, Tsuji reintroduced the IWGP Heavyweight Championship—which had been retired in 2021 and succeeded by the World Heavyweight—to replace the World Heavyweight, retroactively merging the lineages of both titles as one, with all former IWGP World Heavyweight Champions recognized as former IWGP Heavyweight Champions. The IWGP Intercontinental Championship history—which had been unified with the Heavyweight in 2021 and also retired to create the World Heavyweight—would also later be amended with all former World Heavyweight Champions also recognized as former Intercontinental Champions, with Tsuji recognized as its final holder.
Also at Wrestle Kingdom 20, Hiroshi Tanahashi lost to Kazuchika Okada, ending his 25-year professional wrestling career.
January 6 – Backstage during New Japan Pro-Wrestling's New Year Dash, Yota Tsuji announced that Bullet Club would be dissolved going forward, marking the end of the stable after 12 years.
January 8 – WWE Main Event premiered on YouTube in the United States, after streaming on Peacock since 2021.
January 15 – TNA iMPACT! premiered on AMC and AMC+, after airing on AXS TV since October 2019, TNA+ since January 2024, and New England Sports Network since January 2025.
January 31 – At WWE's Royal Rumble, AJ Styles lost to Gunther via technical submission, ending his 27-year professional wrestling career.
March 9 – Outside of the United States and Canada, All Elite Wrestling (AEW), in partnership with Kiswe, launched MyAEW, an over-the-top streaming service and digital television network, hosting all episodes of AEW's programs and all pay-per-view (PPV) events, live and on-demand, as well as hosting the archive for all prior programs and PPVs. It also hosts the archive for Ring of Honor.
March 15 – In the United States, NXT's livestreaming events were removed from Peacock following the expiration of that portion of WWE's contract with NBCUniversal. NXT's next livestreaming event, Stand & Deliver, aired on YouTube on April 4, with NXT's livestreaming events subsequently going to The CW and ESPN Unlimited starting with The Great American Bash on June 28.
March 31 – The New Japan Pro-Wrestling Board of Directors transferred all shares of World Wonder Ring Stardom, which had operated under the trade name Stardom Co., Ltd. since their acquisition in April 2024, back to their parent company Bushiroad.
April 1 – The standalone WWE Network permanently shut down in its last remaining countries—Austria, Germany, Italy, and Switzerland—which transitioned to Netflix, bringing a complete end to the service after 12 years.
April 28 – WWE announced that beginning with NXT The Great American Bash on June 28, NXT's livestreaming events would begin airing on The CW's linear channel in the United States under a multi-year agreement that includes 20 livestreaming events. The CW channel had already been airing the weekly NXT program since October 2024.
April 29 – In the United States, ESPN revealed a deal with The CW that would include NXT's livestreaming events and the weekly NXT program, with these events simulcast on The CW's linear channel and ESPN Unlimited, later confirmed to begin on August 4.
May 1 – NWA Powerrr premiered on Comet, after airing on The Roku Channel since July 2025. This put the National Wrestling Alliance (NWA) back on over-the-air television for the first time in over 30 years.
May 26 –
Nicola Glencross and Damian Mackle (best known as Nikki Cross and Killian Dain in WWE, respectively) purchased both Progress Wrestling and DEFY Wrestling.
Major League Wrestling (MLW) announced a partnership with Veeps to stream MLW's relaunched weekly series, Fusion, starting May 30, as well as quarterly pay-per-view events, on the platform, with Fusion also available on YouTube.
May 27 – Bushiroad transferred all shares of New Japan Pro-Wrestling to a consortium between TV Asahi and CyberAgent, after the promotion had been a consolidated subsidiary of the company since 2012.
May 30 – At Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide's Noche de Los Grandes, El Grande Americano defeated "The Original" El Grande Americano in a No Disqualification Mask vs. Mask match, with "The Original" El Grande Americano being revealed to be Chad Gable.
June 24 – The National Wrestling Alliance (NWA) announced a partnership with Tubi to stream NWA Powerrr.
June 28 – In the United States, WWE's livestreaming events for NXT began airing The CW's linear channel, starting with that night's The Great American Bash. These events were previously streamed on Peacock until March, with one event streamed on YouTube in April. Outside the US, these events remain on Abema in Japan, SuperSport in Sub-Saharan Africa, and Netflix everywhere else.
July 3 – WWE SmackDown returned to two hours after airing for three hours since January 2.
July 15 – Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling's weekly series, Mayhem, premiered on TSN2.
August 4 – WWE's livestreaming events for NXT as well as the weekly NXT program began simulcasting on The CW's linear channel and ESPN Unlimited.
August 30 – The WWE Women's Speed Championship was retired after it was unified with the NXT Women's North American Championship at Heatwave. Women's North American Champion Zaria defeated Women's Speed Champion Wren Sinclair and Kali Armstrong in a Winner Takes All triple threat match to unify the titles, with Sinclair recognized as the final champion.
September 1 – The men's WWE Speed Championship was retired on NXT after NXT General Manager Robert Stone had Lexis King relinquish the title.

==== Raw and SmackDown ====
Raw and SmackDown each exclusively have a world and secondary championship for both the men and women, as well as a tag team championship for men.


==== NXT ====
NXT exclusively has a primary, secondary, and specialty championship for both the men and women, as well as a tag team championship for men.


==== Unbranded ====
The following title is non-exclusive, available to wrestlers from Raw, SmackDown, and NXT.


==== WWE Evolve ====
Evolve is a developmental brand focused on trainees from the WWE Performance Center, and has two championships, one each for the men and women.


==== WWE ID ====
The WWE Independent Development (ID) program has two championships, one each for men and women, which are defended exclusively across partner independent promotions. Additionally, if a non-WWE ID wrestler wins either title, they also earn a WWE ID contract.

As an [[archipelago]], the [[Philippines]] comprises over 7,600 islands<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.namria.gov.ph/list.php?id=1032&alias=administrator-tiangco-welcomes-2017&Archive=1 |title=Administrator Tiangco welcomes 2017|publisher=National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA)|access-date=November 15, 2017}}</ref><ref name=namria>{{cite news|last1=Mayuga|first1=Jonathan|title=Namria 'discovers' 400 previously 'unknown' PHL islands using IfSAR|url=http://www.businessmirror.com.ph/namria-discovers-400-previously-unknown-phl-islands-using-ifsar/|access-date=February 12, 2016|publisher=BusinessMirror|date=February 10, 2016}}</ref> clustered into [[Island groups of the Philippines|three major island groups]]: [[Luzon]], the [[Visayas]], and [[Mindanao]]. Only about 2,000 islands are inhabited,<ref name="phislands">[http://www.philippinetourism.com.au/pressoct10.html Magical Islands] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130707073614/http://www.philippinetourism.com.au/pressoct10.html |date=July 7, 2013 }}, Philippine Tourism, retrieved 2012</ref> and more than 5,000 are yet to be officially named.<ref name=namria/>

==Largest islands of the Philippines==
Below is a list of the largest Philippine islands. There are discrepancies in the area estimates across various sources, which would change the rankings of some smaller islands. The areas given may not be definitive.

The 50 largest islands have a combined area of around {{Convert|321000|km2|sp=us}} and a combined population of about 100.9 million (2015); thus they contain about 99% of the Philippines' total land area and total population (2015). Combined population of Luzon and Mindanao accounts for 80% of total population of the Philippines.

== Largest islands of the Philippines ==
Below is a list of the largest Philippine islands. There are discrepancies in the area estimates across various sources, which would change the rankings of some smaller islands. The areas given may not be definitive.
The 50 largest islands have a combined area of around 321,000 square kilometers (124,000 sq mi) and a combined population of about 100.9 million (2015); thus they contain about 99% of the Philippines' total land area and total population (2015). Combined population of Luzon and Mindanao accounts for 80% of total population of the Philippines.

'''Salvador Navarrete''' (born 16 February 1992), better known by his stage name '''Sega Bodega''', is an Irish-Chilean music producer, singer, songwriter, DJ, and co-head/founder of the record label and collective Nuxxe. Sega Bodega is known for his futuristic,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2020-05-12|title=Sega Bodega|url=https://notion.online/sega-bodega/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Notion|language=en-GB}}</ref> bass-heavy and leftfield take on [[Electronic music|electronic]] and [[Club Music|club music]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=2016-12-12|title=The Glaswegian producer designing club tracks + tracksuits|url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/33995/1/the-glaswegian-producer-designing-club-tracks-tracksuits|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Dazed|language=en}}</ref> fusing various elements of [[UK bass]] and [[Hip hop music|hip-hop music]], [[deconstructed club]], and [[trip hop]] music into his songs. He rose to prominence producing tracks for London-based rapper, co-founder of the Nuxxe label, and close collaborator [[Shygirl]], gaining attention from the likes of [[Rihanna]], using various Nuxxe tracks for her [[Fenty Beauty]] commercials<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Pro Filt'r Foundation Extension Shades {{!}} Fenty Beauty - YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=040SbPYgkYY&fbclid=IwAR0TAZ-gWHlm7LOJ4RBj4Jsmp68iEmRHpR2xw-_8NwfHQV-W37e4IVVQjHw&ab_channel=FentyBeautyByRihanna|access-date=2020-11-19|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=All New Bold Stunna Lip Paints {{!}} Fenty Beauty - YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zsww8YPxKus&ab_channel=FentyBeautyByRihanna|access-date=2020-12-08|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref> and fashion shows.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2018-05-24|title=Club collective Nuxxe is bringing new sound to dance floors|url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/40130/1/nuxxe-shygirl-new-ep|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Dazed|language=en}}</ref> Sega Bodega released various EPs before releasing his debut album, ''[[Salvador (Sega Bodega album)|Salvador]]'', in 2020, and his second album, ''[[Romeo (album)|Romeo]]'', in 2021.

== Early life ==
Salvador Navarrete was born on 16 February 1992, in Galway, Ireland to a Chilean father and an Irish mother. He lived in Ireland until he was 10 when he relocated to Glasgow.<ref name=":0" />

He had ambitions of being a producer since 2008, playing in various bands until he could understand how to use [[Digital audio workstation|DAWs]].<ref name=":0" /> 

Initially, from about 2010, Navarrete operated under the moniker Peace but retired it when the [[Peace (band)|indie rock band of the same name]] began rising to fame.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ferocious Perfectionist: Sega Bodega Interviewed|url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/ferocious-perfectionist-sega-bodega-interviewed|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Clash Magazine|date=11 December 2013 |language=en}}</ref> He would later settle on his Sega Bodega moniker in 2012.

== Career ==

=== 2012–2015: Early beginnings ===
Navarrete first began gaining traction through various remixes, from which he gained widespread attention, and DJ gigs, supporting [[Lil B]] in Glasgow and playing the [[Field Day (festival)|London Field Day]] festival in 2012.

In February 2013, Navarrete released his debut EP ''Song Dynasty'', a collection of tracks recorded as far back as 2010, but refined and polished after developing a better understanding of the technicalities to music production.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ferocious Perfectionist: Sega Bodega Interviewed|url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/ferocious-perfectionist-sega-bodega-interviewed|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Clash Magazine|date=11 December 2013 |language=en}}</ref> The EP was released via the London-based label, Week of Wonders. This was followed by his ''34'' EP, released in May 2013, also via the Week of Wonders label.

In May 2014, Navarrete was a part of the lineup for [[BBC Radio 1's Big Weekend|BBC Radio 1’s Big Weekend]] festival, where he played his re-released single "Stay Nervous", and "Maryland", which would later appear on his 2018 EP ''self*care'', among other tracks.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2014|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/events/ep3g9r/artists/by/a-z|access-date=2020-11-19|website=BBC Music Events|language=en}}</ref> He also relocated to London in 2014.

After taking a hiatus from releases, Navarrete returned with the October 2015 release of the first ''SS'' project, containing reimagined and 'alternative' takes on cult film scores, such as [[A Clockwork Orange (film)|A Clockwork Orange]], [[Eraserhead]], [[Akira (1988 film)|Akira]] and [[Boyz n the Hood]], among others.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-10-30|title=Hear the reimagined soundtracks for Kids, Gummo and Akira|url=https://www.dazeddigital.com/music/article/27203/1/hear-the-reimagined-soundtracks-for-kids-gummo-and-akira|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Dazed|language=en}}</ref> The project was self-released. This was followed shortly after by the ''Sportswear'' EP, released via the Activia Benz label.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-10-22|title=Stream Sega Bodega's Sportswear EP|url=https://www.factmag.com/2015/10/22/sega-bodega-activia-benz-sportswear-tracksuit/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Fact Magazine|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2016–2018: Nuxxe, ''Ess B'', early collaborations and ''self*care'' ===
In June 2016, London rapper [[Shygirl]] released her debut single, "Want More", produced by Navarrete. The single marked the first release of collective and label Nuxxe, co-founded by Navarrete, Shygirl, and French producer and performer [[Coucou Chloe]], formed from a desire to create music and art with an easy-going, free-flowing, and fun attitude, separate from other pre-establishing labels, and to introduce a sound that no one had heard before to the world.<ref name=":2" /> The single would also appear in a [[Fenty Beauty]] commercial later in 2019.<ref name=":1" /> The release of "Want More" was followed by a collaborative single in October 2016 from Navarrete and Coucou Chloe titled "SPIT INTENT", under the moniker Y1640.

February 2017 marked a further collaboration with the single "CC", featuring Shygirl. The track was the lead single from Navarrete's next EP, titled ''Ess B'', released later that month via the Crazylegs label,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-02-15|title=⚡ Sega Bodega shares collaboration with Shygirl "CC," announces new EP|url=https://highclouds.org/sega-bodega-shares-collaboration-with-shygirl-cc-announces-new-ep/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=HighClouds|language=en-US}}</ref> followed by one other Crazylegs release: the "Nivea" double single in July.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-07-18|title=Sega Bodega pays it forward from his hard-bodied 'Nivea' video by sharing five of his favourite tracks of now|url=https://www.aqnb.com/2017/07/18/sega-bodega-pays-it-forward-from-his-hard-bodied-nivea-video-by-sharing-five-of-his-favourite-tracks-of-now/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=atractivoquenobello|language=en-US}}</ref> More Nuxxe releases continued shortly after ''Ess B''<nowiki/>'s release, such as another Y1640 single in March, titled "WEEP", Shygirl's double single "MSRYNVR" in May,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Essential: Shygirl's dynamite new single, 'MSRYNVR'|url=https://mixmag.net/read/essential-shygirls-dynamite-dual-single-msrynvr-essential-listening|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Mixmag|archive-date=1 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210401183708/https://mixmag.net/read/essential-shygirls-dynamite-dual-single-msrynvr-essential-listening|url-status=dead}}</ref> and Coucou Chloe's EP ''Erika Jane'' in September, on which Navarrete is featured.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Review: Coucou Chloe - Erika Jane|url=https://www.residentadvisor.net/reviews/21477|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Resident Advisor}}</ref> In October, Navarrete released a second installation of the cinema-inspired project, ''SS'', featuring more reimagined takes on film scores such as [[Requiem for a Dream]] (this track also features Shygirl on vocals), [[Alien (film)|Alien]] and [[Ghost in the Shell]], among others.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sega Bodega Launches 'SS (2017)' Mixtape|url=https://www.clashmusic.com/news/sega-bodega-launches-ss-2017-mixtape|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Clash Magazine|date=24 October 2017 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Dunn|first=Frankie|date=2017-11-09|title=sega bodega just rescored all your favourite cult movies|url=https://i-d.co/article/sega-bodega-just-rescored-all-your-favourite-cult-movies/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=i-D|language=en}}</ref>

March 2018 marked the first release from French singer and producer [[Oklou]] on the Nuxxe label: her EP ''The Rite of May'', on which Navarrete contributed co-production on the final track, "Friendless".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Oklou Unveils Wondrous EP, The Rite of May|url=https://indie30.com/2018/03/17/oklou-unveils-wondrous-ep-the-rite-of-may/|access-date=2020-11-19|language=en-AU|archive-date=2 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202155352/https://indie30.com/2018/03/17/oklou-unveils-wondrous-ep-the-rite-of-may/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Navarrete also released a piano version of the song later in the year. The two would continue to collaborate further down the line.

In May 2018, Shygirl released her debut EP via Nuxxe, ''Cruel Practice'', featuring production from Navarrete on every track. The EP gained positive attention from multiple high-profile publications, such as [[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shygirl : Cruel Practice|url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/shygirl-cruel-practice/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Pitchfork|language=en}}</ref> [[Crack Magazine]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shygirl's cybernetic tracks and downplayed style is constructed for the club|url=https://crackmagazine.net/article/aesthetic/aesthetic-shygirl/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Crack Magazine|archive-date=2 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202105318/https://crackmagazine.net/article/aesthetic/aesthetic-shygirl/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and [[Tiny Mix Tapes|Tiny Mixtapes]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Music Review: Shygirl - Cruel Practice|url=https://www.tinymixtapes.com/music-review/shygirl-cruel-practice|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Tiny Mix Tapes|language=en}}</ref>

In October 2018, Navarrete unveiled his next EP, ''self*care'', his first full-length project released via Nuxxe. For the EP, Navarrete invited 6 filmmakers – [[Bryan M. Ferguson]], [[Brooke Candy]], Jade Jackman, Tash Tung, Jasper Jarvis, and BEA1991 – to create their own interpretations of 'self care'.<ref>{{Cite web|title=BBC Radio 6 Music - Tom Ravenscroft, Jaakko Eino Kalevi guest mix and Sega Bodega interview, Sega Bodega on his new multidisciplinary EP project self*care|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p06pjw2f|access-date=2021-05-25|website=BBC|language=en-GB}}</ref> The EP also marked a new direction for Navarrete, as he began using his own vocals more prominently than on any other previous release. The EP is also notable for having artwork designed by [[PC Music]] musician and visual artist [[Hannah Diamond]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-10-03|title=Sega Bodega unveils multidisciplinary project self*care|url=https://www.factmag.com/2018/10/03/sega-bodega-self-care/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Fact Magazine|language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2019–2021: ''Salvador'' and ''Romeo'' ===
In January 2019, Navarrete surprise-released the "Mimi" single,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sega Bodega Shares Gorgeous New Single 'Mimi'|url=https://www.clashmusic.com/news/sega-bodega-shares-gorgeous-new-single-mimi|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Clash Magazine|date=23 January 2019 |language=en}}</ref> as well as playing a headlining live show in London's Hoxton Hall in February.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sega Bodega's Disruptive Pop Vision Feels Utterly Alive|url=https://www.clashmusic.com/features/sega-bodegas-disruptive-pop-vision-feels-utterly-alive|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Clash Magazine|date=12 February 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

2019 bore many collaborations with other indie artists, such as Cosima,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dunn|first=Frankie|date=2019-02-15|title=cosima's 'r u lonely 2?' and everything else you need to listen to today|url=https://i-d.co/article/cosima-r-u-lonely-2-best-new-music-playlist/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=i-D|language=en}}</ref> Col3trane,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Col3trane Delivers New Solo Track "Problems In Us"|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/165554-col3trane-delivers-new-solo-track-problems-in-us-new-song|access-date=2020-11-19|website=HotNewHipHop|date=May 2019 |language=en}}</ref> Nadia Tehran and MISOGI, among others, as well as further collaborations with Oklou<ref>{{Cite web|date=October 29, 2019|last=Chris|title=Oklou – Forever|url=https://www.gorillavsbear.net/oklou-forever/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Gorilla vs. Bear|language=en}}</ref> and Shygirl.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kim|first=Michelle|title=The Ones: Shygirl's "Uckers"|url=https://pitchfork.com/thepitch/shygirl-uckers-new-song-listen/|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Pitchfork|date=19 June 2019 |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Review: Shygirl - BB|url=https://www.residentadvisor.net/reviews/24446|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Resident Advisor}}</ref> Nuxxe also released Coucou Chloe's ''Naughty Dog'' EP in May.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-05-23|title=Coucou Chloe shares 'Silver B' from new EP, Naughty Dog|url=https://www.factmag.com/2019/05/23/coucou-chloe-naughty-dog/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Fact Magazine|language=en-US}}</ref>

2019 also marked Nuxxe's highest profile artist signing and album release: American rapper and singer [[Brooke Candy]] and her October-released debut album, ''[[Sexorcism (Brooke Candy album)|SEXORCISM]]''. The album features a slew of features from the likes of [[Charli XCX]], [[Iggy Azalea]], and [[Rico Nasty]], among many others. Candy had faced many delays and blocks towards releasing her debut album, with plans to release it dating as far back as 2014. When Candy and Navarrete spoke on a panel together for LoomFest May 2019 in Barcelona,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Loom Festival 2019|url=https://www.residentadvisor.net/events/1228723|access-date=2020-11-19|website=Resident Advisor}}</ref> Candy was made aware of the Nuxxe label that Sega Bodega co-runs and conversations on releasing the album on Nuxxe were struck.<ref>{{Cite tweet |title=Yeah so me and Brooke did a panel… |number=1187660592011722752 |user=segabodega |archive-date=2019-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191025092917/https://twitter.com/segabodega/status/1187660592011722752 |url-status=live |access-date=18 June 2023 |lang=en |url=https://twitter.com/segabodega/status/1187660592011722752}}</ref> Navarrete himself co-produced one track on the album: the single "[[Drip (Brooke Candy song)|Drip]]" featuring American singer, actress, and television personality [[Erika Jayne]].

In November 2019, Navarrete released the single "U Suck",<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-11-04|title=Sega Bodega is horny and petty on new single, 'U Suck'|url=https://www.factmag.com/2019/11/04/sega-bodega-u-suck/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Fact Magazine|language=en-US}}</ref> which would be the lead single for his debut album ''[[Salvador (Sega Bodega album)|Salvador]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-11-30|title=Here's Where Sega Bodega's Head Is At|url=https://www.papermag.com/sega-bodega-interview-2019-2641485076.html?rebelltitem=19#rebelltitem19?rebelltitem=19|access-date=2020-11-20|website=PAPER|language=en}}</ref> The single delved into a more synth-pop direction, and again featured Navarrete's vocals prominently. He then played a headlining show in [[St Pancras Old Church|St Pancras Old Church, London]] with a backing string quartet in December, to promote the single and premiere upcoming music from his album.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Evans|first=Georgia|date=2019-12-20|title=Sega Bodega // Live Review {{!}} LONDON IN STEREO|url=https://www.londoninstereo.com/sega-bodega-live-review/|access-date=2020-11-20|language=en-US|archive-date=2 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202155404/https://www.londoninstereo.com/sega-bodega-live-review/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The track was also accompanied with a music video by frequent collaborator [[Bryan M. Ferguson]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-11-05|title=The Greatest 'F**k You' Anthem of 2019 Is Here|url=https://www.papermag.com/sega-bodega-u-suck-2641174537.html|access-date=2021-05-25|website=PAPER|language=en}}</ref>

In early January 2020, Navarrete announced his debut album ''Salvador'' for a 14 February release. The same day as the announcement, he released the single "Salv Goes to Hollywood".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sega Bodega Announces Debut Album 'Salvador'|url=https://www.clashmusic.com/news/sega-bodega-announces-debut-album-salvador|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Clash Magazine|date=15 January 2020 |language=en}}</ref> The track combines the more vocal-heavy ideas of his recent work, with his roots in deconstructed club music and intense bass.

''Salvador'' was released in February to acclaim from publications like [[Paste (magazine)|Paste Magazine]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-02-21|title=Sega Bodega's Salvador Is a Disturbingly Raw Deconstruction of Club Music|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/music/sega-bodega/sega-bodega-salvador-review/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=pastemagazine.com|language=en}}</ref> [[Resident Advisor]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Review: Sega Bodega - Salvador|url=https://www.residentadvisor.net/reviews/24831|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Resident Advisor}}</ref> and Pitchfork,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sega Bodega: Salvador|url=https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/sega-bodega-salvador/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Pitchfork|language=en}}</ref> among others, and fans alike.

Navarrete released a Bandcamp exclusive covers EP, titled ''Reestablishing Connection'', in May 2020. All profits were donated to the AIM COVID-19 Crisis Fund. It featured [[Lafawndah]], covering [[Massive Attack]]'s "[[Teardrop (song)|Teardrop]]", [[Låpsley]], covering [[Gwen Stefani]]'s "[[Cool (Gwen Stefani song)|Cool]]", [[Dorian Electra]], covering [[Wheatus]]' "[[Teenage Dirtbag]]", [[Teddy Geiger|Teddy<3]], covering [[Britney Spears]]' "[[Sometimes (Britney Spears song)|Sometimes]]", and Oklou, covering [[Mauro Picotto]]'s "Komodo".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Reestablishing Connection, by Sega Bodega|url=https://segabodega.bandcamp.com/album/reestablishing-connection|access-date=2021-03-12|website=Sega Bodega}}</ref>

Navarrete also continued to collaborate with Oklou on her debut mixtape ''[[Galore (Oklou mixtape)|Galore]]'', released in September, contributing production to two tracks,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wang|first=Steffanee|title=Oklou Welcomes You To 'Galore,' A Fantastical Pop Escape|url=https://www.nylon.com/entertainment/oklou-galore-album-interview|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Nylon|language=en}}</ref> and Shygirl's ''ALIAS'' EP, released in November, acting as co-executive producer alongside Shygirl on the project.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-21|title=Shygirl announces new EP, 'ALIAS', with SOPHIE, Sega Bodega, more|url=https://djmag.com/news/shygirl-announces-new-ep-alias-sophie-sega-bodega-more|access-date=2020-11-20|website=DJMag.com}}</ref> Among these established collaborators, Navarrete also contributed heavily to American rapper [[Zebra Katz]]'s debut record ''LESS IS MOOR'' in March,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-01-23|title=Zebra Katz meshes industrial hip-hop and drum 'n' bass on debut album, LESS IS MOOR|url=https://thevinylfactory.com/news/zebra-katz-debut-album-less-is-moor-vinyl/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=The Vinyl Factory|language=en-US}}</ref> and appeared on Dorian Electra's ''[[My Agenda]]'' project in October, as a featured artist (which was his first time appearing as such) and as a co-producer on two tracks.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dorian Electra talks through their My Agenda collaborators|url=https://theface.com/music/dorian-electra-new-project-my-agenda-special-guests-rebecca-black-village-people-sega-bodega|access-date=2020-11-20|website=The Face|language=en-gb}}</ref>

In early November, Navarrete released a collaborative single with English musician [[Låpsley]], titled "Make U Stay".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-11-06|title=Listen to Sega Bodega and Låpsley's new collaboration 'Make U Stay'|url=https://www.nme.com/en_asia/news/music/listen-to-sega-bodega-and-lapsleys-joyous-new-collaboration-make-u-stay-2811923|access-date=2020-11-20|website=NME Music News, Reviews, Videos, Galleries, Tickets and Blogs {{!}} NME.COM|language=en}}</ref> The track was released with a music video directed by regular collaborator [[Bryan M. Ferguson]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sega Bodega and Låpsley play for keeps on their new single "Make U Stay"|url=https://www.thefader.com/2020/11/05/sega-bodega-lapsley-make-u-stay-video|access-date=2021-05-25|website=The Fader|language=en}}</ref>

In an Instagram Q&A in early May 2021, Navarrete revealed a slew of artists he has been collaborating with, including [[Caroline Polachek]], [[Arca (musician)|Arca]], [[FKA Twigs|FKA twigs]], [[Charlotte Gainsbourg]], [[slowthai]], and [[Christine and the Queens]], among many others.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sega Bodega collaborations - May 2021|url=https://imgur.com/Xq0GjJI|access-date=2021-06-06|website=Imgur|language=en}}</ref> The same month, he announced a vinyl reissue of his ''Salvador'' album, including the bonus track "Heaven Fell (Reprise)", which features additional vocals from Polachek. He also hosted a special concert performance film, available via ticket purchase, to close off the era of the ''Salvador'' album.

Navarrete released a single titled "Only Seeing God When I Come" on 8 September, indicative of a new musical era,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sega Bodega returns with 'Only Seeing God When I Come'|url=http://diymag.com/2021/09/09/sega-bodega-only-seeing-god-when-i-come|access-date=2021-09-19|website=DIY|language=en}}</ref> followed soon after by "Angel On My Shoulder", and the announcement of his second studio album, ''[[Romeo (album)|Romeo]]'', which released 12 November 2021, and features Arca and Charlotte Gainsbourg.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-09-29|title=Sega Bodega announces new album 'Romeo', shares single 'Angel On My Shoulder'|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/sega-bodega-announces-new-album-romeo-shares-single-angel-on-my-shoulder-3058431|access-date=2021-09-30|website=NME|language=en-GB}}</ref> "I Need Nothing From You" was released as the final single from the album. Navarrete toured the album throughout 2022, including as a supporting act on tour with [[Flume (musician)|Flume]] in California and Arizona.

co-produced Björk and [[Rosalía|ROSALÍA]]'s collaborative single "[[Oral (song)|Oral]]", which released in November 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Christopher |date=2023-11-22 |title=Björk teams up with Rosalía for charity single |url=https://www.wecb.fm/bjork-teams-up-with-rosalia-for-charity-single/ |access-date=2023-12-05 |website=WECB |language=en-US}}</ref>

Navarrete began teasing his next album ''[[Dennis (album)|Dennis]]'' with the single "Deer Teeth" in January 2024,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-29 |title=Sega Bodega Releases New Single "Deer Teeth": Listen |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2249566/sega-bodega-deer-teeth/music/ |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=Stereogum |language=en}}</ref> followed by "Set Me Free, I'm an Animal" in February.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-27 |title=Sega Bodega unveils atmospheric video for new single ‘Set Me Free, I’m An Animal’ |url=https://diymag.com/news/sega-bodega-set-me-free-im-an-animal |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=DIY |language=en}}</ref> He announced the album for release on 26 April 2024 alongside the release of the next single "Elk Skin" in March.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-26 |title=Sega Bodega Releases Single ’Elk Skin’ Off Of Upcoming Album ’Dennis’ |url=https://uproxx.com/indie/sega-bodega-elk-skin-dennis/ |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=UPROXX |language=en-US}}</ref> A final single titled "True" was released the week before the album's release in April.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Interviews |first=Clash Magazine Music News, Reviews & |last2=Murray |first2=Robin |date=2024-04-22 |title=Sega Bodega's 'True' Relishes Honesty {{!}} News |url=https://www.clashmusic.com/news/sega-bodegas-true-relishes-honesty/ |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=Clash Magazine Music News, Reviews & Interviews |language=en-GB}}</ref> He will embark on the Tears, Tours and Sighs tour to promote the album, visiting Europe and North America from September through November 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hatfield |first=Amanda |title=Sega Bodega announces North American tour |url=https://www.brooklynvegan.com/sega-bodega-announces-north-american-tour/ |access-date=2024-05-02 |website=BrooklynVegan |language=en-US}}</ref> Additionally, Kiss Facility will support Danish singer [[Erika de Casier]] on tour throughout Europe from May through July 2024.

== Personal life ==
Navarrete has been open about his struggles with alcoholism, stating he often hid his anxieties behind drinking, "For the first two years when I got to London, I kind of just partied more, and more... I was the intense guy who was always drunk. It actually takes a long time to re-establish yourself as not 'that' person."<ref name=":0" /> He has also stated that quitting alcohol was the hardest thing he has ever done.<ref>{{Cite web|title=20 Questions: Sega Bodega|url=https://crackmagazine.net/article/long-reads/20-questions-sega-bodega/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=Crack Magazine}}</ref>

Navarrete has also been open about his struggles with mental health, writing an [[op-ed]] and guide on [[self-care]] in 2018 for [[i-D]], coinciding with the release of his EP titled ''self*care''.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bodega|first=Sega|date=2018-12-13|title=Sega Bodega's guide to self care|url=https://i-d.co/article/sega-bodega-self-care-guide/|access-date=2020-11-20|website=i-D|language=en}}</ref>

Navarrete formerly had a relationship with Mimi Wade. He is currently in a relationship with Mayah Alkhateri, his bandmate in Kiss Facility.
